passages.title: Shard of Kozak
passages.text: <The Shard of Kozak tugs as if it wants to fly into place.>

passages.title: Shard of Kozak
passages.text: <The Shard of Kozak locks into position next to the portal. You can feel the dark writhing of fel energy surround you as it collects near the portal.>

passages.title: Bad Apples
passages.text:
That fruit over there? That's a pale imitation to what I can grow.

But that accursed Daglir somehow manages to gain the favor of the courts, so we must dine on mediocrity!

We must teach Daglir a lesson for stealing my crop, but we must be discreet.

Outside the shield grows a purple flower called Shadowbloom. Fetch some for me and we'll make sure that he pays dearly for his insolence!

passages.title: Bad Apples
passages.text: I would avoid eating any food until you've washed your hands.

passages.title: Bad Apples
passages.text: Excellent. This will be enough for my purposes.

passages.title: The Key Is Around Here Somewhere...
passages.text:
Well aren't ye a sight fer sore eyes!

It's no use tryin' to bust open this cage, this one needs a key!

Now, I know what yer thinkin', "How is it possible that the Burnin' Legion could capture a dwarf as mighty as ol' Angus here."

Ye can rest easy knowin' I let myself be captured. I'm here to rescue a dear friend o' mine, an' gettin' captured was the only way!

I had the key in me pocket... but it musta' fell out.

It's errm... around here somewhere.

A felhunter ate it a wee while back...

passages.title: The Key Is Around Here Somewhere...
passages.text: Did ye find the key?

passages.title: The Key Is Around Here Somewhere...
passages.text:
Ye found the key! Quickly, see if it fits...

Aye, that's the one! Ye did it!

passages.title: Search and Rescue!
passages.text:
We've got to find Brambley before it's too late!

Ol' Brambley an' I have been fightin' side by side since the Third War. When the Burnin' Legion invaded, we didn't think twice about coming to the Broken Isles.

Fightin' is what we do best!

During the battle ol' Brambley got caught too deep an' got himself captured. Now we've got to rescue him!

Last I saw, the demons were keeping him in a prison cell not far from here... let's go!

passages.title: Search and Rescue!
passages.text: Have you found the key yet?

passages.title: Search and Rescue!
passages.text: It's good to finally be free from this dreadful cage. As thanks, I will keep my word to you and your grotesquely hairy friend.

passages.title: Dispensing Compassion
passages.text:
There is much you need to learn about our city.

First and foremost, Arcwine. It is the vehicle by which we imbibe the Nightwell's energies. Without it, we wither and die.

Palace lackeys have seen fit to ration it, thinking this will control us. Keep us quiet, complacent.

I would like you to look for those in need near the tavern. You will find many, but those most desperately afflicted by this rationing will be obvious.

Take this flask. Revive them. Tend to their suffering.

passages.title: Dispensing Compassion
passages.text: Have you served those who suffer?

passages.title: Dispensing Compassion
passages.text: Your eyes are opening to our reality. I can see it in your expression. Good.

passages.title: Deciphering Demonology
passages.text:
I found a piece of what appears to be a key to something. I'm certain I can restore it if we can find the other bits.

After that, we need to figure out what it's a key to. An' I think I know how to do that.

I've been studying some of the artifacts I've found, and they seem to be pointing to a hidden chamber. I jes' need some more artifacts to study.

passages.title: Deciphering Demonology
passages.text: How goes the search?

passages.title: Deciphering Demonology
passages.text:
I'm startin' ta think you may be as good an archaeologist as I am. But don't let that go ta yer head, lad.

<Brann lets out a chuckle and begins to study the artifacts you brought him.>

Aye, that's it! I know where the chamber is. And once I've reassembled tha key, we're in business.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Through the Fog
passages.text:
I can't believe that after all that searchin' ye did, it's still missing a chapter!

I'm willin' ta bet that those satyrs got a hand on it and took it somewhere. Probably somewhere dark where no one could find it.

I've heard rumors of a place, the Darkheart Thicket they call it, where the strongest of the satyrs are.

If I had ta guess, I'd say ye need to go there and look around fer it.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Through the Fog
passages.text: A world of nightmares is nowhere where anyone should have ta go to.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Through the Fog
passages.text:
Oh ho! Ye found the missing chapter AND a piece of me titan disc?!

This truly is a day of celebration. I'll let ye have the book, and ye can tell me what 'appened at tha end of it.

passages.title: Tried and True
passages.text:
I have realized through experience that the old methods are usually the best and for good reason. I'm done with alternate means of digging for now, and wish to focus on the right way to do things.

That being said, I believe I've found a new powerful artifact and I'll do literally anything to have it.

I've uncovered a fragment that appears to be a mold for a key. I now simply need the other pieces.

passages.title: Tried and True
passages.text: Have you recovered any of the other pieces yet?

passages.title: Tried and True
passages.text:
Yes, I believe that's all of them.

<Tae'thelan carefully reconstructs the mold.>

And now we just need to forge a new set of keys.

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Misdirected
passages.text:
I've been looking into the history of Huln Highmountain, a legendary warrior from the War of the Ancients whom this very land is named after.

Allegedly some of his personal effects were carried here after his death and have been lost in time.

After some digging around I believe I have discovered the location of one of his artifacts to be in a place called Neltharion's Lair.

I'm no fighter, <name>, but you are. Will you go and recover this artifact for me?

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Misdirected
passages.text: If I've followed the clues correctly, then this could lead to one of Huln's weapons.

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Misdirected
passages.text:
This is... not a weapon of Huln's. From the looks of it, I believe this to be the Spear of Rethu, an ancient tauren miner.

I have no interest in this artifact, <name>. You may have it.

passages.title: All That Glitters
passages.text:
Now that the shield is down, the older settlements outside the city have been on my mind.

Did you know that I helped create the filigree on the arcane lamps that are used throughout the city? A simple task, one of my first...

No matter. Nostalgia is the enemy of progress. The lamps are made of material better used in my new works.

Those wretched harpies probably have several decorating their nests. Bring back any you find.

passages.title: All That Glitters
passages.text: Can you imagine, a Lespin original hiding under a pile of leaves? What a waste.

passages.title: All That Glitters
passages.text: Excellent. I shall have these melted down and turned into ingots for my next batch of commissions.

passages.title: Service with a Smile
passages.text:
Oh, simple <race>. Simple, simple <race>.

I did not 'forget' to sweep up those reins from that foolish cakewalk of a knight they call the Lich King. I simply did not bother, as I already received the mighty steed during my raid last week.

<Johnny motions to the horse on his left.>

Since you're here and clearly intrigued by my sweltering greatness, won't you take that superfluous stallion to the assistant resort director in town? My coffers could use a bit of extra lining.

passages.title: Service with a Smile
passages.text: Do not tarry, <class>. The longer you take, the longer until you may dote on me as one of my many admirers.

passages.title: Service with a Smile
passages.text:
<Johnny raises his arm exaggeratedly, glancing at his naked wrist.>

My, my, quite the LETHARGIC adventurer, aren't you? That just might cover my repair bills from the many dungeons I've plundered.

passages.title: Estate Jewelry: A Braggart's Brooch
passages.text:
Amateur merchants worry about losing face from bad products. Masters worry about losing face from bad customers.

Naltethis Springblade has grown too bold for his station, and as such has lost much standing in the eyes of the city's elite.

I sold this man a brooch, a clasp he wears on his cape. I am careful to only sell to those above my station.

My pieces never tarnish, but my name and reputation are much more fragile. Relieve him of my property before he lowers me further.

passages.title: Estate Jewelry: A Braggart's Brooch
passages.text: That oaf will undo years of hard work. It is so much easier to fall than it is to climb...

passages.title: Estate Jewelry: A Braggart's Brooch
passages.text:
Ahh, see! I told you it would not tarnish. Now there's nothing linking me to that fool...

What's that? A plot to weaken his position? Regardless, the damage has been done. Better safe than sorry.

passages.title: Written in Stone
passages.text:
<You bundle the notes and store them away in your pack.

According to his final journal entry, Kel'danath used something called a "spellstone" in his experiments.

The spellstone, if not the arcanist himself, must be nearby.>

passages.title: Written in Stone
passages.text: <This withered seems entranced by the spellstone. He is completely pacified.>

passages.title: Written in Stone
passages.text: <A small tag hanging from his sleeve reads "16 - Theryn.">

passages.title: Firing Up the Forge
passages.text:
Are you familiar with the Obliterum Forge? It can be used to destroy crafted gear, yielding valuable Obliterum. I'm personally quite curious to see it in action.

One of my many admirers recently gifted me a set of adventuring robes, but I'm afraid they're not quite my style.

Place them inside the forge and see what happens.

passages.title: Firing Up the Forge
passages.text: What are the results, <name>?

passages.title: Firing Up the Forge
passages.text:
Success! While their interior decoration sensibilities may differ significantly from those of Dalaran's architects, the demon hunters do make an efficient forge.

You keep the obliterum, <name>. I have a feeling you'll be needing it eventually.

passages.title: The Taken
Ice and Shadow
passages.text:
We took down one of the Necrodark. Ebonhorn found that it held a shard of ice infused with shadow essence.

Perhaps the villains are using these shards as a kind of talisman. I suggest you deprive them of their trinkets.

I know little of such magics, but it seemed that Ebonhorn had a use for them in mind.

passages.title: Ice and Shadow
passages.text: Did you find more of the shards?

passages.title: Ice and Shadow
passages.text: Perfect timing, <name>. These shards will prove very useful in what I'm about to do.

passages.title: Dazed of the Past
passages.text: Let's begin crafting this mount armor, shall we?

passages.title: Dazed of the Past
passages.text: I'm quite anxious to see how it turns out.

passages.title: Dazed of the Past
passages.text:
Is there anything we can't do? I'm starting to think not!

I'll make sure this barding gets to Mei. You hold on to the pattern and maybe you can make some profit with it.

passages.title: First Contact
passages.text:
Time to put your new disguise to the test.

Your first contact is Vanthir, a merchant from the common district. He is in the Grand Promenade today visiting one of his suppliers.

Tell Vanthir to pay me a visit regarding a shipment of dusk lily bulbs. He will understand.

Beyond that, we will need time to prepare. You should return to Thalyssra.

<Ly'leth hands you a corked bottle of faintly glowing fluid.>

Give her this, with my regards. We will call upon you soon.

passages.title: First Contact
passages.text: Have you made contact with our sympathizers?

passages.title: First Contact
passages.text: The Lunastre family is well-connected. They will be of great help to us when the time comes.

passages.title: Thalyssra's Drawers
passages.text: Thalyssra's ransacked estate still contains a number of items important to Thalyssra. Collect them and return them to her.

passages.title: Thalyssra's Drawers
passages.text: What did you find?

passages.title: Thalyssra's Drawers
passages.text: This is a comfort beyond words.

passages.title: The Arcway: Long Buried Knowledge
passages.text:
Beneath Suramar City is an ancient network of tunnels known as the Arcway.

They were abandoned some time ago as part of the cavern became unstable. Since then, who knows?

Regardless of what is currently down there, I believe you will find something essential to our continued success.

Long ago my people took a thorough survey of the ley lines in and around Suramar. This they would have stored in the library in the Arcway. 

Find this map for me.

passages.title: The Arcway: Long Buried Knowledge
passages.text: Did you find it?

passages.title: The Arcway: Long Buried Knowledge
passages.text: Excellent! I will study this immediately.

passages.title: Sharing the Wealth
passages.text:
Lately there have been a disturbing array of changes involving our most precious resource, Arcwine. 

I imagine Thalyssra has thoroughly educated you about what happens when a Nightborne does not have access to a source of power like Arcwine.

With the presence of the demons came rationing. There are many who do not have enough to sustain themselves.

Bring me as much Arcwine as you can carry. I will see that it gets to the right people.

passages.title: Tracking Down the Scepter
passages.text: The logbook contains the latest information on the Scepter of Sargeras. It appears to have been written by an extremely agitated, excited, or psychotic imp and is barely legible. Take this to Calydus for translation.

passages.title: Fragments of Disaster
passages.text:
In the hall beyond rests the bones of the failed arcan'dor.

I will take fragments of the crystallized tree and attempt to read them. We must discover the root cause of this destruction.

Only then do we have any hope of preventing this disaster from repeating itself.

passages.title: Fragments of Disaster
passages.text: Do you have the shards?

passages.title: Fragments of Disaster
passages.text: I will study these carefully. If we are fortunate, there will be answers.

passages.title: The Stuff of Dreams
passages.text:
This arcan'dor is one of an ancient species. They were not bred, but created. In them the arcane and primitive druidic magics merged into something greater than both.

The arcane will soon devour it whole.

We can restore balance, but it will require wild magic. Magic trapped in another realm.

You must enter the Emerald Dreamway and bring back the essence of life itself.

Only then can the arcan'dor find stability and begin to thrive once more.

passages.title: The Stuff of Dreams
passages.text: Do you have it?

passages.title: The Stuff of Dreams
passages.text: I do not know how you obtained this, but I know it was not easy. Much stands against us, but you prevailed. Come. Let us restore the arcan'dor.

passages.title: Ephemeral Manastorm Projector
passages.text:
Oculeth's theory is sound. Reckless, but sound.

A small warp-field could trap and excite ambient mana in the conduit, thus creating a manastorm similar to when the arcan'dor fell out of balance.

I can build a device to generate the warp-field, but I need materials.

Specifically, warp-resistant alloys - such as the armor plating of high-end security constructs in the noble district.

Those constructs are deadly. If anyone owes you a favor, now is the time to call it in.

passages.title: Ephemeral Manastorm Projector
passages.text: Without those plates, the E.M.P. would rip itself apart in seconds.

passages.title: Ephemeral Manastorm Projector
passages.text: These will do nicely.

passages.title: Leyline Feed: Ley Station Moonfall
passages.text:
<This leyline feed appears to be damaged. The large collector at the top is broken.

The broken piece must be around here somewhere. There are rough scuff marks on the floor that appear to be made by something larger than the creatures inside.

Much, much larger.>

passages.title: Leyline Feed: Ley Station Moonfall
passages.text: <The feed pulses softly.>

passages.title: Leyline Feed: Ley Station Moonfall
passages.text: <As you place the broken piece onto the pillar and begin infusing it with mana, arcane energy begins to repair the break. It slowly begins to turn as the leyline is activated.>

passages.title: Trading for Dreams
passages.text:
From the look of you, I take it you're an alchemist, yes?

I'd be willing to trade my services with you for a price that I deem is fair.

I have been away from Suramar for some time now. I long for an Ysera's Dream Draught. To concoct it, you'll need some dreamleaf as well as the leaves of a Dreamer's Tear.

One grows not to far from here in the clearing of some ruins. Take my flask, make this drink for me, and I'll do as you ask.

passages.title: Trading for Dreams
passages.text: <Leyweaver Erenyi seems lost in thought.>

passages.title: Trading for Dreams
passages.text:
You've crafted this rather well. I'm slightly impressed.

Now let me see that silk of yours...

passages.title: Advanced Quenching
passages.text:
Now that we have a frost mage at our disposal, testing this method out should be a cinch.

Here are the plans for what I'd like you to make. Get to work and give me the armguards when you're finished.

passages.title: Advanced Quenching
passages.text: How's that technique coming along?

passages.title: Advanced Quenching
passages.text: Look at that shine!

passages.title: Grimwing the Devourer
passages.text:
You have my thanks for rescuing me from captivity, <name>.

However, Azoran is no mere demon. He is a powerful eredar who commands great rank within the Burning Legion.

Before we can get to him, there is another that must be destroyed.

Grimwing the Devourer is the strongest of the felbats. Place the basilisk flesh upon the altar to the north and slay Grimwing when she appears.

Then, return to me with her head. My thirst for vengeance must be quenched.

passages.title: Grimwing the Devourer
passages.text: What news do you bring of Grimwing the Devourer?

passages.title: Grimwing the Devourer
passages.text:
Grimwing was a formidable demon... I must say I am always impressed with your skill, <name>.

There are many more demons here to kill. It is good to be at your side once more.

passages.title: Return to Karazhan: The Big Bag Theory
passages.text:
I'm sure you've heard, <name>, that a bigger bag is always better. I disagree. I believe it's the quality of the bag that makes all the difference.

Just look at those tattered things around your person. They make you look... well, quite plain.

I'll prove it to you. Allegedly there are some bags in Karazhan that hold an almost infinite amount of items, but the materials required to make such bags are... well, you'll see.

passages.title: Return to Karazhan: The Big Bag Theory
passages.text: After this lesson, I trust I won't have to prove anything further to you.

passages.title: Return to Karazhan: The Big Bag Theory
passages.text:
Now, look closely.

<Tytallo goes into a lengthy explanation concerning the thread count, weaving techniques, and other miscellaneous details that, to a tailor, are fascinating.>

You still seem confused. Here, take the pattern and see for yourself. Perhaps then you'll learn a thing or two.

passages.title: Waxing Crescent
passages.text:
His captor is familiar to me. He is one of Aluriel's lieutenants and a skilled spell-fencer at that. You will need Silgryn's help to retrieve the key to Vanthir's prison.

Our friend's life hangs in the balance. Even if we manage to wrestle him from the executioner's grasp, he may well Wither before we can act.

I need you to take an Arcan'dor fruit to him. They are precious, and few, but for Vanthir this is the only chance he has.

Go quickly, and good luck.

passages.title: Waxing Crescent
passages.text: <Vanthir shudders violently and stares blankly ahead. He does not seem to be aware of your presence.>

passages.title: Waxing Crescent
passages.text: <Vanthir's hands dart up to snatch the fruit from your grasp.>

passages.title: Tea Party
passages.text:
I...I-I'm sorry. I... I can't...

<You hear footsteps behind you.>

A... Abby? Wh...

passages.title: Tea Party
passages.text:
Was that really Abby? Did she bring forth that... thing? We thought her dead not long ago.

What could we have done to bring such... such horror upon our village?

passages.title: Learning From the Dead
passages.text:
I heard you were traveling to Black Rook Hold.

It was once home to the legendary Lord Ravencrest, a brilliant tactician. His knowledge may be exactly what we need to give us an edge against the Duskwatch.

While you are at the Rook, keep your eyes peeled for any books that might have survived the ages that outline the Ravencrest's strategems.

passages.title: Learning From the Dead
passages.text: How goes the search?

passages.title: Learning From the Dead
passages.text: Excellent. The knowledge in these books should prove very useful in the days to come.

passages.title: Unwanted Evidence
passages.text:
<You find a shattered remnant of fel crystal clutched in Skovald's hand, still glowing with demonic power.

It seems the god-king didn't want it found. Did the crystal contain the message sent to him by Gul'dan?

If anyone can glean the meaning of the broken crystal, it's Khadgar.>

passages.title: Unwanted Evidence
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>.

Did you intercept Gul'dan's message to Skovald?

passages.title: Unwanted Evidence
passages.text:
You believe Skovald didn't want you to find this crystal, eh? Let me have a look.

<Khadgar peers at the fel crystal fragment, tracing the lines of power that run through it.>

I have seen this sort of crystal before. They are used to convey orders that come from the highest ranks of the Legion.

This is not good.

passages.title: Snowfeather Bonding
passages.text: <Your snowfeather hatchling keeps getting into your pack and making a mess. It squawks loudly whenever you remove it, and rams you with its head. Maybe you can distract it with a tiny pack of its own?>

passages.title: Snowfeather Bonding
passages.text: <Your snowfeather hatchling looks at you inquisitively.>

passages.title: Snowfeather Bonding
passages.text: <You feel a special bond form between you and the hatchling. It will need some time to recover from this adventure.>

passages.title: Direbeak Bonding
passages.text: <Your direbeak hatchling puffs up its feathers and growls at you in a display of dominance. It seems unhappy with the results, as you are not cowering in fear. It might like to dress up like a grown-up falcosaur and try again.>

passages.title: Direbeak Bonding
passages.text: <Your direbeak hatchling looks at you inquisitively.>

passages.title: Direbeak Bonding
passages.text: <You feel a special bond form between you and the hatchling. It will need some time to recover from this adventure.>

passages.title: Sharptalon Bonding
passages.text: <Your sharptalon hatchling will instinctively run into the kitchen of any inn you enter and make a mess of the pots and pans. It has a tendency to get into any dishes that are laying about, especially the dirty ones. You may be able to curb this behavior by finding it some silverware of its very own.>

passages.title: Sharptalon Bonding
passages.text: <Your sharptalon hatchling looks at you inquisitively.>

passages.title: Sharptalon Bonding
passages.text: <You feel a special bond form between you and the hatchling. It will need some time to recover from this adventure.>

passages.title: Bloodgazer Bonding
passages.text: <Your bloodgazer hatchling seems to love rolling around in flowers. You surmise that an affinity to flowering plants has probably helped the flock locate fruits to consume in the past. It would probably be quite excited to have a special flower of its own!>

passages.title: Bloodgazer Bonding
passages.text: <Your bloodgazer hatchling looks at you inquisitively.>

passages.title: Bloodgazer Bonding
passages.text: <You feel a special bond form between you and the hatchling. It will need some time to recover from this adventure.>

passages.title: Stealing the Source of Power
passages.text:
My prisoner is a chatty one, <name>. He tells me that the Cult of the Green Flame is harnessing fel energy to fuel their efforts of bringing Kanrethad back from banishment.

Within their compound they are powering fel crystals that can hold a great amount of fel magic. Without the proper power to perform their ritual, the occultists will have a tough time succeeding in their task.

Steal their fel crystals, but don't destroy them. We can always find a use for something so powerful.

passages.title: Stealing the Source of Power
passages.text: Have you obtained the fel crystals?

passages.title: Stealing the Source of Power
passages.text: Excellent work, as always, Netherlord. This should certainly buy us some time.

passages.title: Signs of Madness
passages.text:
<Whoever this buyer is, they seem to have left in a hurry. Acrid fumes sit heavy in the air around you, and a campfire in the center of the area smolders.>

<Perhaps something here can point you in the right direction?>

passages.title: Harnessing Power
passages.text:
These fools are using the power of Rimefang's harness to subjugate the frost wyrms. Their leader, Andjor, sits inside on the back of the broodmother and mocks us.

He should breathe no longer.

passages.title: Harnessing Power
passages.text: This harness will bring us great power!

passages.title: Harnessing Power
passages.text: During my training, Mograine told me of what we could achieve with this harness. I look forward to the results.

passages.title: A Giant Problem
passages.text: Destroy The Ship

passages.title: Taking Control
passages.text:
I've been withering away in this cage, prisoner to a wretch called Reyln.

He leads a group of nightborne that are using fel magic to corrupt and control the native wildlife.

The Burning Legion's reach has already spread too far for my liking.

Kill him and recover his control orb, so I can be released from this arcane prison!

passages.title: Taking Control
passages.text: Relyn's control orb is the only thing that can break this magical barrier.

passages.title: Taking Control
passages.text: I have encountered many outsiders in my time patrolling the city, but never one quite as resourceful as you.

passages.title: Snakes and Stones
passages.text:
When the demons attacked, they captured two very powerful possessions of mine: my companion Arikara and the Doomstone.

While death matters not to Arikara, the Legion surely has ulterior plans for him. And the Doomstone... such an artifact of power belongs in my hands, not theirs. We must split up to find them.

For the world's sake, do be careful. I don't need you clumsily destroying everything.

passages.title: Snakes and Stones
passages.text: Greetings, Farseer. What have you found?

passages.title: Snakes and Stones
passages.text: I reclaimed Arikara. Did you find the Doomstone?

passages.title: The Accursed Thicket
passages.text: There is one last task for you and the Doomstone. Thunderaan will explain all.

passages.title: Leather to Legendary
A Few Things First
passages.text:
Lately I've been working with the ore of this land, leystone it's called. I've found its qualities to hold remarkable strength and durability. We'll need a lot of it for this.

There is felslate, but that's a probably too tainted for what you're looking to do with this barding.

You know, I also like to adorn my pieces with something sparkly, like a jewel. I've heard that the elves of Suramar have particularly beautiful ones. Perhaps you could acquire one for this project.

passages.title: A Few Things First
passages.text: I doubt you'll have a problem getting the leystone, but the sapphire might be a bit harder to acquire.

passages.title: A Few Things First
passages.text:
You got them! Now to upgrade your barding.

Never say a blacksmith can't improve on a leatherworker's work, I always say. I mean never. I mean... well you know what I mean.

passages.title: The Archmage Accosted
passages.text:
With the barrier dispelled, Archmage Xylem is finally within reach!

Hopefully he'll be cooperative in returning the Iris...

passages.title: Crystals Not Included
passages.text:
Turalyon is safe, and we can start to fight back.

First things first, we must secure what supplies we can from the crash.

Even though we are blessed by the Light, our ships still rely on crystal technology. From powering our defenses to arming our weapons, we will need to collect as much as we can to fight back against the enemy.

Venture out into the crash and retrieve what crystals you can. While you are out there, keep an eye out for Y'mera. She was separated from us, and will need help.

passages.title: Crystals Not Included
passages.text: I hope you brought backup with you.

passages.title: Crystals Not Included
passages.text: You brought crystals with you? Thank the Light, that's just what we need!

passages.title: Smelly's Luckydo
passages.text:
You! Please help! Stupid hozen stole Smelly's luckydo! 

Now, Smelly always unlucky. Just turned around and look, pack is on fire.

Not going to put fire out because then something ELSE unlucky happen. Maybe something worse!

You beat up hozen, yes? Get back luckydo? Smelly will help you, any way he can!

passages.title: Smelly's Luckydo
passages.text: Find my luckydo yet? Getting kind of hot here.

passages.title: Smelly's Luckydo
passages.text:
Smelly has a new idea! Leave his pack on fire!

Nothing else bad happen while pack on fire! Pack on fire IS Smelly's new luckydo! You keep old one.

Oh, you looking for big tiger? Smelly saw big glowy tiger. Went towards monastery. Smelly was helpful?

passages.title: Spiders, Huh?
passages.text:
I feel like they're still crawling all over me. I squished one egg and all of a sudden I'm covered head to toe in baby spiders.

<Shivers>.

That treasure is just sitting there now. The next guy better not be arachnaphlipic... arachnaphonetic? Arachniphant? Afraid of spiders!

passages.title: Spiders, Huh?
passages.text: I'm always lookin' for more treasure!

passages.title: Spiders, Huh?
passages.text:
Oh, look here! You went and got that treasure! Hey... You still got a spider on your shoulder.

Lets see what fantastic treasure you brought me... This is it? This is worthless! Here you keep it.

Tough break, kid. Keep at it.

passages.title: Grave Robbin'
passages.text: I am not a grave robber, but is it technically grave robbing if the treasure is sitting on a field of bones? It's not like it's buried or nothin'. I'm just gonna sit this one out, just in case.

passages.title: Grave Robbin'
passages.text: I'm always lookin' for more treasure!

passages.title: Grave Robbin'
passages.text:
You found a key in a chest? Nothing else?

I'm guessing the last guy took all the goods, then accidentally locked the key in the chest. So, you just found a key to a chest that you've already looted. Fantastic work... And people say I suck at this job.

passages.title: Ship Graveyard
passages.text: I haven't told you that I was part of the original landing party when we lost almost everything. I don't care what treasure is left there, I'll never go back to that beach. Never.

passages.title: Ship Graveyard
passages.text: I'm always lookin' for more treasure!

passages.title: Ship Graveyard
passages.text:
It's... Wet. This thing is most likely worthless now.

Is there a good piece of treasure on this cursed island? I may not be the brightest tool in the bag, but I'm starting to think this place doesn't really fit my "chance of death versus treasure" ratio.

passages.title: We're Treasure Hunters
passages.text:
I have a feeling you're just using me for tips on where all the best treasure is. From now on I'm naga tell you anything. Did I say, "naga" just then? I meant to say, I'm not gonna to tell you naga. I mean nada! Darn it!

Okay. Seems you got me on this one. I'll tell you what, fetch me whatever is in that chest near those naga freaks and I'll make it worth your while.

passages.title: We're Treasure Hunters
passages.text: You fetch that treasure yet?

passages.title: We're Treasure Hunters
passages.text:
This is it? You sure you didn't find anything else? Like a giant pile of gold on top of a statue made of diamonds which was holding a scroll listing the combination to the vault in Ironforge? That would have been pretty sweet.

Oh well. I can make this into a paper weight or throw it at a squirrel.

Come back tomorrow, I'll have another job for you.

passages.title: To Track a Demon
passages.text:
I took the initiative to scout around before I grabbed that wyrmtongue. It seems like their forces are holed up in a camp in Impsorrow Approach. What I've struggled to figure out, however, is who their commander is and if he's nearby.

If he's leading from elsewhere, the troops need to have some commands on them. Let's go see if we can find any... on their dead bodies!

passages.title: To Track a Demon
passages.text: Collecting some missives should allow me to figure out the commander's position.

passages.title: To Track a Demon
passages.text: Let me take a look at these... I think I've got it!

passages.title: The Legend of the Threads
passages.text:
Tailoring is the noblest of professions because clothing is universal. Most dress with nary a thought. If you analyze the legends, some races stand out from all others. 

The Nightborne are masters of style! Much of the brilliance is in their materials--in particular their thread and their looms. We will take advantage of both. Before you gather materials, I need to confirm my list. Find the fashion treatise I brought with me. Perhaps I dropped it by the flight master?

passages.title: The Legend of the Threads
passages.text: I need a copy of Nights with the Nightborne so we can focus our efforts. I probably left it on my flight over.

passages.title: The Legend of the Threads
passages.text:
Ah thank you for locating that. Let me see--we'll want to target the most stylish of the Nightborne... this seems like the perfect list... oh, she's dangerous... so's that one... very well. 

There is a lot to do so you should get started!

passages.title: The Thread of Shadow
passages.text:
Vandros of the Nightborne. There is an elf who knows how to dress. Ever since he was a young noble in the Court of Farondis, Vandros has been known for snappy, fashion forward outfits. 

I've never been able to see his garments up close but my research tells me that his tailor's technique is not so much in the fabric as it is in the thread. It appears to be spun of the very shadows themselves. 

You have your methods to obtain it, I'm sure. Get his robes and get the thread.

passages.title: The Thread of Shadow
passages.text: Vandros maybe be difficult to defeat but we really need that shadow thread from his robes.

passages.title: The Thread of Shadow
passages.text: Excellent, <name>! Oh the things you will sew!

passages.title: The Thread of Starlight
passages.text:
Melandrus of the Nightborne is First Blade of Elisande. Perhaps you've heard of him? He is a great hero to the Nightborne but, to be absolutely honest, he is a mess with regards to style. 

His accoutrements are somewhat better and a particular pair or bracers are rather nice. In fact, the thead that binds them will be absolutely perfect for your pending outfits. Why don't you get that for me and we will talk further.

passages.title: The Thread of Starlight
passages.text: Did you get the thread from Melandrus' Star-Touched Bracers?

passages.title: The Thread of Starlight
passages.text: Excellent work, my friend! I will find an appropriate use for this as soon as I can.

passages.title: The Thread of Souls
passages.text:
Have you ever had a chance to lay eyes on Elisande, Grand Magistrix of the Nightborne? Stunning! Fashion-forward! Nice posture! 

You'd do well to take a page from her book! In fact, you'd tell well to take the thread from her Suramari Soul Wraps! These hold great symbolic value to her people so it's doubtful she will give them willingly. 

So be it, take her out and get that thread.

passages.title: The Thread of Souls
passages.text: Grand Magistrix Elisande's Soul Wraps  have the most beautiful thread! I don't meant to be pushy but... I'm waiting.

passages.title: The Thread of Souls
passages.text: The soul thread is so beautiful! I am very pleased, <name>.

passages.title: Drapings of the Ancients
passages.text:
<name>, we are going to need a high quality cloth to work with. Thankfully, the weaving quality of nightborne craftspeople from long ago was very good. It is a lost art to some degree but I feel like you can take their masterworks and do even more with it. 

Some of the hostiles in these parts still wear Ancient Imbued Silkweave Armor. Start to unstitch the silkweave cloth from any of that armor that you find on Broken Shore.

passages.title: Drapings of the Ancients
passages.text: Keep your eye out for Ancient Imbued Silkweave. We need a lot of it to start making fabulous things.

passages.title: Drapings of the Ancients
passages.text: Ah, that is just what we need, young <race>!

passages.title: The Wisp and the Shadow
passages.text:
<name>, have you heard of the nightmare lord, Xavius, whose shade haunts Darkheart Thicket? I have heard that this shade is sometimes seen wearing a colorless shroud. 

This shroud is steeped in powerful magic and the wisp will draw it out for you. 

If you can fight the shade, take the shroud, and use your skills to dye it, I will show you how to work wonders!

passages.title: The Wisp and the Shadow
passages.text: Have you obtained and dyed the shroud yet? Make your way to Darkheart Thicket and get it done.

passages.title: The Wisp and the Shadow
passages.text: The shroud is perfect, <name>. Well done!

passages.title: Wisp-Touched Elderhide
passages.text:
Dreadleather, with knowledge carefully reverse-engineered from ancient texts, can be worked into elderhide. It is partly a matter of advanced craftsmanship and partly a simple magic of the earth. 

With the ancient wisps you caught and the materials you've captured and the research I have done, I have put together a Legendary Tanner's Kit for you. Take it to the heirloom hides of Hrul Sharptooth in Thunder Totem. The wisp will help you use the kit there to create Elderhide.

passages.title: Wisp-Touched Elderhide
passages.text: Hrul Sharptooth has hides in his dwelling in Thunder Totem. When you approach them, you will be able to use your kit. Bring it back to me for final inspection.

passages.title: Wisp-Touched Elderhide
passages.text:
The Elderhide leather that you've created is magnificent. Take this, and work your magic to create something of wonder and beauty. 

It is an extraordinary accomplishment and you will look quite dashing--and I should know!

passages.title: The Legend of the Wardenscale
passages.text:
One of my favorite legends is of the Father of Owls on Isle of the Watchers. It is said that his spirit comes to comfort his creatures during times of trouble. 

With the Legion's arrival on the Isle of Watchers, many of the owls are being slain so you can find him there. 

We need to "borrow" him for a short time as he has seen many of the battles where famous warriors and villains have worn armor made of Wardenscale. With his spirit, you can identify items we can extract it from and use it for style!

passages.title: The Legend of the Wardenscale
passages.text: Have you captured the Father of Owls yet?

passages.title: The Legend of the Wardenscale
passages.text: What a magnificent creature! Allow me to attune him to you...there! With his ancient knowledge, we are ready to begin.

passages.title: Mail of the Ancients
passages.text:
There is some wardenscale scattered here and there in the Broken Isles. Various enemies and local monsters seeking to ape the superior races like ourselves will have picked it up and worn it. 

The kind we need is amongst the oldest ever made. It is ancient gravenscale. Keep all that you find and and bring it to me. We will harvest what useful bits we can from it.

passages.title: Mail of the Ancients
passages.text: Do you have the Ancient Gravenscale that we need?

passages.title: Mail of the Ancients
passages.text: That should be enough Ancient Gravenscale. Well done, <name>!

passages.title: Prime Wardenscale
passages.text:
I feel like it is finally time for use to create something truly remarkable. To create the armor that will set you apart from the rest, we need to make the best wardenscale. 

Find the nightelf, Celea, in Azsuna. She has attuned and sanctified the ground where she waits to focus the magic of our world and only there can you make what we need. Go with speed, <name>.

passages.title: Prime Wardenscale
passages.text: Have you found Celea in Azsuna and prepared the Wardenscale beside her? It will only work at that spot. Bring it back to me when you have finished.

passages.title: Prime Wardenscale
passages.text:
The Wardenscale is incredibly light yet strong--I have never seen its equal. <name>, there is nothing else I can do. It is all up to you now. 

Take what you have earned and make wonders with it. Stylish, stylish wonders.

passages.title: The Legend of the Four Hammers
passages.text:
<name>, we should be honest with each other before we begin. You are a blacksmith by trade and this a noble profession. Yet I value style and fashion. Heavy armor and weapons create a certain bulkiness in a hero's profile that I think does no service whatsoever to the cut of one's clothes. 

Fret not--I can at least teach you something about taste in finer materials. 

Go to Dalaran and find a book translated by my brother about 3 forgotten heroes. We will find the finest metals ever forged!

passages.title: The Legend of the Four Hammers
passages.text: Did you find that dusty old tome of Fafnir's? I have to admit that he may have found something interesting in it.

passages.title: The Legend of the Four Hammers
passages.text:
Ah, the book! Let's see... blah, blah, blah, 3 heroes... blah, blah, blah, forge 3 hammers and create the ultimate hammer... blah, blah, blah, forger will be metaphorically crushed and possibly literally killed under impossible expectations, etc. Looks good! 

It appears I can help you find what remains of the armor and weapons of these heroes and these incredible materials can be used to make amazing things!

passages.title: Armor of the Ancients
passages.text:
It is not just the hammers and my careful research that we need, <name>. We also need a lot of the very highest quality of ancient metal to make the final hammer. 

Enemies across Broken Shore that are able to wear armor often collect bits of Ancient Demonsteel here and there. Collect enough of it in your battles for our purposes.

passages.title: Armor of the Ancients
passages.text: Do you have the Ancient Demonsteel that we need?

passages.title: Armor of the Ancients
passages.text: That will be enough for our needs. Good work, <name>!

passages.title: Battle for Azeroth: Tides of War
passages.text:
Champion!

An urgent War Council is underway. Your presence is requested in Stormwind Keep.

passages.title: Battle for Azeroth: Tides of War
passages.text: Thank you for coming.

passages.title: Battle for Azeroth: Tides of War
passages.text:
The Horde have forced our hand yet again.

This cannot stand.

passages.title: The Nation of Kul Tiras
passages.text:
Kul Tiras is the greatest naval power in Azeroth, and a former ally. But we've had little contact with them since Jaina's father, Lord Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, was defeated at Theramore.

Many have criticized Jaina's decision that day, saying she believed so deeply in the promise of peace between the Alliance and Horde that she betrayed her own father.

Perhaps she feels the time has come to atone for this.

Loath as I am to put Jaina in harm's way... Kul Tiras must join the Alliance.

Good luck.

passages.title: The Nation of Kul Tiras
passages.text: Home again, after all this time.

passages.title: The Old Knight
passages.text:
These days Cyrus is the Harbormaster, but he used to be one of Daelin Proudmoore's most trusted knights!

I lost my mother when the Scourge hit Lordaeron. My father sent me here to be raised away from the war. I don't know much about him... just that he was a Stormwind knight who gave his life fighting the Lich King.

Daelin hand-picked Cyrus to raise me and forced him to take a desk job. It's the only reason he wasn't at Theramore.

He's probably checking in that other Alliance ship. Let's go!

passages.title: The Old Knight
passages.text: Sorry, I should have mentioned he can be a bit... long-winded at times.

passages.title: The Old Knight
passages.text:
I've never seen Cyrus fired up like this!

Sounds like we have work to do.

passages.title: Khazaduum, First of His Name
passages.text:
The Argunite Matrix that powered this part of Eredath was shattered by a hulking beast. We had never seen another like him.

He was called Khazaduum and he was a most faithful servant of the Legion. He volunteered to undergo an experimental transformation to become the first of his kind. His arrival was the end of this battle.

As a prize he took the Argunite Keystone from the shattered matrix. Take it back and we can finally end this bloodshed.

passages.title: Khazaduum, First of His Name
passages.text: Please, they should not be made to suffer any longer.

passages.title: Khazaduum, First of His Name
passages.text:
I cannot right every wrong that happened here, but this is a comfort nonetheless.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Shakedown
passages.text:
Where are de guards? 

Princess Talanji has convinced King Rastakhan to permit outsiders in our port. For de first time in centuries, we have allowed non-trolls to set foot on our shores and peddle their wares.

And now trolls of lesser tribes seem to think dey can take advantage of these merchants?

I will not allow dis sort of behavior. While I investigate why de merchants are not protected, I want you to work your way through de bazaar and slay any thugs you find. 

Send dem a message.

passages.title: Shakedown
passages.text: If Zuldazar is to once again be a shining jewel, we must learn to work with de other races.

passages.title: Shakedown
passages.text:
You have my thanks. I think having someone of de Horde dispense dis justice was extra fitting.

De fact dat we have left our harbor so unprotected worries me greatly.

passages.title: Punishment of Tal'aman
passages.text:
Look, Zolani is going about dis all wrong. If you want de Amani, or anyone, to pay attention, take out their leaders.

Go into Tal'aman and look for their mighty gong. Challenge four of their disciples to combat and slay dem.

passages.title: Punishment of Tal'aman
passages.text: De forest trolls can be mighty mean.

passages.title: Punishment of Tal'aman
passages.text: It will not be long before these disciples are replaced with new ones. Hopefully, de next ones will learn from de past.

passages.title: Punishment of Tal'farrak
passages.text:
De Sandfury tribe may have had a hand in some crime around here, but it is really their false belief system dat makes dem do dis sort of thing. Enter Tal'farrak, bang de gong within, and face de hydra dey keep as a sacred pet.

Bring me dis thing's tongues.

passages.title: Punishment of Tal'farrak
passages.text: Did you get de tongues?

passages.title: Punishment of Tal'farrak
passages.text: Ha ha ha. You can tell a lot about a tribe by what dey worship.

passages.title: Rastakhan
passages.text:
You stand before General Jakra'zet, lord of de armies of Zandalar, enforcer of her seas and bringer of war.

And I do not like you. 

It took years to earn my place here after your Horde laid waste to my people. You will not undo what I have built.

I will see you kneel before King Rastakhan. I will watch you beg as he lets me take your head for a trophy. I will fling your corpse into de wastes of Vol'dun.

Her "Highness" may object... but she is not queen yet.

Come. Let us fly to your fate.

passages.title: Rastakhan
passages.text: Welcome, Champion of de Horde. I am King Rastakhan, lord of Zandalar and her peoples.

passages.title: Rastakhan
passages.text: Your deeds had reached my ears before your feet ever set foot in my land. It is time we spoke.

passages.title: Speaker of the Horde
passages.text:
Your Horde has grown powerful, eclipsing some of de troll empires in its magnitude.

For saving my daughter, you have earned de right to a presence in my city.

Since my daughter has taken such a fondness to you, you may join her in de Great Seal beneath us. De servants there will answer to you now.

Talanji seems excited by whatever she has planned for your people. I look forward to being amused by it later.

Zolani can show you a way down dat does not involve falling.

passages.title: Speaker of the Horde
passages.text:
Welcome to de Vault of Kings, <name>. We move new treasures dat we find into dis room, all because of dis object on de wall.

Dis object dates back farther than anything we know. It is my hope dat I can one day discover its true purpose.

I should not keep you, however. I am sure you have pressing business with Princess Talanji.

passages.title: Welcome to Zuldazar
passages.text:
Champion of de Horde, welcome to de city of Zuldazar, capital of de Zandalari Empire, de jewel of all troll civilizations.

I would have you ride by my side so we might discuss matters without prying ears close at hand.

passages.title: Welcome to Zuldazar
passages.text: Will you ride with me?

passages.title: Welcome to Zuldazar
passages.text: Dat is far enough, Horde scum.

passages.title: Out Like Flynn
passages.text:
I'm relieved you woke up! Having to carry you would have made this job far less appealing.

The name's Flynn, and my client in Boralus is paying me a king's bounty to break you out of here.

You, my friend, are incarcerated in Tol Dagor. Used to be a legit prison... 'til the Ashvane Trading Company bought it. Now it's Priscilla's own personal fortress, riddled with scum on both sides of the bars.

Wasn't hard to bribe my way into this cell. Now we just have to get out.

Not to worry. I have a plan!

passages.title: Out Like Flynn
passages.text:
Is that the new powder Flynn was talking about?

I'll take it for safekeeping.

passages.title: Out Like Flynn
passages.text:
It's hard to believe the Lord Admiral would willingly hand you and her daughter over to Lady Ashvane.

She must have had her reasons... right?

passages.title: Arkhaan's Prayers
passages.text:
<As you near the statue, a somber voice fills your mind.>

"You must resist the shadow's pull. Come to me, brothers and sisters. Be whole within the Light.

Let Arkhaan show you the way home."

<The rest of the message is garbled, though the nearby broken seem to be gnawing on pieces of the statue.>

passages.title: Arkhaan's Prayers
passages.text: Did you find anything interesting?

passages.title: Arkhaan's Prayers
passages.text: What is this... a sermon? Fascinating.

passages.title: Journey to Nazmir
passages.text:
It is time to put an end to de blood trolls in Nazmir before their monstrous horde descends upon Zuldazar.

My most loyal followers are willing to come with me to dat cursed place. But it will not be enough.

I am relieved dat you and de Horde are willing to help. Rokhan and his darkspears are getting ready to leave.

I will finish my preparations here. Meet with Rokhan and make your way to Nazmir, I will see you there.

passages.title: Journey to Nazmir
passages.text: <name>! You ready ta go ta a cursed swamp?

passages.title: Into The Darkness
passages.text:
We are in Nazmir to stop de blood trolls from destroying Zuldazar. Dis is de start of our campaign to end dem.

Dese monsters want my kingdom and its people destroyed. We are going destroy dem first.

My father thinks de blood troll threat will go away on its own, like it did in de past. But things are different now.

Rokhan and de others are moving north of here to establish a camp for us to stay in, den dey will join us in de fight.

Are you ready?

passages.title: Into The Darkness
passages.text: De blood trolls are monsters, <name>. Dey are all around us. We stop dem today.

passages.title: Improper Burial
passages.text:
De blood trolls are gathering de corpses of my people for their blood magic. Dis ends today.

I will take care of de corpses here. Take dis torch. Its fires are blessed by priests of Bwonsamdi, de loa of death. 

Burn any corpses of my people dat you see. Each corpse burned means less power for dese monsters' blood magic.

passages.title: Improper Burial
passages.text: My people deserve better dan dis. When dis is done, we must properly honor dem in Zuldazar.

passages.title: Mark of the Sentinax
passages.text:
The Sentinax rains down terror upon the Broken Shore, unleashing hordes of demons that menace our forces. The fiends seek to stop us from taking the Tomb.

They will fail.

Lure out the strongest among their vile ranks. Slay them and seize the marks they bear. Make the Legion fear our strength!

passages.title: Mark of the Sentinax
passages.text: The Sentinax is well defended, but we will crush everything it sends against us.

passages.title: Mark of the Sentinax
passages.text:
Even the mightiest demons unleashed by the Sentinax have fallen before you.

Good. The Legion will be driven from our world, no matter what it takes.

passages.title: The Aid of the Loa
passages.text:
De blood trolls are stronger than ever, thanks to dis G'huun... and now dey are empowering a giant construct!

We need a plan to destroy dat construct, G'huun, and de blood trolls. It is not going to be easy.

But I have an idea.

passages.title: The Aid of the Loa
passages.text: We have a lot to talk about.

passages.title: The Aid of the Loa
passages.text:
Getting de loa's help may be de only chance we have at stopping de blood trolls. 

Let's get moving.

passages.title: A Nation Divided
passages.text:
Kul Tiras must be unified before it can be of any help to the Alliance.

Let's get you briefed on the current situation in each of our major territories.

Then you can take a look at the map behind me and make the call on where you want to go first.

passages.title: A Nation Divided
passages.text: Have you figured out your next move? Use the planning map to help you decide.

passages.title: A Nation Divided
passages.text: We'll support you however we can.

passages.title: They Want Us Alive
passages.text:
Blood troll poisons are made to paralyze, not kill. See, dey want us alive.

I do not feel good thinking about why.

I am making antitoxins as quickly as I can, but I need someone like yourself to get out dere and test dem. Take what I have made so far and see if we can get those soldiers back on their feet.

passages.title: They Want Us Alive
passages.text: It worked? Good! I shall have some of de wounded help me craft more.

passages.title: The Blood Gate
passages.text:
We just received word that the Northern border is under heavy attack by an army of blood trolls.

King Rastakhan has called for reinforcements.

You are more familiar with that threat than any of us. Go and do what you can to help them.

passages.title: The Blood Gate
passages.text: Welcome to de edge of my domain, in more ways than one.

passages.title: Ticks
passages.text: Kill those bloodbellies before dey take off with all of my soldiers! I will have my troops prepare for a flanking charge.

passages.title: Ticks
passages.text: We are losing too many, too quickly.

passages.title: Ticks
passages.text: At last, some breathing room. Now we must press our advantage.

passages.title: Rokhan
passages.text:
My scouts have informed me dat your Darkspear shadow hunter, Rokhan, has returned from Nazmir. He is pinned down at de far side of de gate.

We need to break dis onslaught with a flanking maneuver.

Old Rotana is in position. Mount up and smash through de side of those blood troll ranks.

Once down dere, try to find Rokhan.

Oh, and adventurer, be careful. A lot of dark magic is being tossed around down dere.

passages.title: Rokhan
passages.text: Ha! Thought I be singin' with Bwonsamdi soon. But no.

passages.title: The New Frontline
passages.text: Kill anything ya see dat not a Zandalari!

passages.title: The New Frontline
passages.text: It may seem like a lot, but trust me when I say we saw a lot more comin' when on our way here.

passages.title: Warmother
passages.text: Old Rotana be cursed by da warmother dese vile blood trolls brought with dem. We need to take her down so we can get dis old direhorn back in da field.

passages.title: Warmother
passages.text: Dat vile creature took out half da scouts who came with me. Ya did good.

passages.title: The Orphaned Hatchling
passages.text:
<The surviving hatchling bleats piteously as it gazes at its mother's corpse.

It inspects you hopefully and seems to want to follow you.

Perhaps you can find someone in Warbeast Kraal who can care for it?>

passages.title: The Orphaned Hatchling
passages.text:
Are you de Hordemon I have been hearing so much about? I expected you to be a bit larger. Ha!

Hey! What do you have dere?

passages.title: Xibalan Ecology
passages.text:
I had really hoped this area would be more hospitable.

The Zandalari have been no help whatsoever in clearing this space for archaeological exploration. Before we can even begin to uncover Xibala's secrets, we must make it safe for those less combat savvy to do their work.

You will find the ruins ahead infested with all manner of carnivorous beasts. The few intrepid explorers who ventured within have all failed to return.

Local ecology will not stand in the way of progress, <name>. Understand?

passages.title: Xibalan Ecology
passages.text: I hear this region is very supportive of such life. Their numbers will recover... elsewhere.

passages.title: Bulwark of Torcali
passages.text:
We got Old Rotana up on her feet again. Load up an' take her reins.

Give us some cover so Talanji can fight her way in from her side.

passages.title: Bulwark of Torcali
passages.text: Thank you! Though we must not stay here. More blood trolls are coming. Where is my father?

passages.title: Scrying for the Eye
passages.text:
On behalf of the Horde we seek a relic called the Eye of Xibala.

The locals have been no help whatsoever and Miss Tae'shara insists that we use her survey equipment.

I abhor guesswork. Instead we shall use a more direct method: scrying.

I will mark three locations on your map. I would like you to place a scrying vessel at each of them. I will use their measurements to isolate the relic's location and we will be on our way.

passages.title: Scrying for the Eye
passages.text: Excellent work. Allow me to review the results and we will be on our way.

passages.title: The Shadow of Death
passages.text:
We have four loa, but we only know where one is: Bwonsamdi.

As uncomfortable as it makes me, I am prepared to do anything to stop de blood trolls... even if it means dealing with de loa of death.

Ages ago, Bwonsamdi had a temple here in Nazmir. My scrying has revealed a few locations to de north where I sense a magical presence. Search dem for clues.

Hurry, <name>. Zuldazar will fall if we cannot obtain Bwonsamdi's help!

passages.title: The Shadow of Death
passages.text: Having any luck in de search?

passages.title: The Shadow of Death
passages.text:
You are looking for Bwonsamdi's temple? You must be desperate to be going dere.

Lucky for you, I am headed dat way myself.

passages.title: A Culling of Souls
passages.text:
Only two types enter Bwonsamdi's temple anymore: those looking to make a deal with death, and de dead. You do not stink, so I guess you are de former.

I am headed to de temple myself, so how about a trade?

See de land across de bridge? Dere is a witch named Najima dat I have been tracking. De blood trolls are corrupt to de core, but their souls are useful as offerings to Bwonsamdi. She is too strong for me to deal with, but if you can slay her, I will take you to de temple.

I give you my word.

passages.title: A Culling of Souls
passages.text:
Dis should do it. Her soul is perfect for an offering.

Now, before we go to de temple, there is one more thing to do...

passages.title: Getting the Message
passages.text:
Da loa be powerful, but we be needin' soldiers if we gonna have a chance of stopping dem blood trolls from building dat giant of theirs. If we not be able ta destroy dat thing before it be finished, den Zuldazar and all of our people gonna be dead!

We need da help of da Horde!

Word of da situation already be sent to da warchief. As soon as we be hearin' her reply, we can mov-- 

Wait... what be dat noise?

passages.title: Getting the Message
passages.text: Goblins... of all da worthy units in da Horde, why da warchief have ta be sendin' us goblins?

passages.title: That Which Haunts the Dead
passages.text:
Bwonsamdi knows why ya be here. Ya be seekin' me favor.

<Bwonsamdi ponders you silently.>

A test, ta see if ya be worth Bwonsamdi's time.

Dere be spirits whose prayers sing of something called "G'huun." Dey pay me homage no more. I will not allow da desecration of me own temple!

Go and subdue da strongest of da ancient spirits.

If ya do dis for me, ya may be worth da trouble after all.

passages.title: That Which Haunts the Dead
passages.text: Ah, I feel their souls strengthening me powers. I knew ya be worth Bwonsamdi's time.

passages.title: 'Til Death Do Us Part
passages.text:
I don't know who you are, but I need your help.

My precious Valjabu always told me he didn't care dat he took de vows of a priest... we would be together forever. 

Well, my time came to pass, and I knew I'd not be able to go on without him. I came back and have been waiting in dis spot for... it seems forever, and Valjabu never showed!

I've been walking around dis world for far too long.

Please, I beg you, bring a memento of my Valjabu back to me!

passages.title: 'Til Death Do Us Part
passages.text: Did you find Valjabu yet? His urn is around here somewhere.

passages.title: 'Til Death Do Us Part
passages.text:
<Salazae looks distraught.>

Oh! Valjabu... why did you go on without me?

<A ghostly tear drops from her eye.>

Thank you, stranger. Now I can pass on with no regrets.

passages.title: We'll Meet Again
passages.text:
Now, it be time for ya ta leave. 

Dere be many of dem blood troll souls for ya ta be sendin' to da Other Side for Bwonsamdi, and ya not gonna find any more of dem here.

passages.title: We'll Meet Again
passages.text: So, you formed a pact with Bwonsamdi, too? Good, de more souls for Bwonsamdi, de stronger he is, and dat works out better for de both of us. Just leave some hunting for Hanzabu. I have my own pact to pay for!

passages.title: The Bones of Xibala
passages.text:
Far to the south you will find the bones of an ancient creature. This is Xibala, the progenitor, first of the devilsaurs. She was mother to Rezan, mother to all that came after. The Zandalari do not live there, as it belongs to beasts now.

I have heard rumors of some of your Horde arriving in search of something among her bones.

This is ill advised. Look into it, won't you?

passages.title: The Bones of Xibala
passages.text: I've waited for such a find all my life. I will make my father proud.

passages.title: Prepare for a Siege
passages.text:
It would seem we must make ready for a siege. For now, return to your Horde in Dazar'alor. Prepare for de coming conflict.

Should de forces of Nazmir surge, I will send word.

passages.title: Prepare for a Siege
passages.text:
Though our warchief may balk at further delays, I believe we are honor-bound to assist the Zandalari. 

This is about more than gaining an ally in wartime. The Horde was founded on the idea of aiding those facing their hour of need.

Just as Thrall once came to the defense of my people, so we must help save Zandalar.

passages.title: Direhorn Daycare
passages.text:
Handler Bazkoji had a real gift with de little ones. If dis hatchling is following you, it must mean Bazkoji is dead.

I don't have time to find another handler. Are you up to de task?

It's a lot of work, and de little ones get attached real fast. If you're going to care for it, it will be a commitment. That baby will be depending on you. I hope you will be up to de task of feeding and protecting it.

First things first: food. Dere is plenty of fodder in de pens and river below.

passages.title: Direhorn Daycare
passages.text: Not bad. Dat baby is looking stronger already.

passages.title: Side Effects May Include...
passages.text:
<Your direhorn companion hiccoughs repeatedly. Each time, it either shrinks or grows by a perceptible amount. It whines at you in distress. 

You could use some help.>

passages.title: Side Effects May Include...
passages.text: I knew it was a bad idea to trust this small green mon.

passages.title: How to Train Your Direhorn
passages.text:
I have to get some of whatever you fed your baby! Wow!

Now dat it's bigger, it is time to teach it to be a reliable battle companion.

Let's see how it does against a tougher challenge, hmm?

Talk to Kraal Master B'khor when you are ready to begin.

passages.title: How to Train Your Direhorn
passages.text: How did de training go?

passages.title: How to Train Your Direhorn
passages.text:
Whoops. At least dat was quite entertaining to watch! Ha ha ha!

I guess you two have earned your places here for sure!

passages.title: Ending the Blood Trolls
passages.text:
De loa are smiling on us today. De "matriarch" of dese blood trolls, a sick monster named Ateena, is up ahead.

We have a change in plans, <name>. We will end dis threat now. We kill Ateena and de blood trolls will be thrown into chaos.

She is a powerful hexxer. Go start de fight and I will ambush and catch her off guard.

Let us get moving. We will be back in Zuldazar before de day is over.

passages.title: Ending the Blood Trolls
passages.text: Ateena will not get away from us, we have to keep moving.

passages.title: A Time of Revelation
passages.text:
I can feel Ateena's dark voodoo up ahead. We need to stop whatever she is planning with dis "G'huun".

Be ready for anything, <name>. We do not know what power Ateena truly has.

I do know one thing. If G'huun is threatening my people, den it will die, just like Ateena.

passages.title: A Time of Revelation
passages.text:
De blood troll threat is bigger than I ever imagined. Dat construct is enough to destroy all of Zuldazar

We need more than de Horde to stop dis.

passages.title: Leave None Standing
passages.text:
Now you see what my father refuses to acknowledge. De blood trolls are slaughtering us, and dey need to be stopped.

Our plan is simple, <name>. We will go out dere and kill as many of dese blood trolls as we can. You go east, I go north.

Meet with me after and we will see what is left to do. We will teach dese blood trolls to fear de Zandalari!

passages.title: Leave None Standing
passages.text: Are you finished? Good, because we are close to ending dis menace.

passages.title: Direhorn Growth Hormone
passages.text:
Nice little critter you got there. Seems a tad too small to be much more than a nuisance though. 

Wanna help a friend make a profit? There's an abundance of opportunity here, but these trolls won't listen to me!

Tell you what, I can make a supplement of sorts that'll make hair grow on your chest! Er, your hatchling's chest! 

I know direhorn are vegetarians and all, but there's a reason all the biggest predators eat meat!

Rapid growth requires protein. LOTS of protein.

You interested?

passages.title: Direhorn Growth Hormone
passages.text: So? Did you get everything I need?

passages.title: Direhorn Growth Hormone
passages.text:
Meat is pretty miraculous stuff, you know!

Er, you might want to keep the details about this to yourself for the time being.

passages.title: Teddies and Tea
passages.text:
There's nobody to play with here anymore. But you'll play with me, right <mister/lady>?

It's time for tea! Help me find the other guests, please!

passages.title: Teddies and Tea
passages.text: This is going to be the best tea party ever!

passages.title: Teddies and Tea
passages.text: Hooray! Only one more guest left to find.

passages.title: Naptime
passages.text:
Your not-so-little guy is looking a bit ragged after such an exciting day. I bet you both need a rest, hm?

Come back later when you're a bit stronger.

passages.title: Naptime
passages.text: I bet you and your direhorn need a bit of rest, hm?

passages.title: Naptime
passages.text: I will look after your little one for de time being. Go on your adventures. Learn de ways of de Zandalari. When you are both ready, I will have an offer for you.

passages.title: Headbutting 101
passages.text:
Your beast is looking well fed. Good. Try and keep it dat way.

Now, next you need to teach your little one to defend itself. Direhorns in de wild are prey for much larger creatures and de young are easy pickings for saurid and their like.

Go out into de Savagelands and show your little one how to fend dem off.

It's all in de horn, <name>.

passages.title: Headbutting 101
passages.text: I see a gleam of confidence in your hatchling's eyes. Good. It will need it.

passages.title: Queenfeather
passages.text:
Ah, so you are de one who inherited Bazkoji's herd. What is left of it, anyway.

I know what killed him, and I tried to warn him. Queenfeather is a vicious ravasaur, bigger than de rest and smarter as well. Most of de eggs around here are hers.

Usually I praise de strength of such a beast, but she has become a nuisance.

You will find her guarding her nests in de feeding grounds. Kill her and bring back one of her head feathers as proof dat de deed is done.

passages.title: Queenfeather
passages.text: Does Queenfeather still stalk us?

passages.title: Queenfeather
passages.text: Good. Now dat de bloodthirsty matriarch is gone, maybe we can plant one of ours back into de brood as a replacement... Hmmm.

passages.title: Discreet Discussions
passages.text:
General Jakra'zet cannot be trusted. 

He is up to something, but I do not know what.

Any who question his actions earn demselves a trip to de sands. 

As long as he remains in power, my city will never be safe.

Speak to his guards. See what you can find out, but be discreet. We do not want to alert Jakra'zet to our actions.

passages.title: Discreet Discussions
passages.text: It is not safe to ask questions about de general around here.

passages.title: Discreet Discussions
passages.text: You are going to make more enemies than allies asking questions like dat around here.

passages.title: Rumors of Exile
passages.text:
Talanji sent you, didn't she? 

De princess needs to know dat it is no longer safe to ask such questions so openly. 

Warguard Rakera spoke out, and no one has heard from her since. 

Rumor has it she was exiled to Vol'dun.

passages.title: Rumors of Exile
passages.text: We will not let Rakera and whatever she knows be lost to de sands.

passages.title: Into the Dunes
passages.text:
Whatever Rakera uncovered, it was important enough to earn her a death sentence to de sands. 

We must head into Vol'dun to find her. 

We cannot let whatever she knows about Jakra'zet die with her in de dunes.

passages.title: Into the Dunes
passages.text: These snakemen will pay for what they've done to my home.

passages.title: Secrets in the Sand
passages.text:
I found this journal buried in the sand. 

Kiro tried to toss it in the fire.

"Our wagon has no space for a diary, Meerah. What practical use does it have?"

Don't tell him I said so, but I think it's fascinating! Can you imagine what kinds of secrets it holds? 

Quite a few pages are missing, but I bet you can recover them out on the dunes!

passages.title: Secrets in the Sand
passages.text: What have you found?

passages.title: Secrets in the Sand
passages.text: Dis is Rakera's handwriting. I'd know it anywhere.

passages.title: Searching for Survivors
passages.text:
It is good to see you are safe, but what of de others? Have dey been lost to de sands?

You need to head back to de crash site and see if de others survived.

I will ask around and see if these fox people can tell us anything about Rakera.

passages.title: Searching for Survivors
passages.text:
Jorana knew de risks when she agreed to enter de sands, but I still can't help but feel responsible for her death.

I can only hope dat Tarkaj somehow made his way to safety.

passages.title: Restorative Venom
passages.text:
Meerah here found your friend in the dunes. The lightning strike nearly killed her. It might still, without treatment. 

The wasps within the grove have a painful sting, but their venom also has restorative properties. 

I can extract what I need from their glands.

With an ample amount of venom, we should be able to soothe your friend's wounds.

passages.title: Restorative Venom
passages.text: Have you brought the glands? We can't heal your friend without them.

passages.title: Restorative Venom
passages.text:
<Kiro quickly inspects the glands.>

These should work well.

passages.title: A Balm to Calm
passages.text:
As promised, here is the balm that should remedy your companion's injuries. 

Apply it liberally to any bits of exposed flesh.

Its effects should be felt immediately.

passages.title: A Balm to Calm
passages.text:
Did these creatures come to our aid?

De last thing I remember, we were flying over de sethrak empire. There was a blinding flash of light before things went dark...

passages.title: Knickknack Takeback
passages.text:
Nisha told me you came here in search of an exile. One named Rakera? 

We don't know her, but we might be able to help you find her. 

You help us, and we help you. Deal?

We survive by scavenging. We trade what we find, but the sethrak that raided our burrows made away with many of our knickknacks. 

I always knew they were ruthless, but never imagined they'd be so greedy.

Take back what the sethrak have taken, and I'll see that you are provided safe passage through the dunes.

passages.title: Knickknack Takeback
passages.text: You help us, and we help you. Deal?

passages.title: Knickknack Takeback
passages.text: You're more resourceful than you look.

passages.title: Aided Escape
passages.text:
The sethrak may be strong, but we're quick. Well, at least Mekaru and I are.

We just barely made it back to the wagon with our tails attached. 

The others weren't so lucky, I guess. We've been waiting a while, and still no sign of them. 

If you're headed into the thick of it, would you mind looking for our friends?

passages.title: Aided Escape
passages.text: We abandoned our scavenging as soon as the sethrak showed up. Not all of us made it to safety...

passages.title: Aided Escape
passages.text: Thanks, <name>. We owe you our lives.

passages.title: Unlikely Allies
passages.text:
I believe this is one of the Keepers' keys! Only Vorrik would know for sure. 

We need to head to the temple at once. 

My pterrordax can take us there when you're ready, but we need to hurry.

passages.title: Unlikely Allies
passages.text: We cannot let the Faithless take this temple!

passages.title: Answering Their Attacks
passages.text:
The sethrak's attacks on our burrows cannot go unanswered. 

They need to learn that not all within the desert will give up so easily. 

The only thing the sethrak understand is blood, so that's the language we'll use to teach them.

<Nisha pauses and looks at you, skeptical that you understood her.>

I'm saying we need to kill the sethrak here. All of them.

passages.title: Answering Their Attacks
passages.text: The sethrak will answer for what they have done.

passages.title: Answering Their Attacks
passages.text: Their blood flows down the dunes back to their fortress. The sethrak will think twice before attacking our burrows again.

passages.title: The Bloodwatcher Legacy
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>.

I have been sent on behalf of my father, High Examiner Tae'thelan Bloodwatcher, to oversee the extraction of all fossils, relics, and artifacts from this area.

My sources inform me that an object that could advance the Horde's cause may be buried beneath this very site.

I will require your help extracting it. You see, these nightborne are not precisely good with their hands. Nor do they enjoy getting dirty.

Could you be a dear and set a good example?

passages.title: The Bloodwatcher Legacy
passages.text: By all means, let us assist young Tae'shara. Such enthusiasm is to be rewarded.

passages.title: The Bloodwatcher Legacy
passages.text: You used your hands! How quaint. The nightborne have devised a number of ways to avoid such petty labors.

passages.title: Your Next Move
Growing Pains
passages.text:
These trolls are missing a real opportunity here! They complain about not having enough beasts to go around, yet have they really tried to mass produce them? Nope!

With my Direhorn Growth Hormone, they'll be able to fill these pens to overflowing! Sure, the overcrowding might lead to disease and excess waste issues, but I'm sure those are solvable.

Ha ha ha this is gonna be great!

passages.title: Growing Pains
passages.text: Well? Did your hatchling try the DGH yet?

passages.title: Growing Pains
passages.text: Wow! That worked even better than I thought! I'm gonna make a fortune!

passages.title: Dire Situation
passages.text:
Good news, we found de source of de corruption.

De bad news, it is a ritual on de apex of Zanchul.

Blood magic wielding heretics are empowering some sort of dire troll up dere.

How it made it all de way to de apex without us catching it is something I am sure Raal and I will be arguing about for de next year.

Come, let us stop dis heresy.

passages.title: Dire Situation
passages.text: What wisdom did de loa priests give you?

passages.title: Dire Situation
passages.text: I will not have dat blood in my temple!

passages.title: Forbidden Practices
passages.text:
You come at a good time, adventurer. I have need of a weapon such as yourself.

Yazma's spies say dere are blood cultists in our ranks. King Rastakhan has charged me with tracking down any trolls guilty of practicing blood magic and purging dem.

Take dis totem, route out those with de stench of blood magic, and cleanse dem from dis holy place.

When you are done, tell dat lazy Hexlord Raal to get off his perch and help keep dis place secure.

passages.title: Forbidden Practices
passages.text: Hello dere.

passages.title: Forbidden Practices
passages.text: What? Dat sneering, vile raptor zealot is calling me out for not doing my share? Bah!

passages.title: Kitty?
passages.text:
You have to find our last guest before it's time for tea!

Smoochums really likes the woods, I bet we'll find him there!

passages.title: Kitty?
passages.text:
Mrrow?

<You find Smoochums, but Abby is nowhere to be seen.>

passages.title: The Bargain is Struck
passages.text:
Now dat you have declared a patron loa for your time here in Zuldazar, you should inform de king of your decision.

He will appreciate dat you chose to follow de great Pa'ku.

passages.title: The Bargain is Struck
passages.text:
So, you have chosen de path of Pa'ku. May de winds of war be ever in your favor.
