For myself, I follow Rezan, de devilsaur loa of kings. He and I have not spoken for many years, though.

Perhaps I shall pay him a visit one of dese days.

passages.title: Offensively Defensive
passages.text:
Let me guess, Loti had you kill any trolls dat smelled of blood magic, yes? Well, dat is barely a half measure.

See, blood magic comes from de old ways, and our people have only been giving in to its allure since de walls fell on our northern border.

Come, we will go for a little ride and patrol de border to Nazmir. Dat is where all dese bad ideas are coming from.

passages.title: Offensively Defensive
passages.text: Winds be our ally.

passages.title: Offensively Defensive
passages.text: Oh, so dat bent-tusk nose-breather is trying to win you over with a little flight and some charm, eh?

passages.title: Restraining Order
passages.text:
"Something feels different"? Dat was all Raal said?

His flock of pterrordaxes have swarmed de courtyard of Zanchul. Dey are being driven mad.

Shoo dem away before dey hurt demselves or others.

passages.title: Restraining Order
passages.text: Why are you scaring away my flock?

passages.title: Pterrortorial Dispute
passages.text:
De courtyard of Zanchul has been overrun by pterrordaxes driven mad by some dark ritual. Power is coalescing here, and it is hard to tell who or what is causing it.

I need to track down de source. In de meantime, you take dis, de power of Gonk, and call his allies to help you in battle. Slay dese maddened pterrordaxes.

When you are done, tell Raal to get his flock under control.

passages.title: Pterrortorial Dispute
passages.text: Did you have to kill so many?

passages.title: Competitive Devotion
passages.text:
Okay, I know dis situation is serious, but she gave you de power of her loa? Sounds to me like Loti is more big on recruiting than on dealing with dis blood troll threat.

Inside de temple behind me are three guardians. When I walked in dere, de things tried to kill me. Me!

Someone has corrupted our own guardians.

Here, I will lend you de voice of my own loa, Pa'ku, de pterrordax. Use it to crush dis corruption.

passages.title: Competitive Devotion
passages.text: Dis is worse than we thought.

passages.title: Picking a Side
passages.text:
Look, dis has gone on long enough, adventurer. I am not one to hold a grudge, but I will be damned if I let you double dip with Raal's loa and my own.

Time has come to pick a loa. De loa are not de sharing type.

passages.title: Picking a Side
passages.text: Have you made a choice?

passages.title: Picking a Side
passages.text: Your choice is made.

passages.title: Gonk, Lord of the Pack
passages.text:
You can find Gonk in his lair west of here, in de Garden of the Loa.

You should be able to see his totems. Run near dem to improve your speed.

I will continue to purge de heretics from dis temple.

Mind your manners around de loa, or he may rip your throat out.

passages.title: Gonk, Lord of the Pack
passages.text: What did he say to you?

passages.title: Gonk, Lord of the Pack
passages.text: Oh, good. He did not rip your throat out. Dat is a good sign. Come, let us show de public your choice.

passages.title: Pa'ku, Master of Winds
passages.text:
Come, ride Ata de Winglord with me, and he will take us to Pa'ku.

Oh, and mind your manners around dat loa. Pa'ku has been known to drop followers she is not fond of from a really great height onto really hard stone.

passages.title: Pa'ku, Master of Winds
passages.text: What did she say to you?

passages.title: Pa'ku, Master of Winds
passages.text: Oh, good. She did not have you dropped. Dat is a good sign. Come, let us show de public your choice.

passages.title: Pests
passages.text:
Let me guess, de saurid stole something of yours as well, eh? Look, I don't have de time to run down every little thing dese ankle-biters snap off with.

You want some coin? Help me kill some of dese snappers.

Otherwise, leave me be.

passages.title: Pests
passages.text: A thief has come to steal from thieves?

passages.title: Curse of Jani
passages.text:
Thief and killer, know dat ya be standin' before da Patron of Scavengers, da Lord of Thieves, da God of Garbage, Master of Minions, and da Keeper of Secrets.

Ya be standin' before me in raiment worth entire kingdoms of gold, bearin' weapons dat cost more than even me most devout and renowned followers will ever earn.

I tink now be a good time ta teach ya a lesson. Maybe show ya high and mighty greatness what it means ta be snappin' in da gutters.

passages.title: Curse of Jani
passages.text: You be bitin' that ratmon yet?

passages.title: Curse of Jani
passages.text: Haha! Well done, wealthy stranger. When ya out and about in dese lands, keep ya eyes open. Ya never know when one of de children might be pointin' ya ta a useful place.

passages.title: The Zanchuli Council
passages.text:
You there, Speaker of de Horde.

My spies have told me of dark heresies being practiced in our sacred temple of Zanchul.

De king sent Loti and Raal to deal with de situation, but those two bickering council members are soft on their own followers.

We need someone more... ruthlessly neutral.

Go meet Wardruid Loti down at de Zocalo and she can tell you de rest.

passages.title: The Zanchuli Council
passages.text: Welcome to de steps of Zanchul, <name>. You will be treading on sacred ground soon.

passages.title: Suspicious Shipments
passages.text:
Normally I wouldn't tell you nothin'... but I'll spill it for Cyrus.

Ashvane's onto somethin' big.

They got guys workin' round the clock in there. Even brought in some muscle to keep everyone uh... "motivated."

I don't know anything about what they're makin', but I know it ain't passin' through here to Boralus.

If I were dumb enough to go snooping around in there, I'd look at the goods themselves. See if they got shipping labels.

But I ain't that dumb, so you gotta do it.

passages.title: Suspicious Shipments
passages.text:
Sounds like they're making a ton of this stuff and keeping it under wraps.

That's bad.

passages.title: Small Haulers
passages.text:
<sniff>

They said they would feed us. Said they'd keep us warm.

<Olive runs the sleeve of her coat across her nose.>

But they were mean! And it was really hard work. And when we tried to rest, they yelled at us!

<sniff>

I got away, but my friends are still in there.

passages.title: Small Haulers
passages.text: These kids are gonna have it hard enough without being under Ashvane's thumb. Thanks for getting them out.

passages.title: Stow and Go
passages.text:
<Flynn lifts his collar to hide his face and speaks to you under his breath.>

You see that ship? I know that ship.

Let's just say her captain and I have a little history.

It's a smuggling vessel. Our illegal weapons are on there for sure. I'd bet my coat on it... and I love this coat.

We need to find out where it's going...

How are you in tight spaces?

passages.title: Stow and Go
passages.text:
You alright, mate? I'm afraid your ship's gone.

Somethin' tells me you weren't really a part o' that crew anyway, were ya? Har har!

passages.title: Remnants of the Damned
passages.text:
Ever since da spirits have begun calling upon dis "G'huun," me temple has been covered with da unbearable taint of da undead. 

Da undead be an abomination, but da bloodstones dat create dem be powerful. Dey could be of use ta Bwonsamdi.

If ya wish ta show me ya fervor, den cleanse me temple of their filth and bring me their bloodstones.

passages.title: Remnants of the Damned
passages.text: Ya got dem bloodstones for me?

passages.title: Remnants of the Damned
passages.text: Mmm, dese will do nicely.

passages.title: A Lonely Spirit
passages.text:
Da spirit of a child named Keula be wanderin' me temple grounds. Her ma'da gave her child up ta me long ago, she be thinkin' that a great sacrifice would spare her from me call, from going to da other side.

Well she be right, I not claim her yet. But she be wrong too. Her child be da one to decide when ta be reunited with her ma'da, and it seem ta me dat da child be no longer be content ta wait.

Dey both belong in my realm.

Go, bring da child to her ma'da.

passages.title: A Lonely Spirit
passages.text: Who be you? Have ya seen ma'da?

passages.title: Insatiable Appetite [UNUSED]
passages.text:
That was incredible! I've never seen such rapid growth! 

Your strange friend here be welcome to stay as long as he likes if he be willing to share his secret with the Kraal.
 
As for you and your beast, he be looking awfully hungry again. I suspect you'll find it will take a lot more food to satisy him now.

Good luck, Apprentice!

[NYI - will be a lengthy progress bar though - preferably filled while doing Nessingwary quests!]

passages.title: Meet the Goldtusk Gang
passages.text:
Greetings, traveler, and welcome to de Goldtusk Inn!

Unless you're here to kill us... In which case, get out.

Otherwise, sit down and enjoy de mess!

I mean, don't mind de mess. EAT DE MESS! No, don't eat de mess. Ignore it!

<Rhan'ka turns to the skull with the eyepatch and shouts furiously in Zandalari.>

Ha, don't mind him. All exiles are welcome to rest at de Goldtusk Inn, de only luxury lodge in dese harsh dunes.

Come, let me introduce you to de staff.

passages.title: Meet the Goldtusk Gang
passages.text: My friends are waiting... Don't be rude.

passages.title: Meet the Goldtusk Gang
passages.text: Don't mind half of what those trolls say. Dey don't really mean it.

passages.title: Rhan'ka's Lost Friend
passages.text:
When you head up to Dead Man's Pass, be sure to say hello to Zulsan.

He's my best friend, even if he doesn't want to be near me most of de time. Ha!

Seriously, though, he's been up on de cliffs for days. If you find him, convince him to come back down to de inn. We need him to restock our breakfast buffet.

Oh, and a completely unrelated question dat has nothing to do with you not being able to find Zulsan and my needing to replace him: How wide is ya head?

passages.title: Rhan'ka's Lost Friend
passages.text: Did you find Zulsan yet?

passages.title: Rhan'ka's Lost Friend
passages.text: Thank de spirits you found Zulsan. Sandfury trolls kidnapped de rest of de gang!

passages.title: The Grinning Idols
passages.text:
Before de curse, we were a loyal crew to a good captain. But de curse corrupted Pirate-King Zem'lan, made him cruel and controlling.

Now, he treats us more like slaves than crewmates. Forced to fight and die for his gain, no treasure for ourselves. No speakin' up without punishment.

Well, us four, we ain't gonna be his slaves no more.

A few of de crew hold onto de idols dat Zem'lan used to curse us. Kill dem and take de idols. I wanna see if we can break dem. Just for fun.

passages.title: The Grinning Idols
passages.text: I'd hoped I'd never have to see those idols again.

passages.title: The Grinning Idols
passages.text: Dese be cursed and evil things.

passages.title: Gozda'kun the Slaver
passages.text:
Dat's it. De Sandfury are officially banned from de Goldtusk Inn!

You can't just ransack a place, kidnap its staff, and mock its owner with an assortment of fruits and vegetables and expect to get away with it!

We gotta teach those thugs what happens when you mess with de Goldtusk Gang!

Gozda'kun de Slaver was bossing around de rest of de Sandfury during de attack.

Take him out, and leave some Sandfury behind to spread de word.

passages.title: Gozda'kun the Slaver
passages.text: Dat'll teach de Sandfury to fear de Goldtusk Gang!

passages.title: Terrace of the Chosen
passages.text:
This betrayal has cut deep into the heart of Zandalar. Half of the Zanchuli Council and their followers have sided with Zul and his... blood god.

Lucky for us not all of Zandalar is behind this betrayal.

We need to topple Zul's cultists before they can rally too many to their cause. Zanchul is the place to start.

Go and see if you can muster any of the Zandalari still loyal to their king.

passages.title: Terrace of the Chosen
passages.text: <name>, glad to see you are not dead yet.

passages.title: Nazmir
passages.text:
The blood trolls within the cursed swamp Nazmir threaten to destroy all of Zuldazar. 

Princess Talanji wants the Horde's help in an expedition to strike at the heart of the blood trolls and end their threat to Zuldazar.

passages.title: Nazmir
passages.text: The swamp of Nazmir represents the largest threat to my people. I am glad you chose to help me in this.

passages.title: Vol'dun
passages.text:
General Jakra'zet detests the Horde and cannot be trusted. As long as he remains in power, the city will never be safe.

We are not alone in our suspicions. Speak to Princess Talanji to follow up.

passages.title: Vol'dun
passages.text: Jakra'zet poses a serious threat to my kingdom and your Horde. It would be good for you to investigate his activities.

passages.title: Zuldazar
passages.text:
King Rastakhan is an ancient ruler who is not quick to trust new allies. We must earn his trust if we are to earn his fleet.

Zuldazar is the seat of power for the Zandalar empire and a good place to start in winning over these potential allies.

passages.title: Zuldazar
passages.text:
My father's trust is not easily earned.

Believe me.

passages.title: Raal
passages.text:
Crazzak is a traitor in priest's clothing who thinks if he tortures enough of us it will hurt our loa.

Dey even have my husband Raal up on de apex of Zanchul. Normally I would say dey could have him, but dey are using his connection to Pa'ku to weaken de loa.

Can't have dat. Let's get to de top of Zanchul and rescue my worthless husband.

passages.title: Raal
passages.text: Dis is a problem!

passages.title: Raal
passages.text: Aya... did you have to bring Loti? She is never going to let me forget about dis.

passages.title: Walls Have Ears
passages.text:
Yazma, mistress of spies.

Bah! A traitor who is into creepy crawlies. She chose to side with Zul, and she uses de children of her loa, Shadra, to watch and track everything we do.

We have to kill all de spiders we see, or dat traitor Yazma will know every move we make.

passages.title: Walls Have Ears
passages.text: Are dey dead?

passages.title: Walls Have Ears
passages.text: Well done. Dat should blind Yazma.

passages.title: Midnight in the Garden of the Loa
passages.text:
Yazma and her henchtroll Vol'kaal have pulled most of their forces back to de Garden of de Loa. 

Something bad is afoot, I can feel it in my spirit. Pa'ku is in danger, along with all de loa who have followers dere.

Come, let's fly dere and put an end to dese heresies.

passages.title: Midnight in the Garden of the Loa
passages.text: From here we can strike back at our enemies.

passages.title: The Hunter
passages.text:
Gonk is in danger. I can hear his call.

My loa has saved my life so many times, it is about time I return de favor.

Come, join me at de Lair of Gonk on de west side of de Garden of the Loa, and we will save a god.

passages.title: The Hunter
passages.text: These zealots who follow Yazma do not fight like normal priests or traitors. Dey have dark magics, and have been planning this for a long time.

passages.title: The Hunter
passages.text:
They seek to kill us. They seek to break us.

All they have done is unite us in what will be the greatest hunt the Zandalari have ever known.

passages.title: Staying Hidden
passages.text:
Dere be trouble brewin', mon. Da blood trolls be on da move! Dey set up a large camp nearby and have been sending a small force to da isle south of here. 

If dey discover our position while we be havin' no defenses, it gonna be game over! We need ta see what dey be up to and get rid of dem.

Our best bet be ta investigate da isle south a here. Ya want ta join me? I be ready ta head out.

passages.title: Staying Hidden
passages.text: I can fight no more. De blood trolls, dey are making a move on Krag'wa in a big way. Dey are going to feed him to their bloody god!

passages.title: Mistress of Lies
passages.text:
If you are done dealing with dese peasant loa, den perhaps you can help with my own loa: Shadra.

My "high" priestess, Yazma, is behind all of dis. If she is having her minions slay other loa, den I can only guess she is also trying to sacrifice my own loa as well.

Shadra's shrine is on de northwest side of de Garden of the Loa. You must stop her from slaying de Mistress of Spies.

passages.title: Mistress of Lies
passages.text: Shadra was... consumed? I have heard of such heresies in Zul'Drak, but to hear of it in Zuldazar...

passages.title: Supernatural Support
passages.text:
The loa can bestow powerful boon's to their followers, aid that can be the difference between victory or defeat in our efforts here.

Think carefully which of the two you would like to ask for their blessing. The loa will not give their assistance to those who are currently pledged to another loa.

passages.title: Totemic Restoration
passages.text:
I am fed and my body is prepared. I can now be instilled with my power of old and for a time will be immune to their blood curses and leeching powers.

Use the magic of the glowflies to channel my power from the totems into me.
Soon you will see me restored. Then we will destroy the army that prepares across the river to take all that is mine by force.

passages.title: Totemic Restoration
passages.text: I had hoped this ritual would never be needed.

passages.title: Totemic Restoration
passages.text: I feel like myself again, back when I had hundreds of followers pouring their faith into me. My power will fade, but the trolls shall learn to fear Krag'wa once more!

passages.title: Restocking the Buffet
passages.text:
Imagine for a moment, adventurer. You wake up in de Goldtusk Inn after a long day of drinking scorpid blood, slaughtering Sandfury, and sharing jokes with your best friend Zulsan.

Ya not fully awake yet, and not feeling ya best. What do you need most at dat exact moment?

An all-you-can-eat breakfast buffet, of course!

I'm working on it, but I need some fruit to balance out my menu. Luckily, I've seen some in de oasis outside.

Bring me some, and I'll give you lifetime access to de buffet.

passages.title: Restocking the Buffet
passages.text: Dis buffet is going to be a disaster if we don't get dat fruit!

passages.title: Restocking the Buffet
passages.text: Breakfast is served!

passages.title: Hidden Motives
passages.text:
I do not understand why the naga would bother attacking a small fishing village.

Why waste their time on our simple tribe? The naga seek power and we have none. It makes no sense!

They must be after something else entirely...

Search Darkwood Shoal and learn of their plans. Whatever the naga are after, it must be quite powerful.

Perhaps if we find it first, we can use it against them!

passages.title: Hidden Motives
passages.text: Have you uncovered their plans?

passages.title: Hidden Motives
passages.text: According to the invasion plans, the naga are after an ancient relic of extraordinary power known as the Ring of Tides. Apparently, it was lost hundreds of years ago in a battle not far from here...

passages.title: The Elder's Wisdom
passages.text:
The naga are searching for a powerful artifact called the Ring of Tides.

According to the invasion plans, the ring was lost long ago in a battle with Eraka no Kimbul, the great tiger loa.

The temple of Eraka no Kimbul is just to the north. If the loa was strong enough to defeat the naga before, maybe he can do it again!

We must let the tribe know what we've found!

Take the invasion plans to Elder Kuppaka. He is the oldest, and wisest member of our tribe. He will know what to do.

passages.title: The Elder's Wisdom
passages.text: Elder Kuppaka will know what to do.

passages.title: The Elder's Wisdom
passages.text: The temple is not far away, but it lies in ruin... abandoned and overgrown.

passages.title: Jungleweb Infestation
passages.text:
The walls of the temple could provide us with vital protection against the naga, but the temple is overrun with jungle spiders.

We'll need to clear out the infestation before the tribe can take refuge at the temple.

Venture into the lower ruins and lay waste to the spiders that have nested there.

passages.title: Jungleweb Infestation
passages.text: Now that the spider infestation has been removed, we can safely relocate the rest of our tribe to the temple. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: All Webbed Up
passages.text:
The lower ruins of the temple are covered in thick webs and spider egg sacs.

Some of our tribesman went down to the lower ruins to clear out the spiders, but they haven't come back.

I fear for their safety.

Please head into the lower ruins and free our brethren before it's too late.

passages.title: All Webbed Up
passages.text: Thank you for rescuing our trapped tribesman. We'll be more careful in dealing with the infestation in the future.

passages.title: Wrath of the Tiger
passages.text:
The Tortaka shall have my protection. Even as we speak, an army of the naga have risen from the depths to attack my temple.

How soon the naga have forgotten their previous defeat!

They seek to reclaim the Ring of Tides, a powerful artifact that I took as my trophy when I killed Azshara's previous champion, Mepjila.

I will send you to the battlefield as my avatar to rain destruction upon the naga. They have forgotten what happens to those who trespass against my followers.

Remind them.

passages.title: Wrath of the Tiger
passages.text: Send the naga army back to the sea!

passages.title: Wrath of the Tiger
passages.text: You fought bravely against the naga army and defended my temple. From this day forward, you will be an honored guest at my temple.

passages.title: They Came From The Sea
passages.text:
You are free to rest your weary legs in our camp, but I'm afraid we have little more to offer you.

Naga have driven us from our village by the sea. We can no longer fish or hunt crabs. I fear we may not survive long if we cannot take back our lagoon.

But taking back the lagoon will not be enough. We must find out why the naga attacked us. What is it they are looking for?

Take this ancient scroll and use it summon the spirits of the naga.

They will only speak truth while under its spell.

passages.title: They Came From The Sea
passages.text:
Thanks to your efforts, Darkwood Shoal is much safer now. Still, I fear that the naga will return in force to search for this Ring of Tides.

We must find a more permanent solution to this problem...

passages.title: Mark of the Loa
passages.text:
You have proven worthy of my blessing, <name>.

This means should you choose me as your loa, you can call upon my power when needed.

Commune at my shrine and make your decision. 

Know that whatever you choose, you will always be welcome within these walls.

passages.title: Mark of the Loa
passages.text: I bestow my blessing upon my followers.

passages.title: Mark of the Loa
passages.text:
So the choice has been made.

If you ever wish to change your mind, you can commune at any loa's shrine to receive their blessing.

passages.title: The Curse of Mepjila
passages.text:
Centuries ago, the sea witch Mepjila attacked my temple with an army of naga invaders.

My followers fought bravely, but I arrived too late to save them.

I defeated the naga army with ease. But as I closed my jaws around Mepjila, she placed a curse upon the spirits of my followers, locking them in an eternal battle they can never win.

This mask will give you the power to enter the spirit realm and end their nightmare.

Defeat the spirit of Mepjila and the curse will be broken.

passages.title: The Curse of Mepjila
passages.text: You must break the curse and free the captive souls of my followers.

passages.title: The Curse of Mepjila
passages.text: At long last, my ancient followers have found peace. You have served well, <name>.

passages.title: Blessing of Kimbul
passages.text:
The entrance to the temple is sealed by a magical barrier.

According to my scrolls, the barrier can only be lowered by one who has gained the Ring of Tides.

There is a statue somewhere in the temple grounds with the power to bestow the ring, but the ruins are overrun with jungle spiders. Tulu and I are not strong enough to explore the lower ruins ourselves.

If you can gain the Ring of Tides and enter the temple, we may finally be able to face the naga head on!

passages.title: Blessing of Kimbul
passages.text: The statue is somewhere within the temple ruins.

passages.title: Blessing of Kimbul
passages.text: Now that you have the Ring of Tides, you'll be able to enter the temple and make contact with the loa.

passages.title: Die, Die, Diemetradon
passages.text:
We are competing, you and I and these other savages.

I find this... amusing.

South of here you will find a number of diemetradons. I challenge you, <class>, to slay more of these creatures than I.

Do you accept my wager?

passages.title: Die, Die, Diemetradon
passages.text:
<It does not seem as though Tracker Burke was prepared for what befell him. He appears to be covered in small punctures and lacerations.

Fortunately for you, he appears to have stashed his wager in his hat.>

passages.title: A Thorn in the Side
passages.text:
You fools speak of "big game" hunting like it is a thing of wonder. Bah! 

None know big game hunting like my kin. Mastery of the hunt, passed down from parent to child, for generations. 

I am here to prove it.

I wager that you could not slay more than eleven of the ankylodon beasts that wander this region.

passages.title: A Thorn in the Side
passages.text: <The fresh corpse of Erak appears to have been slain from behind by darts and is disturbingly missing some pieces. Conveniently, the prize money of his wager still adorns the body.>

passages.title: Predatory
passages.text:
<There is a wound in his back, possibly from a knife.

It seems more than the wildlife is fighting back out here.>

passages.title: Predatory
passages.text: You found some dead ones? Did you bring back de loot?

passages.title: Predatory
passages.text: Hmmm. Dese were left behind on purpose. Someone wanted us to find dem.

passages.title: Hunting the Hunter
passages.text:
Your hunter king, Nesingwary, is a mighty fine bit of prey here. I even thought of hunting him myself.

But someone else is on his trail now. And dat hunter, he is a dangerous one.

If you wish to save your hunter king, you best start tracking quickly. If he made camp, you may be too late already. You cannot paint a target and wonder why you were shot!

I believe he was last seen heading west...

passages.title: Hunting the Hunter
passages.text: Ye shouldn't have come.

passages.title: There Is No Plan "B"
passages.text:
Look, I'll be honest with you. Our mech, the A.M.O.D., was the best we've ever made. It was mobile. It was powerful. It was one of a kind! 

What I'm trying to say is, without it, our whole plan is ruined! We have to salvage and rebuild it!

That big oaf of a sea giant broke the A.M.O.D. apart and scattered its pieces all over the shore. Find its parts and I'll try to hammer them back together.

passages.title: There Is No Plan "B"
passages.text: Got those parts yet?

passages.title: There Is No Plan "B"
passages.text: Looks like you've got everything, well... we've got the important stuff at least. Now we've got a big repair job to do.

passages.title: No Goblin Left Behind
passages.text:
Our mission is dead in the water unless we move fast!

I've found the perfect spot for a new base. While I secure the location, I need you to rescue the team and bring them back. We've trained for this a million times. Just direct them toward the rendezvous point and they'll find the way.

We don't have much time, let's go!

passages.title: No Goblin Left Behind
passages.text: Everyone's present and accounted for. Outstanding job!

passages.title: Revenge: Served Hot
passages.text:
Look, the boss might be keeping a level head here, but we should show these naga what happens when you mess with the Gob Squad. Don't you agree?

The naga are sending their behemoths to destroy what's left of our ship. Why don't you take my rocket launcher and make an example out of them. That'll send the message loud and clear!

passages.title: Revenge: Served Hot
passages.text:
There you go! Let's have a moment of silence for the not so dearly departed.

Aaaaaaand... done!

passages.title: Ready For Action
passages.text:
It's gonna take a bit to get the gun chassis set up. Who knew lifting big equipment could be so hard?

In the meantime, why don't you go check back with your friends. Make sure everything's ready on their end. I'd hate to drive this gun into ANOTHER ambush because they're not ready.

passages.title: Ready For Action
passages.text:
Naga, you say?

Sounds like quite de crisis dere. I am glad you were able to get things back together!

passages.title: A True Loa Feast
passages.text:
The blood troll attacks have not stopped until now. They have weakened me significantly and I need to get my strength back. My followers used to bring me offerings of meat from the nearby lands.

Go and bring back a mighty feast. My strength will return and we will stop these attacks once and for all.

passages.title: A True Loa Feast
passages.text: I hunger.

passages.title: A True Loa Feast
passages.text:
<Krag'wa consumes all of the meat in a couple of gulps.> Yes! I have been hungry for so long. As my followers died, my hunger increased.

Perhaps when more come to follow, eating will once again be just an enjoyable pastime.

passages.title: A Magical Glow
passages.text:
Long ago when the trolls began listening to the whispering darkness, I instilled portions of my power into the totems that surround my lair. I need that power now.

In the swamps north of here are glowflies. Their magical essence will aid me in drawing the stored power from the totems. Collect them and return. Then you will see what I was capable of at the height of my strength.

passages.title: A Magical Glow
passages.text:
I should have done this long ago as my followers were being murdered, but the blood trolls were always too strong.

With you lies the last and best chance of our survival.

passages.title: Rendezvous with the Libation
passages.text:
I be honest wit' ya, mon. I be havin' little patience for goblins and their antics.

Go meet with their leader and ensure dat his crew and da weapon be ready for da assault. Zuldazar gonna be overrun by da blood trolls if we fail.

Good luck, <name>!

passages.title: Rendezvous with the Libation
passages.text:
Our mission is a disaster, a complete disaster!

We were about to drop anchor when naga swarmed the ship! The battle was hard, but we had the upper hand until a sea giant came out of nowhere. It beat the ship harder than a foreman beats a lazy peon.

Don't worry, <name>. We'll get this plan back on track. But first, we need to get the crew together.

passages.title: Powerful Spirits
passages.text:
You prove your worth, adventurer. We be willin' to initiate you into de ranks of de Goldtusk Gang, if you wanna join.

De ritual drink is ready. Boiled scorpid blood spiked with bilewing honey!

Don't mind de smell, it's mostly delicious. It's not terrible. It won't kill you. Usually.

When you are ready to join de Goldtusk Gang, let me know. I'll unite you with de whole gang. It's time you see what we see.

passages.title: Powerful Spirits
passages.text: Embrace de spirits.

passages.title: Powerful Spirits
passages.text: You are a Goldtusk now, <name>. Welcome home.

passages.title: Hunt the Hunter
passages.text:
Please, help us. De Frogmarsh is under siege! My master, de great loa, Krag'wa, is not willing to bend to de will of de blood trolls and their dark god. So now, dey are taking his power by force! Dey are slaying his children and taking his totems of power. Dey will even take Krag'wa and sacrifice him if we are not able to end dis madness!

Stop dem! Slay their leader. Perhaps dat will slow dem down for a while. It will give me time to find a more permanent solution.

passages.title: Hunt the Hunter
passages.text:
Your deeds do not go unnoticed. Zentimo spoke of you, before his passing.

When I did not bend to the blood trolls' corruption, they attacked. Now they seek to sacrifice me to their god.

I have no more followers to work through, but perhaps you will help more.

passages.title: Invasive Species
passages.text:
We should seek out an alternate source of energy just in case I am wrong about the conduits.

Luckily enough, I think I know where we can find one.

The panthara native to Argus are solitary creatures, but it seems whatever magic the Wakeners possessed has drawn them here in great numbers.

This is no time to be gentle with the environment--panthara devour energy to survive.

Slay them and see if you cannot reclaim some of the power they have consumed.

passages.title: Invasive Species
passages.text: There is always room for a backup plan. Did you find what we seek?

passages.title: Invasive Species
passages.text:
I had not imagined the final product to be so... sticky.

<Y'mera wipes her hands on her robes.>

It will do.

passages.title: The Defiler's Legacy
passages.text:
It seems you are not so easily deterred. Very well.

Your deeds qualify you to seek the Sigil. To be clear, I am only permitting you to move on. This does not guarantee your success.

The greatest of your challenges lies before you.

You must go to the Praetorium and face Archimonde himself. Only by defeating the master of the Conservatory will you be worthy of the Sigil.

Few have overcome this obstacle. I hope he does not make too much of a mess of you.

passages.title: The Defiler's Legacy
passages.text: Archimonde himself... what have we gotten ourselves into?

passages.title: The Defiler's Legacy
passages.text:
I have never felt power like this before...

<Y'mera handles the shard cautiously.>

We should get this to Velen as soon as we can.

passages.title: Sound the Alarm
passages.text:
Sirens are nothing but trouble! All they do is capture our men, never to be seen again. How is anybody supposed to get their goods to Boralus quickly with them around?

Since you're already going down there... mind culling their numbers a bit?

passages.title: Krag'wa's Aid
passages.text:
Well done, <name>!

Before we left, I heard dat Princess Talanji be headed ta Gloom Hollow. She should be dere by now.

We better be headin' back. She would want ta hear da tale of ya success!

passages.title: Krag'wa's Aid
passages.text: Krag'wa will make a powerful ally in de coming battle. When de blood trolls are defeated, I have no doubt many Zandalari will come to worship him.

passages.title: Head of the Viper
passages.text:
While I was scouting out the area, I saw a big armored naga bossing the rest of the snakes around. Call it a hunch, but I'm pretty sure he's their leader.

As long as the Naga have a commander our operations here will be threatened. Take him out.

passages.title: Head of the Viper
passages.text: Good job, that should take some of the heat off us.

passages.title: Searching the Ruins
passages.text:
Dese dunes are crawling with assassins. Nowhere is safe, but we must press on.

De ruins aren't far from here. 

Let's continue our search on foot.

passages.title: Searching the Ruins
passages.text: Serrik is weak from poison. We're running out of time.

passages.title: The Loa-Speaker's Betrayal
passages.text:
Listen, stranger. I don't have a lot of time left.

I was in de village when Zolani brought de king to us. Said to keep it a secret, or else Zul would find us.

Look around. Dey found us!

But I know... I know it was not de prophet's doing. Our loa-speaker gave Zolani her pretty words, said she would help, then turned around and sold us out.

It is Kihara's fault dat we are dying now. She brought dis upon us!

Kill her... Make her pay!

passages.title: The Loa-Speaker's Betrayal
passages.text:
Dat snake of a womon helped Zul find de king! It is good dat she is dead, but I would have liked to kill her myself.

<Zolani spits.>

Bwonsamdi can keep her.

passages.title: Partners in Heresy
passages.text:
Rezan struggles against his bonds, but we cannot reach him.

De mogu dat Zul called here have raised a shield dat rejects my magic. Find and kill de creatures dat stand between me and my loa.

I must gather myself for de fight to come. They will know de wrath of TWO kings before dis day is done.

passages.title: Partners in Heresy
passages.text: Finish dis, <name>.

passages.title: Partners in Heresy
passages.text: Good. De way forward is clear.

passages.title: Heads Will Roll
passages.text:
Zul's forces try to lay claim to de loa of kings's temple.

You must teach dese traitors de meaning of their actions.

Sweep de temple of de filth dat defiles it. Destroy those who spit in de face of de loa. Bring me their heads so I may remind others of what happens to those who betray their faith and their king.

When you are finished dealing with de unworthy, come find us. Rezan's altar lies deep within de temple grounds.

In Rastakhan's name, heads will roll!

passages.title: Heads Will Roll
passages.text: Time for us to send dese traitors a message.

passages.title: Heads Will Roll
passages.text: When leaving a message, it is always good to use a language dey can easily understand.

passages.title: The Temple of Rezan
passages.text:
De chronicler's words are dire. If Zul truly does wish to sacrifice Rezan...

Dis will not come to pass! I will defend my loa with my life.

Come, <name>, we go to de Temple of Rezan. We must stop dis heresy at once!

passages.title: The Temple of Rezan
passages.text:
<Rastakhan glowers at the priest's corpse before him.>

Zul will pay for dis. Those who follow him will suffer, mark my words.

passages.title: The Scent of Vengeance
passages.text:
I know my king, and I know he is not weak willed. His spirit struggles under de weight of dis betrayal, and confusion roots his spirit too close to death for my comfort.

We will need to remind him of his purpose. His anger.

I have heard shouts of terror from de village below. Zul's followers torment Zeb'ahari while dey hunt for him. Slay those who would harm his people and bring me their blood.

Perhaps de scent of vengeance can revive de devilsaur inside ol' Rastakhan.

passages.title: The Scent of Vengeance
passages.text: I hope we are not too late, <name>.

passages.title: The Scent of Vengeance
passages.text: De scent of blood is a reliable way to wake a devilsaur. De blood of traitorous wretches, even moreso.

passages.title: House of the King
passages.text:
I hear Rezan's call. I will answer, but first you must help me.

Our loa give us many boons, and we repay dem in worship. Offerings, sacrifices, and idols are our tools to earn favor, but dey are much more to our loa.

Dey are sources of strength.

Zul's dogs have begun to corrupt de great golden statues dedicated to Rezan. Even now, I can feel his power dwindling.

Stop dem. Cleanse de idols to de great hunter. Teach dem to respect de house of de king.

passages.title: House of the King
passages.text: My loa is not dead yet. Now ensure he stays dat way.

passages.title: To Sacrifice a Loa
passages.text:
Rezan's power is fading. My usurpers have nearly completed their task.

I have read of de horrors of Zul'Drak, and I have seen de results of dese acts. To think one of my own people would bring dis heresy here is... unimaginable.

<Rastakhan snarls in anger.>

Come! We will end dis traitor who spits in de face of all loa!

Di chuka Rezan!

passages.title: To Sacrifice a Loa
passages.text:
<Rezan's great sides heave as he recovers from his rampage. He is covered in gore.>

Heretics.

passages.title: Captured and Enraptured
passages.text:
You gotta help me! Me and my crew were running late on a delivery, so we decided to take a detour through this grotto ahead. Boy... that was a mistake. This place is crawling with sirens!

If there's one thing my men like more than women, it's grog! Here, take some. Use it to bring them back to their senses. Might be best to rough 'em up a bit to weaken the enchantment.

passages.title: Captured and Enraptured
passages.text: Were you able to free my men? Without them, I'm stranded!

passages.title: Captured and Enraptured
passages.text: My men have been reporting back to me. Thanks for freeing them, <name>.

passages.title: The Necropolis
passages.text:
A deal is a deal, and I pay my debts.

Bwonsamdi is a mighty loa and you are going to need a powerful ritual to obtain his attention.

You are in luck. I already know exactly what needs to be done.

Bwonsamdi's temple, de Necropolis, is just to de north. Meet me in de courtyard and we shall see about obtaining an audience with de loa of death.

passages.title: The Necropolis
passages.text: Ah, there you are. We are ready to start.

passages.title: Seafaring Necessities
passages.text:
She might not be much to look at, but this boat will take me back to Boralus. 

Before my voyage can begin, I'll need a few seafaring necessities. 

Luckily, everything I need can be found in the Ashvane encampment.

passages.title: Seafaring Necessities
passages.text: Have you had any luck securing those items I asked for?

passages.title: Seafaring Necessities
passages.text: This should all help me get to where I need to go.

passages.title: The Captain's Cache
passages.text:
Well, I'm sure you've figured it out by now, eh?

I never was fixing to abandon the crew, I just wanted to move up the ranks. You've helped me out a great deal in that respect.

Speaking of respect, I believe there's the matter of Captain Hartford's lockbox...

Here's the code, courtesy of the fallen captain. Just as I promised. It's all yours!

Now, don't go telling anyone about our little arrangement, okay? I wouldn't want something like that to spoil such a profitable partnership!

passages.title: The Captain's Cache
passages.text: <The chest creaks open.>

passages.title: Clearing the Fog
passages.text:
Did you lead Kaja here? I told her not to come after me. It isn't safe...

My mind remains fogged, but de memories are slowly returning. Jakra'zet... de weapon...

Come, let us find some fresh air. I will tell you what I've discovered.

passages.title: Clearing the Fog
passages.text: Talanji was right not to trust de general. If he succeeds in finding de weapon, our great city will fall.

passages.title: Zanchuli Traitors
passages.text:
Dey are trying to cast down our loa, claiming dem to be false gods.

Dey have turned to de old ways of blood, sacrifice, and subjugation.

I cannot even begin to say how offensive dis is. Kill any of dese traitors you find.

passages.title: Zanchuli Traitors
passages.text: You killed how many? Well, dat is a start.

passages.title: Rescuing the Taken
passages.text:
We are doing our best to contain de fighting in Zanchul and not let it spill out into de other terraces, but we can't hold for long.

If you are going to help, start by freeing Wardruid Loti. Dey are trying to break her on de platform above with a dark ritual.

Her soul is bound to a fetish. You must find dat fetish if you are going to free her.

passages.title: Rescuing the Taken
passages.text: Find... de... fetish.

passages.title: Rescuing the Taken
passages.text: Free at last! Oh, de pain is coming for dem now.

passages.title: To Serve Krag'wa
passages.text:
There are other forces who seek to disturb my frogs. The vile naga attack my shores and drain my frogs of their magic!

They seek to use my followers as a feast for their thirst for mana. It must be stopped!

A powerful shadow hunter named Narez is currently fighting them. You must go aid her and stop the naga from feasting on my frogs!

passages.title: To Serve Krag'wa
passages.text: <name>! Krag'wa himself sent ya? By da loa, I be blessed dis day ta have him recognize me. I need ya help.

passages.title: Just Say No to Cannibalism
passages.text:
Of course the Natha'vor trolls have Shoak! Why would it be easy?

I'm sick and tired of running from these trolls. That's why you're going in to end this.

The Natha'vor trolls have three powerful troll witch doctors called "corpse mongers". Take them out and you'll send the tribe into disarray.

Of course, this could all fail spectacularly and make my terrible day even worse.

passages.title: Just Say No to Cannibalism
passages.text: Good work. The Natha'vor trolls should be in disarray now that those... things are out of the picture.

passages.title: Profanity Filter
passages.text:
I hate this place! I just want to go home, but I can't because that oaf, Shoak, is missing.

Listen, <race>t, I'll make it worth your while if you help me find that dunce.

I've got a way to find Shoak, but of COURSE these stupid totems are blocking my magic! Why wouldn't they?

Take this scroll and use its magic to burn these totems. I'm going to look around to see if that bonehead is just sleeping somewhere.

passages.title: Profanity Filter
passages.text: You destroy those totems yet?

passages.title: Profanity Filter
passages.text:
Looks like that dunce got himself captured by blood trolls.

This is going to get violent really fast.

passages.title: Shoak's on the Menu
passages.text:
I don't know what stupid thing Shoak did to get captured by the Natha'vor trolls, we'll find out once you rescue him.

I bet they're getting ready to make a meal out of Shoak. You need to work fast and get him out! 

Shoak's one of the largest oafs that I know, those trolls won't be happy that you're taking their "meal" away.

passages.title: Shoak's on the Menu
passages.text: Thanks again, I thought I was done for!

passages.title: Offering for the Loa
passages.text:
The time has come for you to make contact with the great loa Eraka no Kimbul.

I can only imagine what it will be like to be in the presence of such an ancient and powerful deity. You have earned the Ring of Tides, so it must be you that addresses the loa. 

Please present the loa with this offering from our tribe. Tell him of our plight against the naga.

Eraka no Kimbul is our only hope of survival now.

passages.title: Offering for the Loa
passages.text: You must meet with the loa. Are you ready?

passages.title: Offering for the Loa
passages.text: It has been many years since I've had a visitor to my temple and been found worthy to wear the Ring of Tides.

passages.title: If the Key Fits...
passages.text:
These Ashvane are unreasonable. I've tried to bargain for my release, but they refuse any offer I bring to the table. 

All they want is whatever's bubbling up in that mine. My kind know better than to go near that stuff. It's volatile.

There are prisoners in the mine being forced to extract it. Us in the cages? We're back up. When someone dies in the mines, they just send another in. 

If you release me, I'll make sure you're rewarded! We just need to find the right key for this cage...

passages.title: If the Key Fits...
passages.text: We need to find the right key to open this cage.

passages.title: If the Key Fits...
passages.text: None of these keys work! We're going to have to find another way...

passages.title: Crab Trapping
passages.text:
We are trapped here with little in the way of food and supplies.

The territorial sethrak control the land to the west, and the spiteful naga the waters to the east. We are caught between a barren desert and a hostile ocean.

If you are headed to the lagoon to face the naga, will you bring us back some crabs to eat?

I fear that our tribe will soon perish without food...

passages.title: Crab Trapping
passages.text: Do you have a case of crabs?

passages.title: Crab Trapping
passages.text: You've arrived just in time, our supplies were getting dangerously low. The Tortaka tribe thanks you, traveler.

passages.title: To Market, To Market
passages.text:
Thanks heaps for getting us out of that pickle, mainlander. I'd hate to ask, but would you be willing to help with another matter?

Even before this curse struck the village, our sausage shipments from Carver's Harbor started slowing down. If we don't get them sausages, I won't be able to feed my family!

Can you help an honest sausage merchant out? Carver's Harbor is just down the road from here.

passages.title: To Market, To Market
passages.text:
Thank the Light someone came!

I can't handle this myself!

passages.title: Save Their Bacon
passages.text:
This is going to sound strange, <class>, but some of my workers were turned into pigs! Lucky I was out on an errand, or I'd have been caught too! Now my people are tied up awaiting... processing. 

<Thomas suppresses the urge to retch.>

I can't get past those monsters, but you look like the sort who could. Not sure if this helps, but I coulda sworn I heard some wild cackling coming from the warehouse.

Please... save my people!

passages.title: Save Their Bacon
passages.text:
Thank you for sending my workers to a safe spot.

Hopefully my men won't have to remain pigs for long.

passages.title: Big Bad Wolves
passages.text:
Wolves with strange, glowing eyes have taken over the area! I don't know what they are or why they're glowing but it cannot mean anything good. They have to be removed!

Please, <class>, slay them before more of my friends are killed.

passages.title: Big Bad Wolves
passages.text: With those monsters gone, no more of my people are going to get killed.

passages.title: That's Not My Fetish
passages.text:
<The glassy eyes of the pig fetish seem to follow you as you approach. The dark power emanating from the witch's fetish must be what is keeping the workers transformed. 

Perhaps Thomas Staughton might have some idea what to do with it.>

passages.title: That's Not My Fetish
passages.text: Removing it didn't break the curse? Damn. We'll have to try something else.

passages.title: Cured Ham
passages.text:
That foul thing has to be what's keeping my men transformed into pigs.

Hmm. Well there isn't too much that can withstand a good cleansing fire! I say we burn it! 

Toss it into the campfire!

passages.title: Cured Ham
passages.text: Into the flames with that foul thing!

passages.title: Cured Ham
passages.text:
You did it! The spell is broken and my men are back to normal!

Well... mostly. They're alive at least.

Now we can get back to normal around here. If you see Elijah in Fallhaven, tell him he'll get his sausages soon.

passages.title: The Missing Fleet
passages.text:
The tidesage order has a sizable monastery right here in Boralus. I say we start our search for the fleet there.

Someone there has to know something, right? You don't just lose the entire legendary Kul Tiran fleet on accident!

We'll need to take a ferry over to the monastery. Make sure you bring your pass with you!

passages.title: The Missing Fleet
passages.text: I've never been to the monastery before.

passages.title: The Missing Fleet
passages.text: Keep your eyes open. I'm not sure we're entirely welcome.

passages.title: The Warguard's Trail
passages.text:
Rakera's journal suggested she moved south. It's de only lead we have. 

Meerah is headed dat way, and has invited us to travel with her. 

These vulpera know de desert better than any troll I've ever met. 

Our chances of survival are highest if we travel together.

passages.title: The Warguard's Trail
passages.text: Ah, you're looking for de warguard? She's de only reason I'm still breathing.

passages.title: Tiragarde Sound
passages.text: We must convince Katherine Proudmoore to pledge Kul Tiras to the Alliance. Flynn believes the Ashvane Trading Company's new gunpowder is our best lead.

passages.title: Tiragarde Sound
passages.text: Maybe with your help we can restore the people's faith in Proudmoore leadership.

passages.title: Drustvar
passages.text: The stalwart protectors of House Waycrest hold fast along the western border, but recently all contact with them has been lost. We must secure their aid in order to bring Kul Tiras together under the Proudmoore banner.

passages.title: Drustvar
passages.text: I've only been to Drustvar once, on a hunting trip. It's a rugged land with a dark history and superstitious people. Steel yourself for this one.

passages.title: Stormsong Valley
passages.text: The Kul Tiran fleet has been lost at sea. The tidesages of Stormsong, with their mystical oceanic magic, may be our only way to locate the fleet of legend.

passages.title: Stormsong Valley
passages.text: Even under normal circumstances, the tidesages would be wary of outsiders. I'll accompany you on this mission and maybe we can finally get some answers.

passages.title: The Ancient One
passages.text:
Dis is far worse than I thought. Pa'ku is crying out in my mind. Dey are doing something to her. Something old and terrible, smelling of de old ways.

She is nearby, just south of here. Come, adventurer, meet me at Pa'ku's roost and we'll rescue her.

passages.title: The Ancient One
passages.text: What kind of world we live in where da faithful must be da ones to rescue da gods?

passages.title: The Ancient One
passages.text:
Heretics and ingrates! All of them! I will drop every last one of them on a ROCK!

Go, little <race>, and make sure the other loa are not falling into the same trap I did.

passages.title: The Ruined Temple
passages.text:
The loa may be our only hope against the naga, but the temple lies abandoned and broken.

Two of my tribe have gone ahead to scout the ruins. They may be able to help you make contact with Eraka no Kimbul.

If the spirit of the loa remains at the temple, we must find a way for him to hear our plight.

passages.title: The Ruined Temple
passages.text: I am afraid that we haven't had much success contacting the loa. The entrance to the temple is sealed and the rest of the ruins are overrun with jungle spiders.

passages.title: Signs and Portents
passages.text:
<The bulletin that Mayor White was posting at the time he was struck by the spell indicates that there have been some strange happenings in the town lately. 

It is likely these events are connected to whatever cast this spell on the village.

Perhaps there might be records from other villagers that could shed some light on the source of this magic.>

passages.title: Signs and Portents
passages.text: <The town's ledger lists a record of the comings and goings of people and goods through the city of Fallhaven.>

passages.title: Signs and Portents
passages.text:
<The writings you were able to find all have one common thread - an old woman who recently arrived in town.

This ledger may contain some information to her whereabouts.>

passages.title: The Wayward Crone
passages.text:
<The ledger indicates that an old woman named Helena Gentle recently took up residence in a house down the road from the town.

The villagers' writings point to her being involved somehow with a variety of maladies that struck the village recently. 

It's possible that she may know what's behind this spell, if it hasn't afflicted her as well.>

passages.title: The Wayward Crone
passages.text:
Why hello there, young man.

We don't get many visitors to Fallhaven. What brings you to my home?

passages.title: Witch Hunt
passages.text:
A curse on the villagers? Oh my, how dreadful!

Although, to be honest, there have been some strange happenings around Fallhaven of late. I wonder if these could be culprit?

Take a seat and have a spot of tea. I'll tell you all that I know.

passages.title: Witch Hunt
passages.text:
<The crone is defeated, and will no longer pose a threat to the people of Fallhaven.  

However, her curse on the village still lingers...>

passages.title: Furious Familiars
passages.text:
<The wildlife in the foothills appear to be under Helena's spell, and this villager appears to be one of their victims. 

They must be the cause of the recent disappearances from Fallhaven.

Perhaps if their numbers were cut down, they would pose less of a threat to the townspeople.>

passages.title: Cracking the Curse
passages.text:
<In her haste, it looks like Helena left her spellbook behind. The pages of this book detail the ritual that she used to entrap the villagers of Fallhaven. 

It seems the effigy holding the spell in the village is protected by smaller ones surrounding the town. If these are destroyed, you may be able to affect the one holding the spell on the townsfolk.>

passages.title: Cracking the Curse
passages.text: <The magical energies surrounding the effigy have dissipated.>

passages.title: A Touch of Fel
passages.text:
Our warframe is almost operational! It just needs a good jolt to revitalize its systems.

Warlocks in the pools below infuse pieces of Argus with fel energy to create living siege weapons. If you can extract one, we can use it to jumpstart the warframe's Judgment Core!

passages.title: A Touch of Fel
passages.text: Remember - immaculate!

passages.title: A Touch of Fel
passages.text: Yes! This is it!

passages.title: Killing Cannibals
passages.text:
Shoak and I have had a few run-ins with the Natha'vor trolls. Must be why they wanted to capture that idiot.

The women in that tribe actually eat the men... and anyone else they can get their hands on. I'm sure they're getting ready to eat Shoak.

Do us all a favor and kill some of those cannibals. The world would be a better place without them.

passages.title: Killing Cannibals
passages.text: Well? Did you take care of those cannibals?

passages.title: Killing Cannibals
passages.text:
I could hear their screams from here.

These blood trolls are monsters, <race>. Who eats their own people?

passages.title: The Lord's Behest
passages.text:
Lord Norwington will want to thank you for saving his son himself. Why don't you come to the estate? We're preparing for a festival, and everybody's welcome.

We'll go ahead and tell him of all that has happened. See you there!

passages.title: The Lord's Behest
passages.text:
You're <name>? The hero that saved my son from the troggs?

Hohoho! You are very welcome at my estate! You must regale me with your tales of your gallant rescue!

passages.title: Be Our Guest
passages.text:
My dear friend <name>, I do hope you enjoy the festival. I throw it every year to bring riders from all over Kul Tiras together for a grand celebration of the sport!

In fact, you deserve the whole nine yards. Please, tour the estate at your leisure and partake in the delicious food and drink, introduce yourself to the people. I insist!

passages.title: Be Our Guest
passages.text: Have you taken your tour yet? Take a break from adventuring and relax!

passages.title: Be Our Guest
passages.text:
How are you enjoying the grounds? We are still setting up, so it will be even more marvelous soon!

To tell you the truth, I have to one-up myself every year. It's quite exhausting organizing it all, but it's so very rewarding!

passages.title: Dangerous Cargo
passages.text:
By the time I realized what was happening, it was too late.

People had been acting strange, but I thought nothing of it. After all, they seemed to still be doing their jobs.

While inspecting some of the cargo, this grub jumped out in an attempt to latch onto my face. I managed to take it out, but it was too late.

All of the shipments are infected. Take this torch. Destroy them.

passages.title: Dangerous Cargo
passages.text: If I had only noticed sooner, perhaps some of this could be avoided.

passages.title: Dangerous Cargo
passages.text: All we can do now is try to contain the threat.

passages.title: Betrayal of the Guard
passages.text:
My boys have gotten in too deep.

They've given in to whatever dark forces are at work here.

Do not hesitate to do what you need to and put them down. They knew what they were signing up for when they picked the wrong side.

passages.title: Betrayal of the Guard
passages.text: You did what needed to be done.

passages.title: Clear the Riffraff
passages.text:
The naga sent their tiny, foul, muck-smelling minions into our camp. They are quite bothersome. 

If we do nothing, and their numbers continue to grow, they could pose a threat.

You look quick and handy. Could you perhaps expunge a few for us?

passages.title: Clear the Riffraff
passages.text: Maybe, some day, they will learn to think for themselves. Or at least choose a master more wisely.

passages.title: The Scrolls of Gral
passages.text:
These gilblins are ridiculous! They are like a swarm of angry bees, buzzing around.

Hmm, maybe not bees. Bees are useful, and make honey, and don't steal things.

They ransacked our scrolls. Most were unusable, but there were three that are quite... potent. 

It would be most unfortunate if those made it back to their masters, the naga. Please clean up their mess and bring back our scrolls.

passages.title: The Scrolls of Gral
passages.text: Ah, <race>. I was always fascinated by your native language.

passages.title: The Scrolls of Gral
passages.text:
These scrolls must be kept safe.

I dare not think how the naga could have used the secrets within, should they have deciphered them.

passages.title: Orders Received
passages.text:
We need ta be knowin' who be leadin' da naga in snatchin' all dese cute frogs. 

Dey got chests around here dat have some kind of scroll dey be readin'. Da ladies be tellin' da men to remember dem orders.

Get me some of dem scrolls so we can be seein' who be callin' da shots.

passages.title: Saving for Later
passages.text:
We need time to recover the artifacts from this place. Time the naga will not let us have.

However, we do have a plan.

We simply hide what we don't want them to find, and then come back in a decade or two. They will have forgotten about this place by then.

Take this illusion scroll and use it to conceal the notable artifacts of power.

passages.title: Saving for Later
passages.text: How is that scroll working out?

passages.title: Saving for Later
passages.text:
Naga may be long lived, but their attention spans are not what they once were.

These antiquities should remain safe and preserved until we return.

passages.title: Beneath the Waves
passages.text:
Those witches dare! In my temple? 

Siavass is stretching past the realm of that which she can comprehend. There is a darkness seeking them, and they call to it! Her kind will become no more than a hollow tool to those who may answer.

I feel it moving beneath us, around us. I feel it like a tremor through my being. 

There is a pressure there, it has a weight greater than that of the deepest ocean. 

We must stop them. They are not welcome here!

passages.title: Beneath the Waves
passages.text: The naga are trying to hide something. My strength may be waning, but one should never underestimate a loa.

passages.title: The Norwington Festival
passages.text:
To whomever receives this invitation,

You are cordially invited to the 15th annual Norwington Equestrian and Hunt Festival!

People of all walks of life from across Kul Tiras shall gather to delight in life's greatest competitions, equestrianism and hunting, while meeting those of like minds and fine tastes.

Hunting events shall start first, led by Abbey Watkins in Foxhollow Woods. They shall be followed by equestrian events at the Norwington Estate.

We hope to see you there posthaste!

passages.title: The Norwington Festival
passages.text: Welcome, traveler! Care to join in the hunt?

passages.title: The Stoat Hunt
passages.text:
One of the greatest hunting sports amongst the nobles of Boralus is the stoat hunt. It is a sport of determination, patience, and skill. Do you think you can rise to the challenge?

Stoats are agile, sneaky, and sharp. They're next to impossible to catch out in the forest, so the best way to find one is to find its burrow and scare it out.

Find their burrows and bring back their pelts. Their fur is soft and much loved amongst the nobles.

passages.title: The Stoat Hunt
passages.text: Have you collected enough stoat pelts?

passages.title: The Stoat Hunt
passages.text: Not only will these pelts please the nobles, they also prove your worth as a hunter.

passages.title: An Element of Danger
passages.text:
These nobles really think killing weasels is the mark of a good hunter? Ha!

It ain't hunting if there isn't a bit of danger involved. There are boars in these woods. That's more our speed out in the mountains! Why don't you kill some of those, then bring me their tusks as proof?

passages.title: An Element of Danger
passages.text: Boars actually present some semblance of challenge to the hunter.

passages.title: An Element of Danger
passages.text:
<Harold lets out a hardy laugh.>

Now that's what I'm talking about!

passages.title: No Party Like a Trogg Party
passages.text:
Troggs? At my party?

My grandfather pushed them back to that cleft years ago to build this estate. To think that they would attack in such force after all these years?

This is just what we needed to make this year's festival the greatest ever!

Show us your heroism firsthand, <name>! Mount Cooper and defeat these troggs! Drag them behind you, jab them with your harpoon... whatever it takes!

passages.title: No Party Like a Trogg Party
passages.text: A grand showing! You had me on the edge of my seat!

passages.title: Mountain Sounds
passages.text:
Kul Tirans won't go down without a fight!

Take this horn. We use it in the mountains to warn each other of danger and lead the charge into battle. Use it to rally our allies against the troggs!

passages.title: Mountain Sounds
passages.text: We are stronger together!

passages.title: Mountain Sounds
passages.text: Our people defend the estate with renewed vigor!

passages.title: Vengeance of the Frogs
passages.text:
Da naga here be led by a priestess, Zaldraxia. She be da one dat figured out how ta drain da frogs of their magic.

Zaldraxia be stoppin' at nothin' ta drain every frog here.

Do what I could not, and kill dis priestess. Show da naga dat Krag'wa ain't a loa ta be takin' lightly.

I be prayin' ta Krag'wa for ya success.

passages.title: Vengeance of the Frogs
passages.text:
Wit' Zaldraxia dead, da naga should be leavin' soon. Ya did what I couldn't, and for dat ya have me thanks.

Krag'wa's blessin' be on ya, I be hopin' soon he recognizes me devotion ta him.

passages.title: A Greater Challenge
passages.text:
<this is a placeholder breadcrumb for a NYI POI.> 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(48104))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(48104))");
 
 
 
 
 
 const cta = WH.Tools.createWowheadClientCta();
 if (cta) {
 $('.db-page-collection-tracker-cta').append(cta);
 }

passages.title: The Waycrest Daughter
passages.text:
You seek House Waycrest? Oh, your timing could not be worse!

I had just received a raven regarding Lord Waycrest's daughter, Lucille, shortly before this... curse came upon us. They apprehended her in Fletcher's Hollow and are taking her to trial.

They say she is a witch, herself! 

If she's found guilty, she will surely hang! You must make haste to Hangman's Point. With what you've seen here, maybe you can convince them of her innocence.

passages.title: The Waycrest Daughter
passages.text:
Can't you see that we're busy here, <class>?

I assume you have a reason for interrupting this trial...

passages.title: The Woods Have Eyes
passages.text:
The sooner I can return the lady Waycrest to Highroad Gate the better, but I will honor her wishes if we can assure her safety.

There are dark things happening in these lands that you don't fully understand. If we must dally, then there are measures that need be taken.

First, the wildlife here can serve as eyes to dark powers. Kill them.

passages.title: The Woods Have Eyes
passages.text: Has our foe been sufficiently blinded?

passages.title: The Woods Have Eyes
passages.text:
Not a beast in sight. Good.

The foes of this land must not find us here in the open.

passages.title: In Case of Ambush
passages.text:
There is more to worry about in these woods than simple beasts. Our enemy employs constructs of wicker and bone that can rip a man apart.

Fortunately for us, these constructs are not very perceptive.

Take these traps and set them up throughout the woods behind us. If our enemies do seek to ambush us here, at least these will slow their minions down.

passages.title: In Case of Ambush
passages.text: We must be prepared. Anywhere can harbor an ambush here.

passages.title: In Case of Ambush
passages.text:
Good, those traps should alert us in case anything tries to sneak up on us through the woods.

You have bought us a modicum of safety, <class>.

passages.title: Trial by Superstition
passages.text:
Witchcraft has long lived in the superstitions of the people here. It is only recently that some of these superstitions have become reality.

According to tradition, one who is tried for witchcraft is allowed to choose the means by which they are tested from among the requests of her peers.

The villagers here no doubt have some strange beliefs of what witches can and cannot do. Speak with them, and see what we can do to prove my innocence.

passages.title: Trial by Superstition
passages.text: What have you learned from the villagers?

passages.title: Trial by Superstition
passages.text:
Well, those are certainly some interesting beliefs. I think it's safe to rule out the fire and drowning, don't you think?

Looks like that leaves us with three tests...

passages.title: A Pungent Solution
passages.text:
The first test should be simple enough. While I may not do so often, I am certainly capable of crying.

Though to be honest, I've never had to cry on cue.

Maybe you could help with that, though. Nearby there is an onion field that belonged to one of the local farmers. It's abandoned, and most of it is dried up by now, but you might be able to find one onion ripe enough in there to cause some tears.

passages.title: A Pungent Solution
passages.text: Have you had any luck at the onion field?

passages.title: A Pungent Solution
passages.text:
Great, you found one! I was worried that there wouldn't be much left growing on that farm. 

The people of Drustvar could learn a thing or two from that hardy onion.

passages.title: Harmful If Swallowed
passages.text:
This last test I am not looking forward to, but it is certainly better than being set on fire. 

They say that a witch can't get sick. We will prove to them that I can.

A venom comes from the saurolisks nearby that is used by our healers when a child swallows something they shouldn't. When ingested, it will make you immediately ill, emptying the contents of the stomach.

You'll need several of their venom glands to get enough venom for an appropriate dose. Removing them intact may prove difficult.

passages.title: Harmful If Swallowed
passages.text: Is the deed done?

passages.title: Harmful If Swallowed
passages.text:
Good. This toxin should have the... desired effect.

Gah, I can't believe I'm going to go through with this.

passages.title: Once Bitten, Twice Shy
passages.text:
I am all too familiar with the bloodfly's bite. We had them all over the fields surrounding Waycrest Manor.

Though I'm loath to subject myself to them on purpose, if it will help convince these people, I am willing to deal with that nuisance. 

Find a jar and collect as many bloodflies as you can. They are common in these parts, and shouldn't be hard to find.

passages.title: Once Bitten, Twice Shy
passages.text:
Well done. 

With this many bloodflies at least one is bound to bite.

passages.title: The Curse of Fletcher's Hollow
passages.text:
It's obvious the constable won't be swayed until we discover what happened at Fletcher's Hollow. I know very little myself--only that the village has been overrun by monstrous creatures.

I must ask that you travel there in my stead and try to uncover what befell the village. I'm sure Marshal Reade will prevent the constable from harming me while you're away.

Do this for me, and I will help you as I can.

passages.title: The Curse of Fletcher's Hollow
passages.text:
You're looking to help solve this curse? Well, that's good to hear. We can surely use all the help we can get.

I'm happy to help you get to the bottom of this. First things first, though, we need to save some of our villagers.

Care to lend a hand?

passages.title: Big Trouble in Little Tortolla
passages.text:
I received a message asking for a sword hand in Little Tortolla. The Tortollan Seekers there are greatly admired by King Rastakhan and have special privileges assigned to them.

Go see what they want and you will have the favor of the King.

And adventurer, be respectful. Tortollans live long enough they can hold your children's children accountable for your actions.

passages.title: Really Big Problem
passages.text:
Hey! Mainlander!

I know I'm supposed to be trying to knock over cairns and hauling out lost rangers, but d'you see that massive stone monster? I'm thinking that's gonna be a problem.

You look like you know how to handle yourself. Think between the two of us we can take it down?

passages.title: Really Big Problem
passages.text:
I suppose I'm not really surprised Arthur didn't exactly follow orders. But I don't think I can complain with the results.

Thanks for making sure he wasn't entirely in over his head.

passages.title: Total Cairnage
passages.text:
My mentor sensed the activation of ancient powers here. We came to stop them but were too late. We banded together with the rangers for mutual protection, but our task remains unfinished.

There is a set of ancient cairns here. These help empower the Drust constructs. Destroying them will also help to settle the undead stirring from the land.

Destroy the cairns and we'll be able to bring sanity to this place.

passages.title: Total Cairnage
passages.text: Power within those cairns does not bode well for anyone in Drustvar.

passages.title: Total Cairnage
passages.text: Thank you for destroying those cairns. We should be able to dismantle the Drust constructs and risen dead more easily now.

passages.title: The Hills Are Alive
passages.text:
The Drust constructs are drawn from the land, but the heart of these constructs is a runic power core. 

We have been trying to collect and destroy as many of these cores as we can. We know of a way to disrupt the magic in the core. Doing so will prevent more of these monstrosities from being created around the dark hearts and protect the land and all living in this region.

Bring me as many Runic Power Cores as you can find and the Thornspeakers will see they are put to good use.

passages.title: The Hills Are Alive
passages.text: We would appreciate any runic power cores from the Awoken Guardians you might find.

passages.title: The Hills Are Alive
passages.text: Excellent, <name>. We can use these to protect the land and the people and creatures living here.

passages.title: Pieces of History
passages.text:
There is an opportunity here.

Learning more about the Drust can not only help us understand the texts that Lady Lucille found, we might be able to discover greater details about how they and their constructs were finally defeated. Filling in the gaps of history could be key to victory now.

This was one of their settlements before it became the place of their final defeat. Let's look for clues in the ruins.

passages.title: Pieces of History
passages.text: Gorak Tul's death shattered his army! The carvings here all show that, but now I wonder... Did Gorak Tul actually die?

passages.title: Following Eddie's Trail
passages.text:
My life is equestrian. I'm not a fighter. I could maybe take a trogg or two, but not a whole tribe.

Please, go into Mistfall Cleft and see if you can find Eddie. Lord Norwington would be furious if something happened to him, and nobody wants to bear witness to that!

passages.title: Following Eddie's Trail
passages.text: Are... are you here to save me?

passages.title: Following Eddie's Trail
passages.text: You saved me! Those troggs are really scary. They took Hotshot and dragged me through their camp!

passages.title: The Power to Reforge
passages.text:
I forged the key using a pristine argunite crystal. Unfortunately, the only ones remaining are used by the Army of the Light's defenses.

Hmm... dendrite clusters might be an alternative. They were used by the elite of Eredath to power simple devices. If enough of the city ruins are still intact, I'd wager the fallen magi or the broken may still have some in their possession. 

Of course, I would need a great many clusters to reforge the key. It seems you have your work cut out for you.

passages.title: The Power to Reforge
passages.text: Were you able to find enough clusters?

passages.title: The Power to Reforge
passages.text: Ah, yes. Combined, these clusters should provide just enough power for me to fuse the key fragments back together.

passages.title: Standing Accused
passages.text:
So you wish to speak with the accused? I see no reason why not.

Be quick about it, though. I will not have our trial delayed. This woman will answer for the fate of our village!

passages.title: Standing Accused
passages.text: What is your business here, mainlander?

passages.title: Standing Accused
passages.text:
So Lady Waycrest has asked that you convince me to let her stand trial?

I think she underestimates the danger of this situation...

passages.title: Nature's Remedy
passages.text:
Your friend doesn't have much time left. The scorpid venom is likely rotting his veins right now. 

He will certainly meet death without a cure.

I will help. 

The first ingredient I'll need is the root of the prickly plum cactus. Its natural healing properties will make a suitable base for the salve.

passages.title: Nature's Remedy
passages.text: Do you have the prickly plum for the salve?

passages.title: Nature's Remedy
passages.text: These cactus roots will do nicely.

passages.title: Creeping Death
passages.text:
Scorposhi venom usually induces a slow, creeping death.

It's remarkable that your friend has survived this long.

As with most antivenoms, the thing that kills is also the thing that heals. 

I'll need to extract the venom from several scorpashi stingers to craft the cure.

When the extracted poison is mixed with cactus root salve, we will have the antivenom we need to treat his wounds.

passages.title: Creeping Death
passages.text: Do you have the scorpashi stingers?

passages.title: Creeping Death
passages.text: Be gentle with the scorpashi stingers, it will only complicate matters worse if one of us become poisoned. The venom of the scorpashi is highly toxic.

passages.title: Hollow, Empty Eyes
passages.text:
<Carved into the ancient statue are two eye sockets that look like they once held gems. 

Perhaps the missing gems can be found within the ruins?>

passages.title: Hollow, Empty Eyes
passages.text: <Carved into the ancient statue are two eye sockets that look like they once held gems.>

passages.title: Hollow, Empty Eyes
passages.text: <The gems slot perfectly into place.>

passages.title: The Best Kill is Overkill
passages.text:
I watched you kill those Sandfury earlier, adventurer. You have blood instinct. I like dat.

I bet de others have you hunting frivolous luxuries for de inn. I'll give you an assignment worth your talents.

Dis oasis is full of dangerous beasts dat'll scare away guests and harrass my pterrordaxes flying in and out.

Kill dem.

Once de skies are clear, my pterrordaxes can fly you wherever you want.

passages.title: The Best Kill is Overkill
passages.text: Are de skies clear?

passages.title: The Best Kill is Overkill
passages.text: Dere are still plenty of things for our guests to kill for recreation. At least now, dey won't be hunted on their way in.

passages.title: Creative Marketing
passages.text:
De Goldtusk Gang is de best gang in all of Zandalar.
