I know dat. You know dat. Everyone in de gang knows dat.

But we need to make sure dat everyone who sees our inn knows dat too.

We need something big... Something like a massive gold tusk!

I don't know where we'd find one of those, but I got a plan.

Dere's a huge saurolisk in de oasis. Bring me one of its giant bones and I'll take care of de rest.

passages.title: Creative Marketing
passages.text: If dis doesn't work, we can always be de Bloody Rib Gang.

passages.title: Creative Marketing
passages.text: Oh yeah, I can work with dis.

passages.title: A Goldtusk Greeting
passages.text:
Thanks to you, de Goldtusk Inn has never looked better!

We got food, we got beds, we got piles of dead Sandfury nearby. Dis is everything I ever dreamed it be!

<Rhan'ka looks out into the oasis.>

You hear dat? Sound like we got our first guest of de day!

Why don't you greet dis one? Show 'em all de great amenities ya built here!

passages.title: A Goldtusk Greeting
passages.text: Our first guest of de day. So exciting! Don't kill 'em!

passages.title: A Goldtusk Greeting
passages.text: De Goldtusk Inn be open to all exiles. We stick together out here.

passages.title: Lost in Zem'lan
passages.text:
Legends say that a mountain of treasure sits deep inside the Port of Zem'lan, pillaged from every corner of Azeroth. But it's guarded by unkillable, eternal monsters.

No vulpera or exile has ever stolen treasure from the Port of Zem'lan and made it out alive.

My caravan was going to be the first. Our scout, Meeki snuck in to figure out a route, but he never came back.

It would be wisest for you to leave here and never return. But, if you go into the port, please find Meeki.

passages.title: Lost in Zem'lan
passages.text: <Meeki has been stabbed multiple times. He is clearly dead.>

passages.title: This Be Mutiny
passages.text:
It be time to face Pirate-King Zem'lan and bring dis mutiny to bear, adventurer.

Zem'lan keeps a gong at de top of his treasure isle dat any crew member can ring to challenge him to a fight. I only ever seen one lass brave enough to ring it, and it didn't end well for her.

But you and me, we be de scourge of de seven seas, aye? Even mighty Zem'lan be no match for de two of us together.

Ring de gong, and let's make Zem'lan pay for cursin' his crew and treatin' us like dogs.

Mutiny or de yard arm!

passages.title: This Be Mutiny
passages.text: Yarr! Vengeance and treasure!

passages.title: A Strange Delivery
passages.text:
The last time our caravan rolled through the Whistlebloom Oasis, we found an odd Zandalari living in a cave. We traded a few things and he paid me upfront to bring him a pineapple. I don't know why.

It took me a long time to find one, but a vulpera holds up her end of the trade.

I was planning to stop by and drop it off after we finished here. But, thanks to your help, we've got a lot more treasure hunting to do here at the port.

If you have time, would you deliver it for me?

passages.title: A Strange Delivery
passages.text:
<Rhan'ka closely inspects the pineapple.>

 This... is... the perfect pineapple!

passages.title: Beaten But Not Broken
passages.text:
<Beastbreaker Hakid's crystal-encrusted key looks like it will open the large cage nearby.

The pterrordax inside that cage, Scion of Rakjan, is stronger than the other hatchlings you've seen in the Crackling Ridge. He holds his head high and doesn't seem bothered by the myriad scars and fresh wounds that cover his body.

If you release him, he'll likely want to return to Rakjan the Unbroken at the top peak of Crackling Ridge.>

passages.title: Beaten But Not Broken
passages.text: <Rakjan lowers his head in respect.>

passages.title: Zandalari Treasure Trove
passages.text:
We've looted some quality goods already, but the real reward is still ahead. The big chamber in the back of the ruins is filled with powerful artifacts.

A treasure trove like that is the sort of thing that can save lives and sell for a fortune out here in Vol'dun.

But those specters you killed weren't lying. Their master or king or whatever is very well-protected in there.

We'll have to take this one down as a group. Let me know when you're ready to head up to the chamber.

passages.title: Zandalari Treasure Trove
passages.text: I'm glad you're with us on this one.

passages.title: Zandalari Treasure Trove
passages.text:
With Zak'rajan out of the way, we've got first claim on all the treasure he's been hoarding here!

You get your fair share, of course. A worker's worth his wage.

passages.title: Ranishu Are Resources
passages.text:
We can't afford to waste resources out here.

Over time, we've learned to take anything that looks even remotely useful, and be creative using what we have. I've turned a skull into a boat and a sethrak into a tent flap.

I can't spit dust when it comes to magic, but I can mix poisons and potions with the best of 'em.

Ranishu stomach acid makes wicked poison, but it's nasty to collect. Don't try to bottle it. Just bring me their stomachs whole and intact. No leaks!

passages.title: Ranishu Are Resources
passages.text: It looks like you've still got all your fingers. That's good.

passages.title: Ranishu Are Resources
passages.text:
Can't say I've seen someone carry that many stomachs at once.

I don't know if I'm impressed or disgusted.

passages.title: They've Got Golems
passages.text:
I've sacked countless ruins across Vol'dun. Everything from saurolisk-infested dens to the cursed Port of Zem'lan.

I don't say this to brag. I want you to understand that I know what I'm doing.

I've survived this long because I take my time, avoid risks, and only take what I need.

That's what we'll be doing here today.

Omi reported heavy golem activity on her first scouting trip into the ruins. Zandalari golems are formidable. We need to learn what's powering them before we head in.

passages.title: They've Got Golems
passages.text: Did you discover the golems' power source?

passages.title: They've Got Golems
passages.text:
The golems are powered by souls? Hmm... 

We're dealing with a very powerful enemy. We should take extra precautions.

passages.title: The Strongest Rope in Vol'dun
passages.text:
You ever tried tying up a sethrak with vulture string? Won't hold 'em for long.

When you really gotta keep something, or someone, tied down, you need sandspinner silk.

Thick, pliable, and not as sticky as you'd think.

This isn't a tailoring lesson. Omi's scouting report showed a lot of sandspinners inside the ruin courtyard. Get their silk and bring it back to me.

passages.title: The Strongest Rope in Vol'dun
passages.text: Don't even bother trying to tear it. You can't do it.

passages.title: The Strongest Rope in Vol'dun
passages.text: Not every treasure is gold, <name>. We vulpera have learned to recognize value wherever it hides in Vol'dun.

passages.title: Anglepoint Wharf
passages.text:
HELP WANTED.

An unidentified illness has cropped up in Anglepoint Wharf. Those experienced with medicine or healing should report to the Therold Wavestone at their earliest convenience.

Citizens are advised against visiting Anglepoint on personal business until further notice.

Thank you for your cooperation.

passages.title: Anglepoint Wharf
passages.text:
Oh! Are you here because of my posting?

Thank the sea, I need all the able-bodied help I can get.

passages.title: Stinging Barbs
passages.text:
The Outrigger hunters exhibit the pinnacle of Kul Tiran brawn. But they would indubitably be unable to succeed in taking down the most impressive of their prey without my own inventions!

I present to you, the most ordinary of harpoons. However, with just a tad of gnomish ingenuity, this average weapon can become so much more! 

All that I need are barbs from the rays in the harbor. Using them, I can fashion a poison that can stun even the most colossal of sea monsters!

passages.title: Stinging Barbs
passages.text: Be careful with those stingers, <name>! They'd put someone of your frame down easily!

passages.title: Stinging Barbs
passages.text:
Well throw me a hammer and call me Nancy!

Thank you kindly pal. This should be plenty! I'll get to work!

passages.title: A Cure from the Sea
passages.text:
You may not believe it, but seaweed is one of the most important gifts the sea grants to us. Without it, my tonic shall be useless.

I know it is much to ask, but can you go into the harbor and collect some for me? The water is tumultuous in this trying time, but I will give you my blessing.

passages.title: A Cure from the Sea
passages.text: The sea cannot offer its guidance when it is in such pain. I feel as if one of my senses is blinded.

passages.title: A Cure from the Sea
passages.text: Glorious! This should be plenty.

passages.title: Tainted Shipments
passages.text:
If one shipment was compromised, who knows how many of the others are.

Nearby, the fishpackers prepare shipments to be sent to the rest of Kul Tiras. We must check the rest of the shipments before this plague can spread!

passages.title: Tainted Shipments
passages.text: I am... aghast. How could this happen right under our very noses?

passages.title: Evacuate the Premises
passages.text:
The people of Anglepoint need me to stand tall, to not panic in the face of the unknown.

I will admit to not being the best at this.

Even now, the fishpackers are handling the tainted product and preparing it for shipment. They are in great danger, and we cannot allow them to stay in harm's way.

We must get them to safety!

passages.title: Evacuate the Premises
passages.text: If there is even a chance of harm to innocents, we must protect them at all cost.

passages.title: Paddle to Safety
passages.text:
Perhaps... perhaps I can still help my people.

I overheard conversations between the foreman and his men. It sounds as if the source of this corruption comes from the deeper waters, where the Stormriggers do their monster hunting.

Please, assist me in investigating this. I can still redeem myself and this operation.

passages.title: Paddle to Safety
passages.text: I can't sit idly by anymore.

passages.title: Paddle to Safety
passages.text: From here, we can launch our investigation.

passages.title: Those Aren't Fish Eggs
passages.text:
Corruption has seeped into the sea.

Part of our job is to keep the monsters of these parts under control. A cruel magic has taken over many of the beasts. I take the challenge of the hunt with pride, but too many and we are overrun!

Monster eggs are scattered across the breeding grounds, pulsing with a dark energy.

Get your stompin' boots on.

passages.title: Those Aren't Fish Eggs
passages.text: Ah, the satisfying squish of a monster egg under your boot. What a feeling!

passages.title: Those Aren't Fish Eggs
passages.text: It's best to not know what corrupted eggs will hatch into, though I could imagine the fight that we may now never see.

passages.title: Emergent Strategy
passages.text:
My son went where? Chasing our workers into the woods once again?

That boy is too soft-hearted. No matter what I do, he will never be strong enough to take over the family business.

I demand he come back this instant. He's got better ways to spend his time than going on wild goose chases for our employees!

passages.title: Emergent Strategy
passages.text: Father is blinded in his pursuit of success. If he won't listen to our employees, I must!

passages.title: Death in the Depths
passages.text:
My own people have fallen to the mad whispers of the voices of the deep, deep sea.

Cultists inhabit caves in the ocean, spreading hysteria deeper and deeper into Tiragarde with their mad rituals.

We must put an end to them, <name>, before they get even more out of hand.

passages.title: Death in the Depths
passages.text: Perhaps now the danger may come to an end.

passages.title: Eldritch Invocations
passages.text:
This is my fault, my friend.

The leader of these cultists is none other than Director Deepwarden, a man who I once trusted as an advisor and business partner.

It seems he did not approve of how I ran our operation... to a ludicrous degree.

He gave his humanity for power, using his frustration to overthrow the village from the inside. Who knows what he plans next.

I can no longer stand idly by. Take out Deepwarden. Show him that Anglepoint will not fall to his madness.

passages.title: Eldritch Invocations
passages.text: Is this truly the end?

passages.title: A Dark (Iron) Tide
passages.text:
Their red eyes... flaming beards... dark, dusky skin. These can only be Dark Iron dwarves. I have never seen one before this day.

It is my understanding that they have been sent here on an errand for the Alliance. Given my people's allegiance, I believe we are now placed in a position to better demonstrate our loyalty to the Horde.

The Dark Iron must die. See that they do not claim so much as an inch more of this beach.

passages.title: A Dark (Iron) Tide
passages.text: Let there be no confusion on where we stand, <name>.

passages.title: A Poisonous Touch
passages.text:
You... I saw you speak with Zentimo. Please, I don't have much time left...

These trolls, they came for our blood. I was already nearly bled dry before this one succumbed to my poison.

Search it's body, the blowgun and darts should still be there. Dip the darts into my blood and use them to weaken as many of their number as you can. 

I will not let my death be in vain! If these trolls want our blood so badly, then they shall have it!

passages.title: A Poisonous Touch
passages.text:
I see, You've brought meaning to Mag'ash's sacrifice.

Thank you for your valor, <name>.

Please, take the weapon with you and go with my blessing.

passages.title: Mista Nice
passages.text:
I am normally not a violent tortollan, but if there is one thing I cannot abide, it is a scoundrel using children for his own profit.

The street scamps appear to be working at the behest of a ring leader. I do believe they call him "Mista Nice" though I suspect the name to be sarcastic in nature.

I have a scroll here that can let you move among the scamps and see if they lead you back to Mista Nice. If they do, slay him and I shall pay you a bounty.

passages.title: Mista Nice
passages.text: Any luck finding that voice of corruption for the youth of tomorrow?

passages.title: Mista Nice
passages.text: Excellent. One less evil troll on the streets. Of course, you can assume they will organize again soon. They always do.

passages.title: Lured and Allured
passages.text:
Lookin' for a friend from the wreck, eh?

If he survived he may have wandered up the path to our camp.

Now if he ain't up there toastin' his buns by the fire, well... lotta poor souls fall victim to the song of the sirens. 

You should check the camp before you go wadin' out into the tideway. Ask our leader, Stabby Jane. She'd know for sure if a new survivor showed up!

passages.title: Lured and Allured
passages.text:
Ugh... Was I... Was I crying?

Let's agree to never speak of this again.

passages.title: Blood in the Tides
passages.text:
Curse these slimy wenches!

Their singin' sets men's hearts afire and their brains adrift. 

My ship's aground. My cargo's lost.

Nothin' for it now but to fight!

passages.title: Blood in the Tides
passages.text:
<Keelson looks up at you from a pile of siren corpses.>

I need a drink.

passages.title: The Spiritwalkers
passages.text:
Ebonhorn is in the care of Spiritwalker Graysky. A cure is proving elusive... he has asked for your help.

Please speak with him at once, <name>. The spiritwalkers are the keepers of our past. I pray the answer lies somewhere in the ancient truths they hold.

passages.title: The Red Market
passages.text:
You came with de Princess Talanji?

I need a hand with a most unsavory task. Crimson cultists have made demselves a market for blood magic. Dis is bad, mon. Dis is very bad indeed.

I need you to go down dese steps and bring back any evidence you can of blood practices. And destroy their chalice. Big chalice. Don't forget de chalice.

passages.title: The Red Market
passages.text: In Zuldazar, such magic is forbidden for a reason. Dey say you give in to dis magic, you hear voices. And sacrificing, well, dat is de practice of de lower tribes.

passages.title: The Red Market
passages.text: Blood magic is an infection. It spreads like a disease if not purged.

passages.title: Evidence of Evil
passages.text:
Jakra'zet refused to patrol dis area. Yazma's spies did not warn us of de evil lurking beneath our city. And Zul did not foresee blood magics festering under our noses.

These are serious allegations, and de evidence is in your hands. Present dem to Zolani, Blade of the King. She will know best their meaning and how best to present dem to de king.

passages.title: Evidence of Evil
passages.text:
Blood magic being practiced in open daylight? Dis cannot stand.

You have done well in bringing me dis information. I will present it to King Rastakhan at de first opportunity when his council is away.

passages.title: Witch Doctor Jala
passages.text:
adventurer, I received word dat an old friend of mine is down here and in need of some extra muscle.

Witch Doctor Jala. She is an old crone, but de loa find her amusing enough to keep around.

Seek her out for me and lend what aid you can.

passages.title: Witch Doctor Jala
passages.text: Greetings, <class>. I am Witch Doctor Jala. And you are right on time.

passages.title: Bwonsamdi's Deliverance
passages.text:
We be havin' a task from Bwonsamdi, da loa a death, ta purge dis place of its undead.

Dey be controlled by a monster called Kel'vax.

Can ya help? Dere be zombies destroyin' Bwonsamdi's temple over dere, and we no have da strength ta fight 'em all.

Take dis torch. Kill dem zombies, den burn them corpses with da torch. It should be deliverin' their souls ta Bwonsamdi.

Ya do dat, and we be one step closer ta stoppin Kel'vax.

passages.title: Bwonsamdi's Deliverance
passages.text: Ya did good, I can tell Bwonsamdi be pleased by ya releasin' his followers.

passages.title: Seeing Spirits
passages.text:
The spirits in the cemetery are riled up! I'd ask 'em direct but I don't have any of the necessary salve I use to commune with the dead. My family's been making it for ages!

The herbs and tools I use to make it are inside, but I can't get over there! Some of those spirits are beyond reason and attack me on sight!

Why don't you go collect those herbs, make the salve with my tools, and ask one of the calmer spirits what's going on. Aaron Cresterly is a good spirit to look for.

passages.title: Seeing Spirits
passages.text: Stranger, lend me your aid! I am ensnared in a witch's foul magic and I do not know how much longer I can resist! Destroy the circle binding me!

passages.title: Seeing Spirits
passages.text: A witch has infested this goodly place with her foul power. Stranger, you have proven yourself a friend. Perhaps you will be our salvation!

passages.title: Split Party
passages.text:
In life my compatriots and I were valiant champions as you are. In death we are potent souls to make the witch's accursed minions even more powerful. 

With your help I have resisted thus far, but this foul witch pulled brave Bridget from her justly won rest. She is now trapped in one of these macabre constructs. This witch intends to use Bridget to bring death upon the lands she was oathsworn to protect!

Free Bridget Fairwater's soul from the construct which entraps her!

passages.title: Split Party
passages.text:
Why that pustulent boil on a toad's rump! Use me as a pawn? Fie! I will see her sent screaming to the foul pit she crawled from!

My thanks. The witch will pay for her heinous actions!

passages.title: Looking For One More
passages.text:
Our loathsome foe, 'Sister' Westwood, yet continues her work. After subjugating myself, she set her malicious sights on my companion, fair Mercy. 

Of us three, Mercy was most kind and possessing of uncommon inner strength, yet I fear for her. Corrupting such a soul would make for a fearsome creature, indeed.

Stop the vile ritual before Mercy is taken. Allow the dead their rest. Slay Sister Westwood and free us from her grasp!

passages.title: Looking For One More
passages.text:
Our thanks to you, brave champion. You have freed us from the witch's vile influence and stopped her corruption from spreading. Our very souls have been saved by thy actions.

Now we may rest.

passages.title: Bones for Protection
passages.text:
Kel'vax be havin' powerful voodoo on his side, da kind dat could kill ya instantly if ya not careful.

I know how we can be stoppin' dis magic, but we need bones. Lots a them. We be lucky, Kel'vax be havin' a large skeleton army.

I need ya ta be goin' out dere and collectin' their bones. Bring 'em ta me and I'll prepare 'em ta be used against his voodoo.

passages.title: Bones for Protection
passages.text: Did ya get them bones? We need 'em if we gonna stop Kel'vax's voodoo.

passages.title: Bones for Protection
passages.text: Good! I be workin' on usin' dese bones to counter Kel'vax's dark voodoo.

passages.title: The Fall of Kel'vax
passages.text:
We be ready ta kill Kel'vax and send his soul ta Bwonsamdi for judgment. Ya should know someting before ya go in.

Kel'vax was our son. Dat be why Bwonsamdi chose us ta stop dis madness.

I not be knowin' why Kel'vax chose ta forsake everyting we believed in centuries ago... but here we are.

Even without his undead, Kel'vax be very powerful. Be prepared... dis be our shot to end him and find our rest.

passages.title: The Fall of Kel'vax
passages.text: Ya must destroy Kel'vax once and for all!

passages.title: The Fall of Kel'vax
passages.text:
It be over. As ya can see, Kel'vax be trapped in his phylacteries.

All dat's left for us ta do is ta destroy da containers ta send him ta Bwonsamdi for judgment.

We couldn't have done this without ya. May Bwonsamdi be wit ya... and may ya be wise enough ta know when ta make a deal with him.

passages.title: Getting a Leg Up
passages.text:
I seem to be in a bit of a... predicament.

My squad was scouting on behalf of Lady Sylvanas when we were ambushed by some snake men calling themselves "sethrak".

As you can see, my legs have been separated from my body in the ambush. It's just a flesh wound, luckily.

Care to help me get re-attached? Then we can get down to this business of vengeance against these sethrak.

passages.title: Getting a Leg Up
passages.text: That feels a lot better, I think. Time to get down to the business of some proper revenge.

passages.title: Reuniting the Company
passages.text:
Right, then. First order of business, rescue the remnants of my company. 

These sethrak kept yelling about expanding their empire and conquering Azeroth as they attacked us. Lovely, really.

They killed most of my company and took some hostages. I assume they're being told how grand the sethrak empire is.

I'd like the remnants of my company back, if you please. I'll put in a good word with Lady Sylvanas, once this is all over. 

...not that someone like you needs it.

passages.title: Reuniting the Company
passages.text: Fine work! It's good to be reunited, both with my body and with my squad.

passages.title: Show of Force
passages.text:
These things called the sethrak think that we're easily handled. That's only because we were ambushed and not ready for a fight.

Well, all right, perhaps we were easily handled. But that doesn't mean we won't strike back.

Kill as many of those sethrak as you can. I don't know who they are or what they want, but I do know one thing.

They signed their death warrants when they attacked my squad and cut me in half.

passages.title: Show of Force
passages.text: Good! I could hear their screams from here. They will remember the Horde!

passages.title: No Mercy for Sithis
passages.text:
Heh heh... thanks for the rescue! I could use your help in a little plan that I have.

The commander of this place is a sethrak called Sithis. He's got this thing called a "skycaller gem."

Word is they're looking for some sort of shadow magic in Nazmir to try and really power this thing up.

Heh heh... luckily, yours truly has her own shadow magic to do just that! Maybe you do, too. I don't keep up on what powers you keep getting.

Get the gem from Sithis and we'll have some REAL fun afterwards.

passages.title: No Mercy for Sithis
passages.text: Do you have Ingrid's gem? Please tell me you do... she's been absolutely insufferable about it.

passages.title: No Mercy for Sithis
passages.text: Excellent work freeing Ingrid. She has told me about this particular gem, and the company has voted that you should test it out on our snake enemies.

passages.title: Return to Dust
passages.text:
It appears the sethrak are quite serious about keeping this gem. I do wonder where they found it in the first place.

Hrm... perhaps Lady Sylvanas would be interested in this as well. Something to ponder.

Ingrid believes this gem can unleash lightning and shadow magic of, her words not mine, epic proportions.

I do believe it would be best for everyone if you tested it out on the small sethrak army currently looking for us.

passages.title: Return to Dust
passages.text: Would you please hurry and deal with the sethrak? I'd prefer to get everyone's bloodlust dealt with before heading out.

passages.title: Return to Dust
passages.text:
Good work. The sethrak will be back, but we've proven our point, which is don't cross the Horde.

With that business over with, my squad will be off. Hopefully the next time we meet will be under... nicer circumstances.

passages.title: Through the Old Roads
passages.text:
Lady Waycrest has entrusted me with securing the town of Falconhurst and the services of Master Alchemist Ashton who lives there. However, I have found out no one has heard from Falconhurst in some time.

The skies above the forest are impassable, so we must travel the old roads through Drust ruins in the mountains. A small capable party has a better chance to bypass the growing forces of the witches and to help secure Master Alchemist Ashton.

To that end, I ask you to assist me.

passages.title: Through the Old Roads
passages.text:
Something has disturbed the spirits here.

The spirits of the departed still fight with constructs and the shambling dead. 

Our goal is Falconhurst, but a quick investigation of this area might help us fight our foes better.

passages.title: Lovesick and Lost
passages.text:
Ugh. My head. My HEART.

Feels like a good hangover and a bad breakup put together.

On the bright side, I think I know where we are. And where that ship was headed.

Freehold.

It's a... free town. For, uh... free folk. The only rule is that there are no rules. Lotta guys with peg legs and eye patches and exotic pets. Catch my drift?

There's a trail through the hills that'll take us there. Pretty sure I remember the way...

Let's get moving. Gotta walk off that damn siren's witchery.

passages.title: Lovesick and Lost
passages.text: Told you I knew how to find it!

passages.title: Silver Blades
passages.text:
<This drust warrior was felled by a silvered blade long ago. This blade is still good despite the ages.

Perhaps these weapons could be brought into service of fighting the Drust once more.>

passages.title: Toxic Community
passages.text:
A traveler? Nobody uses this trail unless they got a death wish.

The only thing more poisonous than the marrowflies are the saurolisks that eat 'em all day.

That marrowfly toxin is what I'm here for. Y'see, I'm a purveyor of, uh... specialty goods. And my clients are just dyin' for more of my product. Heh.

You bring me their stingers, I pay you. Simple as that. 

You can even find 'em in the saurolisks, if you don't mind gettin' your hands dirty.

passages.title: Toxic Community
passages.text: You got them stingers?

passages.title: Toxic Community
passages.text:
Pleasure doin' business with you.

In the future I'll make sure you get a special discount. Heh.

passages.title: Honorable Discharge
passages.text:
Some of the spirits on the battlefield are too weary to go on. These were brave Kul Tirans. They have more than earned their rest but their sense of duty holds them here.

Order the most weary spirits off the field of battle. Hopefully they will be convinced to rest.

passages.title: Honorable Discharge
passages.text: It is good their spirits returned to their final rest once more. May they never be disturbed again.

passages.title: Save Who We Can
passages.text:
These things seem intent on capturing our people... but we're not quite sure what for.

The ones in the town might be too tough to reach right now, but we might be able to save some of the woodsmen who work along the strand.

Head to the lumber fields just east of here, and see if there's anyone still alive out there. We can shelter them here until we can arrange safe passage out of here.

passages.title: Save Who We Can
passages.text:
Good work, <class>! Even if we don't manage to take the town back, it's good to know we were able to save some of our people.

Now we just have to get them out of here...

passages.title: The Three Sisters
passages.text:
If you're looking to absolve Miss Waycrest of this mess, you'll need to head into the town. Recently, I've seen some oddly dressed women among the creatures, who seem to be calling the shots.

It's likely that they're the key to this whole nightmare, but we can't get in to question them. Their minions don't seem to slow you down, though. 

If you can get to them, you might be able to find some answers for the both of us. Be careful, though. They likely aren't very friendly.

passages.title: The Three Sisters
passages.text:
They weren't willing to talk?  That's unfortunate.

At least with them gone, we may stand a chance to take back the town.

passages.title: A Revealing Missive
passages.text:
<The strange woman possessed a letter from someone calling herself "Matron Levae" which appears to have orders to take the town of Fletcher's Hollow.

This could be the evidence needed to absolve Lucille Waycrest. Mayor Pare should be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: A Revealing Missive
passages.text:
It would seem we were mistaken. Miss Waycrest was just in the wrong place at the wrong time.

However, this also means that Fletcher's Hollow may be in even more danger.

passages.title: The Murderous Matron
passages.text:
I know that you've got what you came for, but I need to ask you one more favor. This town won't be safe until this Matron Levae is taken care of. 

According to the letter, she must be holed up in that cave. None of our people have been able to enter it, but I know I've seen their constructs go in!

This charm you found might be the key. If you can take control of one of these wicker men and send it after her, we might have a shot!

passages.title: The Murderous Matron
passages.text: Is she gone?

passages.title: The Murderous Matron
passages.text:
It worked?! Well, I'll be a kraken's uncle! You really did save our hides!

I'm not sure how we can repay you, but this should be a good start!

passages.title: Culling the Coven
passages.text:
If the mine really was their objective, I can only imagine they'd have even more forces in there. 

My men and I may be able to take care of the remnants out here, but if an even bigger force comes out of that mine, we're not going to stand a chance.

While you're hunting down the matron with this wicker contraption, do you think you could... you know... soften them up a bit?

passages.title: Culling the Coven
passages.text:
Wait... you're telling me it was even worse in the mines?

You know what? Just don't tell me about it. So long as you killed... whatever was in there... I think we'll be okay.

passages.title: Ravenous Landsharks
passages.text:
Warbeast Kraal is important to de empire. All de beasts dat haul our goods, carry our armies, and fight our wars are born and bred here. 

If you want Rastakhan's support, you had better impress us. I have some thoughts on where you can start.

We have ourselves a diemetradon problem. Usually nothing to worry about, but dey had a big hatching dis year. Now dey're breaking into de pens and eating our eggs.

Kill diemetradons, protect our beasts, and we will see about de rest.

passages.title: Ravenous Landsharks
passages.text: Were you able to kill any diemetradon?

passages.title: Ravenous Landsharks
passages.text: You are good at dis. Almost like you have done it before.

passages.title: Hungry Mouths To Feed
passages.text:
We don't have much in de way of supplies right now.

Mojambo and his gang will be back to finish us off, of dat I'm sure. But without food and supplies, dere will be none of us alive for dem to kill.

Our cook is looking for someone to help gather supplies so we can feed de camp.

Speak with him and see if you can find what he's looking for.

passages.title: Hungry Mouths To Feed
passages.text: A newcomer, eh? You picked a bad time to join our tribe. You'd find better luck wandering de wastes in search of mirages.

passages.title: I Heard You Lost the Herd
passages.text:
Our herd of alpacas went missing dis morning.

It may seem like we have more pressing matters to worry about, but de meat and milk de alpacas provide are essential to our survival.

Those alpacas won't survive long on de dunes. Speak with Mugjabu and help him find de alpacas before it's too late!

passages.title: I Heard You Lost the Herd
passages.text: Razgaji sent you? I'm not sure why he cares so much. When Mojambo and his gang come back, we'll all be dead anyway...

passages.title: Mystery Meat
passages.text:
Mojambo's gang may be coming to kill us, but we've still got to eat. And when you live in a harsh wasteland, you make do with what you've got.

Sometimes fresh meat is hard to find.

Dat's how I came up with de idea for my famous mystery meat pie.

De secret ingredient is dung beetle, but with enough seasoning you can't even tell!

Our food supplies are dangerously low right now. I need someone to go beetle hunting as soon as possible!

passages.title: Mystery Meat
passages.text: Do you have de "mystery ingredient" for de mystery meat pie?

passages.title: Mystery Meat
passages.text: Just look at all dese juicy intestines! We'll have enough pies to feed de entire camp!

passages.title: Alpacas Gone Wild
passages.text:
Our herd of alpacas escaped dis morning. Dey're out dere wandering de dunes as we speak.

Probably for de best, if you ask me. We'll all be dead soon once Mojambo comes back.

Since you seem to care so much, take dis alpaca whistle and use it to round dem up. I blow de whistle every day at feeding time, so de alpacas should come running home when dey hear de sound.

passages.title: Alpacas Gone Wild
passages.text: Looks like you recovered most of de herd. Good work... even though Mojambo and his henchmons will probably murder us in our sleep and take de alpacas for demselves...

passages.title: Vol'duni Fried Chicken
passages.text:
Have you ever tried my delicious Vol'duni fried chicken?

Me neither! Probably because dere aren't any chickens in Vol'dun.

Dere are plenty of vultures, though. Why don't you see if you can find some tasty vulture meat?

De secret to delicious fried chicken is to roast de meat before you fry it, but it only works if de meat is fresh.

I've soaked dese arrows in alpaca fat. If you ignite de arrows and shoot down de birds, dey'll start cooking before dey're even dead!

passages.title: Vol'duni Fried Chicken
passages.text: Do you have de buzzard meat?

passages.title: Vol'duni Fried Chicken
passages.text:
It may not be chicken, but it's food! With enough seasoning nobody will know de difference.

Everything tastes like chicken, right?

passages.title: Snarltooth's Last Laugh
passages.text:
It's not just Mojambo's gang we have to worry about. We also need to keep a watchful eye at night due to frequent hyena attacks.

De most dangerous of de hyenas is Snarltooth. He ambushes us at night, laughing maniacally as he slaughters his prey.

I need you to slay de beast once and for all! Snarltooth's den is just south of de arena in de Arid Basin.

passages.title: Snarltooth's Last Laugh
passages.text: Did you take care of Snarltooth?

passages.title: Snarltooth's Last Laugh
passages.text:
It's good to finally see dat hyena got what he deserved! If you're strong enough to slay Snarltooth, maybe we stand a chance against Mojambo's gang...

Who am I kidding, we're dead meat.

passages.title: An Airtight Alibi
passages.text:
It'll take us a while to clean up the beasts that are left over, but I'm confident we'll be able to take back Fletcher's Hollow--thanks to you, of course.

Here, take this letter to the constable. It should be enough to clear Miss Waycrest's name. 

I'm sorry you had to witness all of this, mainlander. We are good people, but these are terrible times.

passages.title: An Airtight Alibi
passages.text:
What's this? A letter from Mayor Pare?

<Constable Framer reads Evelyn's letter.>

Well... it appears we were... mistaken.

passages.title: Freehold
passages.text:
Well, there she is: Freehold.

You can get anything you want there, provided you can pay for it. 

Whether you pay with gold or steel is up to you.

Take a look.

passages.title: Freehold
passages.text:
Look, I'm worldly, but I don't have anything you can catch from my eyes.

Just use the spyglass, would ya?

passages.title: Freehold
passages.text: Ready to head face-first into a den of snakes?

passages.title: Grozztok the Blackheart
passages.text:
A group of us were dropped off here and left to die. 

Our first night at camp, I was jolted from sleep by de gurgling cries of my fellow exiles. Jakra'zet sent assassins to our camp, looking for Rakera. 

Their leader, Grozztok, came for me, but Rakera intervened. 

She chased him into de dunes, but dat was days ago. 

If you cross paths with Grozztok, don't hesitate to drive a blade into his black heart.

passages.title: Grozztok the Blackheart
passages.text:
You saw Jakra'zet? What would he be doing trying to break into de old pyramid?

Whatever de reason, it can't be good.

passages.title: Stolen Satchels
passages.text:
One within our group spoke of a temple in de mountains dat welcomes exiles, though none are permitted to enter without an offering to their loa.

I would have given anything to find some solace in dis wasteland, but now I have nothing, thanks to those thieving assassins.

Each of us had a satchel dat carried de last of our possessions. We didn't have much, but it was more than one troll would need. 

If you search de dunes looking for your friend, could you keep an eye out for our satchels?

passages.title: Stolen Satchels
passages.text: Have you recovered our belongings?

passages.title: Stolen Satchels
passages.text:
<Jorak quickly digs through the satchels.>

Much is missing, but hopefully dere's enough here for a worthy offering.

passages.title: Wither Without Water
passages.text:
The flora in this area weren't always so aggressive. 

Without water, the thistlevines wither and waste until they become something unrecognizable and angry.

Take my watering can and wet the withering thistlevines to prevent them from becoming carnivorous.

passages.title: Wither Without Water
passages.text: Look how happy those plants are! You made that happen.

passages.title: Let it Flow
passages.text:
The fountains here have seen better days. They're currently incapable of holding water, but we can fix that!

You can use my spare tools to repair the cracks. 

With a little luck and elbow grease, the fountains will be flowing again in no time!

passages.title: Let it Flow
passages.text: Getting the fountains working again is my top priority.

passages.title: Let it Flow
passages.text: Hrm, this fountain in front of me still isn't functioning? But my work was impeccable!

passages.title: We Can Salvage the Seeds
passages.text:
I've studied the flora within the terrace extensively. Once a thistlevine completely dries out, it's too late for the plant to be saved. 

Its seeds are still viable, however. Under the right conditions, they can be used to cultivate new, healthy thistlevines. 

Salvage seeds from the carnivorous thistlevines that can no longer be saved, and plant them within the fertile mounds of dirt. 

The thistlevine plant is extremely quick to sprout, so the terrace should be filled with seedlings in no time!

passages.title: We Can Salvage the Seeds
passages.text: Thistlevine seeds need three things to thrive: water, fertile soil, and lots of sunshine.

passages.title: We Can Salvage the Seeds
passages.text: Look how much you've helped bring this place to life! You've got quite the green thumb.

passages.title: Sowing Saplings
passages.text:
Algerson destroys the forests and leaves nothing remaining! It is up to us to take care of Azeroth, to help her live and grow as she was meant to!

Take these seeds, find the soil that calls for them, and help our planet recapture her grace and vitality!

passages.title: Sowing Saplings
passages.text: Algerson's greed may have hurt this land, but it can still be saved.

passages.title: Pulling Fangs
passages.text:
I need more things to help me get strong. I need you to get me some saurid teeth.

No, Sur'jan, you're not trusting <him/her> TOO much. Just enough. I won't be betrayed again.

I need dese teeth for a ritual I'm gonna perform to help me get my power back. Once I'm not so weak, you and I are gonna take down dis undead monster.

passages.title: Pulling Fangs
passages.text: You got enough teeth for me?

passages.title: Pulling Fangs
passages.text:
Lemme count dem... good! Dis will work.

Shh, I said it will work, not dat we'd be done. Stop annoying me, Sur'jan!

passages.title: Safe Flying
passages.text:
I'm feeling... stronger! But I need more power before we take down Urok.

No, Sur'jan, YOU are scared of Urok more than me. I'm not scared of nothing!

You got an attachment to me now after dat ritual. I need you to go kill de skyterrors nearby. Their deaths will fuel my strength.

Take my grappling hook. You can drag de skyterrors down from de sky with it, and it'll put de hurt on dem too.

passages.title: Safe Flying
passages.text: Good! I am feeling stronger already. De three of us make a good team.

passages.title: Terrorizing their Eggs
passages.text:
Sur'jan, I should be doing dis! What do you mean, I need to recover? Bah, fine.

I need more power, and de skyterrors have eggs nearby. I need you to bash some of their eggs to fuel my energy.

Those eggs got lots of life force in dem. You destroy dem, and I will feel de energy coming back to me.

Come on, Sur'jan, dis will be easy! I can do dis! Hmph... well, you make a good point. You always were de smarter one out of us.

passages.title: Terrorizing their Eggs
passages.text: I feel better already! Maybe I should destroy more of those eggs in de future.

passages.title: There's No Eye in Skyterror
passages.text:
There's a real big skyterror dat I name Jarkadiax. I need his tongue...

What's dat, Sur'jan? Not his tongue? His eye? You sure? Hrm.

I need his eye for my next ritual. I know what you're thinking. De tongue makes more sense. Dat's what I--

Look, Sur'jan, I still think it's his tongue. We'll see which of us is right!

Go get Jarkadiax's eye and bring it back to me for de next ritual.

passages.title: There's No Eye in Skyterror
passages.text: I need dat eye. You get it yet?

passages.title: There's No Eye in Skyterror
passages.text:
You got de eye!

I feel de power coming from dis thing. Can you see it?

Shut up, Sur'jan. I know YOU can see it, I was talking to him!

passages.title: A Good Spanking
passages.text:
Pinky is contained in de direhorn pen for now, but de handlers are having a real hard time with him!

Dis calls for some tough love.

Will you help dem?

passages.title: A Good Spanking
passages.text:
You're certainly de talk of de kraal, <name>!

Dat Pinky will be great in battle when he grows up, don't you think?

passages.title: The Blood of My Enemies
passages.text:
I feel my power returning, but we aren't done yet. We need more power to kill dis undead Urok.

We'll be pushing in to Urok's lair. Dreadticks are swarming in de area. I want you to bring me their blood for de final ritual.

Take dis. It's my trusty dreadtick gasser. Throw it in de area, dreadticks sniff it... den DIE! Hahaha! Now get going!

...Sur'jan, you keep telling me to let <him/her> do dis sorta work, but I could do it too! Fine, I'll just work on getting de ritual ready.

passages.title: The Blood of My Enemies
passages.text: You get me dat blood yet?

passages.title: The Blood of My Enemies
passages.text: Dis will work. We are so close to getting my power back!

passages.title: Wasteland Survivor
passages.text:
<The leather has become dry and cracked in the sun, but the supplies inside are mostly intact.

It's unknown what gruesome death befell the backpack's former owner, but supplies like these are in high demand among the outcasts.

The desert has claimed many lives... perhaps there are more supplies to be found among the dunes. >

passages.title: Wasteland Survivor
passages.text: What do you have for me?

passages.title: Wasteland Survivor
passages.text:
I see you made a scavenging run and came back alive!

We will put these supplies to good use among the tribe. You have my thanks.

passages.title: My Head and Shoulders
passages.text:
If we're going to fight Urok, I will need my gear back. It was all lost when I was running from Urok de first time.

Shut UP, Sur'jan! I had to ditch it in order to run faster.

Bring my gear back to me, and I'll be ready to fight Urok with you.

passages.title: My Head and Shoulders
passages.text: You got my gear?

passages.title: My Head and Shoulders
passages.text: My gear! Ah, dey smell brand new, too. Did you clean dem?

passages.title: Urok's True Death
passages.text:
This is it! My power is back; we are ready to put down Urok. He used to be a noble beast, you know. Big, strong.

Now Urok is just a mindless undead. It isn't right. We'll put him to rest.

I'm going to run up ahead. When you get near Urok, I'll hop out to ambush him. Let's do dis!

Shut up, Sur'jan. Of course we're going to win! If we don't, I'll just find another <class> to help me out.

passages.title: Urok's True Death
passages.text:
We did it! Urok is gone for good. It was a shame to put him down, but dat sort of creature isn't supposed to be.

I have lots of other things to do, like finding de two other trolls out here and killing dem.

What do you think, Sur'jan? Should I tell him? No? Okay, fine.

I'll be seeing you. Oh, and don't stay in Nazmir. Only crazy people come here.

passages.title: Saurolisk Escape
passages.text:
You cautiously approach a saurolisk tied to a post. It doesn't snap at you, but looks at you with defeat in its eyes.

The troggs seem to be keeping these saurolisks against their will. They should be freed before they are abused further.

passages.title: Saurolisk Escape
passages.text:
Troggs training saurolisks to be ridden? Seems they've learned from watching us after all.

It's better that you freed them. I don't particularly want to imagine what would happen if the troggs were widely successful in their new riding endeavors!

passages.title: Home Again, Home Again
passages.text:
I can't thank you enough for the help here! You showed up just in time.

Here is Elijah's sausage order. Don't worry, it's just regular sausage- nothing questionable.

Now if you'll excuse me I have to see to my workers.

passages.title: The Vanishing Lord
passages.text:
Unfortunately, we don't have any contacts within House Waycrest, so our efforts in Drustvar will have to start from the ground up.

We have arranged for a ferry to take you to Fallhaven - a farming village in eastern Drustvar. The mayor there, Cyril White, is a longtime friend of the Proudmoores, and I think he can help us get in touch with someone from the house.

I hope you can get to the bottom of their absence, <name>. Their martial might is invaluable to the Kul Tiran fleet.

passages.title: The Vanishing Lord
passages.text:
<The effigy is protected by powerful magic. 

It seems it will take more than brute force to break this curse.>

passages.title: A Bejeweled Prison
passages.text: <As you gaze into the strange gem you feel a sudden need to travel into the swamps of Nazmir and return the gem to it's rightful resting place, wherever that may be.>

passages.title: The Chef's Apprentice
passages.text:
<Sezahjin rummages through his cooking ingredients in frustration.>

Where is Junji? I sent him to scavenge for vulture eggs, but he hasn't returned.

<Sezahjin pauses for a moment.>

He was just going on about de size of saurolisk eggs, but those oversized lizards are far too dangerous for a boy! He can't possibly be so foolish...

If he has gone to de saurolisk breeding grounds... he may already be dead. Please find him before it's too late!

passages.title: The Chef's Apprentice
passages.text: You can't fool me, saurolisk! I know you're out dere waiting to eat me! Oh wait... you're a grown up! Please, get me out of here! Help!

passages.title: Savage Saurolisks
passages.text:
Please, help me! I'm trapped in dis box and I can't make it out alone!

I came here to collect eggs. I knew it was a bad idea, but I thought I could sneak around and grab de eggs before de saurolisks noticed.

I was wrong...

I hid underneath dis crate to avoid being eaten!

Can you clear out de saurolisks and tell me when it's safe to come out?

Please, don't leave me here!

passages.title: Savage Saurolisks
passages.text: Are de saurolisks gone yet?

passages.title: Savage Saurolisks
passages.text: De saurolisks are all gone and it's safe to come out? Thank you so much! I never thought I'd make it out of here alive!

passages.title: They Might Be Delicious
passages.text:
Saurolisk eggs are de most delicious eggs in de desert!

I mean, I've never tried dem myself... but look at de size of them! Dey're huge! Bigger is better, right?

If I go back to camp empty handed, Sezahjin is going to kill me! We have to get some of those eggs!

You sound a lot older and stronger than I am. Gather up de eggs so we can take dem back for everyone to eat.

Don't worry about me, I'll wait for you here. It's not like I'm going anywhere...

passages.title: They Might Be Delicious
passages.text: Do you have de saurolisk eggs?

passages.title: They Might Be Delicious
passages.text: You have de eggs! Be careful not to break dem... just roll dem under da box... gently... gently now...

passages.title: Urok, Terror of the Wetlands
passages.text:
You! You can help me!

I know, Sur'jan, <he/she> looks like a <class>, but I know we can trust <him/her>.

Urok, de terror of de wetlands, is undead now. We have to put it down before it tries to destroy dis entire place.

Just give me a minute, and you will see dat Urok is bad news.

Shhh, Sur'jan, dey gonna see, dey are all gonna see!

passages.title: Urok, Terror of the Wetlands
passages.text: Just give me a chance and you'll see!

passages.title: Urok, Terror of the Wetlands
passages.text: Now you see? We must beat Urok. I know how to do it, but I can't do it alone.

passages.title: Runaway Rider
passages.text:
Lord Norwington demanded I take Eddie out riding in the woods, but I knew it was too soon! I just knew it!

We've got to go find him. Meet me across the river!

passages.title: Runaway Rider
passages.text:
How could this get any worse?

The troggs have captured Eddie!

passages.title: Wicker Worship
passages.text:
Hail, traveler! You look like just the sort who might be able to help me out with a predicament!

It's my son Edwin, you see. We were travelling through Drustvar to ply our wares when the damned fool ran off to join some cult here in Autumnvale! Since then we haven't seen a trace of him, and the brown-robed loons won't speak a word of his whereabouts!

Could you see if you could persuade them to talk? His poor mother is worried sick!

passages.title: Wicker Worship
passages.text: What brings you to our valley, <class>?

passages.title: Questionable Offerings
passages.text:
So the traders sent you? As I told them, I only discuss the happenings of our family with those who understand our cause.

If you wish to know his whereabouts, you must prove that you do.

Behind us are several items gathered for offering to the Wicker Man. Bring us the items you feel will most appease it, so that it might give us its blessing.

Choose the correct offerings, and we will know your intent.

passages.title: Questionable Offerings
passages.text: You must bring the correct offerings if you wish to show us your understanding.

passages.title: Questionable Offerings
passages.text:
Your offerings pleased the Wicker Man. 

Very well, ask your questions, <class>.

passages.title: Mind the Hives
passages.text:
The one called Edwin came to us not long ago, seeking to earn the blessings of the Wicker Man. He wandered off into the hills looking for his own offering.

Unfortunately, he managed to disturb one of the nearby beehives, causing the insects to become rather frenzied.

That was the last I saw of him, I'm afraid.

passages.title: Mind the Hives
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Mind the Hives
passages.text:
You were the one looking for Edwin, weren't you!?

You must help him!

passages.title: A Simple Sacrifice
passages.text:
You must hurry! Lord Autumnvale brought Edwin off to that cave right when he returned, saying something about "an offering of blood!"

I think they mean to sacrifice him to appease the Wicker Man!

Just what kind of crazy cult is this?!

passages.title: A Simple Sacrifice
passages.text: Help me!

passages.title: A Simple Sacrifice
passages.text:
Those cultists tried to kill me!

I don't know about you, but I've had about enough of this Wicker Man business!

passages.title: On the Move
passages.text:
Jorak's wounds have healed enough for him to travel.

He has agreed to guide us to de temple. 

De sooner we leave, de better. Rakera won't survive in dis desert for long.

passages.title: On the Move
passages.text: Dis temple is not quite what I expected it to be.

passages.title: Sneaking into Zalamar
passages.text:
I know you might think nothing has changed, but trust me, de voodoo worked... I think.

You should transform into one of de blood trolls when you are near Zalamar, one of their villages.

Jo'chunga should be dere somewhere, most likely near a large gathering of blood trolls.

Find Jo'chunga and tell him I have sent you, den see what he knows about de situation dere.

passages.title: Sneaking into Zalamar
passages.text: Good, we will be safe in here. I am happy dat you are here, because I am not able to stop dis alone.

passages.title: Akunda Awaits
passages.text:
I've spoken to every troll out here, asking if they've seen Rakera. As you might have guessed, Akunda is de only name dey know. 

Let's hope someone within de temple will be able to tell us something useful.

passages.title: Akunda Awaits
passages.text: Dis is Rakera. I have no doubt. But for some reason, she does not remember me... or herself, it would seem...

passages.title: A Need For Coal
passages.text:
Ah! <name>! Just the person I was hoping to see!

I was just getting ready to smelt some monelite down into ingots, but I noticed my coal supply was running low.

Well, I mean... I have coal, yes, but I prefer using Ashvane Coal. It puts out less smoke and burns hotter, so I need less of it.

If you can get some Ashvane Coal from the Ashvane Foundry south of here, I'd be more than willing to give you a couple pointers for mining monelite. Deal?

passages.title: A Need For Coal
passages.text: Have you gone to the foundry yet?

passages.title: A Need For Coal
passages.text:
Thanks! You can never be too careful when it comes to breathing thick clouds of smoke from burning coal and molten metal.

Now I owe you a lesson about monelite. Let's see, what to teach...

When you're mining monelite, instead of chipping away at the rock, try using the pick to pierce the metal, and pull all of it away from the rock like it was taffy.

passages.title: Emergency Transplants
passages.text:
With everything that's been happening over in Drustvar, there's been a sudden surge of wildlife in the sound. Normally, I wouldn't care, but they've been eating all the riverbud!

If things don't improve soon, we could try thinning their numbers so they don't consume everything, but I'll consider that the last resort.

Instead, could you go plant some of these seeds to produce additional food for them?

passages.title: Emergency Transplants
passages.text: Have you planted the seeds yet?

passages.title: Emergency Transplants
passages.text:
I can't thank you enough! Riverbud is absolutely critical to the wildlife here. Regardless, I said I'd teach you if you helped out, and I'll ever be true to my word.

The biggest mistake that most herbalists out here do is allow the riverbuds to blow out when harvested.

When you go to pick riverbud, you can't just rip them off the stem, or all the water will spill out. Instead, give them a twist first so they pinch the stem closed. Try it out!

passages.title: Breaking The Food Chain
passages.text:
The extra riverbud you planted has helped, but it's not enough. Some of the local wildlife are consuming the riverbud before they mature. The more riverbud that is eaten, the less we have for our own needs.

The largest group of young riverbud consumers are the turtles.

If the riverbud becomes a threatened species, we'll need to regulate harvesting it. Instead, go thin the number of the turtles in the area.

Do that and I'll teach you everything I know about riverbud.

passages.title: Breaking The Food Chain
passages.text:
Good work, <name>. I can sleep soundly now that those turtles won't be gobbling up all of our precious riverbud.

If I recall correctly, I offered to teach you how to collect riverbud more effectively as thanks for you doing your part.

Well, the secret to riverbud is that there are a couple extra bulbs in the root system. Just pull it by the coil firmly with steady pressure.

passages.title: Here In Spirit
passages.text:
Hey, <name>, how would you feel about doing some legwork for a favor?

We have a tradition here in Kul Tiras, that during a celebration, be it funeral, wedding, or birthday, we incorporate star moss into the decorations. We do that so those who are no longer amongst the living can be here in spirit.

With the recent fighting, my stores are near empty due to the number of funerals we've had.

If you bring me fresh star moss to restock my supply, I'll share a secret on how to get more from each star moss.

passages.title: Here In Spirit
passages.text: There was a funeral the other day, seem to be more and more as of late. Any chance you gathered that star moss I asked for?

passages.title: Here In Spirit
passages.text:
I appreciate you doing this, <name>. It's been hard to get out and gather anything myself, but the war doesn't wait for me.

As for that favor, how about a secret to harvesting star moss, something no one else would teach you?

The thing about star moss is that its magic is sensitive to emotions. When you go to harvest, clear your mind and think of those you've lost. That feeling of loss, reverence, and the joy they once brought will keep the bloom from wilting. That is why we use it for celebrations.

passages.title: Ghost Busting
passages.text:
I hate to ask this of you, but are you available for some more grunt work? I'd do it myself, but this seems beyond my capabilities.

Remember how I told you we use star moss to allow those no longer living to join us for a special day?

Yeah, well, sometimes once they show up, they don't want to leave. There is a spirit on the other side that is lashing out, harming those it should be protecting.

Take this smoldering star moss and cleanse the area until you find the offender and help them move on.

passages.title: Ghost Busting
passages.text: Have you banished the spirit yet?

passages.title: Ghost Busting
passages.text:
I can't thank you enough, <name>. Now that the spirit has been been put to rest, I'll send word to the family so they can get back to their normal lives.

Once again, you've proved that I can rely on you. If you swear to tell no one, I'll tell you the best kept secret of star moss.

This is going to sound crazy, but engage it. Talk to it, sing, hum, anything. I'm not sure why, but since I started I've noticed one or two extra flowers will bloom before my eyes!

passages.title: Disgustingly Damp Flower
passages.text:
Rummaging for pollen as usual, you use the harvesting technique you learned from the bees. However, when you pull your hand away from the flower, you find that there is no pollen on your gloves.

Looking inside the swirl of petals, despite it being a mature flower, you see that there is no pollen at all within it. Upon closer inspection you see that the flower is filled with a viscous liquid. Could the flower have done this?

While unpleasant to touch, you carefully pluck the flower to show Declan.

passages.title: Disgustingly Damp Flower
passages.text:
Curious. There's no pollen at all? Can't say that I've heard of a plant doing that before.

Hmmmmmmmmm�

What I think we have here is a more effective way of harvesting pollen than that of the bees.

passages.title: Spiderphobia
passages.text:
You're no stranger to monster fighting, right?

The other day I found a spider just outside my house. Nothing out of the ordinary, except it was the SIZE OF A HORSE!

Twenty-five minutes of screaming and pick-axeing later and I had managed to kill it.

I spoke with one of the guards, and he said that there was a huge nest of them just over the hill to the northwest.

If you can slay them or whatever you do, I'll teach you a secret to mining monelite. Otherwise, I'm going to have to move.

passages.title: Spiderphobia
passages.text:
I can't stand spiders.

<Myra shudders.>

Have you dealt with them yet?

passages.title: Spiderphobia
passages.text:
I'm glad to see you made it back in one piece. I'm tempted to ask how it went, but frankly, thinking about it has been causing me quite a bit of anxiety.

If you don't mind, I'm going to distract myself from the thought with a lesson.

You've probably noticed that monelite is really maleable, right? You can use that, even before smelting it.

By using your pick to deform the metal while it's still in the vein, you can heat it up and get a bigger haul using the other technique I taught you.

passages.title: Meet Sweetflower
passages.text:
It looks like you've become familiar with the plants around here. There's a flower that grows in the snowy parts of the continent, but I can't tell you much else about it. Can't stand being cold.

However, if you're interested in learning more, I know of someone who may be able to teach you.

Her name's Xun Xun Sweetflower, and last I heard she set up shop on the outskirts of Anyport over in Drustvar. Tread carefully, though, that area is crawling with Irontide Raiders.

passages.title: Meet Sweetflower
passages.text: Oh, you'd like to learn about harvesting winter's kiss?  Well that's very fortunate, for both of us...

passages.title: The Frigid Boon
passages.text:
While harvesting this winter's bite, you managed to pluck the flower without breaking any petals, a feat you had not accomplished before.

Taking a quick mental note of every detail about yourself and your surroundings, one point sticks out to you.

The heat from your breath appears to have made the petals supple enough to bend instead of break. You also believe that this may be a way to prevent the flower from activating its defensive cold blast.

If that is the case, it could be extremely useful.

passages.title: Don't Pick a Fight
passages.text:
Hey, you're not busy, right? I could use your help.

Ya see, I was out mining in Stormsong Valley, when this huge, two-headed monstrosity started chasing after me!

I ran away, but I was back in Boralus when I realized I dropped my favorite mining pick!

I know this may sound stupid, but if you could get it back for me I'd be grateful.

You don't need to do something crazy, like fight them. Instead, sneak by them and grab it.

I'll show you a trick to mining monelite seams for your troubles.

passages.title: Don't Pick a Fight
passages.text: Did you get my mining pick back?

passages.title: Don't Pick a Fight
passages.text:
You're a life saver! Well, a livelihood saver!

As for that trick I had mentioned: Don't bother using a pick to separate the rock from the ore when pulling it from a monelite seam.

If the ore is big enough, once you remove it from the earth, you can peel the metal back and remove the rocks by hand.

passages.title: Seams Familiar
passages.text:
You find a necklace in the shape of an anchor with the name "Cabot" etched in a banner.

The name immediately brings up Myra Cabot, the mining trainer in Boralus.

The condition of the necklace makes it look like it has been well maintained. She probably wants it back.

passages.title: Seams Familiar
passages.text:
By the Light! I thought I lost it forever!

This used to belong to my great grandfather.

<Myra clutches the necklace close to her heart for a moment as a tear runs down her cheek. After a moment, she looks around, shaking her head.>

Nothing here can remotely repay this. It's not much, but I can show you how to get the most out of mining monelite seams.

<Myra spends the next several minutes explaining several techniques to increase the amount of monelite mined from a seam.>

passages.title: Brined Justice
passages.text:
<name>, I just got word that one of our ships was attacked and a large amount of storm silver stolen!

The sacred materials can't be replaced. Once it is blessed by the seapriest, it is buried underwater for a year!

From what I heard, a group of pirates followed the ship to see where the metal was buried on the sea floor before killing the crew and taking her cargo.

Kill the pirates and get back that metal.

passages.title: Brined Justice
passages.text:
Damn those pirates!

Have you recovered the bars?

passages.title: Brined Justice
passages.text:
Ah!  This is fantastic news! I will have someone run these out to the docks right away.

I was starting to fear that they may have gotten you, too.

That said, you have avenged my people.  In exchange, let me show you the finer points of harvesting storm silver.

<Myra takes the next several minutes to explain what she knows about harvesting storm silver deposits.>

passages.title: Papers, Please
passages.text:
All this legwork will be for nothing if we can't show Katherine hard proof linking the Ashvane Company to the freebooters here in Freehold.

Ashvane might have been careful to encrypt their books, but I doubt the dockmaster here has any reason to be so secretive.

Check his office and find us something--anything--that connects him to Ashvane.

passages.title: Papers, Please
passages.text: Lady Katherine is as stubborn as a whale shark. She won't buy our story without proof.

passages.title: Papers, Please
passages.text:
Nice work! This is undeniable proof that Priscilla has been selling weapons to pirates.

It's high treason!

passages.title: The Beatings Will Continue
passages.text:
Ain't seen you before. You a mercenary? 

I got some guys need roughin' up.

<The grizzled woman spits through a gap where her front tooth should be.>

Ever since Harlan started fancyin' himself an admiral, his Irontide guppies been struttin' around like they own the place. Forcin' other crews to swear loyalty to Harlan, beatin' on us what can't defend ourselves.

Freehold was never a safe town, but at least it was free.

<She runs her tongue along the gap in her teeth.>

Bastards.

passages.title: The Beatings Will Continue
passages.text: Well is you a merc or isn't you? Get to merc'in!

passages.title: The Beatings Will Continue
passages.text:
Haha!

<Geraldine spits again out of her tooth gap.>

Had it comin' they did!

passages.title: Rig Robbing
passages.text:
I'm out here tryin' to enjoy my break, but I ran outta hooch.

Got some grog hidden in the water just off the dock, stashed in a crate tied up to some of the rigging. 

Do me a favor and fetch it, will ya? Rigging's pretty tangled so you might have to pull in a few lines before you get the right one.

I'd do it myself, but if they see me they're gonna force me back to work unloadin' them new weapons.

passages.title: Rig Robbing
passages.text: You get my stash?

passages.title: Rig Robbing
passages.text:
Ah, there she is! Good show.

Whaddya say to a toast?

passages.title: Stolen Goods
passages.text:
It was brought to my attention recently dat many of our supplies went missing overnight.

I suspected dat Tongo's crew was behind de theft, but we didn't have de strength or numbers needed to confront dem.

I want you to search de hideout for signs of our missing supplies. If dere's anything left when you arrive, bring it back here and I'll make sure you're compensated.

If we're going to survive Mojambo's assault we're going to need those stolen supplies back as soon as possible.

passages.title: Stolen Goods
passages.text: You've located de supplies and dey appear mostly intact! You have done a great service for our tribe, <name>.

passages.title: Menace to Society
passages.text:
These troggs are a menace to the whole area! They raid camps and caravans and eat the livestock when they come down from their caves. The kids being up there might set them off!

Slay some of those troggs before they decide to cause trouble.

passages.title: Menace to Society
passages.text: There are a lot of troggs around. More than I expected to see.

passages.title: Menace to Society
passages.text:
You look like you've been in a fight. Did you introduce those troggs to the business end of your weapon?

That's what I would have done! Give 'em a good right hook! And then a left! Pow! Bam!

I bet they're sorry for messing with you!

passages.title: The Adventurer's Society
passages.text:
Thank the Light!

I was taking care of my grandson and his friends. I told them to play quietly while I took a nap. When I woke up they'd left a note saying they were 'Going on an Expedition'. They think they'll find Titan relics in the trogg caverns!

They're too young to fight troggs and I'm too old! My bad knee almost gave out getting here.

You look strapping. Find my grandson and the rest of the 'Adventurer's Society'. Send them home!

passages.title: The Adventurer's Society
passages.text: Hey! You found our stuff!

passages.title: The Adventurer's Society
passages.text:
Nigel's grandpa is nice and all, but he'd have slowed us down! Adventure, fortune and fame awaited!

Maybe we should have brought a weapon or something though.

passages.title: Mistakes Were Made
passages.text:
My friends and I wanna be explorers so we made the Society. There are troggs here, right? So that means there's probably ancient stuff nearby!

The books say troggs like shiny things so we pooled some of our allowance and gave them gold so we could dig.

It didn't work out like we expected.

I escaped but they've got my friends! I've been trying to think about how to get them out.

Could you do it? We'll include you in our exploration report as an honorary member!

passages.title: Mistakes Were Made
passages.text: Hey! Are you gonna help my friends?

passages.title: Mistakes Were Made
passages.text:
Yay! You saved my friends!

I mean, they probably could have escaped on their own, but it was nice you could distract the troggs for 'em.

passages.title: Research Recovery
passages.text:
<The discarded paper contains a list of the items the Adventurer's Society has found during the course of their 'excavation' here at the Northern Caverns.

It is unlikely they actually found relics, but there's no harm in recovering the items the kids found. At the least they're souvenirs of the adventure.>

passages.title: Research Recovery
passages.text: Woah! You found our relics! Aren't they neat?

passages.title: Research Recovery
passages.text:
Isn't our stuff neat? We found real relics!

I bet Brann Bronzebeard will be impressed. We're gonna write to him once we get back home.

passages.title: Thesis Statement
passages.text:
My thesis!

Those smelly troggs took my thesis paper and fed it to their boars! Can you believe it!?

I worked forever on it! Two whole days! If I don't get it back I'm ruined! Absolutely ruined!

Please get my thesis paper back for me?

passages.title: Projection Destruction
passages.text:
Dis lich, Zardrax, be tryin' ta corrupt us ta join his side, <name>. I not be fallin' for it, and I know how ta be stoppin' it.

He be gatherin' power from dem mounds of skeletons. We gotta burn 'em ta cut Zardrax off a some power.

I be strong in da fire mojo. I can be impartin' some of me connection to da fire to ya ta burn dem mounds.

I be stayin' here with Kal'dran. I tink Zardrax be gettin' ta him.

passages.title: Projection Destruction
passages.text: Ya better get movin' and destroy dem skeleton mounds.

passages.title: Projection Destruction
passages.text: I saw dem fires burnin' from here. Zardrax gonna be hurtin' from dis one.

passages.title: Power Denied
passages.text:
Ah! Oh, it's you, <name>. Zardrax has me on edge, saying we are all doomed, dat dere is no hope.

I had a plan to stop him. All we had to do was kill a hexxer, Nana'kwug, who is helping spread Zardrax's power, and steal de fetish she is using.

Den you'd give dat fetish to Da'jul and he'd use his voodoo to grant us more power.

But it is hopeless now. Maybe we should just side with Zardrax. How can we stop someting as big as dis?

passages.title: Power Denied
passages.text: Ya got dat fetish yet? Maybe Kal'dran be calmin' down when he sees we be havin' a chance ta survive.

passages.title: Power Denied
passages.text: Good job on gettin' dis fetish. Dere be a lot dat I can be doin' with dis ting.

passages.title: Ruins-Level Marketing
passages.text:
Now dat de Goldtusk Inn be open for business, we gotta make sure everyone in Vol'dun knows about it!

I think we should focus on those wagon-riding vulpera first. Dey don't even have real homes!

In fact, I saw a pack of vulpera up at de ruins to de north de other day, and dey barely had anything.

Take dem dis coupon and tell dem to stop by for a free first stay.

passages.title: Ruins-Level Marketing
passages.text:
<Kenzou looks skeptically at the leaf you handed him.>

No, I will not be going there. But are you looking for some real work?

passages.title: Liquid Motivation
passages.text:
<Zauljin motions for you to come closer. He is clearly drunk.>

If I had information concerning Mojambo...<hick!>...how much would dat be worth to you?

You don't...<hick!>...believe me? Nobody suspects a drunk. I hear all sorts of things...

What do you have to lose? All it will cost is a bottle of...<hick!>...Zanchuli Reserve!

Whaddya say, mon?

passages.title: Liquid Motivation
passages.text: What do you have for me?

passages.title: Liquid Motivation
passages.text: Mojambo is teaming up with an outside gang to attack us? I knew he meant business, but I didn't expect him to go dis far. We need to come up with a plan as soon as possible...

passages.title: Arming the Tribe
passages.text:
We spotted some of Tongo's gang scouting de arena while you were away. It seems dis may be de calm before de storm.

We need to get de weapons you brought back from Tongo's hideout into de hands of our fellow outcasts. Mojambo's gang could attack any minute now.

We need to be prepared. Take de weapons and get dem to de unarmed members of de tribe.

If Mojambo thinks he can raid our home without a fight, he's got another thing coming.

passages.title: Arming the Tribe
passages.text: De time for war is nearly upon us.

passages.title: Arming the Tribe
passages.text: It's a good thing you armed de tribe! Mojambo and his gang are attacking as we speak!

passages.title: Tongo
passages.text:
If Mojambo hired Tongo's gang as reinforcements, we're in even more trouble than we first thought.

Tongo is a cruel and sadistic marauder who takes great delight in suffering. His gang is notorious for torturing their prey.

We won't be able to defend ourselves against both gangs at once. Our only chance of survival now is to strike first.

If you take out Tongo before de ambush, Mojambo will be expecting reinforcements dat never arrive. We may be able to use dat to our advantage...

passages.title: Tongo
passages.text: Has Tongo been defeated?

passages.title: Tongo
passages.text: With Tongo out of de way, all we have to worry about now is Mojambo...

passages.title: Terminal Degree
passages.text:
That's everyone but Nigel.

He's in the big cave! I bet he went in there to look for relics, but now he's tied up!

Would you save him too?

passages.title: Terminal Degree
passages.text: Thanks! Negotiation is a lot harder than Brann's book makes it out to be.

passages.title: Terminal Degree
passages.text:
Thank you for saving my grandson and his friends.

 I'm sure they will make fine explorers when they're adults.

Which will be about the time they are no longer grounded!

passages.title: Offer of Power
passages.text:
Ah... a <class>. You must be <name>... I have heard whispers of your name. Maybe you are smarter than dese two.

Zuldazar will fall to de blood trolls. You know dis. 

You can be saved, if you promise to serve me. I can give you more power than you have ever imagined.

Listen to what I can offer you...

passages.title: Offer of Power
passages.text: Show dis lich what ya be thinkin' of it!

passages.title: Offer of Power
passages.text: Zardrax be temptin' us ta join him, but dat ain't gonna work. We gonna stop dis lich and anyone else who wants ta help da blood trolls!

passages.title: Conduit Interruption
passages.text:
Dere be skeletons dat be funnelin' blood magic inta Zardrax's barrow. Me guess be Zardrax created dem ta help gather more power.

Ya gotta kill dese skeletons if ya want any shot at killin' dis lich. He should be gettin' weaker if he not be havin' dem as a source a power.

I be stayin' here in da meantime ta be watchin' our backs, no tellin' if dere be blood trolls comin' ta attack us.

passages.title: Conduit Interruption
passages.text: I can be tellin' from here dat Zardrax's power be gettin' weaker. We close ta endin' dis.

passages.title: All Hope is Lost
passages.text:
I am not doing dis anymore! You and Da'jul are WRONG! Dere is no stopping Zardrax!

I am leaving, and you cannot stop me. Zardrax will save us all from destruction and give us new power!

passages.title: All Hope is Lost
passages.text: Did ya find where Kal'dran ran off ta?

passages.title: All Hope is Lost
passages.text: We got no time ta be mournin' Kal'dran. He made his choice, so now we be makin' ours ta defeat Zardrax.

passages.title: Payback's a Lich
passages.text:
We can't be focusin' on da loss of Kal'dran. He be givin' up hope, and dat be someting we not gonna do.

Dis be da time ta strike at Zardrax. His power be waning. 

Go inta da heart of his barrow and destroy him, once and for all. Dat should show dem blood trolls who dey messin' with!

I'd help ya, but I be weakened from da blood trolls dat be attackin' me when ya were gone. 

Don't worry 'bout me, I can still be handlin' dem animals if dey come back.

passages.title: Payback's a Lich
passages.text: We need ta destroy Zardrax. Dis be our chance!

passages.title: Payback's a Lich
passages.text:
Ya did it! Zardrax be gone, and now da blood trolls be losin' a major source of their power.

I be makin' my way back ta da camp ta let Princess Talanji know 'bout Kal'dran.
