She deserves ta be knowin' dat he lost hope in our cause... might be good ta be seein' if anyone else is havin' doubts about what we be doin'.

passages.title: Rescue the Relics
passages.text:
According to the information you brought us, we should be adding those relics to our collection.

Explore the ruins and see if you can find any of these "tokens of affection" the sethrak may have left for their Keepers. 

Better we find hands that will cherish them, than ones that will destroy.

Plus, add a little time, and anything becomes interesting... to the right people.

passages.title: Rescue the Relics
passages.text: Did you find the relics?

passages.title: Rescue the Relics
passages.text: Perfect. The power of nostalgia is fascinating. These relics will hold great sentimental value. The monetary value won't be bad, either.

passages.title: Expedite the Excavation
passages.text:
Everywhere we go, there they are. Sethrak. And it's never the ones you want to see.

It seems they are looking for some key. With this new information, I do not think they are looking in the right place.

Really, as entertaining as it is to confound them, we need to wrap up our work here and move on.

If you could remove some of them, it would greatly help our crew!

passages.title: Expedite the Excavation
passages.text:
I need to mark this down. 

How many sethrak have you killed?

passages.title: Expedite the Excavation
passages.text: Well done! They must be so irritated. This is great fun!

passages.title: A Grizzly End
passages.text:
This lodge serves as the largest supplier of furs and leather to Boralus.

<Kennings puffs out his chest a bit.>

And as its proprietor, it is my duty to ensure every request is met on time. With recent delays, I've decided to take a trip out here to see if the Holtons need my assistance.

We could use any available hands! Take this knife and bring back some pelts from the bears in the nearby pass.

passages.title: A Grizzly End
passages.text: I see that Lord Kennings' idea of assistance hasn't changed since his last visit.

passages.title: A Grizzly End
passages.text: These furs appear to be in fine shape. Your skills should easily make up for any setbacks caused by 'accidents'.

passages.title: Pardon Our Rust
passages.text:
The traps we've set up in the field require routine maintenance checks. Some of them are fairly old and will spring at incorrect times. If only we could get more funding for these sort of supplies. 

<The huntmistress glances towards Lord Kennings.>

While you're out hunting, could you reset any sprung ones that you find?

passages.title: Pardon Our Rust
passages.text: It seems that you still have all of your limbs attached, and here I was hoping that I could talk Kennings into buying us new traps. Fair work.

passages.title: A Hunt for Hawk Eggs
passages.text:
Before Alanna sends us on our grand hunt, there is something more immediate demanding our attention...

I'm absolutely famished! No good man can hunt on an empty stomach.

There are hawks in the area, which means that there are also hawk eggs. I'm not sure how well they'll do in an omelet, but I'm always one for a culinary adventure!

Good <class>, could you bring back a few before we get started?

passages.title: A Hunt for Hawk Eggs
passages.text: Have you found enough eggs yet? You know what those small goblins say, time is money!

passages.title: A Hunt for Hawk Eggs
passages.text: Fantastic! Here's hoping that hawk eggs aren't too gamey...

passages.title: Mean Gulls
passages.text:
Must... catch... Need more...

The gulls... they bite... scratch... take...

I need them gone... but... I must... catch...

passages.title: Mean Gulls
passages.text:
The gulls are... no more...

Now... I can catch more...

Yes... catch more...

passages.title: The Reel Deal
passages.text:
<These fishing rods must have been left behind when Art moved from the beach. Most of them seem to have bites.

Maybe you should reel them up and see what's hooked?>

passages.title: The Reel Deal
passages.text:
<That looks like the last of Art's rods.

You manage to salvage some of Art's bait with your catch. 

Waste not, want not>

passages.title: I Like Fish Guts and I Cannot Lie
passages.text:
<It looks like some of the fish the gulls have been stealing from Art are still intact.

He'd probably be happy to get the innards from these as well.>

passages.title: I Like Fish Guts and I Cannot Lie
passages.text: What's... this?

passages.title: I Like Fish Guts and I Cannot Lie
passages.text:
Yes... yeeesss...

More entrails... more innards... only the best...

passages.title: Cleanse the Mind
passages.text:
If you wish to invite Akunda into your mind, it can't be bogged down by fear or regret. 

Meditate at de Shrine of Thunder and confront whatever demons linger in de dark recesses of your mind.

passages.title: Cleanse the Mind
passages.text: Some who meditate at de shrine hear de voice of de loa himself, though most only hear silence or de sounds of their failings.

passages.title: Cleanse the Mind
passages.text: I can tell you found success. You are at peace.

passages.title: It Springs Eternal
passages.text:
Water is a sacred resource in dese dunes, but those within dis temple never know thirst. 

Akunda commands de storm, allowing de nearby spring to never run empty. 

Unfortunately, our eternal water source attracts a variety of animals dat are a plague upon our temple. 

Rid de valley of their presence before you return.

passages.title: It Springs Eternal
passages.text: De spring is a gift from de loa and must be preserved at all costs.

passages.title: Repairing the Past
passages.text:
Dis explains why de loa has been silent. Akunda himself has forgotten who he is!

Someone or something must be abusing his power. 

We won't know how to help without speaking to de loa.

I can perform a ritual dat may repair Akunda's mind, but it is not without risk.

passages.title: Repairing the Past
passages.text: I seek your help, <name>.

passages.title: How to Be a Blood Troll
passages.text:
You will have to blend in if you don't want anyone getting suspicious. This won't be pretty.

Dere are drudges around de camp who have been tied up as part of a ritual. Dey get beaten as a test to make dem stronger.

Any who fail de ritual are sacrificed. De ones who succeed are allowed to fight de Zandalari.

If you are going to blend in, you need to "test" dese drudges as part of de ritual. It's weird, but dat's how dey work.

passages.title: How to Be a Blood Troll
passages.text: It is not a pretty task, but dese trolls are not our allies.

passages.title: How to Be a Blood Troll
passages.text: Good work, nobody suspects a thing. Did any of dem crack under de pressure?

passages.title: Trial of Truth
passages.text:
Those within our temple have left their past lives behind. They devote themselves entirely to Akunda. 

Dis final test is perhaps de most important. 

Dis is de moment of truth. 

You will speak your name, as you will be known from dis day forth.

passages.title: Trial of Truth
passages.text: You have proven worthy of entering our temple, Akunda.

passages.title: The Perfect Offering
passages.text:
Dis offering is all dat I have to my name, but it wouldn't be right for me to use it for myself when I know your friend is in danger. 

She saved my life, now I can save hers.

Take de offering. Don't make me ask twice.

passages.title: The Perfect Offering
passages.text: Do you come bearing gifts to our loa?

passages.title: The Perfect Offering
passages.text:
Dis is a generous offering, but a gift alone isn't enough to enter our temple. 

Redemption can't be bought, it must be earned. 

Lucky for you, dere is much work to be done.

passages.title: Knowledge of the Past
passages.text:
An old friend of mine came to de sands willingly to gain knowledge of de past. 

If anyone can locate dis weapon, it would be Julwaba. 

Last I heard, she planned to excavate de ruins surrounding de great pyramid.

passages.title: Knowledge of the Past
passages.text: How did Jarka'zet's men know where we'd be?

passages.title: Knowledge of the Past
passages.text: It's clear dat Jakra'zet won't stop until I'm dead.

passages.title: The Bargain is Struck
passages.text:
Now dat you have declared a patron loa for your time here in Zuldazar, you should inform de king of your decision.

He will appreciate dat you chose to follow de mighty Gonk.

passages.title: The Bargain is Struck
passages.text:
So, you have chosen de path of Gonk. May de loa forever reveal de tracks of your enemies.

For myself, I follow Rezan, de devilsaur loa of kings. He and I have not spoken for many years, though.

Perhaps I shall pay him a visit one of dese days.

passages.title: Lucky Charm
passages.text:
My daddy would never admit it, but he's really superstitious. I don't think he'll ever feel safe on a horse unless he has a lucky charm!

I heard about a fox somewhere around here that's been eating a lot of chickens, and escaping everybody trying to catch him. I bet he's really lucky! Maybe if you got his tail and gave it to my dad, he'd feel lucky too!

passages.title: Lucky Charm
passages.text: Tails are real lucky, <name>. I think this one will give my dad heaps of courage!

passages.title: Lucky Charm
passages.text: I think I can feel the luck too!

passages.title: Safety First
passages.text:
The connection between horse and rider is fascinating to me, and I will never truly understand until I experience it.

But, well, you know... armor! How could I possibly even think to mount one of these beauties without some proper protection?

I saw some waterfalls nearby. There must be shells near the banks of its pools! Would you entertain an old Tortollan by collecting some for his safety?

passages.title: Safety First
passages.text: Protection, yes. Can't put yourself in a dangerous situation without the proper protection!

passages.title: Safety First
passages.text: Ah yes, these shells will help keep me well safeguarded!

passages.title: The Perfect Horse, of Course
passages.text:
With all that you've collected for me... I guess it is time to mount, isn't it?

Hoo! I haven't felt such nerves for three hundred years! Would you mind assisting me in finding a suitable equine partner? I could not trust myself to make the decision alone!

passages.title: The Perfect Horse, of Course
passages.text: My dad thinks horses can have lots of personalities, just like us. We gotta find him the perfect horse for his first ride!

passages.title: The Perfect Horse, of Course
passages.text:
He's on! He's on!

Don't worry, <name>. I'm sure he'll be fine! Thanks for all of your help!

passages.title: Take the Bait
passages.text:
The bait... almost gone now... must catch...

The crabs... find them... get more...

passages.title: Take the Bait
passages.text: Almost gone...

passages.title: Take the Bait
passages.text:
Yes... more meat!

I must not... can not... stop!

passages.title: Unappreciated Scrolls
passages.text:
Since you're here in Natha'vor, you might as well help out the rest of the pilgrimage with a problem.

These trolls have stolen several of our scrolls. Why they would, I have no idea, I doubt they're smart enough to even read.

I want you to get them back. I'm not young anymore, I can't just be casting magic off the top of my head! 

Especially healing magic... which I'm sure Shoak is going to need when you rescue his dumb shell.

passages.title: Noble Responsibilities
passages.text:
From the state of this body, I would say a beast with formidable claws or fangs ravaged this camp. You say the trail leads westward? This camp usually houses more than one of Alanna's hunters. I wonder if they are tracking the beast down as well.

Hurry it up! I don't want to spend the day waiting around. Track our dangerous quarry!

passages.title: Noble Responsibilities
passages.text: Thank you for dealing with the threat. I'll see that the men who died out there have a proper send off.

passages.title: A Slight Detour
passages.text:
If this coven is drawing its power from these ancient ruins, then I may just know of something that could help us fight back.

Meet me at the first fork along the Highroad Pass. There is something there I want you to see.

passages.title: A Slight Detour
passages.text:
Good, you are here.

Unfortunately it looks like we're not going to have an easy path to our destination.

passages.title: Yeti to Rumble
passages.text:
It would seem that the guard have been lax in patrolling the Highroad Pass. The mountain yetis have taken advantage of their absence, and now lie directly in our path.

I am no soldier, <class>, so I will need to ask that you take care of them while I try to sneak past. If we can drive them off the road, at least it will make the pass safe again for travelers.

passages.title: Yeti to Rumble
passages.text: We should drive the yetis back from the road. Having a major trade route cut off by monsters isn't going to help our fight against the coven.

passages.title: Yeti to Rumble
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>. Keeping the pass clear will ensure a steady stream of supplies to Highroad Gate.

We will need them in the battles to come.

passages.title: Unlocking History
passages.text:
I'm sure you're wondering why I've brought you here. 

Located somewhere inside this cottage is a hidden door. If we can find a way to access it, the answer to your questions, and possibly our survival against the coven, should lie beyond.

Help me search for it, <class>.

passages.title: Unlocking History
passages.text: The opening must be here somewhere...

passages.title: Unlocking History
passages.text:
You found it! I knew that they were more than stories!

Come, let us see what's inside.

passages.title: The Ruins of Gol Var
passages.text:
What lies beyond are more ruins, much like those the coven sought. 

However, these ruins served a different purpose, one that established the legacy of House Waycrest thousands of years ago.

Let us head inside, and I will explain.

passages.title: The Ruins of Gol Var
passages.text: Just a little further...

passages.title: The Ruins of Gol Var
passages.text:
Who would've thought that from this stuffy little chamber would rise some of the greatest warriors of House Waycrest's history?

Are you prepared to follow in their footsteps?

passages.title: The Order of Embers
passages.text:
The Order of Embers was the name given to those who took up these arms against the Drust. Using the tools and methods uncovered by the scholars, they were able to counter the Drust's magic, and ensure our victory in the war.

If the coven wants to use the Drust's magic against us, then we'll use the order's weapons against them.

The knowledge of the order rests here, but without a hand to wield it, it will do us no good. 

Will you be that hand, <class>? Will you revive the Order of Embers?

passages.title: The Order of Embers
passages.text: What say you?

passages.title: The Order of Embers
passages.text:
You do great honor to my family, <class>.  The most noble of Waycrests were once inquisitors of the order.

It is only fitting that it is you who takes up its mantle now.

passages.title: Gol Koval
passages.text:
A group of hunters went up into the hills awhile ago and we haven't heard back from them. 

My niece is up there and it isn't like her to be out of touch for so long! Would you please find her?

She was headed towards Gol Koval.

passages.title: Gol Koval
passages.text: My aunt sent you? Oh, Light bless that woman.

passages.title: The North Pass Caverns
passages.text:
Please, you must help!

My grandson got lost around the caves to the north, and I'm so afraid that the troggs might have got him! 

My husband went after him, but he's getting on in years, and I fear he imagines himself tougher than he really is.

Could you help them? You should be able to catch up with Thaddeus along the northern road.

passages.title: The North Pass Caverns
passages.text: I'm not lost! My grandson and his friends ran off and I've been looking for them. I wanted to find them before the troggs did!

passages.title: Weeds of the Mire
passages.text:
<Magura weakly opens her eyes as you approach.>

Help me... weak... can't heal...

<Magura struggles to raise an arm to point towards a nearby plant.>

Graveweed... help... more... please...

passages.title: Diversionary Tactics
passages.text:
Our destination is that cottage up ahead. I know it doesn't look like much, but a great deal of history is hidden inside.

First, though, we'll need to deal with that massive yeti camped just outside. I'd hate to ask it of you, but I'll need you to draw his attention so I can slip inside.

Once you've taken care of him, I'll meet you within.

passages.title: Diversionary Tactics
passages.text: I'll meet you inside, <class>.

passages.title: Diversionary Tactics
passages.text:
That was close! 

I'm glad to have such a capable <class> as my guardian. I would hate to be your enemy.

passages.title: Settle the Score
passages.text:
A year ago I lost my daughter to the largest boar in the forest.

I have tracked him since, trading blows back and forth. But this time...

Let's just say I don't have much time left.

All I wish for is vengeance. Please <class>, avenge us so that my soul can leave this plane and join my daughter, wherever she may be.

passages.title: Settle the Score
passages.text: Though my lifeblood drains, all I yearn for is vengeance.

passages.title: Settle the Score
passages.text:
<Caleb's body is lifeless, still warm. His wounds claimed him while you were gone.

His face seems content, as though he knew you would finish the job.>

passages.title: Take the High Road
passages.text:
Let us continue to Arom's Stand. It will take some time to parse the knowledge of the tome and train more inquisitors for our cause.

If the order's weapons are as effective against the coven as they were against the Drust, we may stand a chance of rescuing my family and restoring this land to its former glory.

I will make my way there on foot. Until we meet again, <class>.

passages.title: Take the High Road
passages.text:
I'm glad you made it, <name>. 

We'll need to get started right away if we want to use the knowledge in this tome to fight the coven.

passages.title: Valley of Sorrows
passages.text:
Your friend's memories are gone. 

Dat is Akunda's gift to us. He takes away our painful memories, but a lot more than dat has gone missing lately. 

I can't even remember what I had for breakfast, and it's getting worse by de day. 

Something's not right. 

Meijani and I had a plan. We were going to do... something... in de Valley of Sorrows. It's where Akunda keeps de forgotten memories. 

If you're looking for answers, finding Meijani is de best place to start.

passages.title: Valley of Sorrows
passages.text: Who are you? Have we met before?

passages.title: Memory Breach
passages.text:
De memories of Akunda's followers rest within dis valley. 

Most are best left forgotten, but dey may be our only chance to find out what happened to Akunda. 

Look back upon de memories here. See if you can find any clues about what happened to our loa. 

Be warned. Dis task is not for de weak. What you witness in dese memories can't be unseen.

passages.title: Memory Breach
passages.text: Peer into de memories. See what you can find.

passages.title: Memory Breach
passages.text: It is as I feared. De loa's own memories have been taken from him.

passages.title: Vile Infestation
passages.text:
Redemption must be earned. 

We do good works to show Akunda we are worthy of his blessing. 

De ranishu are a plague upon these lands. Dey devour everything in sight, with no regard for taste or texture. 

If dey go unchecked, those vile pests will eat their way straight to de temple.

Rid de mesa of their presence. Show Akunda you are worthy of his gift.

passages.title: Vile Infestation
passages.text: Akunda smiles upon you. He knows what you have done here today.

passages.title: Sacred Remains
passages.text:
Dis area was once a lush jungle, home to many great and powerful thunder lizards.

De bones of those ancient and powerful creatures are still buried around de temple.

Great power lingers within those ancient remains... you will need such power to call upon Akunda.

Search de area and return to me with de ancient bones of de thunder lizards.

passages.title: Sacred Remains
passages.text: Have you found de ancient bones?

passages.title: Sacred Remains
passages.text: Dese bones still resonate with power.

passages.title: Powerful Conductors
passages.text:
Akunda offers us a chance to start anew. 

Through a sacred ritual, de loa enters our mind and removes de memories dat cause us pain. 

If you seek Akunda's blessing, den you must first prepare for de ritual. 

De pests dat feed on de wildlife here have antennae dat are great conductors for magic. De larger, de better. 

Their leader's antennae should do de trick. He's easily three times de size of de normal ranishu.

passages.title: Powerful Conductors
passages.text: Do you have de antennae?

passages.title: Powerful Conductors
passages.text: Yes... dis will work well.

passages.title: Ending the Madness
passages.text:
Akunda the Exalted is not who he seems. 

He poisoned the eternal spring, sickening all who drank from it. Even I was not immune to his abhorrent alchemy. 

Now he drains my power, abusing my gift to wipe the minds of all who might try to stop him. 

We will not let him succeed. 

What little power I have left, I will lend to you. 

Use it to call the storm and end the madness that has taken over my temple.

passages.title: Ending the Madness
passages.text:
You wield my gift well, <name>. 

Now that my power has returned, I can heal the minds of my children.

passages.title: Inconvenient Spirits
passages.text:
The sethrak have oppressed vulpera like me for countless generations.

You can't fight 'em. Trust me, adventurerr. My caravan tried.

I took that beating as a lesson, and then I found a new pack to run with.

Here, we keep our distance from the sethrak and scavenge ruins like this one for anything valuable we can use or trade.

You want in? We could use a fourth. This one's protected by nasty spirits that keep harassing us.

Take them out and you're in.

passages.title: Inconvenient Spirits
passages.text: I've never met a spirit that made my day better.

passages.title: Inconvenient Spirits
passages.text: Well, you're good at killing. I could tell that even from back here. Welcome to the crew.

passages.title: Vengeance From Above
passages.text:
Emperor Korthek hides deep in his stolen temple below ground. We must create such chaos that he has no choice but to emerge to face us.

The vulpera riot is a good start, but it will not be enough. Alone, they are no match for the Faithless army.

Thankfully, they are not alone.

We will ride the mighty Rakjan through the skies. While you throw lightning bombs, I'll use my charged staff to blast the Faithless armies below.

Let us hope that is enough to lure out Korthek. I am eager to finish this.

passages.title: Vengeance From Above
passages.text: Emperor Korthek is certainly on his way to us by now. We must prepare quickly.

passages.title: Shattered and Broken
passages.text:
Something is terribly wrong.

Unwanted memories have been released from their magical confines. 

Akunda's power is supposed to keep dem sealed away...

De physical manifestation of our most haunting memories have no place in dis world. 

Dey must be destroyed.

passages.title: Shattered and Broken
passages.text: You did what was right. Memories like those have no place in dis world.

passages.title: A Sweater for Rupert
passages.text:
The nights are cold in this area, and I am worried my poor dog will freeze to death. I wish to sew him a sweater, but I have no materials to make one with.

I would pay anyone who brings me a pair of porcupine quills and four raccoon tails.

-Kolta

passages.title: A Sweater for Rupert
passages.text: Is there something you need from me?

passages.title: A Sweater for Rupert
passages.text: Thank you, my dog and I are eternally grateful.

passages.title: The Start of a Monster Hunt
passages.text:
This is the closest I've been to a dead body, how exciting! What do you think murdered him?

Regardless, it is my duty to ensure the safety of individuals under my employ. With a combination of my wit and bravery, and your practical skills, we should be able to track it down.

This will be a tale for the ages!

Let's start with looking around the camp, see if you can find any clues.

passages.title: The Start of a Monster Hunt
passages.text: Did you find anything? I'm still caught up in examining this poor fellow.

passages.title: The Start of a Monster Hunt
passages.text: A trail, you say? I wonder where it leads...

passages.title: Fond Farewells
passages.text:
Dis is where we part ways, <name>.

I'm going to take de name Akunda, and start a new life here. 

When you find Rakera, and I know you will, give her my thanks. 

She saved my life, and I'm going to make sure to live a life dat was worth saving. 

If you find yourself back in de city, could you deliver dis note for me? I trust you not to open it, though I doubt you could read my scrawls anyway.

passages.title: Fond Farewells
passages.text: What is dis?

passages.title: Fond Farewells
passages.text:
<B'wizati reads the note and wipes a tear from her eye.>

He may choose to forget, but I choose to remember, no matter what pain it brings me. 

At least he is safe. Loa watch over him.

passages.title: The Bones of Xibala
passages.text:
Our allies in the Explorers' League have alerted us to an exciting find. They have set up camp in the Xibala region of Zuldazar.

Make your way to the camp and help them uncover anything that may advance our cause.

passages.title: Xibalan Ecology
passages.text:
I want to take me boys out and really dig our picks in, but every scout I've sent into the ruins just came back half mauled to death.

Some didn't come back at all.

From what I can tell, the ruins are home to more'n just these spiky grass-eaters. Do you think you could be a peach an' thin their numbers a bit?

I'd caution ye against tamperin' with the local ecology an' all, but in the interest of not gettin' eaten I think I'll let ye make the call.

passages.title: Xibalan Ecology
passages.text: Glad it weren't me, but here's a nice little reward for yer trouble!

passages.title: Torga, the Turtle Loa
passages.text:
Name's Lashk. We're not here to join any cause, we just want to hear Torga's legendary stories.

I don't know if he'll help, but you can try persuading Torga, loa of the turtles, and see if he'll help you fight these blood trolls.

You can join on our pilgrimage to Torga, just keep quiet. Follow the path and find Kisha, she'll tell you where to go.

passages.title: Torga, the Turtle Loa
passages.text: Dis is de work of de blood trolls, I am certain of it. We will get to de bottom of dis.

passages.title: Encase of Emergency
passages.text:
The cliffs here are well known for the crystal clear ice which forms at their base, and even more so for the elementals that are responsible for such. The hunters in my lodge use shards from the primal bodies to keep their stock frozen for transport. 

More importantly, think of how useful it could be for making and serving drinks!

Let's see if we can't find some elementals and gather shards from them.

passages.title: Encase of Emergency
passages.text: I've heard that destroying some of the larger ice structures in the area angers them, so do what you do best and destroy any that you come across!

passages.title: Encase of Emergency
passages.text: Perfectly chilled drinks, here I come! And there is enough for the hunters here too.

passages.title: Beseeching Bwonsamdi
passages.text:
We must talk to Torga's spirit and find out what exactly happened here... and how we can stop it.

Hrm, you mentioned dat you are linked to Bwonsamdi now.

It is time to test dat link. We need Bwonsamdi to get us Torga's spirit.

passages.title: Beseeching Bwonsamdi
passages.text: We must get started summoning Bwonsamdi.

passages.title: Beseeching Bwonsamdi
passages.text: For better or worse, we have Bwonsamdi's aid. Let us get to de killing.

passages.title: WANTED: Ol' Frostclaw
passages.text:
Old Frostclaw has once again been spotted near the edge of the pass. Hunters in the area are advised to keep caution. This larger than average bear has killed four people to date, I'd hate for you to make it a fifth. 

Any individual who kills the beast will be rewarded, regardless of their occupation.

-Alanna 

<Below the huntmistress' signature is a child's drawing of a bear with the words "Ol' Frostclaw" above it.>

passages.title: WANTED: Ol' Frostclaw
passages.text: Is this about the wanted sign? You better hurry, a good number of hunters are after it as well.

passages.title: WANTED: Ol' Frostclaw
passages.text: I'll let the hunters know they were beaten to the kill by a passerby. That should humble some of them.

passages.title: Westward Noble
passages.text: While I am loath to involve you in this further, I don't have the men to afford an escort for Lord Kennings. If he gets hurt, we'll all be out of a job. Can you make sure he at least made it to the west camp?

passages.title: Westward Noble
passages.text: Oh, you finally made it! I think we have more pressing matters on our hands than hunting deer.

passages.title: Poisoning the Brood
passages.text:
Now we have room for our plan to kill Hir'eek. You see, <name>, my specialty is in making potions and poisons.

I am working on a poison to use on Hir'eek, when de time comes. I have no idea if it will work or not.

I want you to take what I already made and use it on de bats around here. It should kill dem instantly. 

If it works, den I can make it stronger with my voodoo and give us a chance at killing Hir'eek.

passages.title: Poisoning the Brood
passages.text: Did you poison de bats yet?

passages.title: Poisoning the Brood
passages.text: I knew my poison would work! I just need to put a bit more of my voodoo in dere for it to be ready for Hir'eek.

passages.title: Hir'eek, the Bat Loa
passages.text:
Hir'eek knows we are here. If my knowledge of Hir'eek is correct, he will personally kill us after we present ourselves.

It is time, den. You and I will walk out dere into a horde of blood trolls who want to watch their loa kill us.

Take dis dagger. It is coated with de poison I made. I trust you to survive longer than me to use it.

You pretend to cower to Hir'eek, and I will do de talking. On my signal, you jump on Hir'eek and start stabbing!

...And den we hope for de best.

passages.title: Hir'eek, the Bat Loa
passages.text: <Cough> Well... at least my spine wasn't snapped.

passages.title: Cease all Summoning
passages.text:
I feel something dark and powerful being summoned in de husk of Torga. You need to stop it!

Dere must be a summoner using Torga's blood to finish a ritual.

Do what you can to stop dem. I will stay here to keep dese tortollans safe from de blood trolls.

passages.title: Cease all Summoning
passages.text: Did you kill dat summoner?

passages.title: Cease all Summoning
passages.text: We are too late? Den we can only hope Torga can help us destroy... whatever it is dat you saw.

passages.title: To Kill a Loa
passages.text:
I am badly hurt... I don't think I can move. Don't worry, I have some potions dat can heal me... slowly.

Hir'eek is just down de cavern dere. De poison injured him, but he is a loa, and it will take more than dat to take him down.

I can't believe we... YOU are going kill a loa. It's just not someting we do... but Hir'eek serves G'huun. We have no choice! 

It's all up to you, now. Kill Hir'eek and end dis madness!

passages.title: To Kill a Loa
passages.text: Hir'eek still lives! Go kill him!

passages.title: To Kill a Loa
passages.text: I know. It is done. Hir'eek is dead. Nazmir is a cursed place, <name>. We never were meant to kill a loa... but here we are.

passages.title: Speaking with the Dead
passages.text:
Ya be livin' up ta ya part of da bargain. I be ready ta show ya what remains of Torga's soul. 

I gonna need a little part of ya ta act as a conduit ta be summonin' Torga. Don't worry, I be givin' ya all back.

Mostly.

After we be done, I be headin' out. Ya always welcome ta call on me again... but only if ya got another deal ready.

passages.title: Speaking with the Dead
passages.text: Ya ready ta speak ta Torga's spirit?

passages.title: Speaking with the Dead
passages.text: We may not have Torga's aid, but we can stop whatever de blood trolls are planning.

passages.title: A Port in Peril
passages.text:
A group of mogu have taken hold of Warport Rastari and now threaten to encroach further into my city.

It would seem Zul is losing his grip over his pets. 

Dat port is vital to our military fleet. If de brutes succeed, Zuldazar will fall, and dere won't be a fleet to aid your precious Horde.

You wish to prove yourself an ally of de Zandalari? Meet my blade and shield at de port and clean up dis mess.

passages.title: A Port in Peril
passages.text:
Things are worse than we thought.

Much worse.

passages.title: Captain Gulnaku's Treasure
passages.text:
<This map is poorly drawn and covered in stains, but appears to identify three possible locations where a pirate captain may have buried treasure around the Port of Zem'lan. The treasure could be at any of the three locations.

At the bottom of the map, someone scrawled an order: Set traps!>

passages.title: Captain Gulnaku's Treasure
passages.text: <It's firmly locked. You'll need the captain's key to open this.>

passages.title: Captain Gulnaku's Treasure
passages.text: <The chest is filled with shiny treasure.>

passages.title: Diplomacy and Dominance
passages.text:
May I entrust you with my staff, adventurer? I do not offer this lightly, so do not accept it lightly either.

We will need every advantage when we face Emperor Korthek, and I've identified an opportunity to increase the power at our disposal.

The Faithless maintain a series of suppression spires on the ridge above us to subjugate the pterrordax. My staff can drain power from the spires to bolster its own potency.

Meanwhile, I will recruit a much-needed ally for the next stage of our mission.

passages.title: Diplomacy and Dominance
passages.text:
<Vorrik smiles as he takes the staff back from you.>

Thank you, <name>. I must confess I was anxious for your return. It's been many years since this staff has left my side.

My trust in you was well placed, however. The staff is practically rippling with power.

passages.title: Essence of the Light Mother
passages.text:
This is a crucial moment, <name>. Our campaign must not lose momentum.

Though she has fallen, I still sense Xe'ra's presence all around us. The Light that shone within her heart can yet be a source of strength for our cause.

No doubt the loss of Xe'ra has deeply wounded Turalyon. I will do what I can to ease his troubled spirit while you gather the vestiges of the naaru that remain.

passages.title: Essence of the Light Mother
passages.text: Though Xe'ra is gone, her essence can still aid us in our struggle.

passages.title: Essence of the Light Mother
passages.text: Ah yes, I sense the Light within these fragments. Do not lose hope, <name>!

passages.title: Wrath of the Zandalari
passages.text:
Dere is no reasoning with de mogu. Dey only value one thing: strength.

Dat is something de Zandalari have like no other, but our forces are spread thin. We are simply not prepared to fight dem.

You have proven yourself a capable warrior, for |5<race>. Would you be our "ambassador" to dese brutes? Show dem dat de Zandalari do not stand alone!

passages.title: Wrath of the Zandalari
passages.text: You fight well, but our work is far from over.

passages.title: No Troll Left Behind
passages.text:
Dis is de primary port for de Zandalari fleet. Thankfully most of our ships were out when de mogu came, but Rastari is still an active fortification for de city.

De mogu did not land on abandoned shores, <class>. Dere are all manner of brave warriors stationed here, fighting for their lives.

Take dis whistle and rally all you can. Our warriors will hear its scream and know dat dey are not alone.

passages.title: No Troll Left Behind
passages.text: Our strength is in unity. It is what makes us Zandalari.

passages.title: No Troll Left Behind
passages.text: Our warriors won't soon forget you risking your own life to save theirs. Thank you.

passages.title: Show of Strength
passages.text:
Their leader's time is coming soon now, but we need to dispose of his lieutenants first. Our momentum will be lost if dey reform ranks.

Jao-Ti is de first. Legend has it Lei Shen himself said he showed a great connection to de storms. He is leading de mogu's stormbinders.

De other is Subjugator Zheng, a slaver dat would make de Kul Tirans blush. You have never seen depravity like his.

Kill dem both, and make dem suffer. De mogu are no strangers to war, but neither are we.

passages.title: Show of Strength
passages.text: Is de deed done?

passages.title: Show of Strength
passages.text: Dey deserve worse fates, I assure you.

passages.title: Crumbling Apart
passages.text:
De mogu army grows with each passing moment thanks to their animated stone warriors. It is only a matter of time before their forces are back at full strength.

A thousand curses upon Zul. He was forbidden from bringing his pets here--and from resurrecting de Thunder King in Pandaria.

We are de only thing standing between dem and de city. We've got to stop dis while we still can!

passages.title: Crumbling Apart
passages.text: Dey will reinforce their lines if we do not act soon. Dis may be our only opportunity.

passages.title: Embrace the Voodoo
passages.text:
Dese heathens think we are weak. Dey think we are broken.

But Zandalari never truly die.

I've blessed dat skull Habutu gave you with a bit of voodoo dat will let it break through to de Other Side. You will need to use my spirit obelisks to channel its power. Dey will take it from dere.

passages.title: Embrace the Voodoo
passages.text: Nobody will ever take dis land from us.

passages.title: Embrace the Voodoo
passages.text: Can you feel it? De spirits are flowing through you, and dey are pleased.

passages.title: Torga's Eternal Return
passages.text:
Well, we did it. Doesn't make the plan we had any less crazy. But there's still one more thing left to do.

I've been visiting Torga for years. He told me stories of powerful scrolls, one in particular that he said was meant to be used to put a loa's spirit to rest.

I think you should be the one to read it. I mean, if you're SMART enough to read it. 

Bah! Just take the scroll and read it before I have second thoughts.

passages.title: Torga's Eternal Return
passages.text: You can read that scroll, can you?

passages.title: Torga's Eternal Return
passages.text:
I guess we're in this for the long haul. Lashk and I have a lot to take care of if we're going to help.

I even know where you could go to find that troll friend of yours... and Krag'wa.

passages.title: Glimmering Locket
passages.text:
<A glint of metal catches your eye among the gently bobbing flotsam. Digging into the tangled seaweed, you discover a locket of simple, yet sturdy design.

Opening the locket reveals a hand-drawn picture of a woman with fiery red bangs. 

Her arm is around a woman with short-cropped auburn hair, and the two are proudly displaying warm smiles for the artist.>

passages.title: Glimmering Locket
passages.text: Hm? What's that you've got there?

passages.title: Glimmering Locket
passages.text:
Is that?

<Jane takes the locket and opens it tenderly. Tears begin to well up in her eyes as she closes it and tucks it away in her jacket.>

Thank you.

passages.title: Catching Up
passages.text:
Good to see you in one piece, <name>. Nazmir is a place of nightmares, but you seem to be surviving.

Rokhan and I convinced your Horde dat we need more support. He is getting ready to meet with reinforcements.

We still need to get de loa's aid. What happened with Bwonsamdi and Hir'eek?

passages.title: Catching Up
passages.text: Well? What happened?

passages.title: Catching Up
passages.text: Our luck may be looking up. Perhaps we can get Torga's aid.

passages.title: The Castaways
passages.text:
I see the sirens have made another catch. You're lucky they haven't stripped your bones yet.

If you need to trade supplies or just warm yourself by the fire, there's a camp up the hill behind me.

Everyone there washed up in the tides, just like you. Figure we've got folks from at least four or five shipwrecks now. All banded together, just tryin' to survive.

Talk to Stabby Jane. Don't worry about her nickname, she's actually real nice.

passages.title: The Castaways
passages.text: Ah, you must be from the latest wreck. Those damn sirens are getting bolder by the day.

passages.title: The Long Con
passages.text:
Hello again my young friend! I have good news.

Our mutual acquaintance Carentan -- the man who scammed us in Freehold -- has finally come out of hiding.

I have been communicating with him in letters delivered by various middlemen and even completed a few proxy trades to earn his trust. In our last correspondence, he agreed to meet for an in-person trade.

He thinks he is meeting with a Ms. Pixy Spindlespark, gnomish hairdresser with a weakness for poached furs.

But he'll be meeting you instead.

passages.title: The Long Con
passages.text: Don't let him get away this time!

passages.title: The Long Con
passages.text: Slow and steady, my friend.

passages.title: Chasing the Leader
passages.text:
The locals and the league have been working together tae reclaim relics in this here cave up the hill. But it seems that we've angered the previous residents. I think the marines can keep the expedition safe fer now, but I dinna how long they can keep it up. 

We need yer help before things go south! Find Hilde Firebreaker, the leader of our expedition. She ran back into the cave fer somethin' or another.

passages.title: Chasing the Leader
passages.text: Yer here to help? Finally!

passages.title: Silencing the Sisters
passages.text:
The sirens in this tideway have drawn countless ships to their doom. Wiping them out would be a boon to all seafaring folk.

But you can't very well kill all of them. Only a fool would try that.

The real dangerous ones are the elders. The "sisters" as they're known. Bigger, smarter, and stronger than the younger ones. Their voices carry far out to sea and bring in all the big "catches."

I managed to track two of them to a den at the northern end of the tideway, but I can't take them alone.

passages.title: Silencing the Sisters
passages.text: Sirens can be handled with relative ease. The older ones take a bit more work.

passages.title: Silencing the Sisters
passages.text: By quieting their deadly song, you have saved countless lives.

passages.title: The Master Key
passages.text:
None of the keys you found were the right fit! We're going to need another plan...

I've heard that Overseer Morrison has a master key that can open any lock in the compound. It's dangerous, but I need you to get that key for me!

You'll find her running the mining operation inside the cave. Once you get the key, make sure you rescue any vulpera captives that you find.

Once you've rescued my friends, meet me back here and release me. Good luck!

passages.title: The Master Key
passages.text: You keep your end of the bargain, and I'll keep mine.

passages.title: The Master Key
passages.text:
Sure am glad to see you again, <name>. A reliable rescuer has been hard to come by.

I'll pay you as promised, I but won't be sticking around for long!

passages.title: The Ruins Fought Back
passages.text:
Something set off a trap in the cave, and then the ruins themselves came tae life. I expect that most of our lads still in that cave aren't in fightin' form.

Could ye clear out some of the livin' ruins tae help them escape?

passages.title: The Ruins Fought Back
passages.text: I've fought off spirits afore, but ne'er the actual ruins themselves.

passages.title: Local Flavor
passages.text:
I'm STARVING.

Not actually starving, like when I first got here, but you know... Emotionally starving.

Haven't had any luck with the oysters lately, and seaweed soup really upsets my guts. If I eat any more of that stuff, I think the other castaways might actually feed me to the sharks.

How about them tidelurkers? They look pretty juicy. Bet you could steam those up real nice.

Can you get me some? I'm not much of a hunter. But I'll share it with you!

passages.title: Local Flavor
passages.text: <Sam's stomach growls audibly.>

passages.title: Local Flavor
passages.text:
Oh, you're a lifesaver!

Hang on just a sec, I'll cook these up in no time!

passages.title: Salvaging a Disaster
passages.text:
Birch and I are helping out the expedition with field studies. I'm not much of a fighter, but I can't make another mistake, they might demote me!

Could you recover some of the relics we packed up in boxes around the cave?

passages.title: Salvaging a Disaster
passages.text: Did you find enough relics?

passages.title: Salvaging a Disaster
passages.text: I can't wait to see what sort of power I can squeeze out of these.

passages.title: I'm a Druid, Not a Priest
passages.text:
The remains of previous trespassers also arose when we set off the main trap.

Cranklefuse here has been demanding that I help them, and while I can't say I'm too familiar with turning the undead, I believe I have found a solution.

I've modified my staff to remove their curse. Take it and see if you can't help them.

passages.title: I'm a Druid, Not a Priest
passages.text: Have you tried out that staff yet?

passages.title: I'm a Druid, Not a Priest
passages.text: Another victory for druid magic! This staff is much more effective than any of Cranklefuse's gadgets.

passages.title: A Marine Out of Water
passages.text:
A giant one of those stone creatures killed quite a few marines while we were trying to evacuate the cave. It didn't chase us too far, but ignoring it outright is too big of a risk.

It needs to fall!

passages.title: A Marine Out of Water
passages.text: I heard the falling of stone echo through the cave from here. Nice work.

passages.title: Dress to Impress
passages.text:
Freehold used to be open to anyone, but now it seems the Irontide Raiders have declared themselves the owners. They're locking the place down and turning away anyone who isn't part of the crew.

Fortunately, they're also hiring.

Put this on. Don't think about where it came from.

We'll pose as new recruits, get in, gather some information, and be back in Boralus in time for supper! Cyrus may be salty, but he's a decent cook.

passages.title: Dress to Impress
passages.text: Don't worry, Venrik's a good man. I trust him with my life.

passages.title: Quill or Be Quilled
passages.text:
Oh, hello there. Sorry, we don't get many mainlanders in these parts.

This plot was my husband Sam's farm. He used to tend to the onion fields every day before the curse befell Glenbrook and took him with it.

With my husband gone, this farm is all I have left, and these quillrats are making sure I don't get even that.

I'd hate to bother a perfect stranger, but could you help quell this infestation?

passages.title: Quill or Be Quilled
passages.text: These quillrats are truly a menace!

passages.title: Quill or Be Quilled
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>.

Maybe in reviving these fields I can bring a bit of Sam's goodness back to this accursed land.

passages.title: Backup While I Pack Up
passages.text:
I came in here tae try an' reclaim as many relics as possible. Sneakin' in was easy, but I'm worried about things noticin' me while I pack up. 

Mind watching me back while I get the relics stored in a safe place in my bag?

passages.title: Backup While I Pack Up
passages.text: Everything worth our attention should be stored in my bag, many thanks.

passages.title: Crabby Crew Stew
passages.text:
Shouldn't you be in the mines? Look, I won't tell Morrison if you won't. I wouldn't want to be stuck in those mines, either. 

We could use a hand out here, though. The crew is getting crabby. We've been eating nothing but slop and the occasional rat for weeks. 

I hear one of the deckhands makes a marvelous crab stew. Can I count on you to secure the meat?

passages.title: Crabby Crew Stew
passages.text: It'll be nice to eat something other than rat for a change.

passages.title: Crabby Crew Stew
passages.text: You've done good, <name>. We'll be eatin' like kings tonight!

passages.title: Gang Bustin'
passages.text:
It's difficult to run a tight ship when you're so far from home. The crew has a tendency to get restless when they've been landlocked for too long.

I've heard reports of deckhands sneakin' around and stealin' supplies. If the crew thinks they can steal from our employer on my watch, they've got another thing comin'!

I need someone to crack down on these shady deals and send a message to the crew.

Thievin' won't be tolerated!

passages.title: Gang Bustin'
passages.text: We murder mutineers 'round here.

passages.title: Gang Bustin'
passages.text: Glad I can count on you to keep things from gettin' out of hand.

passages.title: Sharks in the Water
passages.text:
Recently a large gam of sharks has moved into the shallower water in the harbor. I have dealt with minor illnesses before that were caused by creatures carrying foreign contaminants to shore.

Perhaps the sharks have brought something in from the deeper waters? Cull some of the sharks that have wandered too close to the pier. I shall read the tides for any changes.

passages.title: Sharks in the Water
passages.text: Unfortunate... the tides still speak the same.

passages.title: The Thrill of Exploration
passages.text:
Name's Acadia, Acadia Chistlestone!

I represent the interests of the Explorers' League at this site. Where there's dirt to be turned, we're happy to do the digging!

<Acadia's smile falters.>

These Dark Iron, though, they're keen on delving deeper and faster than I'm comfortable with. Since you're a strong, capable member of the Alliance, do you think you could ah... lead by example?

Go on, there's a fresh fossil here that could use some attention.

passages.title: The Thrill of Exploration
passages.text: Acadia tells me you're in charge, now. We'll see about that.

passages.title: The Thrill of Exploration
passages.text:
We both know ye didn't really want all that dirt under yer nails.

Yer welcome.

passages.title: Spiritual Restoration
passages.text:
Dis is a sacred place to Bwonsamdi, but now it is little more than a ruin. Even de spirits are unable to escape de passage of time and have faded away, leaving only their drained husks behind.

We will return dem to life.

Here, I have been collecting de souls from my hunt into dis charm. Use it on de drained spirits, and we will bring dis place back to what it once was.

passages.title: Spiritual Restoration
passages.text: You finished with de spirits yet?

passages.title: Spiritual Restoration
passages.text:
De spirits watch over Zo'bal again!

Now, about our deal...

passages.title: Morgrum's Extended Survey
passages.text:
I've looked over the readings my little boxes gave an' I think I know where to look next. The Ashes of Xibala are practically mine.

Ye'll want to meet me in the middle of the ruins, under that big ol' leerin' skull on the mountainside, to continue my survey.

Readin' these contraptions is hard work, an' I don't think we'll be alone up there.

Think ye can watch me back?

passages.title: Morgrum's Extended Survey
passages.text:
That no good dirty ash-thievin'--!!

We're goin' after her, <name>.

passages.title: Who Seeks the Seekers?
passages.text:
Let me tell you, Zandalar is filled to the brim with ancient secrets. It's quite fascinating.

We heard tales of a region, to the southeast, where ships were losing their way. Some even vanished!

Raku, along with a team of particularly curious Seekers, has been exploring a cove near there for some time. Shipwrecks and mysteries, what isn't to like?

We should have heard back by now. We tortollans may not be fast, but we are reliable.

Will you check on them, and make sure they are well?

passages.title: Who Seeks the Seekers?
passages.text: We must thank him for his concern. We thank you for your arrival.

passages.title: Tiny Treasures
passages.text:
My adults are in the field doing some research. So I stay here, patiently waiting, as they told me to do.

These monsters came and took my special treasures! They took my best friend in the whole world, my slug, Spitzy!

They took them all. They ran far. I do not move fast...

Could you please get them back, and find my family?

passages.title: Tiny Treasures
passages.text: My hatchling... if they laid a finger on him...

passages.title: Tiny Treasures
passages.text:
Koba's favorite things! I do hope he stayed put. He is filled with such haste.

Thank you, <race>, my boy and I will be reunited soon.

Also, Spitzy asks that you take this little sluglet with you on all your adventures.

passages.title: Caged Wisdom
passages.text:
Oh, hello, friend. 

It seems there is more here than for what we prepared. 

We sought. We found. We studied... and then we were taken. There are naga here. We did not expect this.

There is a nasty fellow in this cave. If you could get the key from him, it would help us greatly.

No need to fret, we'll wait here.

passages.title: Caged Wisdom
passages.text: Were we asking too much?

passages.title: Caged Wisdom
passages.text: We best get moving. I do not believe we can wait for the naga to move on, this time.

passages.title: Lost Chelonians
passages.text:
Tidemistress Nazesh has been channeling on a rock they found in one of the pools above. She has been trying for days. They grow desperate.

The rest of my team was taken and locked up in cages. They want secrets from us that we do not know.

When they realize we tortollan cannot be coerced, I expect the naga will do something most dire.

Release the Seekers. We will thwart the naga plans together.

passages.title: Lost Chelonians
passages.text: As long as my friends are safe, I can continue without worry. Many thanks, <class>.

passages.title: Scrollhunters
passages.text:
When they captured us, they took everything we had - including our wonderful scrolls!

Those naga witches are building storms. They try to hide what they do here, and seek power for their queen. 

We see past their madness, they are driven for a purpose.

Retrieve our work from the Nazeshi Tempest-Wielders, else they may use them for nefarious gains.

passages.title: Scrollhunters
passages.text: I really need to invest in some more scroll cases...

passages.title: Scrollhunters
passages.text:
Looks like everything is here, and with little damage done! Very impressive!

What do we have in here? Let's see...

passages.title: Aged to Perfection
passages.text:
Greetings, young one. I am Roko. I trade in specialty goods and exotic wares.

<Roko pulls a small wooden cask from beneath his shell.>

This bourbon is one hundred years old. I know, because I bought it one hundred years ago.

A man in Freehold is prepared to trade me a rare scroll for this, but alas I am barred from entering. It seems this town is not so "free" anymore.

If you can get in, perhaps you could make the trade on my behalf? I would be in your debt.

passages.title: Aged to Perfection
passages.text:
Are you with the Irontide?

I've already paid you people! Leave me alone!

passages.title: Aged to Perfection
passages.text:
Oh! The bourbon from that turtle fellow!

So... he's not coming himself? And I take it you're no Irontide loyalist.

Very well, hand it over.

passages.title: Clear-Cutting
passages.text:
We've managed to hold this hill, but the wicker creatures have moved in to surround us. 

We're not going to be able to move into the town if we don't get them off our flanks. This is where you come in, <class>.

See if you can clear out some of their numbers in the lumber fields. That way, when we move in, we only need to worry about one front.

passages.title: Clear-Cutting
passages.text:
Excellent. 

It was starting to feel a bit claustrophobic on this hill.

passages.title: Enemy Within
passages.text:
I won't sugarcoat it, kid. It's a madhouse here.

The leadership has fallen, selling their own souls as well as the souls of the workers to some darker forces.

I will not give in.

Overseer Bates surrendered the guard in his hunger for power. Show him that he is a fool.

passages.title: Enemy Within
passages.text: After the guard fell, it was easy to get to everybody else.

passages.title: Enemy Within
passages.text: Bates gave everything he had for greater power. Shame it had to go that way.

passages.title: The Deadliest Catch
passages.text:
Oi! No time to waste!

Seems Deepwarden had one more thing up his sleeve... and it's the catch of the day!

This'll be a hunt for the ages, and I won't let ya miss out.

Okri will fly you out to the wall. Get ready!

passages.title: The Deadliest Catch
passages.text: I've never seen a monster with such dark energy. We can't let it get through!

passages.title: The Deadliest Catch
passages.text:
My inadequacy to rule lead to Deepwarden's near takeover of not only the fishing operation here, but the village as a whole.

I can no longer allow myself to sit quietly and allow people like him to walk over me to do as they please! I've learned that, thanks to you.

passages.title: Thunder's Fall
passages.text:
Warlord Kao commands de mogu from dis warship. It is time to put an end to dis incursion.

I should be able to hold off any stragglers dat may come to Kao's aid, but I can only maintain dis barrier for so long.

Be careful. Kao was one of de Thunder King's top generals. He will not fall without a fight.

passages.title: Thunder's Fall
passages.text: Without Kao at their head, de mogu will fall easily.

passages.title: Thunder's Fall
passages.text: De king is in danger!

passages.title: The Prophet's Ploy
passages.text:
King Rastakhan's life is in grave danger. Zul is far more powerful than he appears.

We do not have much time. You have to warn de king before Zul can act.

Habutu and Zolani can take you dere. Now go!

passages.title: The Prophet's Ploy
passages.text: We are betrayed.

passages.title: Hunting Zardrax
passages.text:
<name>, maybe you be helpin' me wit' sometin'.

Talanji said dat Shadow Hunter Da'jul and her retainer, Kal'dran, ran off ta hunt down a lich named Zardrax.

They be goin' off ta a place called Burial Mound. I be worried dey be in over dere heads.

Can ya check ta see if dey be needin' help? We can't be losin' any of our allies in dis place.

passages.title: Hunting Zardrax
passages.text: About time... someone... showed up...! Ya gotta get... this lich... away from us!

passages.title: Push Them Back!
passages.text:
The faithless are laying siege to our home. 

This isn't the first time they've attacked, nor will it be the last, but we must protect the temple!

Do whatever you can to disrupt their siege and push them back.

passages.title: Push Them Back!
passages.text: The faithless will never stop their siege, but your efforts have bought us time.

passages.title: Building Our Arsenal
passages.text:
Our fight against the faithless is an uphill battle we're bound to lose. We are outnumbered and out armed. 

What few weapons we have aren't enough to outfit the entire temple. 

With a few more spears and daggers, we might stand a chance fighting them off until our loa can be returned to us.

passages.title: Building Our Arsenal
passages.text: We need weapons, <name>.

passages.title: Building Our Arsenal
passages.text: You've brought enough to put a weapon in the hands of everyone willing and able to fight.

passages.title: A Powerful Prisoner
passages.text:
It appears the Faithless broke through our defenses while I was away. 

They must be after Vorrik's key. It's the only reason they would have taken him alive. 

Please, <name>. You must secure our leader's safe return.

passages.title: A Powerful Prisoner
passages.text: I owe you my life, <name>.

passages.title: Skycaller Slaughter
passages.text:
Some among the faithless are gifted with the ability to command the storm. They call themselves skycallers, and they use their magic to summon great spires that turn the earth into sand.

Skycallers are the only ones capable of summoning these spires. If you kill the skycallers, you also kill the sethrak's ability to expand their warcamps.

passages.title: Skycaller Slaughter
passages.text: Without their skycallers, the faithless' incursion will falter.

passages.title: A Desecrated Temple
passages.text:
Da spirits of da faithful flock ta me temple. Ya see dem out dere, yes? 

Dey come ta enter da Other Side an' join me realm. However, spirits who've turned their backs upon Bwonsamdi, dey too have come to me temple grounds. Dey praise one called "G'huun," and spread their blood magic desecration across da Necropolis.

Dis ends now!

Go out dere and remove da desecrations dat be infesting me temple.

passages.title: A Desecrated Temple
passages.text: Ya done good, mon. Da Necropolis already startin' ta feel more like home again.

passages.title: Aid the Wounded
passages.text:
<This Zandalari appears to be barely holding on.

There is a broken dart lying on the ground next to him. He appears to have dropped this bottle before he collapsed.

You grab the vial. Could it be some kind of antidote?>

passages.title: Aid the Wounded
passages.text: Thanks, stranger. Dat was too close.

passages.title: Rescue the Chronicler
passages.text:
Just ahead, Chronicler Jabari is being held in a cage, waiting to become a sacrifice.

One by one, I see dem taken away, I hear de screams. Blood drained to feed blood magic, and what was left... was food for a beast.

He is de only one left, and I don't have de strength to save him yet.

Get Jabari out of dere, so we can return to Princess Talanji.

passages.title: Rescue the Chronicler
passages.text: Well, dat was terrifying. Just a few more pieces, and we can be forever away from dis place.

passages.title: Just One Thing
passages.text:
You are just in time! Chance be high dat my blood was de next to spill.

It is my fault we stopped here. Our team wanted to head back.

Crawgs are de trouble, you see. De sanguinous birth of dese young be corrupted by cruel training. They are quite impressionable and dey will follow with just a little enticement.

Capture the attention of one of de little squirmy ones nearby. We will see if my theory is correct.

passages.title: Off With Her Head
passages.text:
Warmother Nagla is driving her forces with a brutality and strength we did not expect. 

Blood trolls desecrate all dey touch, and are preparing to wreak havoc on all dat remain. 

As dey say, "cut off de head, and de beast will be dead". 

I will have her head as a trophy to show dat our brothers were avenged!

passages.title: Off With Her Head
passages.text: Does she still live?

passages.title: Off With Her Head
passages.text:
<Satao spits on the ground.>

De world is better without dat monster in it.

passages.title: Earn Their Trust
passages.text:
If de young one can be taught to trust, dere is a chance for dis species.

Dey may have been born of bad blood, but is dat what makes dem monsters? If you can build his confidence, a mighty ally he could one day be.

A little care could be de thing, and don't forget food! I think some blood trolls may be extra tasty.

passages.title: Earn Their Trust
passages.text: He is sated now! Well done!

passages.title: Crawg Free Zone
passages.text:
Crawgs dat have been battle trained are already set in their ways.

Cleansing dem from de camp may be de only way to give de young ones a chance.

passages.title: Crawg Free Zone
passages.text: Their suffering is over now.

passages.title: Bad Juju
passages.text:
Look, between you and me, dere is no way we will drag my friend outta here without what got us into dis mess.

We saw three orbs in dis camp. Dey are filled with de power of blood magic and are used in dirty rituals. 

Blood is drained from "volunteers" to corrupt de tadpoles of Krag'wa into vicious crawgs.

If dis is a possible fate for children of loa, we must end it. 

Take dis vial and bleed de orbs dry. De chronicler will need to do research.

passages.title: Bad Juju
passages.text:
Ugh! Even I feel de corruption. I am sure Jabari will be able to find de secrets locked away in here. 

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: It Seems You've Made a Friend
passages.text:
Dis young one has bonded with you. 

Bring him to Krag'wa. 

See if dere is anything to be done to heal him of de corruption.

passages.title: It Seems You've Made a Friend
passages.text:
This young one is no longer one of them, but he can never be one of us. Take care of him!

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Roughnecks
passages.text:
NEW JOB OPPORTUNITIES!

Do you seek danger? Beasts in great quantities? Perilous adventure?
Do you also prefer the rugged outdoors to the dainty frilly froo-froo estate life?

Well, you might be cutout to be a ROUGHNECK, suppliers of all gryphon mounts in Kul Tiras.

Inquire at the Roughneck Camp in Westwind Weald about this exciting new opportunity.

Applicants must NOT be afraid of heights, feathers, and/or death.

passages.title: The Roughnecks
passages.text: Here for the job are ye? Well buckle up house cat, it gets rough from here on out.

passages.title: Hold Still
passages.text:
If you want to be a Roughneck, you're going to have to pass a few... trials. Every one of us has done 'em, so I don't want to hear any whining.

Take these clippers and get me some goat fur. You have to clip 'em while they're alive, because thems the rules. Oh, and cover your bits when you do it, they like to kick.

passages.title: Hold Still
passages.text: Got the fur?

passages.title: Hold Still
passages.text: You actually did it! Tell me, how did they like it? Any of 'em give you the horns? Hahaha!

passages.title: Raise a Glass!
passages.text:
Pleased to meet you. Name's Venrik. I been scrapin' out a living here in Freehold for years.

Flynn used to be a regular back when he... well I shouldn't say too much. A man's past is his own.

I'll help the two of you out, but first I demand that you let me give you a proper Freehold welcome: A drink!

passages.title: Raise a Glass!
passages.text: What'sa matter? Cat got yer tongue?

passages.title: Raise a Glass!
passages.text: Ah, nothing like sharing a drink with an old friend... and a new one!

passages.title: Recruiting Efforts
passages.text:
The captain of the Irontide Raiders, Harlan Sweete, has it in his tiny head that he's in charge of Freehold now. 

He's been forcing the smaller crews to pledge their loyalty, and littering the whole town with his damn recruiting posters.

Do me a favor and take down any of them posters you find. Just don't let them catch ya doin' it, or it's a long walk off a short plank.

passages.title: Recruiting Efforts
passages.text: Makes me sick seein' those damn posters all over this town.

passages.title: Recruiting Efforts
passages.text: Hah! That oughtta slow 'em down, or at least piss 'em off.

passages.title: Rodrigo's Roost
passages.text:
We should check in with Cyrus and Taelia before we get in too deep.

<Flynn pens a note on a scrap of parchment and tucks it into a small courier bag.>

This is all of the evidence we've gathered so far linking the Ashvane Trading Company to the weapons and pirates here in Freehold.

Take it to Rodrigo, on the rooftop just behind this tavern. He raises parrots that make great messengers. Some are even big enough to ride!

Rodrigo's a few planks short of a poop deck, but he's trustworthy!

passages.title: Rodrigo's Roost
passages.text: Talk to Rodrigo and send that evidence off to Taelia.

passages.title: Rodrigo's Roost
passages.text: Alright, now that the boss is updated, let's get back to work.

passages.title: Flew the Coop
passages.text:
Yes, yes, you can ride the pretties. They like it! They're good pretties. They like helping!

Do you like helping, too? Maybe you can help me!

Some of the loud men came here and threatened me. They don't scare me! But they made the pretties fly away.

If you see any of my pretties out there, please feed this to them!

It's my special treat. I know it will make them come home.

passages.title: Flew the Coop
passages.text: Did you find any pretties? Oh, they must be so hungry out there.

passages.title: Flew the Coop
passages.text: You did it! So many pretties came back!

passages.title: Rodrigo's Revenge
passages.text:
The loud men are mean, but you seem nice!

Want to have fun fun?

The pretties love my special biscuits, but it makes them full full. Then they have to... go. You know?

Let's prank the mean men! Fly fly on the pretties and make them go.

passages.title: Rodrigo's Revenge
passages.text: Go! Go! Go!

passages.title: Rodrigo's Revenge
passages.text: That'll teach 'em!

passages.title: Fairwind's "Friends"
passages.text:
Someone must have recognized Flynn and ratted him out! A bunch of Irontide thugs dragged him off to the Ring of Booty for a "special audience" with Captain Harlan Sweete.

Flynn doesn't like to talk about this, but he used to captain his own crew. With Harlan as his First Mate.

The two had a falling out after a messy job and Flynn lost all taste for freebooting. Just disappeared one day.

Harlan took the nastiest of the crew and formed the Irontide Raiders.

In other words; it's personal.

passages.title: Fairwind's "Friends"
passages.text: I'm so sorry, <name>. I came as fast as I could!

passages.title: Defenders of Daelin's Gate
passages.text:
Daelin's Gate has protected the southern channel for decades. If it falls, the pirate fleet can sail straight into Tiragarde Sound!

The marines at Vigil Hill will need our help. Let's go!

passages.title: Defenders of Daelin's Gate
passages.text: You've come to help? Oh, thank the tides.

passages.title: Trixie Business
passages.text:
Usually this is the part where I hand you the scroll and send you on your way.

Sadly, friend, these are unusual times.

How's a man expected to run an honest business dealing in highly illegal goods when the Irontide Raiders are shaking down good folk like myself?

I'm prepared to offer you a handsome sum - and the scroll for our shelled associate - if you rid me of the damnable woman who collects these tributes.

You'll surely find her at Harlan's table at the bar, getting drunk on MY gold!

passages.title: Trixie Business
passages.text: Stay your hand, friend! If you harm me, you'll never find the scroll!

passages.title: Trixie Business
passages.text: You actually did it? Color me impressed.

passages.title: Helping Henry
passages.text:
The Roughnecks told me to clear the rocks in the forest. I didn't know they meant THIS!

You look tough, you have to help me! I'll get killed if I get anywhere near that thing. I'm also super allergic to bees...

passages.title: Helping Henry
passages.text: That thing sure hates bees...

passages.title: Helping Henry
passages.text: Thanks so much! I'm off to my next task!

passages.title: Roughneck Riders
passages.text:
Rulf sent word that you're needed for another job.

A rich house cat is willing to pay top dollar for a male aerie alpha and there is only one that fits the bill, Greatfeather. I gotta head back to camp to help train a particularly wild female, so this is going to be a solo job.

Find Greatfeather and hit him with the Tether Shot. From there, you'll have to wing it.

passages.title: Roughneck Riders
passages.text: I can't believe you did it, kid! I knew you'd be Roughneck material!

passages.title: Big Boss
passages.text:
With a performance like that, it's clear you're one of the top dogs here. Boss Tak will want to see you. He's up north checking on one of our camps in Waning Glacier. Head up that way and give him a hand.

Oh, and I don't recommend looking him straight in the eye... or at his feet... or really anywhere near him. Best bet, close your eyes when you're talkin' to him.

passages.title: Big Boss
passages.text: You the new kid? Frankly, it doesn't matter. I got a problem and you're going to help me with it.

passages.title: Frozen
passages.text:
Hurp me pwease! Oh, it's woo. I can sill muv my wips a wittle.

Fin me sumfin to 'et me owdda 'ere.

passages.title: Frozen
passages.text: Woo 'ave somefin?

passages.title: Frozen
passages.text: Whank woo!

passages.title: Hunting Zul
passages.text:
Zul is pulling all of his forces back to his stronghold at the Temple of the Prophet.

Rastakhan has sent word that he is marshalling an army in the Zocalo with anyone still loyal that can carry a weapon. Looks like the old king had more loyalists than Zul expected.

That, and he has three of their eldest loa gathered to his side.

Go and lend your strength to their army.

passages.title: Hunting Zul
passages.text: When hunting one who has foreseen de future, it is best to proceed with a measure of caution.

passages.title: Heretics
passages.text: Descend on Zul's fanatics and mogu allies. Hunt them down and slay them all with the fury of a true predator. Show them the true price of their betrayal.

passages.title: Heretics
passages.text: How fares your hunt?

passages.title: Heretics
passages.text: With de sky clear of ballistae fire, Pa'ku can start doing what she loves: dropping those who cross her from a really great height.

passages.title: The Full Prophecy
passages.text:
Dat snake of a prophet, Zul. I never trusted him. Always felt like he was never telling us de whole prophecy.

Enter de Temple of dis "Prophet" and see if he recorded any of his visions.

We must learn of what our prey intends, before our real hunt may begin.

passages.title: The Full Prophecy
passages.text: Zul is not liked enough for his followers to go on blind faith.

passages.title: The Full Prophecy
passages.text: Zul has fallen so low as to wish to raise Dazar himself? Can Zul even be called a Zandalari anymore?

passages.title: City of Gold
passages.text:
Rezan and Rastakhan did not wait for us. Dey are marching up de mountain to Atal'Dazar, de City of Gold.

You, Loti, and I need to catch up quick and give dem some air support. Hop aboard.

passages.title: City of Gold
passages.text: Zul thinks to bar me from MY domain? I will consume his soul.

passages.title: Not Our Purple Elves
passages.text:
Ye know, <name>, these elves might be purple, but they're no' with the Alliance.

Leastwise, they're a lot more aggressive than this ol' Dark Iron is comfortable with.

On the off chance it'll piss off the Horde, ye mind killin' a few of them?

passages.title: Not Our Purple Elves
passages.text: I'm guessin' they weren't friendly. Well, that's a weight off me mind.

passages.title: Grand Theft Telemancy
passages.text:
I'm not opposed to honest competition, <name>.

But teleportin' it right out from under our noses leaves me feelin' dirty.

Go teach that thievin' elf what it means t'steal from the Alliance. If they're fightin' dirty, then so will we.

passages.title: Grand Theft Telemancy
passages.text: Ye get the Breath of Xibala back?

passages.title: Grand Theft Telemancy
passages.text:
I'm a dwarf of me word, <name>.

Here's yer cut. I'll see to it that this here... pot... is delivered to the Alliance with my praise for yer actions.

It's a little underwhelming, isn't it?

passages.title: Warm and Cozy
passages.text:
Heya! Isn't this place a dream? I couldn't be more relaxed. Well, I could be if these annoying cloud jerks would leave me alone. 

Why don't you go punch some in their cloud faces. Oh, and bring back their essences, they help keep my tub warm.

passages.title: Warm and Cozy
passages.text: I need more steam! Hurry, the tub is getting chilly!

passages.title: Warm and Cozy
passages.text: Ooooh, that's nice. Real nice. Hop in if you want, the water is great! Ignore the bubbles.

passages.title: The Forlorn Soul
passages.text:
Where's my ma'da? You seen her?

"I'll be right back," she said. I'm a good girl, I wait. I wait and wait, I'm not sure how long I've been waiting here for.

It's cold and lonely here. Hey... could you help me find ma'da? I swear I won't cause you any trouble.

passages.title: The Forlorn Soul
passages.text:
Keula's ma'da be foolish ta tink she never gonna pass on to da Other Side, but now dey be together an' I be havin' two more souls in me realm.

You done good, mon.

passages.title: Wendies
passages.text:
It's a mystery where these boys were taken, but it ain't much of a mystery who did it. Roughnecks believe an eye for an eye and then some.

Let's put down some of those monstrosities.

passages.title: Wendies
passages.text: This'll help protect my boys down the hill. Well done.

passages.title: Where'd They Go?
passages.text:
My boys are missing. You're going to help me find 'em.

Got it?

passages.title: Where'd They Go?
passages.text: Find anythin'?

passages.title: Where'd They Go?
passages.text: Pity. At least I can tell the rest of the boys they went down fighting.

passages.title: Tattered Note
passages.text:
<The short, hand-written note is scrawled in blood.>

They captured me soon after I was exiled. I was too weak to be a slave and too starved to be food for the beasts.

They were going to kill me, but one called Shath'kar intervened. He said it would be amusing to watch me starve to death among his prisoners.

I have not lived a good life. I deserve nothing. But, to any fellow Zandalari who finds this, I have one request...

Stick a blade in Shath'kar's belly and twist it until the snake is dead!

passages.title: Tattered Note
passages.text: I've heard the other vulpera whisper Shath'kar's name in fear. Thank you for ridding us of him.

passages.title: Boss' Revenge
passages.text:
Revenge has never really been my thing, but whatever is in there killed my crew and I am not going to let it stand.

Everybody fights, nobody quits.

passages.title: Boss' Revenge
passages.text:
To survive out here, we do what we have to. Today that meant avenging members of the pack.

Thank you for your help. If you ever need anything, don't hesitate to call on the Roughnecks.

passages.title: A Lesson in Witch Hunting
passages.text:
While I appreciate the dedication that went into compiling this tome, this thing reads like engineering instructions for a siege engine!

I'll need some time to comb through this information for anything that might be useful to us. I wouldn't mind some assistance, if you have a moment.

For starters, I could use some more light in here...

passages.title: A Lesson in Witch Hunting
passages.text: Did you find it?

passages.title: A Lesson in Witch Hunting
passages.text:
Ah, you found it! Excellent.

<Lucille produces a long sewing needle from the kit>

...You look confused. Let me explain.

passages.title: Leather - Rank 1 Unlock
Incident Reports
passages.text:
No wonder our workers are terrified to go into these woods. Generally the bears and spiders stay out of the way of humans... 

But these are no ordinary beasts!

Father would be furious if productivity came to a halt. Please, cull these beasts so that the ridge can be safe once more!

passages.title: Incident Reports
passages.text: I have never seen beasts so... soulless. It's as if they're under some sort of spell.

passages.title: Time Off Requests
passages.text:
My father is incapable of seeing what's in front of his very nose. He holes himself up in his office, not leaving to go home until late at night...
