Here I am, his only son, trapped out here along with all of his workers. Are they in trouble? Yes! But father will never believe them.

If he won't try to get to the bottom of this attack, I will do it myself!

passages.title: Time Off Requests
passages.text: My son is far too soft-hearted. He needs to harden up if he's going to run this business one day!

passages.title: Give a Dam
passages.text:
These loggers are destroying the forest, and harming the wildlife!

Beavers need this wood for their dams, but have had to resort to scrounging for scraps.

It's not safe for them anymore! Please, help me chase them back to the safety of the water.

passages.title: Give a Dam
passages.text: Hooray! Now the beavers will be safe from the lumberjacks and the spiders!

passages.title: Pest Prevention
passages.text:
These woods have never been so densely littered with spider eggs.

If these are recent... they must also be corrupted! We cannot allow them to hatch into more of these aggressive spiders.

While you are in the woods, destroy those eggs. Any more spiders could lead to an uncontainable infestation!

passages.title: Pest Prevention
passages.text: I will admit to not being the biggest fan of spiders. Fewer spiders sounds pretty good to me.

passages.title: Pest Prevention
passages.text:
Thanks for that.

I uh... I think you got some spider egg goop on your cloak.

passages.title: Leather - Rank 2 Unlock
Leather - Rank 3 Unlock
Bones - Rank 1 Unlock
Bones - Rank 2 Unlock
Bones - Rank 3 Unlock
Scales - Rank 1 Unlock
Scales - Rank 2 Unlock
Scales - Rank 3 Unlock
Saurolisk Tails
passages.text:
Among the upper echelons of Kul Tiran society, there is one cuisine that escapes all but the most determined of chefs. Nobles will pay exorbitant amounts to have just a taste of this delicacy, spiced and cooked to one's delight.

I speak, of course, of the saurolisk tail.

I must discover the finest method of cooking this sought after comestible! Boiled? Braised? Poached? Perhaps steamed or blanched is the most appropriate method!

I will, of course, need a few tails to test.

passages.title: Maximizing Resources
passages.text:
Let me tell you a thing about my employees.

They're always blowing things out of proportion! I give them a good job with a steady wage and what do they do? They try to make excuses as to why they can't work!

They say the trees have come alive. Trees? Walking and fighting? If you're going to lie, at least make it more believable.

If they want to convince me, I'm going to need cold hard proof.

passages.title: Maximizing Resources
passages.text: I give them an honest job with good pay. This is the thanks I get?

passages.title: Maximizing Resources
passages.text:
<Algerson examines the skull.>

Now this... this is something! Why are my workers running, they should be harvesting!

We could make a killing with these!

passages.title: Witch of the Woods
passages.text:
A... a witch?!

I uh... I would love to help you, truly I would but... I must report to my father.

Why don't you go stop the witch yourself? For a brave adventurer like you, a witch should be no problem.

I'm sure my father would reward you greatly!

passages.title: Witch of the Woods
passages.text: My son told me about the witch, <name>. I've come up here to take care of her! If you want something done right, you need to do it yourself.

passages.title: Witch of the Woods
passages.text:
<Maynard studies the locket.>

That ungrateful woman!

passages.title: Required Webinar
passages.text:
I'm not surprised some of the workers stayed in the woods, even amidst the beasts. While he won't admit it, some of father's workers are extremely dedicated.

And now they're trapped by the spiders!

Perhaps they have information about what is going on here. Free them from their webbings and see what they know!

passages.title: Required Webinar
passages.text: A witch?! This is all because of a witch?!

passages.title: Surprise Backup
passages.text:
<You find a torn Horde missive on the ground...

It appears that a group of forsaken, led by a man named Chadwick Paxton, were sent here to investigate Nazmir.

You're unable to discern why they were sent here, but there are coordinates that indicate where they were going.

You may be able to find the scouts at the coordinates and enlist their aid in fighting the blood trolls.>

passages.title: Surprise Backup
passages.text: Oh. Hello there, fancy meeting you out here in a swamp. Yes, I'm Chadwick Paxton, or approximately half of him. Care to help?

passages.title: Didn't Stop to Think if They Should
passages.text:
The sethrak seem to believe there's something in Nazmir that can unlock the destructive power of this gem.

We don't have that, but we have the next best thing. An insane warlock who is willing to experiment with magic.

Speak with Ingrid and have her begin the process to unlock the true power of this gem.

passages.title: Didn't Stop to Think if They Should
passages.text: Just be careful around Ingrid, she can get a little carried away.

passages.title: Didn't Stop to Think if They Should
passages.text: That gem appears ready to do some damage. Let's just... point it elsewhere, for now.

passages.title: Tal'gurub
passages.text:
My prophet is a loyal servant, but he has his own ideas of how things must be.

I am sending him to Tal'gurub to deal with a mess of his own making. One of his pupils, a witch doctor by de name of Vol'jamba, has taken de Gurubashi enclave as his own and has ousted my guards.

Meet Zul at Tal'gurub and ensure dis nuisance is dealt with. Do not let him get... distracted.

passages.title: Tal'gurub
passages.text:
Ah, yes, my new escort!

You are here to enforce de king's will. I would hate for ol' Rastakhan to become disappointed with you, especially after your performance in Stormwind.

passages.title: Needs a Little Body
passages.text:
I am here primarily to deal with my wayward student. His followers, however, I will leave to you.

I have seen a possible future dat is... concerning. Rivers running red with poison, dead filling de streets. And dese... "Jambani" asserting themselves as de new rulers of Zuldazar. Dis cannot come to pass.

Fortunately for you, I know how to avoid dat fate. I think you will find their cauldrons are missing one key ingredient.

<He stares at you.>

Something to give it a little body, perhaps?

passages.title: Needs a Little Body
passages.text: We would not want dem to forego a crucial ingredient, would we?

passages.title: Needs a Little Body
passages.text: Fight fire with fire, dey say. Or in dis case, poison with idiots who chew de ankles of their betters.

passages.title: The Urn of Voices
passages.text:
Vol'jamba does possess de Sight, and so even now he is taking precautions against us.

Regrettably his vision is incomplete. You will help me prepare for his demise and deal with his followers simultaneously. De tool you will use is called de Urn of Voices.

Take it and venture into Tal'gurub. Slay his followers, destroy their golems and masks. Their spirits, once released, will fill de urn.

Oh, and try not to die while holding it. De Urn of Voices is not discerning.

passages.title: The Urn of Voices
passages.text: Vol'jamba will pay for his transgressions.

passages.title: The Urn of Voices
passages.text: All according to plan. Do not worry for dem... dis was always their fate.

passages.title: Fuel for the Voodoo
passages.text:
Dere be no time! Dey be draining our spirits... using us... dark voodoo...

<Loa Priestess Izita's spirit grows dim, and her voice is soft and distant.>

Da totems... burn dem...

Den we be free...!

passages.title: Fuel for the Voodoo
passages.text: <The brazier burns brightly.>

passages.title: Fuel for the Voodoo
passages.text: <As the fire chews away at the totems, Gurubashi spirits rise from the ashes.>

passages.title: Arrogance of Vol'jamba
passages.text:
Vol'jamba thinks his Sight has surpassed mine. I warned against such arrogance many years ago, but we see how well he listened.

<Zul chuckles.>

No doubt he will attempt to deter us as we encroach upon his sanctum. Listen if you like, but remember dat he is desperate to save himself. His truth is distorted by fear.

Destroy his masks and we will walk unharmed through dis passage.

passages.title: Arrogance of Vol'jamba
passages.text: His arrogance blinds him. He will soon learn de error of his ways.

passages.title: Arrogance of Vol'jamba
passages.text: As I said, his truth is distorted by fear.

passages.title: Zul's Ethical Dilemma
passages.text:
Hm.

De Gurubashi have earned a reputation for betrayal and weakness. Their activities in Zul'Gurub will be a stain on our records for generations to come.

On de other hand...

De Zandalari are above de use of slaves. We are strong, capable. De very existence of mindslaves in dis great city is insulting.

Dere is a chant dat will free their minds. Use it near de mindslaves to free dem. 

Or you can simply kill dem. It makes no difference to me.

passages.title: Zul's Ethical Dilemma
passages.text: Weakness or pride... I think often on de Zandalari's priorities.

passages.title: Zuvembi Brew
passages.text:
Zuvembi brew is arguably a witch doctor's most insidious concoction.

Driven by de cauldron master's strength of mind, Zuvembi brew takes de will of those who breathe its fumes. It makes dem compliant, easily manipulated.

It is low magic, relying upon ancient cantrips and recipes known only to witch doctors of a certain skill. If we want to eradicate dis brew, we must slay those dat brew it.

Find de Zuvembi brewer lurking here and see dat dis knowledge is erased.

passages.title: Zuvembi Brew
passages.text: Dis primitive magic cannot be allowed to proliferate.

passages.title: Zuvembi Brew
passages.text: Good. Dis thread has been severed.

passages.title: Enforcing Fate
passages.text:
Vol'jamba is busy consolidating his power. His Sight has shown him dat he will fight, and perhaps even dat he will die, and so he looks to all his tools to save himself.

I will need you to be my hands, as he will come as soon as I show myself. You will undo all de preparations he has made for dis day.

Do as I say and we will both find ourselves enjoying de king's favor.

passages.title: Enforcing Fate
passages.text: His vision is imperfect. We will use dis to end him.

passages.title: Enforcing Fate
passages.text:
<Zul rubs his hands together.>

Good. Now we are ready to draw him out.

passages.title: Carentan's Payment
passages.text:
Well done, my friend. Well done, indeed.

You see that dusty crate in the corner of the room? You'll find it contains the ancient scroll and a generous purse of gold, as we agreed.

Please, take your reward. You've certainly earned it.

passages.title: A Bad Deal
passages.text:
<Carentan escaped!

Roko, the tortollan merchant who set up this deal in the first place, will want to know what happened.

When you last spoke, Roko said he would be heading to Boralus.>

passages.title: A Bad Deal
passages.text:
Hmm. A scam, was it? You have my apologies for putting you in harm's way.

This man should be delivered to justice. He may be in hiding now, but I am very, very patient.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Frostfire Ridge!
passages.text:
All able-bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Farseer Drek'Thar in Frostfire Ridge.

The destruction of the Dark Portal has stopped the Iron Horde invasion of Azeroth, but now we must to take the fight to them.

With Farseer Drek'Thar's aid, we will be able to establish a strategic position in Draenor to fight against our enemies.

For the Horde!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Frostfire Ridge!
passages.text:
I am glad to see you are well after Tanaan Jungle.

We have much to do.

passages.title: A Rocky Start
passages.text:
<As you thumb through the book, the pages are unusually thick and embedded on their surface are runic-shaped jewels. Samuel Colton notices you looking and approaches.>

Ah, now that's a treasure I've had for many years. Beautiful, isn't it? No clue what it says, but I've always reveled at the thought of something being transcribed in jewels.

Come to think of it, I wonder if Zooey Inksprocket would be able to decipher it. Say, <name>, would you mind taking it over to her and see if she can translate it?

passages.title: A Rocky Start
passages.text:
Y-yes? Can I help you?

<You hand the book over to Zooey and ask for it to be translated. As she turns each page, wondrous expressions cross the scribe's face.>

Oh my, I've only ever heard of such books in existence but have never seen one up close. Do you know what this is?

It's ancient earthen. And this book must be centuries old!

Of course I'll help translate it! Only... well... my ancient earthen isn't so great. I'll need some reference materials.

passages.title: The Shrine of the Sea
passages.text:
This next shrine is right here, in Tiragarde Sound.

According to the journal, the earthen mentions creating bluish hued jewels. I wonder if that's anything like the kyanite we have here.

Go and see if the shrine still stands. Hopefully it's still in a usable state.

I'll continue to study the journal for more information.

passages.title: The Shrine of the Sea
passages.text:
<As you peer at the shrine in front of you, you can't help but revel at the construction of it.

Seamlessly constructed with azure jewels placed just so in a radial pattern, collapsing towards a single point.

A single, empty point.>

passages.title: Tol Dagor: Jewel of the Tides
passages.text:
<An absence you assume to be a mistake, you quickly survey the area for something that might fit there yet you find nothing.

However, there appears to be a drunk here shouting at the shrine. Perhaps he might know the whereabouts of the shrine's missing piece.>

passages.title: Tol Dagor: Jewel of the Tides
passages.text: <Perhaps finding the missing centerpiece will give you a clue into the shrine's operation?>

passages.title: Tol Dagor: Jewel of the Tides
passages.text:
<As you affix the gem back into the center of the shrine, a strange pulse emanates from it.

The shrine, now whole again, begins to hum with energy.>

passages.title: High Prospects
passages.text:
<Checking your notes, you find that the earthen had extracted the gems from some earth elementals to the south.

Looking at your map, you wonder if he was referring to the now ruins of a once ancient settlement that has become littered with constructs and undead.

Perhaps investigating there will yield some clues as to where to find these jewels.>

passages.title: High Prospects
passages.text: <All of the cracked jewels will definitely need to be replaced.>

passages.title: High Prospects
passages.text:
<You begin to remove all the cracked gems from the shrine and carefully start placing the new ones in.

Placing the final one, a pulse radiates from the shrine, as the light in the area seems to draw into it.

That strange, similar glow now emanating from the shrine leads you to believe it is once again active.>

passages.title: Cracking the Surface
passages.text:
<Checking your notes, the earthen mentions having prospected the jewels from a nearby mountain to the northwest.

Perhaps you can prospect the earth in that area to find more of those jewels and repair the shrine.>

passages.title: Cracking the Surface
passages.text: <The placement of the jewels on this shrine appear to be placed in a rather intricate fashion.>

passages.title: Cracking the Surface
passages.text:
<Using your tools, you carefully shape the jewels and affix them into the empty slots on the shrine.

Using the remainder, you are able to fill in the cracks of the center jewel, giving it a flush surface.

As you place the final jewel, a similar pulse of energy radiates from the shrine as the light in the area seems to draw into it. A strange glow now emanating from the shrine leads you to believe it is once again active.>

passages.title: Atal'Dazar: Not All That Glitters...
passages.text:
<You reference your notes on the shrine and discover that these jewels came from a "golden sanctuary".

Given your location, that can only mean Atal'Dazar. Perhaps you could find a replacement from that ancient city.>

passages.title: Atal'Dazar: Not All That Glitters...
passages.text: <When you're done replacing the central gem, you think you might still be able to sell the old one.>

passages.title: Atal'Dazar: Not All That Glitters...
passages.text:
<Returning to the shrine, you begin to pluck the old gem from its holding place. As you do, the gem cracks again and shatters in your hands.

Apparently these gems are much more fragile than you originally thought.

Very carefully, you replace the gem you obtained into the slot.

Once affixed, the familiar pulse radiates once more from the shrine and the glow emanating from it confirms its restoration.>

passages.title: Out With the Old
passages.text:
<It's clear though that time has had its way with these gems, some eroded and chipped in places.

Repairing this shrine may be as simple as replacing the old gems with newer ones of the same type and cut.>

passages.title: Out With the Old
passages.text: <Interesting that the cut should be so similar, you wonder how the design has persisted all these years.>

passages.title: Out With the Old
passages.text:
<Replacing each gem, they fit perfectly into the slots confirming your suspicions of their similarities.

As you place the final gem, a peaceful glow now emanating from the shrine leads you to believe it is once again active.>

passages.title: The Missing Chapter
passages.text:
<Samuel puts down the journal and looks back up at you.>

While trying to figure out where the shrines reside, I came across an entry that mentioned him exploring an area that sounds very similar to Dustwallow Marsh.

He mentions hiding something of great importance there.

It's a long shot, given when this earthen roamed Azeroth, but perhaps if you were to retrace his final steps you may find something.

I'll mark the location on your map.

passages.title: The Missing Chapter
passages.text: Who knows what you may find out there. Hopefully something...

passages.title: The Missing Chapter
passages.text:
What did you find?

<You hand the final chapter and its transcription over to Samuel. As he reads through it, he reaches the page with the design for the lens and his eyes go wide.>

You've found it, <name>! We can construct a lens now and use it with the shrines.

Although, the reagents for this design are quite... rare. But nevertheless you've done it!

It was an honor to work with you on this, <name>.

passages.title: A Rocky Start
passages.text:
<As you thumb through the book, you see odd-looking runes carved out of jewels embedded in the stone pages. Seshuli notices you looking and approaches you.>

Ah, dat's been a treasure of mine for many years. Beautiful, isn't it? No clue what it says, but I've always reveled at de thought of something being written in jewels.

Come to think of it, I wonder if Grazzul would know what it says. <name>, would you mind taking it over to him and see if he can translate it?

passages.title: A Rocky Start
passages.text:
What do you need?

<You hand the book over to Grazzul and ask for it to be translated. As he turns each page, wondrous expressions cross the scribe's face.>

I've only heard of such books in existence but I've never seen one before. Do you know what dis is?

Dis is ancient earthen. And dis book is centuries old!

Of course I'll help to translate it, only... well... my ancient earthen isn't so great. I'll need some things to do dis.

passages.title: The Shrine of Nature
passages.text:
Another shrine resides right here in Zuldazar.

According to de journal, de earthen talks about creating green hued jewels dere. I wonder if dat's anything like de viridium we find in de ore we mine.

Go and see if de shrine still stands. Hopefully, we can still make use of it.

I'll continue to study de journal for more information.

passages.title: The Shrine of Nature
passages.text: <As you observe the shrine, it's quite clear that the central jewel is badly broken and in need of replacement.>

passages.title: The Missing Chapter
passages.text:
<Seshuli puts down the journal and looks back up at you.>

While trying to figure out where de shrines reside, I came across an entry dat mentioned him exploring an area dat sounds very similar to Dustwallow Marsh.

It could be a long shot, given when dis earthen roamed Azeroth, but maybe if you retrace his final steps, you may find something.

I'll mark his last location for you on your map.

passages.title: The Missing Chapter
passages.text: Who knows what you'll find out dere. Hopefully something...

passages.title: The Missing Chapter
passages.text:
Did you find anything?

<You hand the final chapter and its transcription over to Seshuli. As she reads through it, she reaches the page with the design for the lens and her eyes go wide.>

You found it, <name>! We can make a lens now and use it with de shrines.

Although, de reagents for dis design are quite... rare. Still, you've done it!

It was an honor to work with you on dis, <name>.

passages.title: Trust of a King
passages.text:
Well, now dat you are settled in, you had best go speak with my father. You can find him up upon de throne, his advisors close at hand, pouring poison in his ear, no doubt.

De lift behind you can take you to de Golden Throne above us.

passages.title: Trust of a King
passages.text: Very prompt. Now, I have need of your hands.

passages.title: Locally Sourced Eggs
passages.text:
There is nothing in the world greater than food made from the best, freshest ingredients!

My good friend I am on a hunt. A hunt for the perfect eggs! I have heard tale of eel eggs. A delicate texture, a slight undersea saltiness... such a unique flavor profile! I must have them!

The eels here lay their eggs on the land before returning to the sea. Please, gather these eggs for me so that I may create only the most elegant of omelets!

passages.title: The Missing Key
passages.text:
Korthek has grown spiteful and arrogant over the years, but I realize now that he has grown mad as well.

Mythrax will kill all of us if he is released.

For too long, I've held out hope that I could convince Korthek peacefully to abandon his heresy. I was wrong.

All of Zandalar is at risk while Korthek and his allies hold even one key to Mythrax's prison.

Meet me outside his fortress in the north. We will confront my old friend "Emperor" Korthek and end this together.

passages.title: The Missing Key
passages.text: We are surrounded by Faithless out here, <name>. We must move quickly.

passages.title: False Prophecies
passages.text:
Now dat dis nuisance is out of de way, I can return my focus to de city. Zuldazar has languished while I was away.

You should return to Rastakhan. Let de king know dat his will has been carried out and dat dis false prophet is no more.

You might think to share Vol'jamba's prophecy with him, if you feel it worth his notice. I cannot say it will change anything at all.

passages.title: False Prophecies
passages.text: Perhaps Zul will remember his place going forward.

passages.title: Allies in Anarchy
passages.text:
Even after all these years, I can feel the ancient power of Sethraliss in this place. My loa endures.

Our task ahead is great and I will need a clear, focused mind to accomplish it. Allow me a few moments to meditate here, like I did in ages past.

In the meantime, you should help the vulpera stir up trouble however you can. They seem to know you, and a large enough disturbance will distract the Faithless from our mission.

Meet me back here when you're done and we'll proceed together.

passages.title: Allies in Anarchy
passages.text:
<name>?! We gotta stop meeting in places like this.

Actually, let's ALWAYS meet in places like this!

You up for killing some Faithless?

passages.title: Ready to Riot
passages.text:
Do you remember how we met, adventurer? You were trapped in a Faithless cage, just like the ones in the crater below.

Together, we slaughtered Faithless and earned your freedom in blood.

The vulpera trapped in shackles below can do the same. They just need to be given the chance.

Steal Faithless weapons and give them to the vulpera slaves below. They'll rise up and help you fight the Faithless.

We're going to start a revolt right under their arrogant noses.

passages.title: Ready to Riot
passages.text: Look at my people fighting! The Faithless don't stand a chance!

passages.title: Make Them Fear Us
passages.text:
I carry this banner into every battle because I want the Faithless to fear it. To fear my people.

If I die in the battlefield, surrounded by Faithless, I will die happy.

On that day, I will not need a burial or prayers. But I will need someone to pick up my banner and carry it into the next battle.

If you are of the same mind, plant these banners into the corpse of every Faithless you slay. Let the survivors know who's coming for them.

passages.title: Make Them Fear Us
passages.text: And that's just the start! Now the Faithless know who's coming for 'em.

passages.title: The Little Ones
passages.text:
Just when I thought the Faithless couldn't get any worse, I find out that they're keeping vulpera children trapped down in that crater!

The other vulpera we rescued told me that a big sethrak, Appraiser Versik, is inspecting them on the central platform to determine what he can sell them for.

Selling vulpera kids! Oooh, those Faithless make me so angry!

Please, adventurer. I'm no fighter. I can't rescue those kids. But if you bring them up here to me, I promise I'll get them out of here safely.

passages.title: The Little Ones
passages.text:
Thank you, thank you, thank you!

These children have already experienced more hate and pain than anyone ever should. I'll make sure they feel love in equal measure.

passages.title: Light Up the Gulch
passages.text:
Don't mistake my caution for hesitance, adventurer. I will defend the vulpera with my dying breath... I'd just prefer to avoid taking that breath today.

While Nisha rushes to the front line, I work behind them to ensure our success.

Meet me at the Faithless beast pens if you'd like to help.

Oh, and take this torch. You'll be going through their marketplace, where they auction off slaves.

Starting a few well-placed and metaphorically poignant fires along your route will make things easier for all of us.

passages.title: Light Up the Gulch
passages.text: The fires are spreading quickly. Let's hurry, while the Faithless are distracted.

passages.title: Unleash the Beasts
passages.text:
The Faithless are arrogant hoarders, capturing people and beasts that can never be truly tamed. All to fuel their endless lust for war.

I've even seen their slavers dragging blood trolls and other dark monsters from the swamps of Nazmir.

I heard terrible noises coming out of a cave while I was scouting the feeding pits up ahead.

Whatever monsters they are hiding in there, find a way to free them and let them exact revenge on the Faithless.

passages.title: Unleash the Beasts
passages.text: Crawgs are violent, filthy things... Yet another reason to avoid Nazmir.

passages.title: Dressed for Battle
passages.text:
Kiro's the leader of my caravan. He's always been far too passive.

I warned him we needed to make a preemptive strike against the sethrak, but he insisted that we keep our heads down and continue to quietly do business.

Look where that got us.

Our caravan was completely unprepared for their attack. 

Now I'm ready to fight for what's ours, but I'm not exactly dressed for battle.

Help me scavenge some suitable equipment here among our enemies. We will use their own tools against them.

passages.title: Dressed for Battle
passages.text: Killing an enemy with their own sword is an even bigger insult, no?

passages.title: Dressed for Battle
passages.text: Now we are ready for a real challenge!

passages.title: Plans for Attack
passages.text:
Before we were attacked, I had a plan to take the fight to the sethrak. 

It was devised with flawless intel. I know, because I gathered the information myself. 

I surveyed their entire compound and created a map based on my findings. 

My plan relies on that map, but it's now in the hands of Fangcaller Sraka, the brute who's leading this assault on my home.

Help me kill her so I can take back what's mine!

passages.title: Plans for Attack
passages.text: My plan for attack is both detailed and dangerous.

passages.title: Plans for Attack
passages.text: These plans will be our key to taking the fight to the sethrak.

passages.title: I Spy a Spire
passages.text:
It is good you have come. Dol'watha be under attack by these snake-men.

Soon as they arrived they started pulling these weird spire-things out de ground. I seen a bunch of snake-mons with feathers in their caps getting zapped by them, but they not be dying.

If it not be bad for them, that means it's good for them. And that be bad for us.

Destroy those spires. Hopefully whatever boon they be getting will go away and they will be easier to kill.

passages.title: I Spy a Spire
passages.text: Not so much static in de air now. That's good. Means we did something right.

passages.title: The Sethrak Incursion
passages.text:
Dol'watha be a small village. Got a few farms, some beasts, and a decent view of a swamp.

Loa know we not be ready for this...

De snake-men popped out of de ground by de hundreds. Slaughtered my beasts, my family, my friends. One minute de earth rumbling, de next we be running for our lives.

I heard about snake-men from de deserts of Vol'dun but I never believed I would see them in my life...

Help us fight back. Kill as many of them as you can. Dol'watha won't be beaten that easily!

passages.title: The Sethrak Incursion
passages.text: Won't bring back de ones we lost, but it show them that not even little Dol'watha be going down without a fight.

passages.title: Skycaller Soltok
passages.text:
As if snake-men with swords not be bad enough, they brought a powerful skycaller along.

 I hear skycallers can tempt great storms into being. They be to blame for de spires and lightning flying everywhere.

There be one who wear a bigger feather than most, likely de leader. Calls herself Soltok or something equally hissy.

Don't care. Kill her.

passages.title: Skycaller Soltok
passages.text: Good, very good...

passages.title: Lil' Tika
passages.text:
<The tiny armored raptor scratches pitifully at the cage's wooden bars. As you approach, the miniscule reptile wiggles frantically and issues a piercing screech for help!

Perhaps you can open the cage and let it free.>

passages.title: Lil' Tika
passages.text: My poor beasts...

passages.title: Lil' Tika
passages.text:
Why is she covered in blood?

On secon' thought, nevermind.

Praise all deh loa, at least dis little one made it!

passages.title: Turn to Drust
passages.text:
There are blood scribe masters all over the place who'll teach you what you need to know. The first master I'd recommend seeking out is Kronah.

She's a bit... eccentric to say the least. One of the few tortollan who've experienced a thing or two.

She's the one who taught me the blood contract I know how to invoke!

She likes to hang out at the Smuggler's Cove on the western coast of Drustvar. Oh, and could you say hi for me when you see her?!

passages.title: Turn to Drust
passages.text:
<Kronah eyes you up and down warily.>

Say ahhh for me, would you young one?

<Kronah peers inside your mouth.>

Nice teeth you have there. Would fetch a fine price. But that's not really what you're here for, is it?

No, you're one of those who think they can handle the trials of the blood contracts, aren't you? Very well.

passages.title: House Stormsong
passages.text:
I have little information to offer, I'm afraid. I've scarcely left Brennadam as of late.

What they said is true. Our militia now enter town only to collect rations rather than guard traders or keep the quilboar at bay.

They say they are under orders, but those orders would only come from my brothers at the Shrine. We take oaths to serve our people... it simply does not add up.

Brother Addington is nearby at Mariner's Strand. Perhaps he knows more than I.

passages.title: House Stormsong
passages.text: What has become of our people...

passages.title: Haywire Harvesters
passages.text:
See the golems down there? Farmers use their sharp claws to reap the harvest, but these are cutting timber... 

Why would they need them here when they have so many laborers on hand?

I think the militia is using them to intimidate their own people!

See if you can get ahold of an intact mainspring from one. I've helped repair a few back in Boralus. I should be able to figure out who is messing with their innards.

passages.title: Haywire Harvesters
passages.text: Any luck? The mainsprings are usually brittle and easily damaged.

passages.title: Haywire Harvesters
passages.text: Perfect! Here, let me take a closer look.

passages.title: Unnecessary Duress
passages.text:
Lord Stormsong has never taken kindly to dissent, but this is madness. These laborers are being worked to death!

Addington was a good man. We cannot stand for such cruelty.

Take this vial and apply it to the laborers. It contains blessed seawater that will rejuvenate their strength.

Avoid engaging what troops you can. They are merely following orders. More death will only worsen matters.

passages.title: Unnecessary Duress
passages.text: There is much work to be done, but not at the cost of our own people's lives.

passages.title: Proclamation Investigation
passages.text:
My lord seldom leaves our holdings along the northern coast, and visitors are expressly forbidden. For most, tidesages like myself are their only connection to the house proper.

Lord Stormsong usually delivers orders through proclamations posted throughout the valley. None have reached Brennadam, but if there are any posted here we may be able to find some answers.

passages.title: Proclamation Investigation
passages.text: Lord Stormsong is a bit aloof, but his power over the tides is beyond measure.

passages.title: Proclamation Investigation
passages.text:
Independence?!

This is too far. A shattered Kul Tiras will never stand!

passages.title: An Offering of Eggs
passages.text:
Our work isn't only to capture and tame gryphons, it's also to preserve them.

Rescue any eggs remaining in nearby abandoned nests. Set them in one of the new nests we've built for the displaced gryphons. I am sure one of the gryphon females will adopt them.

passages.title: An Offering of Eggs
passages.text: You find a safe nest.

passages.title: An Offering of Eggs
passages.text: The eggs fit nicely into the new nest.

passages.title: Trouble at Greystone Keep
passages.text:
A friend of mine, a fellow military courier, had a job at Greystone Keep. The fort lies just outside of Boralus, so I would've expected him to be back by now.

I have another job lined up, so could you go check out the fort for me? I'm probably just being paranoid.

passages.title: Trouble at Greystone Keep
passages.text: A courier? I think we lost him in the coup.

passages.title: A Lesson on Trust
passages.text:
The men in the fort were once under my command, and so, they are now my responsibility. Each of them should have a badge we use for identifying individuals under certain circumstances. I would ask you to bring back a number of these as proof of thinning their ranks.

These men are no longer soldiers of Boralus, and as such, no longer deserve to carry the Proudmoore anchor.

passages.title: A Lesson on Trust
passages.text: Did you bring me those badges?

passages.title: A Lesson on Trust
passages.text: A grim task, but one that needed to be done.

passages.title: Getting Paid
passages.text:
Now that we got our mitts good and bloody, I think it's time we head back to camp.

I'll run ahead, so you can finish up whatever business you got. Just remember to meet Tagart for your pay.

passages.title: Getting Paid
passages.text: Here's your pay. You seem suited for the Roughneck life. Come back sometime if you need work.

passages.title: Free Bird
passages.text:
Skyheart invited me here to teach some of his city boys how to train the local sea hawks. Some of my students went and sided with the mutiny force. Seems these soft marines have forgotten what the consequence is for betraying a Drustvar soldier.

Worse yet, they've locked up quite a few of the younger birds we were training. I've got my hands full with these hawks, so if you could free a few of the young'uns while you're in the fort, I'd appreciate it.

passages.title: Free Bird
passages.text: Any luck? Hopefully they didn't nip you too much.

passages.title: Free Bird
passages.text: My birds deserve better partners than men who betray their own country.

passages.title: A Risky Ploy
passages.text:
Things are worse than we thought. These people are about to tear Brennadam apart!

We'll never get a chance to talk to Brother Pike in this mess.

I have an idea, but if it doesn't work, well... I hope you have your running boots on.

Trust me?

passages.title: A Risky Ploy
passages.text: We haven't had visitors here in quite some time.

passages.title: A Risky Ploy
passages.text: Ah, Brother Alen sent you. Good.

passages.title: WANTED: Thundersnout
passages.text:
Thundersnout is the largest of the boars in the valley. She is wreaking havoc on the nearby farms and their crops.

Mayor Roz of Brennadam has issued a bounty for proof of her demise.

Thundersnout's location is near Briarback kraul, so be on the look out for quilboar!

passages.title: WANTED: Thundersnout
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: WANTED: Thundersnout
passages.text: The death of the matriarch means the next generation of boars will be delayed. Nice work.

passages.title: Fond Farewells
passages.text:
Dis is where we part ways, <name>.

I'm going to take de name Akunda, and start a new life here. 

Rakera saved my life, and I'm going to make sure to live a life dat was worth saving. 

If you find yourself back in de city, could you deliver dis note for me? I trust you not to open it, though I doubt you could read my scrawls anyway.

passages.title: Fond Farewells
passages.text: What is dis?

passages.title: Fond Farewells
passages.text:
<B'wizati reads the note and wipes a tear from her eye.>

He may choose to forget, but I choose to remember, no matter what pain it brings me. 

At least he is safe. Loa watch over him.

passages.title: Patching Up the Rear
passages.text:
Most of my men were injured when we were escaping the fort, those that weren't were injured holding this position.

<Tallis hands you a stack of stained cloth.>

All of our better supplies are behind those walls, so we've been forced to make do with what we have. Everything that's not being worn on a soldier's person as we speak has been shredded for use as bandages. We don't have the staffing to take care of everyone.

Head out and replace the worst of our injured's bandages.

passages.title: Patching Up the Rear
passages.text: My gratitude, that should help alleviate some of the soldiers' pain.

passages.title: Patching Up the Rear
passages.text: My gratitude, that should help alleviate some of the soldiers' pain.

passages.title: Targeting a Turncoat
passages.text:
The instigator of this mutiny is a man named Fernn. He has always shown discontent with House Proudmoore and his position here. But to betray the men he works with? That seems beyond even my expectations of him.

Take him out, and show this mutiny the mistake of crossing truly loyal marines.

passages.title: Targeting a Turncoat
passages.text: Good work. That should be enough help to get my men back in that fort and manning it again.

passages.title: Protect the Nests
passages.text:
Now that Tagart is done with your hazing... I mean... trials, you can start helping us with some of the work around here.

Some of the nearby gryphon nests have been overrun with saurolisk. I fear that the gryphons will make new roosts elsewhere if we don't clear them out.

Head up the road towards the waterfall and take out those saurolisks. Report to Shawn when you're done. He's posted as a lookout there.

passages.title: Protect the Nests
passages.text: Get bit?

passages.title: Protect the Nests
passages.text: Bloody saurolisks. Good riddance.

passages.title: Air Raid
passages.text:
Those pirates have air support! They're torching our farms and splitting our attention away from the front lines. 

Take 'em outta the sky!

passages.title: Air Raid
passages.text: Damn fine work! I'll recommend you for a medal of valor!

passages.title: Cease Fire!
passages.text:
The enemy has turned our forward cannons around on us.

Scuttle that equipment to stop the bombardments!

passages.title: Cease Fire!
passages.text: The thunder of cannons can strike fear or inspire hope, depending on which end you're standing.

passages.title: You Have Their Orders
passages.text:
The Horde is an army, make no mistake. And armies need orders.

Someone must be giving orders here. They know the plan, and I want to know the plan too.

Look for the people who seem to be in charge and see if you can uncover any intelligence so we know what to do next.

passages.title: You Have Their Orders
passages.text: You find those orders?

passages.title: You Have Their Orders
passages.text: The Banshee Queen is not like the previous Warchiefs.

passages.title: Not "Only Zul"
passages.text:
Our enemies here either follow de name of Zul, or dey want to use him to take Zandalar.

He has the ego to allow either. 

Dey claim only Zul can lead us.

Dissuade dem.

passages.title: Not "Only Zul"
passages.text: Did ya leave any breathing?

passages.title: Not "Only Zul"
passages.text: Well done, <name>. I wish that put a bigger dent in the threat they pose.

passages.title: Cat on a Hot Copper Roof
passages.text:
My parents said we have to go, but I won't leave Scratchy behind!

She's so gentle and precious and pure and kind and soft and cuddly! She must be so scared up there on the balcony!

Please help her!

passages.title: Cat on a Hot Copper Roof
passages.text: We can't leave Scratchy here!

passages.title: Cat on a Hot Copper Roof
passages.text:
Yay!

Isn't she the sweetest most perfectest kitty cat ever?!

passages.title: Send the Signal!
passages.text:
My crew is not on board with de word of Zul. We saw too much of who he really is. 

Far out in de harbor, Zul's traitors have joined with de mogu to try to take my ships! If we lose de fleet and de harbor, we lose de city!

We must let Zuldazar know we stand strong. We take back de ships. We drive de villains out. 

You must light de towers with loa-blessed flame. Dey will always see dat de Bay of Kings belongs to Zandalar!

passages.title: Send the Signal!
passages.text: Ya got here just in time!

passages.title: Your Next Move
Your Next Move
passages.text:
We have some thoughts on the best way to win over the Zandalari.

The princess is heading to Nazmir to take the fight to the blood trolls. Her voice carries much weight with the council and her father.

General Jakra'zet detests the Horde. Removing his voice from the Zanchuli Council will greatly improve our chances here.

We should also keep working on winning over the King here in Zuldazar. This city is vast and has many secrets.

passages.title: Nesingwary's Trek
passages.text:
De greatest hunter from your lands, de dwarf Nesingwary, has come to participate in de Great Hunt.

If you are enough of a hunter to join him, den travel to de Nesingwary Trek along de northeastern region of Zuldazar.

passages.title: Nesingwary's Trek
passages.text: Welcome to tha hunt.

passages.title: Wreckage of the Cataclysm
passages.text:
In recent years one of the greatest Zandalari loa temples mysteriously fell into the sea. It is a topic of some debate what caused this, and what treasures might have been lost in the catastrophe.

My cousin Rokor was in charge of the salvaging efforts. Within the temple were many great items of knowledge and power. I am sure he will have need of the services of someone like yourself with strong arms and working knees.

passages.title: Won't Leaf Him to Die
passages.text:
I may have done some wicked things in my past, but I won't leave dis guard to die.

Zulajin has taken a nasty bite outta Zaluto... and has also infected him with some weird voodoo.

But don't worry, because today is our lucky day. I have a plan to cure him. Dere are sweetleaf bushes nearby!

De leaves of dis bush are known for their healing properties. You get me some, and I will be able to save dis Zaluto.

It's de only chance we have!

passages.title: Won't Leaf Him to Die
passages.text: Did you get de sweetleaf?

passages.title: Won't Leaf Him to Die
passages.text: You have de sweetleaf! Looks like you gathered just enough, too!

passages.title: Key to the Brig
passages.text:
You can tell a lot about a troll by what they do when they learn who Zul truly is. 

That Garza is a mutinous, foul-tusked, ship stealin' traitor. She is the kind of zealot dat will follow de heretic into the maw of an Old God. 

I am more de type to rip out her tusks and beat her with dem. 

I'd settle for ya taking her key and getting our wavemaster and crew free!

passages.title: Key to the Brig
passages.text: Did ya relieve her of de key?

passages.title: Key to the Brig
passages.text: Garza was lost long ago. It sounds that Maset is as feisty as ever. We will get out to de ships!

passages.title: No Problem Tar Can't Solve
passages.text:
I'm not going to lie... I did wicked things in my youth and I've been living with de shame ever since.

But Zaluto is going to die without my healing, and we're all going to die if dat dino isn't taken care of.

Dere is a lot of tar in dis area. I need it to cure Zaluto of whatever is infecting him here.

Get me dat tar, and I'll be able to save Zaluto from dis fate.

passages.title: No Problem Tar Can't Solve
passages.text: We will need plenty of dat sticky tar!

passages.title: No Problem Tar Can't Solve
passages.text: Good job! Dis is exactly de kind of stuff we need!

passages.title: On The Run
passages.text:
<The guard captain appears to be fatally wounded.>

We were... transporting prisoners when de ambush came... a giant devilsaur... tore through everything.

Most of de prisoners escaped in de carnage... dese are hardened criminals. Dey cannot be allowed to roam free!

I swore a blood oath dat I would deliver dem to Vol'dun... I am probably going to die here, but I will not die an oathbreaker!

Find de escaped criminals and exile dem to Vol'dun.

passages.title: On The Run
passages.text: Have you found de escaped prisoners?

passages.title: On The Run
passages.text: You have my thanks... if I die here, at least I can face my ancestors with my oath fulfilled.

passages.title: Don't Go into the Light
passages.text:
Okay, dis is de moment of truth! We will see if my voodoo can cure Zaluto.

I should have been honest with you... dere is a chance dis won't work. Voodoo isn't a science, you know.

I need you to hold Zaluto down, because dis here is going to hurt. A lot.

passages.title: Don't Go into the Light
passages.text: We can't leave Zaluto to die.

passages.title: Don't Go into the Light
passages.text: Zaluto is free from death's door, but he's still weak. We have more to do.

passages.title: Bad To The Bone
passages.text:
I will not leave here without killing Zulajin, or else it will just go after de next caravan dat comes through.

I have a plan, but we must work together to pull it off.

Dere are skeletal raptors roaming in de area. I do not know what voodoo brought dem here, but we need dem gone.

We are going to need as much space as possible for my plan to kill Zulajin.

passages.title: Bad To The Bone
passages.text: Did you take care of de skeletal raptors yet?

passages.title: Bad To The Bone
passages.text: You have done well taking care of de bone raptors. Even if dis road is only for criminals, dey at least deserve to make it to Vol'dun alive.

passages.title: Recovering Ancient Fire
passages.text:
Zaluto has a crazy plan to kill Zulajin. Never thought a guard could come up with something so clever.

Dere is ancient mojo throughout dis place... who knows what it used to be? But I sense something I can use.

De statues sinking in de tar pits have de fire mojo still burning in dem. We will need it to kill Zulajin.

Take my fetish and use it to absorb what's left of de fire in dese statues.

Just don't get dat fire too close to de tar!

passages.title: Recovering Ancient Fire
passages.text: Do you have de fire yet?

passages.title: Recovering Ancient Fire
passages.text: De fetish is brimming with de fire magic! Good, because you will need it for what comes next.

passages.title: Destroy the Weapon
passages.text:
I did scout de next island. Rezan's Claw has a mighty weapon on board.

I don't know what it is, but dey are confident in its ability to break de defenses of our home.

Get to de ship. Destroy that weapon before dey can use it on Zuldazar!

passages.title: Destroy the Weapon
passages.text: Dat was unexpected.

passages.title: Lost, Not Forgotten
passages.text:
I know not what madness has overtaken my people, but we must stop it together.

Take this bell. It calls the souls of the recently deceased to it for later release. We Stormsong do not bury our dead in the earth. The tides claim all.

If they will not answer to reason, then we must give them eternal peace. Fallen or not, they are Stormsong.

passages.title: Lost, Not Forgotten
passages.text: It is a grim task, but it is our burden to bear.

passages.title: Lost, Not Forgotten
passages.text: It is done. We will release them somewhere a bit more peaceful.

passages.title: Bound and Oppressed
passages.text:
We had our orders: ships, and lots of 'em. I led my boys as best I could.

Everything changed when the tidesages showed up. We figured they was just checkin' on our progress, but the hood-wearin' bastards turned on us!

These anchors bind us here, forcin' us to work to death. No one deserves a fate like that. You gotta free my boys!

passages.title: Bound and Oppressed
passages.text: I owe you one, stranger!

passages.title: The Rising Tide
passages.text:
This mainspring wasn't altered by an engineer. These runes on the surface can only have come from a tidesage.

Their aquatic magic is unmistakable. I'd bet whoever did this is also responsible for Addington's death.

Whoever they are, they're likely still nearby. Keep an eye out... they won't be hard to find.

passages.title: The Rising Tide
passages.text: This does not bode well.

passages.title: Aggressive Mating Strategy
passages.text:
Aggression is good. I agree with Jangalar that Ben'jin needs to be a lot less passive to succeed and I can prove science is the way to do it by making an injection for him.

Alchemy tells us that, for this type of beast, aggression comes from a substance in their bile sacs. The local razorwings are invasive and, as such, have more than enough aggression for our purposes. 

Harvest some of their bile sacs and I'll make a treatment that will have our big boy ready to go again in no time.

passages.title: Aggressive Mating Strategy
passages.text: Did you get all of the bile sacs I need yet? Science is not supposed to be safe...

passages.title: Aggressive Mating Strategy
passages.text:
Just what I needed! Boy do they smell! 

With these bile sacs, I can make enough Aggression Formula for a creature as big as a brutosaur.

passages.title: Implements of Ill Intent
passages.text:
<It looks like some careless witch made a poor attempt to hide this grimoire from sight. No good could come of leaving the possessions of the coven for a hapless villager to find.

It would probably be a good idea to destroy any trappings of the coven that you find in Arom's Stand.>

passages.title: Implements of Ill Intent
passages.text:
That was good thinking to dispose of the witches' trappings. 

I don't want to know what would happen if an innocent villager toyed around with such things!

passages.title: Hidden Dealings
passages.text:
<Among her possessions, the witch carried a crudely drawn map of Arom's Stand. 

A symbol marks what looks like the entrance to a cellar beneath one of the buildings.

If this location is important to the coven, it might be worth scouting out.>

passages.title: Hidden Dealings
passages.text: What's this? A map?

passages.title: Hidden Dealings
passages.text:
You found their leader? Excellent work, <class>!

The people of Arom's Stand will be safe, now that you've so thoroughly dismantled the coven's machinations here.

passages.title: A New Order
passages.text:
Before we leave, I have one more task to ask of you.

While you were busy recruiting our inquisitors and driving the coven away from Arom's Stand, I took the liberty of placing an order with the local tailor. 

Using some of the sketches within the tome, I had him put together some uniforms reminiscent of those worn by the ancient order.

Since you will be leading our inquisitors, I think it's only fitting that you present them with their new regalia.

passages.title: A New Order
passages.text: You should be inducting them, not me!

passages.title: A New Order
passages.text:
There, that was nice and official. 

Now, I think it's time we took the fight back to the Heartsbane. I believe the marshal has a plan.

passages.title: Monstrous Matchmaker
passages.text:
We have a problem, a matter of love, and you've come just in time. 

Two white brutosaurs, de male Ben'jin and de female Maka'fon, are de last of their kind. De rest have passed on. 

Dese two are not in de mood for love. If you can help my new friend Cala and myself, dis may be de only chance to give dem a future. 

Place my voodoo totem close to each one so dat I can feel what dey feel and learn how we can help.

passages.title: Monstrous Matchmaker
passages.text: Place de voodoo totem close to both of de brutosaurs and I will be able to sense what dey feel.

passages.title: Monstrous Matchmaker
passages.text: We need to help Ben'jin to get his mojo back and Maka'fon to be in de mood. Is voodoo or science de better way to go?

passages.title: The Scent for a Brutosaur
passages.text:
Mood is everything for love, and Maka'fon is not in de mood. 

Voodoo incense, specially formulated for brutosaurs by an expert witch doctor like myself, will surely spark de fire of de mother spirit in her heart. 

Certain fragrant rushes work best, and de jungle will provide. 

Zandalari rushes grow near de waters here. Get a good amount for me and I will make an incense bundle big enough to set de mood.

passages.title: The Scent for a Brutosaur
passages.text: Look for de rushes near de life-giving waters dat I might use my voodoo to make incense for de brutosaurs.

passages.title: The Scent for a Brutosaur
passages.text: Well done! I will weave dese rushes into incense bundles and cast my best spells upon dem.

passages.title: Trouble at Fort Daelin
passages.text:
I was sent to Brennadam by my commanding officer to find a tidesage to help us at Fort Daelin to the west. The naga have started another attack on the bastion, and it's larger than any we have seen. 

Lieutenant Bauer is in the middle of helping out civilians at the village near the fort, and she could use any help possible.

passages.title: Trouble at Fort Daelin
passages.text: These fishermen are no pushovers themselves. They should be able to hold their own here with a little help.

passages.title: From the Depths
passages.text:
We must prepare for an attack.

Man the cannons!

Defend the levee at all costs!

passages.title: From the Depths
passages.text: We've done it! The naga are defeated and the levee remains intact!

passages.title: An Illegible Scroll
passages.text:
<Resting within the waterproof container is an illegible scroll of undetermined age and origin. 

Perhaps the tortollans along the coast will be able to decipher what is written upon the parchment?>

passages.title: An Illegible Scroll
passages.text:
What have you found, traveler? Ah, a scroll written in a mysterious language. Quite an interesting find!

<Nola carefully examines the scroll.>

I've never seen characters like these before, but perhaps Kugro has...

passages.title: A Desperate Defense
passages.text:
The soldiers garrisoned here are doing their best to hold out, but they're struggling. Pirates haven't dared attack this gate in years, and never with such a large force.

If you're handy in a fight, Lieutenant Tarenfold will want to meet you. 

He's organizing the militia up ahead.

passages.title: A Desperate Defense
passages.text:
Aha! Reinforcements!

Wait... Where are the rest of you?

passages.title: Size Matters
passages.text:
So the unintended side-effect of Gentle Ben'jin being, shall we say 'fun-sized' is that he is now small enough to get into the cave where the alpha wind serpent is! 

The beast is called Gloomtail and if Ben'jin defeats it, he will feel like this territory is his and will want to fill it with little brutosaurs. So he will seek out a mate. If Maka'fon is receptive, everyone wins! 

Go give him another hit of the formula!

passages.title: Size Matters
passages.text: Size isn't all dat matters. Ben'jin can get to more places if he's small... and fight dere!

passages.title: Size Matters
passages.text:
Dat was incredible! I could hear de snorting and stomping from here. 

Well done, <name>.

passages.title: Against the Tide
passages.text:
De mogu are growin' desperate. Ha! Maybe dey hope to get away from here before de fury of de loa rain down on dem!

De warlord's pet sorcerer set up blockers and dey have taken de tower.

If you can avoid the sting, de lightning rods can have ya feelin' pretty good. One could even say energized. 

Get to Warlord Xiar and relieve him of his life privileges.

Then let our people know we have taken back de Breath of Pa'ku! 

Dis mojo is empowered to ignite de tower with a mighty blast.

passages.title: Against the Tide
passages.text: Not bad, <name>! Our work is nearly complete!

passages.title: By the Book
passages.text:
As you open the book, you stare at a blank page, waiting for something to happen.

Instinctively you flip to the next page only to find it blank as well. Perhaps your trial awaits you further into the book?

passages.title: By the Book
passages.text: I trust you to be careful inside the Bloodshed Compendium. I don't want to find any ripped pages from that weapon you wield.

passages.title: By the Book
passages.text:
You've done well, young one. I recall a gnome not too long ago completing that trial as well.

Her story was quite the read. But between you and me, gnomes smell like porridge.

<Kronah looks off into the distance, lost in thought for a moment.>

But you are now a bearer of the Bloodshed Contract and one step closer to your final prize.

<Kronah quirks a grin at you and goes back about her business.>

passages.title: Lines In the Sand
passages.text:
This was all I had to offer you, young scribe. But your journey is not yet at an end.

If you're up for some traveling, and interested in some of the deadlier blood contracts, you're going to have to travel to Zandalar.

Once there, seek out a sethrak by the name of Veriss in an area known as Vol'dun.

<Kronah grabs an odd-looking jar and opens it. The foulest odor you've ever smelled emanates from it and you reel in disgust.>

Pickled crocolisk eggs are my favorite. Would you like some?

passages.title: Lines In the Sand
passages.text:
Ah! A new initiate! Were you wondering how I knew? Because of the blood on your hands, of course.

<A sly grin crosses over the sethrak's face.>

I am Veriss, the resident keeper of the Zandalar blood contracts.

If you wish to inscribe your name into them, there is something I must ask of you first.

passages.title: Temple of Sethraliss: Booking on a Favor
passages.text:
When the Faithless came to power, we Devoted fled our sacred temple and took shelter here.

However, in the midst of our exodus, many of us were forced to abandon some of our belongings.

I myself left a tome that is used to learn the Oblivion contract. If you wish to proceed with the trials, you must retrieve that book for me, <name>.

I trust you won't disappoint me.

passages.title: Temple of Sethraliss: Booking on a Favor
passages.text: I'll admit, I'm a bit embarrassed to have left it behind. An oversight that I still regret to this day.

passages.title: Temple of Sethraliss: Booking on a Favor
passages.text: I'm relieved you were able to retrieve it. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Brush With Death
passages.text:
<As you open the book, a sudden chill comes over you. You shake the sensation off as you read the verse.>

"A fatal bargain, in blood is struck,
One inks their pledge,
with strokes of luck.
Stay true your lines,
keep still your breath,
Lest you stray too far,
and summon death."

<As you finish reading the incantation, a quill appears next to the book.>

passages.title: Brush With Death
passages.text:
Well done, young blood scribe.

You can now invoke the Oblivion Contract. It lets you summon a creature that, well let's just say, his bite is bigger than his bark.

He likes to prey on creatures that are on the verge of death, yourself included if you're not too careful.

passages.title: The Final Verse
passages.text:
It appears you are finished here, <name>. Thank you again for getting my book back.

But between you and I, this was the easy part. Just wait till you meet the grandmaster.

If you haven't noticed already, you'll need a special quill to invoke those contracts. And he'll be the one who shows you how to craft it.

His name is Miju and he lives out on an island off the southern coast of Zuldazar. Good luck, <name>!

passages.title: The Final Verse
passages.text:
What's this then? Another novice come to learn the ways of blood-scribing?

Very well, for which contract do you need a quill?

<You explain to Miju that you've learned all four contracts and need a quill to invoke all of them.>

ALL FOUR?! Oh my, it's been... let's see here...

<Miju beings mumbling to himself.>

Too long I suppose. But yes. I still know the recipe. Your trial awaits you then.

passages.title: Hope's Blue Light
passages.text:
There is but one step left!

De second tower means the fleet is ours again!

Climb aboard and we will finish dis thing!

passages.title: Hope's Blue Light
passages.text:
You have saved de fleet and protected de Bay of Kings!

Ya did well, <name>! We captains are a wise lot.

passages.title: Follow Your Nose
passages.text:
You there! I could use your help!

The ground isn't safe. The quilboar have established a network of tunnels below us, allowing them to spring up to ambush people who aren't walking carefully.

Luckily for us, Humphrey here has a nose for the Briarback, and can sniff 'em out even when they're underground. Root a few of them out and let's make the farms a little safer to walk through.

There's a particularly large clump of them in the northeastern fields. Good hunting!

passages.title: Follow Your Nose
passages.text: Hah! I bet ol' Humphrey gave them a good spook!

passages.title: Forced Labor
passages.text:
<The laborer struggles to speak through the magic binding him.>

H... help... us...

<He achingly lifts a finger, gesturing towards the nearby anchor.>

Please...

passages.title: Forced Labor
passages.text: <It appears he lacks the energy to respond further.>

passages.title: Forced Labor
passages.text:
At least not all of the tidesages have turned on us.

Not yet.

passages.title: Drustfall
passages.text: I believe I see more carvings at the entrance to that cave over there. Come, we should see what else was left behind.

passages.title: Drustfall
passages.text:
The carvings could have been Drust propaganda stating he lived, but that voice!
<Cleardawn's face becomes grim>
It seems we may have all been mistaken about the ultimate fate of Gorak Tul. I shudder to think what he might be planning now.

passages.title: To Falconhurst!
passages.text:
Our time here was well spent. The guards in Arom's Stand can handle what few Drust forces remain and I suspect the Drust leader and his magic might have some greater part to play here. 

However we must continue on the mission to Falconhurst. The path on the far side of these ruins will take us there.

I will ride ahead and meet you outside of town!

passages.title: To Falconhurst!
passages.text: The town is under siege! No wonder we have not heard from them. We must help them.

passages.title: Making Mysteries
passages.text:
Do you know what people love? The unexplained! Problem is, everything here is explainable. 

So I have a plan to create our own phe-gnome-enon. There are stories that talk about some weird chicken-snake hybrids that can turn you to stone. I've already released the chickens, now we just need the snakes.

The first problem can be solved easily. Just chase down the chickens, and stick one of these robotic tails on them.

passages.title: Making Mysteries
passages.text: How do my petrifyingly scary chickens look?

passages.title: Making Mysteries
passages.text: Stupendous! Now we can start calling our resort tour a "mystery safari"!

passages.title: Clear Victory
passages.text:
<The ghostly captain continues to fight as she speaks, once more locked into the heat of battle, unaware the war has been over for centuries.>

What are you doing standing around? We've ground them down to their final warriors and those damnable runic constructs, but the war isn't over yet!

Colonel Waycrest needs us to hold this line! Kill as many of those Drust as you can and we might see the end of this war, today. Get back out there!

passages.title: Clear Victory
passages.text:
Not bad, marine! We might make a proper soldier out of you yet!

They'll make Colonel Waycrest a Lord for this, I'm sure. Your bravery will be remembered.

passages.title: Atal'Dazar: Yazma the Fallen Priestess
passages.text:
Zul knows dat we cannot let de first king rise from his grave. Dazar would be more than a figure head for Zul's dream troll empire, he would be a force dat could rival de very loa.

But I cannot just let Zul get away. I and mine will follow Zul, but I want you and yours to enter Atal'Dazar. Yazma is trying to buy time and keep de tombs sealed away. You will need to fight your way through to her and you will need some allies to do so. Slay her.

passages.title: Atal'Dazar: Yazma the Fallen Priestess
passages.text: And here I always thought Yazma was just rude. I never expected just how far she had fallen.

passages.title: Atal'Dazar: Yazma the Fallen Priestess
passages.text:
Yazma's betrayal was vile beyond words.

It may take us some time to find our way deeper into Atal'dazar. In de meantime, we have more work to do.

passages.title: To Gloom Hollow
passages.text:
There's only one safe area in Nazmir that this Rokhan and your other Horde friends could be in. Gloom Hollow.

Lucky for you, it's also close to Krag'wa's den. We used Gloom Hollow as a last stop on our pilgrimage.

Make your way to Gloom Hollow along the path I've marked on your map, and tell any tortollans along the way to meet us there.

They'll be interested in seeing the end of this story. We'll make our way there and grab anyone else we find.

passages.title: To Gloom Hollow
passages.text:
Good ta see ya, <name>. Princess Talanji be tellin' me all about Torga and da tortollans. Guess we lucky dat we got sometin' outta dis.

We be here, waitin' on reinforcements from da Horde.

passages.title: Plot Twist
passages.text:
It is time to end Vol'jamba.

I want to make one thing clear. He can still kill you. Your fate, moreso than mine, hangs on your ability to fight dis former student of mine.

He will bring masks, and voodoo, and he will do everything within his power to end you. All we have done is taken away his ability to cheat.

Good luck. For your sake, I hope you do not fail.

passages.title: Plot Twist
passages.text: Let us be rid of dis nuisance.

passages.title: Plot Twist
passages.text: Death is a tool, <name>. Do not forget dat.

passages.title: Back to Brennadam
passages.text:
The naga are mostly cleared out thanks to your help. They'll think twice before attacking again.

Can you return to Brennadam and tell Squire Augustus III to return to his normal station?

passages.title: Back to Brennadam
passages.text: Oh, roger! I'll head back at once!

passages.title: Kaja'mite? Kaja'must!
passages.text:
I been waitin' to talk to the King for a while now, but he not be seein' me! And this pompous lackey not be listenin' either.

We got a problem brewin' in the Village of the Vines, just outside de city. With all the Horde landin' in the Harbor, some goblins got wind of our old kaja'mite quarry. They split outta here like the teeth of Deathwing himself behind 'em.

But that quarry be dangerous. Wicked dangerous. Think you can go to de village an' talk some sense into them goblins?

passages.title: Kaja'mite? Kaja'must!
passages.text: You came just in time pal. There's loads of work to do if there's really kaja'mite here in Zuldazar!

passages.title: Kaja'mite Ore Bust
passages.text:
Kaja'mite! Just saying the name gives my big beautiful ears a buzz. 

These Zandalari were sitting on a huge deposit of it all these years. And they abandoned it just because of a few talking gorillas. By goblin law it's ours for the taking!

Let's see how concentrated a deposit we're talking about. Get a good peek at those vents that are steaming out kaja'mite vapors.

Go into the gorge and plant my scanners on those steam vents. They'll do the rest.

passages.title: Kaja'mite Ore Bust
passages.text:
Thank you chump! I mean chum.

There's enough kaja'mite there to get us started. Too bad about all the talking gorillas in the way.

passages.title: Gorilla Warfare
passages.text:
Your timing is most fortuitous, stranger. I thank you for your assistance.

Things are not peaceful in Gorilla Gorge. The kaja'mite has given us great intelligence and wit. With intelligence has come war. 

My brethren are those who do not wish to fight. Neither the Zandalari trolls nor each other. But for our passivity we have been persecuted.

Please free my comrades. They will be in cages all throughout the gorge and under guard. Make haste!

passages.title: Gorilla Warfare
passages.text: Thank you my friend! I saw the bravery with which you granted freedom to my comrades. We shall speak more anon.

passages.title: King Da'ka
passages.text:
These Zandalari won't go near Gorilla Gorge. All because they're afraid!

It's just a few talking gorillas. And one 'big mon' in particular as the Zandalari call him. 

All we need to do is take out King Da'ka and the villagers will probably throw us a parade! Or at least let us mine that kaja'mite.

Think you can handle one big gorilla, chum?

passages.title: King Da'ka
passages.text: Good. One less mook to deal with. That kaja'mite is as good as ours!

passages.title: The Road to Corlain
passages.text:
Lord and Lady Waycrest lay trapped in Waycrest Manor. Before we can reach them, however, we must brave through the city of Corlain... which is firmly in the grasp of the Heartsbane.

Our first course of action should be to set up a forward outpost. Our scouts have found that the tower at Watchman's Rise is only lightly guarded. I recommend we take the tower from them.

This is now your command, Inquisitor. Say the word, and we ride.

passages.title: The Road to Corlain
passages.text:
Good, you've arrived. 

This tower watches over Corlain and the surrounding lands. Apparently it is of little value to the coven, but to us it would serve as a valuable foothold.

passages.title: Slumber No More
passages.text:
There's something you should look into. You've got the time anyway, those goblins aren't ready yet.

There's a statue nearby. Only, it's not a statue to the trained tortollan eye. It's a deactivated titan keeper!

Noises have been coming from that thing ever since you helped Krag'wa. It must be trying to reactivate itself.

I bet that titan-looking amulet of yours could help restart it. We'd be unstoppable against the blood trolls with a titan keeper's help.

Go see if you can restart this titan!

passages.title: Slumber No More
passages.text: Core detected. Appreciation for retrieval.

passages.title: Slumber No More
passages.text: Your aid is required. We must begin.

passages.title: How to Repair a Titan Keeper
passages.text:
Major system repair possible within nearby structure. Preliminary goal: repair auxiliary systems.

Scans detect three fallen titan keepers. Recover cores. Titan Keeper Hezrel able to retrieve data from cores.

Titan Keeper Hezrel goal: reboot auxiliary systems, reach nearby structure, restore all primary systems, seal corruption.

Result: corruption contained. Titan Keeper Hezrel able to aid against blood trolls.

Blood troll definition not found in databanks.

passages.title: How to Repair a Titan Keeper
passages.text: Insert data cores.

passages.title: How to Repair a Titan Keeper
passages.text: Cores recovered. Data validation and merge will begin shortly.

passages.title: Recovering Remnants
passages.text:
Scan of area indicates roaming spirits clad in armor plating. Purpose: defense of structure, animated by corruption.

Detecting remnants of titan plating within spirits' armor. Request: recover remnants.

Titan Keeper Hezrel capable of breaking down titan plating to reforge into weapon against forces drawn by corruption.

passages.title: Recovering Remnants
passages.text: Titan plating required.

passages.title: Recovering Remnants
passages.text: Sufficient titan plating. Will begin forging process once functionality is restored.

passages.title: Corrupted Earth
passages.text:
Unacceptable levels of corruption detected nearby. Scan indicates vegetation affected by corruption. 

All corruption must be eradicated. Request: destroy any vegetation affected by corruption.

passages.title: Corrupted Earth
passages.text: Vegetation corruption reduced to an acceptable level.

passages.title: So Long, Sister
passages.text:
We have given the defenders some breathing room, but these creatures continue to lay siege to the barricade!

The witch behind the attack fled from the field when we defeated her forces. I saw her go into the mansion on the hill. I will help keep the defenses going here.

You must go into the mansion and slay the witch!

passages.title: So Long, Sister
passages.text: The witch must be slain!

passages.title: So Long, Sister
passages.text: We wouldn't have been able to hold out much longer. You saved us all.

passages.title: Sandscar Breach
passages.text:
I heard some mutterings about sand and snakes.

The plea comes from a tiny village on the very fringes of Zuldazar- hardly more than a few farms. Dol-something I think it was called. Don't know what they be calling it now. Go see what the fuss is about.

Bladeguard Sonji was sent ahead some time ago. She should be able to get you up to speed on that... situation.

passages.title: Sandscar Breach
passages.text:
Rastakhan finally sent someone!

I hope you not be afraid of snakes, mon.

passages.title: Drawing Blood
passages.text:
Hey, <name>! I have something exciting to tell you about, but I need you to keep it secret. Just between us scribes.

<Grazzul gives you a nod and pulls out a large tome.>

Dis is de Bloodbound Ledger. Signing your name in it let's you learn how to craft "blood contracts" which are rather dangerous, but worth de risk.

I only know one of dem and it is quite de rush when I use it because it... well, you'll see.

So what do you say? Interested?

passages.title: Drawing Blood
passages.text:
Let me make sure you did it right.

<Grazzul finds your signature and nods.>

Yes, everything looks in order and it looks like de spell has already taken effect on you.

You are now worthy of knowing how to craft de "blood contracts".

But be careful with dem, <name>. I said it before and I'll say it again. They're dangerous things to play with.

passages.title: Turn to Drust
passages.text:
Dere are blood scribe masters all over de place who'll teach you what you need to know. De first master I'd recommend seeking out is Kronah.

She's a bit... eccentric to say de least. One of de few tortollan who've experienced a thing or two.

She's de one who taught me de blood contract I know how to invoke!

She prefers to hang out at de Smuggler's Cove on de western coast of Drustvar.

passages.title: Turn to Drust
passages.text:
<Kronah eyes you up and down warily.>

Say ahhh for me, would you lad?

<Kronah peers inside your mouth.>

Nice teeth you have there. Would fetch a fine price. But that's not really what you're here for, is it?

No, you're one of those who think they can handle the trials of the blood contracts, aren't you? Very well.

passages.title: Lines In the Sand
passages.text:
This was all I had to offer you, young scribe. But your journey is not yet at an end.

If you're up for some traveling, and interested in some of the deadlier blood contracts, you're going to have to travel to Zandalar.

Once there, seek out a sethrak by the name of Veriss in an area known as Vol'dun.

<Kronah grabs an odd-looking jar and opens it. The foulest odor you've ever smelled emanates from it and you reel in disgust.>

Pickled crocolisk eggs are my favorite. Would you like some?

passages.title: Lines In the Sand
passages.text:
Ah! A new initiate! Were you wondering how I knew? Because of the blood on your hands, of course.

<A sly grin crosses over the sethrak's face.>

I am Veriss, the resident keeper of the Zandalar blood contracts.

If you wish to inscribe your name into them, there is something I must ask of you first.

passages.title: Unwelcome Undead
passages.text:
Corruption reanimating dead creatures nearby. Morphing into monstrosities. Must be stopped.

Cannot kill all, but can reduce numbers. Reduced numbers equates to less corruption outside of containment.

Destroy undead in surrounding area. Keeper Hezrel's systems will continue rebooting while you do so.

Reboot goal: recover data regarding nature of corruption.

passages.title: Unwelcome Undead
passages.text: Undead levels lowered to acceptable amount. Still require method to bypass targets in order to access containment.

passages.title: Blood Purification
passages.text:
<You see a strange blood orb that emanates whispers of suffering and destruction.

These must be the source of energy for whatever corruption Hezrel is hunting. They appear easy enough to destroy.

You can see more of these orbs around the temple grounds. Perhaps destroying them will help to weaken the corruption in the area.>

passages.title: Blood Purification
passages.text: Scanners did not pick up evidence of corrupted energy. Must continue repairs, cannot make same mistake again.

passages.title: The Essence of G'huun
passages.text:
Analysis of blood-infused bones complete. Will be able to create synthetic essence similar to G'huun.

Will take a moment to apply essence, allow you to walk past undead without combat.

Must hurry. More forces of G'huun are around temple. Must get inside to reactivate containment protocols.

passages.title: Not Fit for This Plane
passages.text:
System restoration in progress. Data recovered. Source of corruption is from an Old God entity.

Multiple entities detected nearby, blocking goal of analyzing and containing corruption in Nazmir.

Entities appear to be from the Void. Drawn here from Old God corruption.

Request to destroy Void entities. Void presence inhibiting repair of systems.

passages.title: Not Fit for This Plane
