passages.text: Level of Void entities too high.

passages.title: Not Fit for This Plane
passages.text: Old God minions temporarily reduced. Will not last long without proper containment.

passages.title: Void is Prohibited
passages.text:
Scans indicate errors in reality surrounding nearby structure. Portals directly to the Void.

Current theory, corruption has Old God as source. Void attracted to Old God corruption.

Portals must be sealed to contain entities lured here by Old God corruption.

Take this device. Titan Keeper Hezrel has forged it thanks to help in powering up systems.

Use device to seal Void portals, prevent more void entities from entering area.

passages.title: Void is Prohibited
passages.text: Void portals no longer detected. Must continue.

passages.title: Protocol Recovery
passages.text:
System repairs progressing. One key component needed: containment protocol. 

containment protocol will fully reboot defensive systems. Allow Titan Keeper Hezrel to properly maintain containment.

Scans indicate large creature within temple has absorbed slab containing containment protocol. Creature exists between this plane and Void.

Request: destruction of creature and retrieval of protocol.

passages.title: Protocol Recovery
passages.text: Please present containment protocol.

passages.title: Protocol Recovery
passages.text: Containment protocol obtained. System reboot initiated.

passages.title: Sic 'Em!
passages.text:
Humphrey's a good tracker, to be sure. He's also the orneriest, angriest, most dogged dog if he sets his eyes on a quilboar. This will certainly be useful.

Below our very noses, the foreman organizes and directs the tunnelers to cause the most mayhem and destruction. If you can put an end to him, it should make things a lot easier for us to move around the farmlands.

Humphrey looks a bit hungry, wouldn't you say? Why don't you bring him with you to take care of business?

passages.title: Sic 'Em!
passages.text: If I could rate Humphrey, I'd give him at least a twelve out of ten.

passages.title: Sic 'Em!
passages.text: Jolly good. With him out of the way, the quilboar around here should be less organized and take longer to mobilize.

passages.title: The Warpack
passages.text:
Zul began a coup, but he did not secure de pyramid for himself. Nor has he done anything to rally more to his banner outside of those who were already conspiring with him.

Dis concerns me more than if he had carved his face into Dazar'alor itself.

We must learn what he is up to. Join de disciples of Gonk and ride ahead to de Temple of the Prophet. Look to Wardruid Loti for further orders when you arrive.

passages.title: The Warpack
passages.text: Good hunting.

passages.title: The Warpack
passages.text: Blood calls out for blood.

passages.title: Awaken a God
passages.text:
You see the sinking ruins to the east? They were, not long ago, a temple to the shark loa, Gral.

The naga tore down his temple and are stealing his secrets. If it is for something good, I'll be a rock's uncle.

It would be wise to let Gral know what's going on here. I do not think he would approve.

Gral was quite powerful, and when it came to his knowledge of the sea, none could compare. It never hurts to have a fellow like that on your side.

Some fresh, bloody naga meat may just lure him out.

passages.title: Awaken a God
passages.text: <There is a feeling of anticipation emanating from the bowl.>

passages.title: Awaken a God
passages.text: Now this! This is an offering worthy of my attention!

passages.title: Rest in the Depths
passages.text:
This passage flows through the Shrine of the Storm out into the open sea. We will release the souls of the fallen here.

Legends say that as our spirits pass through the Shrine, they aid in the great blessing rituals that all Kul Tiran ships undergo. 

In that way, we Stormsong never stop serving our people.

passages.title: Rest in the Depths
passages.text: The sea demands respect. To cross it is to invite its wrath upon us all.

passages.title: Rest in the Depths
passages.text: Thank you for aiding me in my solemn task.

passages.title: Featherfeet's Fun Falling's Fun Fee!
Fabricated Fabrications
passages.text:
There was somethin' off with the ship we were building in the yard. I never saw the blueprints, but I've built enough ships in my day to know it wasn't business as usual.

They've kept all the pages under tight guard in the Brineworks up the road lately. Full on militia.

If you can get your hands on enough of them pages, we oughta be able to figure out what Lord Stormsong and his boys are schemin'.

passages.title: Fabricated Fabrications
passages.text: Any luck recovering those blueprints?

passages.title: Fabricated Fabrications
passages.text: I knew they'd still have 'em! If you ever want something gone, lad you'd best destroy it yourself.

passages.title: Rearmament
passages.text:
The people of this valley have true hearts, <name>. They're eager to take back control of their home.

We have to help them.

The Brineworks up the road from here supplies most of House Stormsong's weapons. Our movement here could make great use of them.

If you can collect enough to go around, I'll go over some basic training with our friends here.

passages.title: Rearmament
passages.text: There are still many who don't follow Lord Stormsong. We need to stand by them.

passages.title: Rearmament
passages.text: This valley belongs to its people. We must fight to make it whole again!

passages.title: Storm's Judgment
passages.text:
When I opened my mind to the currents during the ritual, I felt the presence of a member of Lord Stormsong's innermost circle.

Wavespeaker Reid. If anyone can locate the missing fleet, it is him.

I will not stand by while my brothers move against our own people. Oaths be damned.

We must force Reid to see reason.

passages.title: Storm's Judgment
passages.text: This must be done.

passages.title: Storm's Judgment
passages.text: I never thought Reid would succumb to darkness. Things are worse than I feared.

passages.title: Voices Below
passages.text:
The others forged ahead to Port Fogtide. I doubt they will receive a warm welcome. 

We are to meet them there. However, there is something I must do first.

Despite Reid's retreat I still feel a terrible darkness nearby; I wish to listen to the tides for answers. I would appreciate your joining me in case more danger strays into our path.

passages.title: Voices Below
passages.text: We must help the others before they are overrun!

passages.title: Breaking Hag
passages.text:
The town is overrun! 

The guards have fallen back and what is worse, some of the villagers have been twisted by the witches' magic. They are little more than wretched beasts blindly following orders. 

We must release these poor souls and slay the monsters that twisted them!

See what you can do to cut down the numbers of monsters in town!

passages.title: Breaking Hag
passages.text: We have a little breathing room.

passages.title: Breaking Hag
passages.text: Well done. You've thinned their numbers.

passages.title: A Very Precious Cargo
passages.text: We weren't the only ship in our convoy to get caught up in this mess. Our flagship ran aground to the east. It was holding a very precious cargo and I need you to bring it back here.

passages.title: A Very Precious Cargo
passages.text: Who are you? Where's my dad? I'm hungry. Can I have a sword? Where's my dad?!

passages.title: The First Watch
passages.text:
As you can see, the coven has conscripted my own guardsmen into their service. Though I am loath to battle my own, these men are too corrupted by the coven's magic to be saved.

For them, death is the only mercy we can give.

The Inquisitors and I can handle the regiment stationed outside. We will need you to find and take out their leader.

Your Inquisitors await your command, <class>. Are you ready to take the tower?

passages.title: The First Watch
passages.text: We assault the tower at your command.

passages.title: The First Watch
passages.text:
Well fought, <class>.  The tower is ours.

Now, we should set our sights on Corlain proper!

passages.title: Hold My Hand
passages.text:
Take me to my daddy this instant!

Waaaait! You have to hold my hand...

passages.title: Hold My Hand
passages.text: Where is she? Don't tell me you lost her.

passages.title: Hold My Hand
passages.text: You found my precious little sea star!

passages.title: Shipwreck Recovery Crew
passages.text: Fogcliff Strand is swarming with Sirens and Saurolisks! Clear them out and grab any remaining cargo from the ships.

passages.title: Save Our Shipmates
passages.text:
Oh, thank the stars! Our ship ran aground and our men are in desperate need of help.

Find Henry Hardwick down the hill at the shipwreck. He stayed behind to try and help the others.

passages.title: Save Our Shipmates
passages.text: We need your help, sailor!

passages.title: A Weapon of Old
passages.text:
I've been studying the parchment Lady Lucille sent with you and have translated some of the older language. 

They called it "Liquid Fire" and it was used to "burn away the Drust". Using this as a basis I believe we can adapt it to our needs. This is a complex recipe, but it just so happens I have everything we need to make this potent alchemical weapon!

I will need your assistance in creating this. Would you be so kind as to help?

passages.title: A Weapon of Old
passages.text: We'd better get cooking!

passages.title: A Weapon of Old
passages.text: Wonderful! Smells a bit strong but I think it will burn those wooden constructs well! Now it's time to test it out.

passages.title: A Pocketful of Shells
passages.text:
You see the problem? No you don't.

Problem isn't all these dang quilboar. Quilboar I can shoot all day. Been shootin' em all my life, since my pappy gave me my first gun. 

Problem is these pigs are tough. Tougher'n they've been before. Can't kill em like I used to, see? My new modified bullets just get stuck in them and they refuse to die!

Here, take my knife. Go out there and kill some of the quilboar and get my ammo back. Then I can shoot the rest! I won't stop 'till there's none left to shoot!

passages.title: A Pocketful of Shells
passages.text: Pretty sure I'll have to start shootin' my dinnerware, and I only have three sets. Hurry up, will you?

passages.title: A Pocketful of Shells
passages.text: Good! I can keep shooting, and they can't get to me! This is really the perfect setup.

passages.title: Archaeological Efficiency
passages.text:
Miss Tae'shara and I share a passion for uncovering hidden secrets and a deep, abiding respect for this ancient land.

That said! If we were to continue at the pace to which she is accustomed, the Alliance would overtake us before we could make a single discovery. 

It is time to expedite our survey.

The ruins hide many fossils. Take a beacon and use it to summon one of my sweepers. It will clear away the topsoil and allow you to collect samples.

Gather what you can- we can assemble them later.

passages.title: Archaeological Efficiency
passages.text: I simply see no reason to dirty our hands, <name>.

passages.title: Archaeological Efficiency
passages.text:
Hm. These are a little... broken, don't you think?

Ah, well, nothing a little magic cannot fix.

passages.title: The Seething Shore
passages.text:
We've received reports of an island off the coast of Silithus that is ripe with Azerite deposits.

It is vital that we secure the island before the Alliance learns of its existence.

Nathanos Blightcaller is personally leading the expedition force and has requested that you report for duty. Go with honor!

passages.title: The Seething Shore
passages.text: I'm pleased to see that you made it back alive. I'm sure you fought with honor!

passages.title: The Speaker's Call
passages.text:
I been travelin' the land, seekin' out anyone who might know how ta heal Azeroth. I've consulted ancient sages, druids, shamans... from dragons ta titan keepers. Nobody's seen anythin' like this before.

Went ta Karazhan ta speak with Khadgar. Studyin' those old tomes o' his, we came up with an idea. No tellin' if it's gonna work, but we gotta try.

Come ta Silithus. Meet me at the wound. Time is runnin' out fer Azeroth, adventurer.

passages.title: The Witch's Pet
passages.text:
I've seen her! The witch!

Every once in a while she comes down to the cave, checking on her pet. I've never seen a spider so large!

She spreads her spell, cursing all of the animals in these woods to follow her command and attack us.

The broodmother laid all these eggs, and they're hatching into more possessed beasts!

Take her out, and perhaps the infestation will stop.

passages.title: The Witch's Pet
passages.text: <With the spider matriarch defeated, the flow of cursed spiders should slow, if not stop completely.>

passages.title: Can't Hear A Thing
passages.text:
These snake wenches show up and everyone loses their minds! All my men are head over heels for these things. Personally, I don't see it. I mean, I sort of get the appeal, but the wings for arms and snake tails are a big turn off.

There's a big one in a cave to the east. She's got a whole heap of suitors. I need them back to work. Go give her a wallop and get everyone back here.

passages.title: Can't Hear A Thing
passages.text:
I decided if you can't beat 'em, join 'em! That one over there looks available. Think she'll go out with me?

Oh, and thanks for getting everyone back at their posts. We got a lot of cleanup.

passages.title: Fighting With Fire
passages.text:
Excellent! Now that we have these lovely Liquid Fire flasks prepared we have one last thing to do:

Test them out!

There are some of those large abominations lurking about in the woods above my home. I think they would make excellent test subjects for our little alchemical experiment, wouldn't you say?

passages.title: Fighting With Fire
passages.text: Help!

passages.title: Fighting With Fire
passages.text: I tried to stop them but I couldn't. They've taken Master Ashton into the woods!

passages.title: Don't Go in the Basement
passages.text:
We checked everywhere... well, <gulps> everywhere except the basement.

B-b-but, dad told me never to go down there.

He said it's dark, scary, and dangerous to go alone... I could be eaten by a brue!

I don't even know what that is, but I don't wanna be eaten! 

<name>, do you think you could go down first?

passages.title: Don't Go in the Basement
passages.text: The brue, I saw it. He didn't make it up!!

passages.title: A Reason to Stay
passages.text:
<You find a pocketwatch on the ground. It is dirty, but still works. It was taken care of well.

Perhaps there are other objects that Goldfield wasn't able to grab before he had to hole up in his house. He might appreciate it if you brought them to him.>

passages.title: A Reason to Stay
passages.text: For the last time, I'm not leaving! I was here first, THEY can leave!

passages.title: A Reason to Stay
passages.text: You... you found them. I...

passages.title: Goldfield's War
passages.text:
I'm not leaving. I'm never leaving.

Those quilboar, they killed them. I gave her the watch, told her to hurry. Grab our boy and get to the house while I got the gun...

<Goldfield is choking back tears.>

I won't leave. Our family has our roots here. They would want me to stay, don't you understand? This is our farm. My boy, he wanted to join the militia. I made him a sword...

<Goldfield takes a deep breath.>

Now you know. Help me retake my farm. Grab a gun and let's kill every last one.

passages.title: Goldfield's War
passages.text: This is MY home!

passages.title: Goldfield's War
passages.text: It's done. My family is avenged.

passages.title: Detective Mildenhall
passages.text:
Hmm... okay, okay, let's think.

If you were my dad and you accidentally set loose a bunch of honey monsters all over the place, what would you do?

Well, okay, you would probably beat all of them up. But he probably ran away.

If he left in a hurry, maybe he left something for us to find.

passages.title: Detective Mildenhall
passages.text: Did you find anything else?

passages.title: Detective Mildenhall
passages.text: Hmm... we checked everywhere.

passages.title: Brutal Boost
passages.text:
The Aggression Formula is ready and I need you to inject Ben'jin with it. 

Let's show the world, and the witch doctor, that well researched, dramatically overpowered, double-blind, peer-reviewed, super goblin science is the right way to do, uh, pretty much anything!

passages.title: Brutal Boost
passages.text: This is exciting, isn't it?

passages.title: Brutal Boost
passages.text: I spent several moments working out that formula! It should have worked! The reason these brutosaurs are endangered is clearly their unreasonable resistance to science!

passages.title: Rally the Warriors
passages.text:
We have learned so much and came so far thanks to you and de Horde, but all of it will amount to nothing if de blood trolls defeat us here. 

We've all worked hard since we first set foot within dis accursed swamp, without a chance to even get any sleep or have a decent meal. Dey are some of de finest soldiers I've ever encountered, but even dey have their limits. 

Let us remind dem what we are fighting for!

passages.title: Rally the Warriors
passages.text: We must carry on. De fate of my home is in our hands.

passages.title: Rally the Warriors
passages.text: We are ready. Now, it is time for us to bring our fight to de blood trolls!

passages.title: Undying Totems
passages.text:
De blood trolls are putting up quite de fight. Dey are raising de very dead to go against us!

Their necromancers are raising de dead with de help of totems fueled with blood magic. Destroying dem should take de pressure off our troops.

passages.title: Undying Totems
passages.text: Why are you talking to me when those totems are still out dere?

passages.title: Undying Totems
passages.text: Good work, dat should make things easier on us.

passages.title: The Road of Pain
passages.text:
My people continue to be captured and hauled into de blood trolls' village for de slaughter, to be used as fuel for their dark rituals. 

Just ahead, I can see some of de captives who fell along de path. I hear their cries as de blood trolls perform their vile rituals upon dem.

We cannot leave my people to die in de swamp, <name>!

Take dese bandages and save any Zandalari you encounter down dere.

passages.title: The Road of Pain
passages.text: Were you able to help de others?

passages.title: The Road of Pain
passages.text:
Our soldiers will return home stronger, wiser, and most importantly, alive.
 
On behalf of my people, I thank you.

passages.title: Target of Opportunity
passages.text:
It seems our actions here have not gone unnoticed, <name>. I feel a dark presence ahead.

Ateena is near! 

Dis is our chance! If we strike now, we can deal a huge blow to de blood trolls!

We must move!

passages.title: Target of Opportunity
passages.text:
She is... so much stronger than I expected. But, we have some surprises of our own! 

Let us bring up dis gun of yours and see how well it performs.

passages.title: The Crawg Ma'da
passages.text:
No matter what we do, as long as dem blood trolls have their village here, dey gonna be a threat.

We gonna put an end to dat threat!

Amaka be da strongest blood troll I ever seen, and she be right across da way there. She be feedin' da bodies of da Zandalari ta her pet crawgs, makin' dem big, fat, and deadly. It be time for revenge, and we be doin' it wit' da help of her own pets.

Go kill a crawg and cut its poison gland out of its belly. With it, ya can weaken Amaka and put an end to her.

passages.title: The Crawg Ma'da
passages.text:
Well done, <name>! 

Da blood trolls gonna be hurtin' wit' da death of their general. Now, let's keep da pressure on dem!

passages.title: Back On Your Feet, Soldier
passages.text:
I figured any soldiers we be coming across might be wantin' some revenge, so I brought along some extra weapons just in case.

See up ahead? Dem cages be full of trolls awaitin' der turn ta die. We gonna swoop in der and be da answers to der prayers!

Go and arm as many of dem as ya can, revenge gonna be sweet!

passages.title: Ateena's Fall
passages.text:
You have proven to be a much greater ally dan I could have ever hoped. Thanks to you and your Horde, we have come dis far. Now, there is only one thing dat remains. 

We must confront de leader of de blood trolls and put an end to their dark plot once and for all.

Without Ateena's mojo to protect it, we can finally destroy dat monstrosity of theirs before it can be unleashed upon Zuldazar. 

You know what must be done. 

First, I must prepare myself. Go. I will join you when de battle has begun.

passages.title: Ateena's Fall
passages.text:
Finally, our battle here is done!

More importantly, you have made good friends with de tortollans and have gained powerful allies in de loa. I feel dat we will need to call upon their aid in de future.

It is time for me to return to Zuldazar and let my father know of our victory. 

Do you hear dat? Rokhan appears to have a message for us.

passages.title: Golden Fields Forever
passages.text:
I can take care of the rest. That ettin would have given me trouble if I was by myself, so you have my thanks.

I would ask you for one more favor.

My wife, she loved the carnations that grow by the water's edge. If you could gather some, there's a nice spot under a tree by the river. We loved to go there when the sun set after our days in the fields.

Our boy would run around, catching bugs, making reed whistles...

passages.title: Golden Fields Forever
passages.text: That's that, then.

passages.title: Golden Fields Forever
passages.text: Thank you, <class>. They will rest now.

passages.title: Building Defenses
passages.text:
We'll be able to push those monsters back now, but my defenders won't stand a chance unless we build a forward barricade for protection.

There should be plenty of lumber to build a barricade near the entrance to town.

passages.title: Building Defenses
passages.text: We've pushed the front line out. That will give us some room.

passages.title: Building Defenses
passages.text: Thank you. We'll be better able to protect the town.

passages.title: Curiously Strong
passages.text:
I imagine the fires spread while I was down here, yes? First order of business then; making sure the town doesn't burn down! Help solve that problem and I shall be free to assist you in... whatever it is?

Let's see... Yes! Here! Take these. They proved to be bit too... intense for most people, but you seem like a stout sort.

Just be sure you're facing the fires when you use them, and I'm certain those fires will be out in no time!

passages.title: Curiously Strong
passages.text: If we don't stop the fires, they could spread!

passages.title: Curiously Strong
passages.text: Ah wonderful! The fires are out and your breath smells minty fresh!

passages.title: Bearers of Bad News
passages.text:
We must report this attack to Lord Admiral Katherine Proudmoore and prove to her that Lady Ashvane is behind it.

It won't be easy... Lady Ashvane and Katherine Proudmoore have been close friends for years.

Quickly, let us make for Boralus!

passages.title: Bearers of Bad News
passages.text: It seems word of the attack has already reached Boralus.

passages.title: Totems, Totems, Totems!
passages.text:
<This totem pulses with energy, releasing it into the nearby idols and thorns.

It looks rather fragile... It would be a shame if something happened to it.>

passages.title: Totems, Totems, Totems!
passages.text: Good idea! Smashing those will distract their mystics and set back their expansion.

passages.title: Hammering Out Information
passages.text:
I guess you noticed it requires a special anvil to make it. And I suppose you want to know where to find a Khaz'gorian Smithing Anvil?

Well, I don't know where you can find one, not to mention I never said you'd be able to actually craft the dang thing.

Now if you wouldn't mind, I have more of these recipes to sell.

passages.title: Hammering Out Information
passages.text: That recipe really is worth what you paid for it, regardless of whether you can craft it or not.

passages.title: Hammering Out Information
passages.text: Alright, alright, fine! I'll tell you what I know.

passages.title: A Possible Solution
passages.text:
None of dese things are working. I can't believe I'm saying dis, but I think you're gonna have to find Zukashi.

Maybe you could convince him to give up de other half of de recipe. He's pretty full of himself, but he isn't unreasonable.

Last time I heard, he's staying in Nazmir near Gloom Hollow. Maybe it's best to tell him dis isn't about me.

passages.title: A Possible Solution
passages.text:
Who are you? Another one of Kumali's apprentices coming to learn de true art of alchemy?

Or is dere someting else you're interested in?

<You explain to Zukashi that you're researching a special transmutation stone and that he might be able to help you.>

Oh, dat thing, eh? Heh. Ya, dat's a fine thing to have.

But if you want de knowledge I have, you're gonna have to help me with someting first, little mixah.

passages.title: A Deathly Draught
passages.text:
De first thing I'd like you to do for me is to gather some deathshroom.

Don't worry if you're not skilled at herbalism, they're very easy to pick. Dey typically grow where death lingers in the air.

I'd try to de Frogmarsh to de southeast. De trolls dere have been making sacrifices of de creature dat inhabit de area.

passages.title: A Deathly Draught
passages.text:
Have you finally acquired my mushrooms?

It's a simple task, even for someone like you.

passages.title: A Deathly Draught
passages.text: Well done, little mixah! Dat's plenty for what I need.

passages.title: Chemically Compounded
passages.text:
Now dat I have everything I need, I can finish dis project. My latest transmuation will be my finest yet!

But dis is not de place to test it. It could draw too much attention.

If you want to see it for yourself, little mixah, meet me to de north. Dere is a cave dere dat should be a safe spot for testing dis out.

passages.title: Chemically Compounded
passages.text:
This bag must have belonged to Zukashi. As you rummage through it, you see a slip of paper that appears to be torn.

You grab the parchment and begin reading.

passages.title: A Recipe for Success
passages.text:
Looking it over more closely, you're convinced that this must be the missing half of the recipe you came for.

An odd signature completes the recipe, signed, "Silas Darkmoon".

Kumali should be very pleased to see this once again.

passages.title: A Recipe for Success
passages.text:
Ya did it, <name>! Dis is de other half of de recipe!

Here. You take dis copy and don't lose it. I'll make another copy and keep it in a safe place.

Dis way, if one of us forgets it, we'll know how to get it back again, ya see? Also, you make a better partner dan Zukashi ever did. Pleasure working with ya, <name>.

passages.title: Ocular Extracts
passages.text:
My next idea involves a creature whose eyes are useful for certain alchemical recipes. At least for potions they are.

Hopefully they're just what we need for this and there aren't any further... miscalculations. Although, I don't entirely recall seeing them on the recipe's ingredient list... but my memory isn't exactly as good as it used to be.

Oh, you caught me rambling. How about you get those eyes and I'll start making the preparations for them.

passages.title: Ocular Extracts
passages.text: Oh, I do hope you gathered the eyes post mortem. Those creatures make the most awful sound if you try to extract them while they're still alive.

passages.title: Ocular Extracts
passages.text: Very good. These should be plenty!

passages.title: A Possible Solution
passages.text:
Nothing appears to be working. I can't believe I'm proposing this but I actually think we need to contact Quintin.

Well, you should, as I doubt he'll speak to me. Perhaps you could convince him to part with the other half of the recipe?

Last time I heard, he was staying in Drustvar near Arom's Stand. There's a lot of alchemists in those parts, but he shouldn't be too hard to find.

Best not to tell him I sent you. He may not be as forthcoming with the recipe.

passages.title: A Possible Solution
passages.text:
Who do we have here? I don't suppose you're an old apprentice of my little brother, Elric, come to learn true alchemy, are you?

<You explain to Quintin that you're researching a special transmutation stone and that he might be able to help you.>

Oh, interested in making one of those, are you? Well, just like transmutation there must be some equivalent exchange.

You're going to have to do some things for me first. You can have the pleasure of being MY apprentice.

passages.title: A Deathly Draught
passages.text:
The first thing I'd like you to do for me is to gather some deathshroom.

Don't worry if you're not skilled at herbalism, they're very easy to pick. They typically grow where death lingers in the air.

I'd try to the Crimson Forest to the south. The creatures that have overrun it seem to be covered in deathly magics.

passages.title: A Deathly Draught
passages.text:
Have you finally acquired my mushrooms?

It's a simple task, even for someone like you.

passages.title: A Deathly Draught
passages.text: Oh yes, that's plenty for what I need. Well done, apprentice.

passages.title: Chemically Compounded
passages.text:
That appears to be everything. This latest transmutation will be my finest yet. And your prize waits at its completion, apprentice.

But I don't believe this is an appropriate place to test it out. It may draw too much attention.

There's a cave not terribly far from here which would prove to be a more suitable setting for such a test.

Meet me there when you're ready to witness why transmutation is the only branch of alchemy worth learning.

passages.title: Chemically Compounded
passages.text: This seems to contain some of Quintin's things.

passages.title: Chemically Compounded
passages.text:
This bag must have belonged to Quintin. As you rummage through it, you see a slip of paper that appears to be torn.

You grab the parchment and begin reading.

passages.title: A Recipe for Success
passages.text:
Looking it over more closely, you're convinced that this must be the missing half of the recipe you came for.

An odd signature completes the recipe, signed, "Silas Darkmoon".

Elric should be very pleased to see this once again.

passages.title: A Recipe for Success
passages.text:
You have it?! I'm impressed you were able to get it from Quintin.

<Elric grabs your half of the recipe and fetches a fresh piece of parchment. He begins copying down the information and once finished, walks back to you with it in his hand.>

Here, this copy is for you. I'll make another copy for myself and keep it safe this time.

If you don't mind me saying, you've made a much better partner than Quintin ever did. It was a pleasure working with you, <name>.

passages.title: Gadgets and Gizmos Aplenty
passages.text:
The militia may have given up on us, but we haven't given up on me!

I'm a bit of a tinker, and I find that my harvest golems are better than any hired help I've ever had. They just need regular maintenance to keep running.

Of course the Briarback are now taking over my fields, and my farmhands have gone into disrepair.

If you head out into the fields, can you grab the inner mechanisms from any of them that you find? That will stop them from exploding as well as help me plan my revenge.

passages.title: Gadgets and Gizmos Aplenty
passages.text: Do you have the parts yet?

passages.title: Gadgets and Gizmos Aplenty
passages.text: Perfect! With these parts I can rebuild my entire workforce. Or make one of them REALLY powerful.

passages.title: Stop Vining!
passages.text:
You may have noticed that the fields are a little... unstable right now.

The Briarback have been busy, growing those large bramble vines and boring tunnels underneath the farm. The vines have always been an important part of their borders, and they're expanding!

Go down into the lower area and see if you can find who or what is making those vines grow. There's no way that they're growing like that naturally. If we can stop the vines we can retake this area!

passages.title: Stop Vining!
passages.text: Mystics using magic to shape the vines? I don't know much about magic, but I'm glad you stopped them.

passages.title: Farming Stimulator
passages.text:
The plants have gone amok since you defeated their masters! Don't worry though, I've got a plan.

I've been busy fixing up one of the farmhands that didn't go completely haywire. It should have enough juice for one more trip through the fields.

We've got some serious technology in these harvesters. Their tools should be more than enough to take care of some small plants and even a couple quilboar.

What do you say? You up for some farming the Stormsong way? Hop on in and get to work!

passages.title: Farming Stimulator
passages.text: Take out as many of them as you can!

passages.title: Farming Stimulator
passages.text: Yeah, that'll show them! Those quilboar will think twice before invading my farm again!

passages.title: The Battle of Bloodfire Ravine
passages.text:
It is time to strike out and end de blood troll threat once and for all!

We travel back to Bloodfire Ravine, and dis time it is de blood trolls who will be sent running.

Mount up, and together we will show dem we are a force to be reckoned with!

passages.title: The Battle of Bloodfire Ravine
passages.text:
You fought well! 

De blood trolls are on de run. We must keep de momentum!

passages.title: The Missing Link
passages.text:
<Though burned, portions of the note in the architect's hand remain legible.>

They are... everywhere... disguised...

Encrypted... blueprints...

Cipher...

Pontus... watching me...

<The cipher must be needed to read the ship blueprints. It seems Pontus is the likely holder.>

passages.title: The Missing Link
passages.text: We need to get to the bottom of all this before Lord Stormsong goes on the offensive!

passages.title: The Missing Link
passages.text: A cipher? Of course! But by the great sea, what's it covered in?!

passages.title: A Steady Ballast
passages.text:
The Armory presents us a ripe opportunity, <class>... one I suggest we take.

If this battle were to draw out, we have little means to repair our arms and armor. A blacksmith is invaluable to any war effort, and Ballaster is one of our best.

The Armory is but a short ride from here. I suggest you get to Ballaster before it's too late!

passages.title: A Steady Ballast
passages.text:
The blacksmith won't survive long with the coven hunting him down. 

I'd recommend leaving posthaste.

passages.title: A Steady Ballast
passages.text:
Our fortunes are turning up. 

Having a blacksmith at the tower will ensure our Inquisitors stay equipped for battle.

passages.title: Digging for Scraps
passages.text:
Well met, <class>.

I hope you don't mind that I took the liberty to scout ahead and assess the situation at the armory.

The good news is that there still seems to be some salvageable arms left in the armory. The bad news, of course, is that the coven is after them as well.

Additional weapons could be a great boon to our cause. I recommend we take all we can carry.

passages.title: Digging for Scraps
passages.text: What did you find at the armory?

passages.title: Digging for Scraps
passages.text:
So the coven didn't completely clean out the armory? This is good news for us.

Even the most common villager in Drustvar can hold their own in a fight. With these arms we can turn each person we rescue to another soldier on the line.

passages.title: There's Gold in Them There Fields
passages.text:
We've still got some folks missing, and I could use your help finding them.

While Brennadam is now secure, I worry for some of our farms closer to the quilboar kraul. We relied on the militia in the past to keep the quilboar back, but now that they've retreated to the east I worry that our outlying farms are in danger.

Goldfield's farm is almost directly south of us, up the hill by the falls. While it's not surprising that he hasn't left, I would feel better if you checked in.

passages.title: There's Gold in Them There Fields
passages.text: Roz always worries about me. I keep tellin' her I'm fine up here, but she never listens...

passages.title: Checking Out the Collapse
passages.text:
If you've got a minute, there's a farmer out there who hasn't made it back yet.

Name's Burton and he's out by a farm right next to Briarback Kraul. If the quilboar were to strike out, his farm is one of the first in their way.

I haven't heard anything from Burton. He mostly relied on his mechanical farmers to help him, so we don't know the situation out there.

Head to the west and keep an eye out for him, would you?

passages.title: Checking Out the Collapse
passages.text: I stayed behind to see if I could help... Everyone else made it back okay, right?

passages.title: Recovering Raimond
passages.text:
The map we found earlier had some red markings, near the flower field. 

Do you think you could go up there and look for dad?

I'm going to stay here and check out the rest of this stuff. 

I'd go with you... but, I'm sort of allergic to bees.

Oh, and take his boot. Just in case!

passages.title: Recovering Raimond
passages.text: It is about time someone came looking for me!

passages.title: Recovering Raimond
passages.text:
Ahh, hah! Ancel sent you to find me, huh?

Hey, you found my boots too!? Marvelous!

passages.title: Sticky Situation
passages.text:
The scientific breakthroughs I've made, marvelous, absolutely marvelous... I'm so close to perfecting the formula!

The way the honey grows and crystallizes, simply beautiful. Well, as you can see, that's also part of my current predicament.

Perhaps you can lend me a hand? Just fetch some royal jelly from the hives outside.

Oh, don't worry about the bees, they are sweet, gentle things. 

They don't sting... much.

passages.title: Sticky Situation
passages.text: You get all the jelly yet?

passages.title: Sticky Situation
passages.text:
Hope you didn't have any problems with bees. No, of course not... why would you? 

They're totally harmless.

passages.title: The Bee Team
passages.text:
We need to put things in order, and the next item on the list is these blasted wendigos terrorizing the farm. 

If we can cull their numbers, it should be enough to drive them off!

I've synthesized a superb solution that might be just what we need to solvent this sticky situation!

Toss these bottles at your foes and our friendly little apoideas should come to help.

Whatever you do, please don't spill any on yourself...

passages.title: The Bee Team
passages.text:
Hah! Did you see the look of sheer terror on their faces when they saw the bee swarms? 

Marvelous!

passages.title: Royal Succession
passages.text:
I know, I know, okay... the farm is overrun by living honey and the bees have grown to massive proportions.

I'll admit, things didn't quite go according to plan, but, extraordinary advancements in science do not come without some risk!

I've been up here attempting to reduce aggression in the hive, an unfortunate side effect of my miscalculation, but I need another favor...

You're going to have to kill the Hive Mother and retrieve her stinger for me.

passages.title: Royal Succession
passages.text: Oooh, ooh, do you have it!?

passages.title: Royal Succession
passages.text: I'm glad you still have both of your eyes!

passages.title: Into the Crimsonwood
passages.text:
Master Ashton has been taken into the forest. He isn't the only one. Mayor Royston's headcount came up short.

It seems our next steps are clear. We must go into the woods and save Master Ashton.

Marten and I will sneak into the forest and meet you near some ruins further in.

passages.title: Into the Crimsonwood
passages.text: The woods are crawling with witches. We'll have a fight on our hands if we're to save Master Ashton.

passages.title: Precious Metals
passages.text:
<class>, I have another objective we should consider. 

The Bleak Hills Mine is not too far from our location. Though the miners there principally extract iron, they do on occasion find silver among the veins.

We do not know the current state of the mine, but it's unlikely that the coven has passed it over. However, it would be worth braving whatever dangers lie there to recover some silver to use against them.

passages.title: Precious Metals
passages.text: Did you have any luck with the mine?

passages.title: Precious Metals
passages.text:
You found some silver? Excellent!

Though it isn't much, any quantity of silver should help our efforts against the coven!

passages.title: An Eight-Legged Curse
passages.text:
Some terrible old hag unleashed a swarm of these horrible spiders in the mine! I was barely able to make it out alive, but they've got me surrounded!

You can't leave me here! Please kill those things!

passages.title: An Eight-Legged Curse
passages.text:
You... killed them!?

Oh thank you so much! It's been like a living nightmare in here!

passages.title: Hold The Barricade!
passages.text:
<name> they're rallying for a heavy assault!

We'll need to defend these barricades from attack! Are you with me?

passages.title: Hold The Barricade!
passages.text: That earned us some breathing room.

passages.title: Hold The Barricade!
passages.text: That witch! She must be the one guiding these attacks!

passages.title: Bilgemaul's Brigade
passages.text:
<According to these orders, these assassins are being hired by a Sea Dog captain who is establishing a beachhead in Drustvar.

Taking him out would deal a great blow to the Horde�s war effort, and might just put a halt to these ambushes.>

passages.title: A Wee Bit O' Cloth
passages.text:
<name>, is that you I hear rustlin' about out there? It's me, Angus Stormbrew!

There are cultists everywhere, so ye best keep yer voice down. Lean in close and cover yer nose while we talk!

This is the only outhouse in all o' Silithus! Trust me I spent hours lookin' all through the night. I decided to sneak in for a wee drop-off before the cultists woke up, but I've got a uhh problem...

There's no cloth to... you know...

See if ye can find me a wee bit o' cloth and sneak it in through the door!

passages.title: A Wee Bit O' Cloth
passages.text: Did ye acquire "the goods?"

passages.title: A Wee Bit O' Cloth
passages.text: Aye! This'll do nicely! Just give us a wee minute here...

passages.title: No Safe Haven
passages.text:
I brought Rastakhan to Zeb'ahari to hide him, <name>. I did not dream Zul's followers would find us so soon.

De people of Zeb'ahari are being hunted by those who answer to de prophet. I have brought dis upon dem by keeping de king in their village.

Help me save dem, <name>. Gather those who can still walk and send dem to me.

I can do nothing for those who died, but we can still rescue de living.

passages.title: No Safe Haven
passages.text: I hope we can get dem out.

passages.title: No Safe Haven
passages.text:
I will try to help dem secure their village.

Stay sharp, <name>. Zul will not stop while ol' Rastakhan's fate hangs in de balance.

passages.title: Bramblethorn
passages.text:
I was playing with Lord and Lady Sharptooth when Papa made me come with him. I dropped poor Lord Sharptooth and one of those big mean monsters grabbed him! 

Papa said he'd try to get him back but he's been gone a long time. I think he got busy. Mama and all the adults are busy doing stuff for Mayor Royston.

Lady Sharptooth and I are really sad. Can you beat up that mean monster and save my dino?

passages.title: Bramblethorn
passages.text: Did you find Lord Sharptooth? I think one of the really big monsters has him.

passages.title: Bramblethorn
passages.text:
Yay! Oh. Y-you saw someone? My papa?

<Lynn hugs her toy and sniffs>

I haven't seen my Mama in awhile. I hope she's okay.

passages.title: A Slip of the Tongue
passages.text:
<As you approach, the blind Zandalari motions at you impatiently.>

It sounds like ya be headed somewhere in a hurry, little weed!

Sit down and share a tale with an old troll before ya head out on ya next adventa.

I went on many adventas with my pterrordax when I was young. Explored dis whole valley!

My pterrordax died many years ago, but...

<Blind Tra'wala smiles mischievously.>

Sometimes at night, I steal da guards' snacks to trick dese old pterrordaxes into lettin' me ride again. Ha!

passages.title: A Boralus Triple Threat
passages.text:
If Tallis honestly thinks that offing a few random soldiers is going to force us to give up Southwatch, he's in for a surprise. The reason why we haven't chased out the sorry troops in this camp is simply because we have more pressing plans.

Fernn has his lieutenants facing the Watch's cannons straight at Boralus as we speak. Those three are the real driving force of the attack.

<The marine gives you a concerned look as he realizes what he said.>

passages.title: A Boralus Triple Threat
passages.text: What is it?

passages.title: A Boralus Triple Threat
passages.text: We finally got some useful information from him?

passages.title: Spell Bound
passages.text: <The villager is held captive by a binding rune. Destroying the rune should free the villager.>

passages.title: Spell Bound
passages.text: I shudder to think what they would have used those people for.

passages.title: Free the Farmhands
passages.text:
We were running around trying to get the farm under control, but the bees, oh my goodness, the bees!

The giant monstrosities came out of nowhere and started dousing everyone in honey.

I came up here to find Raimond, but before I knew it, I was covered too. 

Then, the strangest thing happened, the honey started growing around me!

Please, the other farmhands are still in trouble, you've got to help them!

passages.title: Free the Farmhands
passages.text: Encased in honey, just waiting to be eaten. That must have been absolutely terrifying!

passages.title: Saving Master Ashton
passages.text:
I believe I see Master Ashton in a cage. He must be freed!

Those witches with the long masks appear to be in charge. I bet they would have the means to open his cage.

I will remain here to protect Apprentice Webb and keep the area secure.

passages.title: Saving Master Ashton
passages.text:
We had a few visitors while you were gone but I took care of them. 

Ashton's back and safe, though it appears he's seen some of the horrors here.

passages.title: Bittersweet
passages.text:
Hey!

I need to get out of here and get back to Falconhurst! My husband and I were looking for my daughter's favorite toy when I was taken. Please, I need to get out of here! I need to know my family is safe. 

They took my gear. It's all around camp. Get me out of here then bring back my gear, please!

passages.title: Bittersweet
passages.text: Thank you. I'll cut a path back to Falconhurst. They will pay for what happened to my family!

passages.title: Deep In the Core
passages.text:
Look, you're gonna have to travel to some place called Deepholm and find an earthen down there.

The guy who sold the recipe to me said he got it from an earthen called...Ormhun! Ormhun something.

I don't know too much about that place, but maybe you can ask the locals or something where he lives.

Now if you don't mind, I have more recipes to sell.

passages.title: Deep In the Core
passages.text:
Looking fer me, are ya? And what can old Ormhun be helping a fleshy out with?

<You explain to Ormhun that you're trying to find a Khaz'gorian Smithing Anvil.>

Ha! Good luck with that! I haven't seen one of those in, oooh... centuries.

Lucky for you though, I know how ta make one. And I like the look of ya.

I suppose I could come out of retirement and help ya for one last craft. It's been so long, it'll be nice to work the forge again. Just gotta find me hammer...

passages.title: Smash and Grab
passages.text:
Most of the materials we'll need can be found right down here in the Deepholm.

We just need ta be discreet about it. If old Therazane catches wind of what we're up to, she might try ta put a stop ta it.

But let's not worry 'bout that. The first thing you'll need is diaminium. There are pillars that grow in the Alabaster Shelf rich with 'em.

Just use yer old blacksmithin' hammer and smash those pillars ta bits. Don't worry about breaking the diaminium. We'll meld it all back tagether.

passages.title: Smash and Grab
passages.text: This'll be fun! I haven't made one of those anvils in ages!

passages.title: Smash and Grab
passages.text:
Oh, did the drakes hear you smashing? Ha ha! Yea, I suppose that'd get their attention.

Still though, this'll be plenty of diaminium.

passages.title: Atal'Dazar: Locking Horns
passages.text:
We've got tha metal for tha base and tha body, but there's one last part...

Tha horn of tha anvil was ta be made of ukrite. But that metal's been gone for ages.

There is another metal tha's very close ta it in terms of its durability. A type of gold tha trolls mined in abundance. And I know where ye can find it.

Tha trolls control an area called Atal'Dazar, a great city made o' tha stuff. If ye can find something horn-shaped in there, that'll save us tha trouble of shaping it from scratch.

passages.title: Titanic Forging
passages.text:
Are ya ready, <lad/lass>?

You'll be doing the hammerin' while I take care of the last reagent we'll need.

passages.title: Titanic Forging
passages.text: Now you'll be able to craft some rather durable equipment. But best you be getting on yer way back.

passages.title: Anvil's Away
passages.text:
Take your anvil, and never speak of its methods of creation to anyone.

Should I find out otherwise, you may find your next visit to my realm an unpleasant one.

passages.title: Anvil's Away
passages.text:
Wait, what?! You actually got one? And you brought it back here?!

<Grix's eyes widen as you drop the anvil down next to him.>

Do you know what this means? It means I can start charging DOUBLE for the recipes!

Thank you, <name>. You're an amazing blacksmith!

passages.title: Hammering Out Information
passages.text:
Let me guess. You be lookin' at da recipe and noticed it require a Khaz'gorian Anvil ta make it. So now you be wantin' ta know where ta find a Khaz'gorian Smithing Anvil?

Look, <brudda/sista>, I never said anyting about bein' able ta craft da hamma. Now if ya don't mind, I have more of dese recipes ta be sellin'.

passages.title: Hammering Out Information
passages.text: Dat recipe really be wort what ya paid for it, no mindin' if ya be able ta craft it or not.

passages.title: Hammering Out Information
passages.text: Easy, brudda. I'll tell ya what I know.

passages.title: Deep In the Core
passages.text:
Look, ya gonna have ta travel ta Deepholm and convince dem ta be givin' up deir secrets. Dat's where da last anvil was made, or so I be hearin'.

And I only be knowin' of one earten down dere who might be willin' ta work wit ya. His name be Ormhun Stonehamma'.

He be kind of an outcast, but not too hard ta find.

passages.title: Deep In the Core
passages.text:
Looking fer me, are ya? And what can old Ormhun be helping a fleshy out with?

<You explain to Ormhun that you're trying to find a Khaz'gorian Smithing Anvil.>

Ha! Good luck with that! I haven't seen one of those in, oooh... centuries.

Lucky for you though, I know how ta make one. And I like the look of ya.

I suppose I could come out of retirement and help ya for one last craft. It's been so long, it'll be nice to work the forge again. Just gotta find me hammer...

passages.title: Anvil's Away
passages.text:
Take your anvil, and never speak of its methods of creation to anyone.

Should I find out otherwise, you may find your next visit to my realm an unpleasant one.

passages.title: Anvil's Away
passages.text:
Wait, what?! Ya actually got one? And ya be bringin' it back here?!

<Zak'aal's eyes widen as you drop the anvil down next to him.>

Do ya know what dis means, brudda? It means I can be charging DOUBLE for da recipes!

Tank ya, <name>. You be an amazing blacksmit!

passages.title: Therazane's Choice
passages.text:
<You explain that you meant no disrespect to Therazane or to steal their secrets.>

Interesting...

I have a wonderful idea on how to solve this issue. Would you like to hear it?

passages.title: Therazane's Choice
passages.text:
To think a creature such as yourself would be freely given our secrets.

I suppose I'll have to keep a closer eye on the goings on within my realm.

passages.title: Therazane's Choice
passages.text: Your choice has been made. And an interesting one at that.

passages.title: Odds and Ends
passages.text:
Master Ashton's going to probably need something bracing once we get him free. I know of a quick potion guaranteed to get anyone to snap out of it, but I'm going to need a few things first.

Those wicker dogs down there have some organic parts I can use and the witches are carrying bags of reagents. They'll almost certainly have what I need.

Bring those to me and I'll handle the rest once we get Master Ashton back.

passages.title: Odds and Ends
passages.text: Did you have any luck?

passages.title: Odds and Ends
passages.text: Hmm... Very interesting. And pungent. Perhaps my first order of business will be something to remove the smell.

passages.title: A Timely Summons from Northrend
passages.text:
The blazing wanes in the shadow of a celestial mass, striking fear in to the seers. Seek out the sage Vormu in Dalaran, and lend her your aid.

No, not this Dalaran, the other one. Yes I know, it's terribly confusing.

passages.title: A Timely Summons from Northrend
passages.text: We're behind schedule - let's get moving.

passages.title: Mojo Mischief
passages.text:
De soldiers you rescued spoke of de raids on Zandalar. Blood troll raiders, frothing at de mouth and possessing supernatural strength, overwhelmed de defenders. 

Dey say dat their strength came from flasks of mojo dat de raiders drink before going into combat. We cannot allow de blood trolls to continue to possess them.

Go down into de camp and destroy any of their flasks you may find.

passages.title: Stopping the Grand Rite
passages.text:
The witches of the Crimsonwood are planning a Grand Rite, a powerful ritual. They intend to rip open reality and bring their dark master through!

I suspect they may be in communion with Gorak Tul. We cannot allow their ritual to succeed.

I need you to be the tip of the spear while I protect Master Ashton and Marten. Cause havoc and disrupt their rituals!

passages.title: Stopping the Grand Rite
passages.text: Destroy the Ritual Foci.

passages.title: Stopping the Grand Rite
passages.text: Damn!. We've slowed them down, but they are still working. To fully stop them we'll need to do more.

passages.title: A Little 'Pick Me Up'
passages.text:
Now to mix this up. 

<Marten begins to combine the components in a mug>

I'm using some rather strong grog as a base, a drop of chilli extract and a handful of hearthbloom... There!

<Marten hands you a mug>

It will taste worse than it smells, but it will bring Master Ashton to his senses. Please give this mug to him.

passages.title: A Little 'Pick Me Up'
passages.text: <Ashton stares into the distance, eyes wide, muttering under his breath.>

passages.title: A Little 'Pick Me Up'
passages.text:
Oh! I say!

<Ashton shudders and coughs>

A bit less hearthbloom next time, Marten, but that did just the trick. Well done both of you.

passages.title: Unconventional Aromatics
passages.text:
A deal's a deal. You got the stingers for me, so here's that big batch of honey I promised.

I hope you and Rhan'ka enjoy it... slowly. Seriously, do not eat this all at once.

Oh, and I'm always looking to trade. Swing by anytime you got something to sell or want to pick up some more honey!

passages.title: Unconventional Aromatics
passages.text:
Thank de loa dat de Sandfury didn't kill you and take dese.

De drinks are almost ready and dey really add the perfect flavor.

passages.title: A Different Outcome
passages.text:
There is no way to know when these orders were sent, or received.

Rokor took some Seekers north some time ago. They must be in that region by now. 

If the temple still stands, warn Gral and his followers.

If it is lost, we must do what we can.

passages.title: A Different Outcome
passages.text: I fear those orders were found too late to help those that served here... about five years too late.

passages.title: Steal Them Back
passages.text:
<This empty crate of supplies is clearly marked with Kul Tiran signage. These must be the spoils of their raids on the farms of the valley.

The citizens would probably like their supplies back if there are any left.>

passages.title: Steal Them Back
passages.text: Keep an eye out for anything useful. This place is very dangerous.

passages.title: Steal Them Back
passages.text: It's not stealing if we're stealing them back. Hey! Are those my lucky anchors?

passages.title: Mayhem at Mildenhall Meadery
passages.text:
Ahhhh! <Sir/Miss>, please, I need some help!

My dad hasn't come back from the meadery and, and... well, when I went to look, there were giant globs of honey everywhere. 

But... but, somehow, they were moving on their own. I even saw one eat a bunny, I swear!

I'm scared to go back by myself, but I think dad is in trouble.

Can you go with me?

passages.title: Mayhem at Mildenhall Meadery
passages.text: Where did all of these things come from?

passages.title: An Overrun Mine
passages.text:
It was horrible! I was in the mine nearby, just picking away at a rock and it jumped up and bit me in the neck! Since when can rocks walk around and bite people?

I hightailed it outta there, but some crazy fools are sticking around trying to take the mine back. If you're eager to punch rocks you can find them down the road to the south.

passages.title: An Overrun Mine
passages.text:
Why aren't you wearing a miner's cap!? It's dangerous out here! Here, put this on.

Now, I got a job for you. Real easy.

passages.title: We Need a Chemist
passages.text:
All this chaos started when we were picking at a large Azerite node deep in the mine. The mine began to rumble and all of these blasted creatures burst from the ground. If we could just get rid of that vein, I am sure we could retake the mine.

First, we need a chemist. The best one we got is in his lab across the river. Find him and he'll give you more instructions.

passages.title: Pinch of Azerite
passages.text:
I don't have time for idle chit chat! If you haven't noticed, rocks are running around doing who knows what?!

How about you help out and retrieve my chemistry kit. While you're out, smash some of those creatures and collect their dust. Prim will need both of those for the next step of the plan.

Maybe we can figure out what has animated the Azerite.

passages.title: Pinch of Azerite
passages.text: Did you bring the dust?

passages.title: Pinch of Azerite
passages.text: Great job! We are going to put this to good use.

passages.title: Boaring Company
passages.text:
I don't see her body anywhere. That means she could still be alive.

The Briarback have been taking prisoners, and anyone who has ever been taken by them was never seen again.

We have a single chance here and we need to take it!

Come with me into the kraul and free as many of the survivors as you can. And if you can, find Farmer Deal. See if she's still alive.

passages.title: Boaring Company
passages.text: Please, find the prisoners!

passages.title: Boaring Company
passages.text: I was sure they were done for. You have my thanks.

passages.title: Look Out!
passages.text:
Some of these quilboar are clearly lookouts. Those horns make it obvious, almost like I could see their task floating above their heads.

I was able to kill one, but not before he blew that horn of his and summoned backup. I suggest you keep them silent before they do the same with you.

If we're going to get anywhere in there, you'll need to do it quietly. Here, Hobbs gave me a few of his sleeping darts. That should keep them quiet.

passages.title: Look Out!
passages.text: I'm amazed I made it here. This place is so heavily guarded...

passages.title: Rock Meet Dynamite
passages.text:
Thanks for your help out there, but we have to ask another favor from you.

These elementals must be coming from somewhere in the mine and we need you to locate that source. 

You seem more than capable of handling yourself in there, but just for extra security I am going to send you with some of Prim's special dynamite. It has an extra kick from the Azerite dust that you gathered.

Get in. Find the source. Put a stop to these elementals.

passages.title: Rock Meet Dynamite
passages.text:
A trogg? Hmmm... He may have eaten quite a bit of Azerite to be able to cause all this.

With him gone, now we can clear out the remaining creatures here and get back to digging! Thank you for your help.

passages.title: Cleanup Duty
passages.text:
Wh...why, why is all of the honey alive and what happened to everybody?

You don't think... oh no! Please, <name>, tell me they haven't been eaten!

Ahhhh! That would be terrible. Please don't let me be eaten too!

passages.title: Cleanup Duty
passages.text: Thanks for getting rid of those things, <name>.

passages.title: War Pigs
passages.text:
They look cute enough now, but that's a new herd of battleboars in training.

Farmers don't like waste, and it would be a shame to get rid of such useful creatures.

Either way, we could use those pigs, and I'd rather have them with us rather than face a bloodthirsty one in a few years. You should find them up on top of the cliffs overlooking the center of the kraul. Go round up as many piglets as you can take with you and we'll make good use of them.

passages.title: War Pigs
passages.text: I will take these and make sure they get to the farms for proper training.

passages.title: Run For the Hills
passages.text:
The quilboar are up to something, something big. You need to stop it!

They've been busy bringing supplies up to the caves above their sanctum. Preserved thorns, cauldrons of venom, giant totems...

They're preparing for war.

Get up there and destroy those stockpiles before they can be used against the citizens of the valley!

passages.title: Run For the Hills
passages.text: Those supplies you destroyed should set them back. They must have been saving them for a while...

passages.title: Anger in a Bottle
passages.text:
<The bottle the quilboar was carrying contains a foul-smelling, orange liquid. You're not sure if it's safe to drink, but it can't hurt to gather some samples to bring back to the citizens of Brennadam.

Maybe their alchemist can come up with an antidote to counter its effects.>

passages.title: Anger in a Bottle
passages.text: Do you have something for me?

passages.title: Anger in a Bottle
passages.text: This stuff smells awful. Maybe Hobbs will know what to do with it. Once we get out of here I'll make sure these samples get to him.

passages.title: Terror of the Kraul
passages.text:
By all the gods of the sea, what a monster!

I can barely believe what I am seeing, <name>. This ettin has undergone the same ritual that the brutes do, and it seems even angrier! If he gets out of here, we won't stand a chance.

I know I ask the impossible, but I must: kill this monstrosity and save the whole valley from its wrath! Here, take one of the potion samples you brought me. It's probably dangerous, but you might need it to defeat this beast.

passages.title: Terror of the Kraul
passages.text: We have to kill that thing!

passages.title: Terror of the Kraul
passages.text: It's done! I was afraid you were done for, but you've saved us all!

passages.title: Deeper into the Woods
passages.text:
We need to go deeper into the forest. The witches are clearly up to something even worse than I'd imagined.

As much as I have a duty to return to Lady Lucille with Master Ashton, I also have a duty to find out more about this threat to our people, and stop it if I can.

Going further into the forest is not without risk, but I believe it is one worth taking.

passages.title: Deeper into the Woods
passages.text: The risk has paid off

passages.title: Deeper into the Woods
passages.text: By my ancestors' anchors that is a large army! At least it doesn't appear to be mobile yet. And the tree... Clearly it is the focus of their efforts.

passages.title: Ride With Me
passages.text:
I have hunted many powerful foes, adventurer. My pack has defended this island and its people from countless outside threats and foreign invaders.

But there is a darkness growing in Zandalar. A corruption so deep and relentless that it consumes the minds of the Zandalari.

I cannot hunt intangible darkness, but I can hunt those who wield it against my people.

Come, ride with me and my pack. I smell the foul stench of blood trolls nearby. We will see how well you hunt with the pack.

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Reel Big Fish
passages.text:
Can ye believe the nerve of these scallywags? Questioning the very Coxswain of this here wharf?

Bah!

Lend me your ear for a moment or three. I've got a tale that'll put brew in your mug and a quiver in your boots!

It was the biggest, deadliest cache I ever did loot on these seas...

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Reel Big Fish
passages.text: Want to hear more?

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Reel Big Fish
passages.text: Don't listen to either of 'em. True every word, I tell ya!

passages.title: Indefatigable Purpose
passages.text:
Its grip weakens, if only briefly. We must claim this place anew!

Flopping, nightmarish horrors have infested the caves amongst the cove. Take the sacred blessings. Venture forth into the dark and find their altars. 

Purge their blasphemous constructions from our lands!

passages.title: Indefatigable Purpose
passages.text: A victory... perhaps a turning point.

passages.title: Flush Them Out
passages.text:
They lurk in the shadows, in the salt-soaked caverns. The dark brine beneath the pure gleam of the surface.

I have seen them. They plague my dreams, their whispers are maddening. They speak of their master, clawing at the barrier...

Search the cliffs for their warrens. Find what lurks within and obliterate them all.

passages.title: Flush Them Out
passages.text: Ignorance of our enemy will invariably lead to defeat.

passages.title: Flush Them Out
passages.text: The things are driven back, for a time.

passages.title: Trinkets and Baubles
passages.text:
Beneath the tides, these terrors do not see fit to stay within their warrens.

They have emerged in the night, stealing away to the villages and indulging in their avarice. They will use the provisions against us, to serve in their rituals. Rituals of summoning and communion with powers too terrible to comprehend. 

The populace is no concern of mine anymore, but I would not see these briny thieves to have their way. Relieve them of their plunder, and let them learn a bitter lesson.

passages.title: Trinkets and Baubles
passages.text: Where there is no peril, there can be no glory!

passages.title: Trinkets and Baubles
passages.text: Paid for in blood.

passages.title: The Weight of My Ambition
passages.text:
As with the other settlements, I too relied on the services of sailors and watercraft to deliver supplies. They proved very useful in their diligence, and their silence.

Predictably, they drew the attention of enemies, including those below the waves. Their anchor was hexed, dragging them beneath the ocean before they could so much as cry out.

I have seen them, hoisting ethereal sails and singing shanties of the damned. If these waters are to be safe again, they must be silenced again. For good.

passages.title: The Weight of My Ambition
passages.text: Finally, a sailor's death.

passages.title: Malign Inspiration
passages.text:
A long time ago, there was a maiden.

A precocious child fond of song, she made it her hobby to shadow my every move. Charming at first.

Walking on the pier's edge, she became entangled within the ropes surrounding a leering idol. At that time a tremor ran through the waves, giving the small push needed to send them both beneath the surface.

I can hear her song still. At first I thought it a passing fancy, music upon the waves. I realize now the voice comes with sinister purpose.

She must die.

passages.title: Malign Inspiration
passages.text: She was made their queen, and their slave.

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Gun Fishin'
passages.text:
Hook's got a screw loose in her head, I tell ya. Sharks workin' together on somethin'... phooey!

It does remind me of one of my favorite tales, though. Have I ever told ya 'bout the time I caught THE single largest, deadliest, most tentacled beast in all o' Azeroth?!

Aye, I thought not. It's not a story I'd tell ya sober. It was a day unlike any other...

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Gun Fishin'
passages.text: Aye, lad?

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Gun Fishin'
passages.text: Ozumat ain't around on account of I shot the blasted beast in its slimy face! Swear on me beard every word is true!

passages.title: A Child of Pa'ku
passages.text:
<The pterrordax egg is warm and trembling. It will hatch soon.>

Perhaps a certain pterrordax loa can help you.

passages.title: A Child of Pa'ku
passages.text:
An egg? It does not appear to be one of my brood.

Where did you find this?

passages.title: The Call of the Skies
passages.text:
<Kua'fon turns his head toward the cliff and chirps eagerly. He spreads his tiny wings and flaps vigorously.>

It is time to leave the nest.

passages.title: The Call of the Skies
passages.text: What do you need, grounded one?

passages.title: The Call of the Skies
passages.text: I regret to say that this is life in the skies, sometimes. Not all hatchlings live to adulthood.

passages.title: A Pterrible Fate
passages.text:
<Kua'fon peers longingly toward the horizon and gives a keening cry.

You can take the pterrordax from the sky, but not the sky from the pterrordax. It's time to do something.

Perhaps Pa'ku could offer some advice.>

passages.title: A Pterrible Fate
passages.text:
It is good that you came to me. I was considering throwing the thing off the roost again.

Perhaps there is another way.

passages.title: Aerial Aspirations
passages.text:
<Kua'fon studies you intensely. One single golden eye is trained on you, unwavering.>

Skree.

<He then turns his maw toward the horizon and spreads his wings wide.>

Skree!

<Is it finally time?>

passages.title: Aerial Aspirations
passages.text: <Kua'fon wheezes.>

passages.title: Fear of Falling
passages.text:
Some young find their wings sooner than others. At least yours had the sense to keep them open.

I would not worry too much about its safety- little ones tend to bounce.

As for this failure... the young must keep trying, and they must learn not to fear falling. It is now your task to teach it.

<The loa smiles at you, all teeth.>

If it is reluctant to learn, you might consider bribery.

passages.title: Fear of Falling
passages.text:
<Kua'fon quivers in fear and chirps at you in distress.

Perhaps a treat could soothe your hatchling?>

passages.title: Fear of Falling
passages.text: <The hatchling inspects your hands warily.>

passages.title: SKREEEEE!
passages.text:
<Kua'fon stares at you for a moment, then opens his maw and unleashes a continuous screech.

You need help.>

passages.title: SKREEEEE!
passages.text:
<The hatchling's gaze scours your person in search of anything edible. It may be best to keep your fingers out of reach.>

Skree!? Skree!

passages.title: SKREEEEE!
passages.text:
<Kua'fon swallows the dino chow whole.>

Skree.

passages.title: Back to the Nest
passages.text:
<Kua'fon peers up at you trustingly.>

Now would be a good time to take him back to the nest.

passages.title: Back to the Nest
passages.text:
<The hatchling settles into the nest.>

Skree.

passages.title: Ruin Has Come
passages.text:
There is a terror beneath the waves. It seeks to destroy my family, my house, and my legacy.

You must come, claim your destiny and deliver us from the terrors of the deep!

Find our estate to the east, among the isles. We lived opulently in the shadow of the great fortress. We believed the priests would deliver us from the darkness below. Now that darkness has bubbled to the surface, whispering madness in our dreams.

Hurry. The air turns the darkest I have seen in my cursed existence.

passages.title: Ruin Has Come
passages.text: You have answered the letter. Now you are bound to this place.

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Sink and Swim
passages.text:
Mph mph!

Mph mph mph mph mph. Mph mph mph.

Mph.

Mph mph? Mph!

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Sink and Swim
passages.text: Mph?

passages.title: Deadliest Cache: Sink and Swim
passages.text: Mph mph mph. Mph.

passages.title: Zanchuli Disbanded
passages.text:
I would like to say we are doing well, but we are not.

De Zanchuli Council is broken. Raal and I are all dat remain who are still loyal to King Rastakhan. You best bring news to your Horde and tell dem what transpired here.

Raal and I will rally what support we can and head for de Zocalo.

And hero, thank you for saving my life and my loa.

passages.title: Zanchuli Disbanded
passages.text: Only two of their six most sacred advisors? I had hoped more would have revoked the dark path they are on.

passages.title: Controlling the Situation
passages.text:
I have been observing this macabre army of, wood, flesh, and bone and how the witches and servitors control the lesser creations with charms. I believe I can craft an even more powerful charm - one we can use.

In the hearts of the servitors are the very strongest charms. They are used to anchor the Ancient Drust into their physical forms. They are precisely what we need.

Good luck. It is doubtful that they will part with them easily.

passages.title: Controlling the Situation
passages.text: Were you able to collect enough charms?

passages.title: Controlling the Situation
passages.text: Excellent. I should be able to do some... Interesting things with these.

passages.title: An Offensive Harvest
passages.text:
So you're takin the fight to the coven with the Waycrest girl, eh? Ya might just be able to take advantage of their apparent onion aversion.

While you're out rootin' in the field, keep an eye out for any onions bulging out of the ground. Those ones should be particularly aromatic, and should cause some fits in the coven's minions if you keep it on ya.

Just try not to take too much, right? I need enough left in the fields to keep the farm safe.

passages.title: An Offensive Harvest
passages.text: Did ya find any good ones?

passages.title: An Offensive Harvest
passages.text: That bunch should serve ya well.

passages.title: Eating Through the Defenses
passages.text:
Not sure why and don't rightly care, but for some reason the coven can't come near my onion field. So long as my crop doesn't give out, I can hole up in here as long as it takes.

Unfortunately, those boars got the same idea and now they're eatin' up my harvest! If they keep that up, soon there'll be nothin' keepin' the coven at bay!

If you can do me a favor and thin them out, I'd be happy to let you take some of these onions with you.

passages.title: Eating Through the Defenses
passages.text: How's the boar situation?

passages.title: Eating Through the Defenses
passages.text:
That oughtta do it for a spell.

Thanks for the help, stranger.

passages.title: A Traitor's Death
passages.text:
It has come to my attention that you intend to assault the camp outside of the walls. If this is so, I have a request.

Though most of the guardsmen who fight against us were turned to the coven against their will, Captain Goodspeed and his brigade of halberdiers gave their souls willingly to the Heartsbane. They are traitors and an affront to the Waycrest Guard.

You will find Goodspeed and his men stationed at the camp. I would consider it a personal favor if you would cut them down to the last.

passages.title: A Traitor's Death
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: A Traitor's Death
passages.text:
Captain Goodspeed was a stain on the reputation of the Waycrest Guard.

I hope his end was painful.

passages.title: Leaving the Nest
passages.text:
It looks like the coven hasn't managed to enthrall all of our falcons. I can see some untainted ones still in cages in the training yard.

Our falcons are well trained, and should know to fly to one of our other yards if something happens to their handlers. 

If you can just release them from their cages, they should be able to make it to safety.

passages.title: Leaving the Nest
passages.text:
Nice work!  With any luck, the falcons should head back to roost at Arom's Stand.

Though really, I'd prefer they be anywhere other than in the coven's clutches.

You have my thanks.

passages.title: The Warchief Awaits
passages.text:
<name>,

There are important matters I would like to discuss with you, but discretion is of the utmost importance. 

Meet me in my chambers in the Undercity where I can assure our privacy has not been compromised. 

Ensure that you are not followed; Orgrimmar has become riddled with SI:7 spies. It would seem that that King Anduin and Mathias Shaw are desperate to know what our next move is. How admirable.

passages.title: The Warchief Awaits
passages.text: Glad you could make it so quickly, <name>.

passages.title: In the Hall of the Drust King
passages.text:
I've been watching a lot of activity going on at the ruins at the base of the massive tree by the lake. What Master Ashton reported is accurate - something important is going on down there. 

We've disrupted their rituals but I worry we might have been too late.

We need to go over there. If there is anything remaining, we must destroy it.

passages.title: In the Hall of the Drust King
passages.text: We must confront Gorak Tul.

passages.title: In the Hall of the Drust King
passages.text: We've wounded him or he wouldn't have retreated as he did. Our victory won't last long unless we do something about his army.

passages.title: Fetching Wrex
passages.text:
When all the commotion started, Ancel's pup ran off. The poor thing was terrified!

A couple farmhands went to look for him, but with all of these monsters terrorizing the farm, I fear the worst!

Can you keep an eye out for Wrex while you're up in the hills? He might have gotten trapped in the honey too.

passages.title: Fetching Wrex
passages.text: Ancel will be happy to know that Wrex is safe and sound!

passages.title: Honey Glazed Sam
passages.text:
Think I heard someone shouting down yonder.

<name>, there might be trouble. Let's go!

passages.title: Honey Glazed Sam
passages.text: I thought I was a goner for sure!

passages.title: Witch Way Out?
passages.text:
There are other Falconhurst citizens to be freed before they become sacrifices.

Free anyone you come across.

The key used to free Master Ashton should still work. Good luck!

passages.title: Witch Way Out?
passages.text: Well done! Not only did you save innocents, you denied the witches fuel for their Grand Rite.

passages.title: Under Their Noses
passages.text:
Figures they wouldn't just put the destination on the crates for us. 

Nothing's ever easy, is it?

If the weapons aren't moving on Cagney's ferry, they must be passing through Bridgeport, the shipping hub just up the road.
