passages.text: Do you have my mind enhancer?

passages.title: Heavy is the Head
passages.text:
Haha! Take that Surgios! 

Look how cool this thing is! You can see why its so precious now.

passages.title: A Stitch in Time
passages.text:
Hm...I don't know that I've ever been to this time, before.

I suppose I should explain myself. My name is Delormi, and I'm the last remaining member of the Synchronous Tailors.

We make sure the fabric of time stays, well, mended. But I've found a number of new tears cropping up.

In fact, I believe that's why I've arrived here in this time. Perhaps you could assist me in tracking them down and repairing them?

passages.title: A Stitch in Time
passages.text: Something strange is happening. These tears have become too frequent as of late.

passages.title: A Stitch in Time
passages.text: And that takes care of those, although...Something's still wrong...

passages.title: The Severed Thread
passages.text:
Do you see that? There's a corpse just ahead.

To think the caverns have been so badly overrun...

We should look at the bodies. Maybe there will be something of use to us.

passages.title: The Severed Thread
passages.text: An ominous portent, isn't it?

passages.title: Rolling Up the Sleeves
passages.text:
The Caverns of Time? Strange... I spent many timelines in this very place.

What's special about here-- now?

We'll have to discern as much later on. It looks like we aren't the only ones who've been affected by these rifts...

Let's do the Bronze Dragonflight a favor and clear out these anomalies.

passages.title: Rolling Up the Sleeves
passages.text: It seems no matter when one is, there's always something to fight...

passages.title: Whatever Happened to Saffy Flivvers?
passages.text:
When Azerite was discovered, my friend Saffy was sent to investigate what it could do. There was an attack and we all thought she'd died. Then it turns out she was forced to work in some kind of goblin think tank in Tanaris! But before we could get her out, the whole place exploded.

Now, my bosses have written her off as dead. But she wasn't dead the first time so I'm not sure she is now. I've been told not to go looking for her, but you could take a look.

Find Saffy, or what's left of her?

passages.title: Whatever Happened to Saffy Flivvers?
passages.text: <You find the charred pieces of some mechanical contraption. A parrot, maybe? It isn't Saffy Flivvers, but it's evidence of her work. Perhaps there are more clues to be found in the area.>

passages.title: Some Reassembly Required
passages.text:
<The word "Feathers" has been etched onto the broken mechanical creature -- the sort of thing the person you are looking for might have created. Collecting the pieces and recreating the mechanical construct will surely give you a clue as to their fate. 

The area is crawling with Venture Co. scavengers and goons. Their pockets are probably filled with mechanical bits you could use to fix Feathers.>

passages.title: Some Reassembly Required
passages.text: <You seem to have collected all the pieces.>

passages.title: Some Reassembly Required
passages.text:
<The pieces go together with some judicious use of applied force and acerbic verbal encouragement. Hopefully the extra pieces you have on hand weren't critical.

The mechanical parrot now hovers unevenly over the sand.>

passages.title: Whatever Happened to Grizzek Fizzwrench?
passages.text:
When this whole Azerite mess began I had a goblin named Grizzek Fizzwrench do some research for me. He was bad for business and had to be removed from the picture. I thought it was a done deal, only now I'm hearing maybe he's not so dead.

I need you to hunt this guy down and see what happened. If he's alive, eliminate him and I'll add the standard mercenary fee to your reward.

passages.title: Whatever Happened to Grizzek Fizzwrench?
passages.text: <You find the charred pieces of some mechanical contraption. A parrot maybe? It isn't Grizzek Fizzwrench, but it's evidence of his work. Perhaps there are more clues to be found in the area.>

passages.title: Re-parrot
passages.text:
<Though very damaged, and filled with insects, you can tell Feathers seems to have some sort of recall program. 

Fixing the mechanical bird and following it back to the source may bring you to the person you seek.

You were able to put the thing back together. How hard could debugging a mechanical parrot be?>

passages.title: Re-parrot
passages.text:
<Debugging Feathers involved actual bugs. Gross. But the mechanical creature seems to be moving better.>

Hello! Systems operating within normal parameters! Hello!

<Feathers looks at you, awaiting input.>

passages.title: Return to the Nest
passages.text: <You decide to activate the recall subroutine. Perhaps the parrot will lead you to the person you are looking for.>

passages.title: Return to the Nest
passages.text:
Feathers! You put him back together!

That's wonderful but... If you could find us then so can others.

passages.title: She's in a Happier Place
passages.text:
Aww, Kelsey...she's been such a good friend. I meant to let her know I was alive eventually, but I got distracted.

Azerite, the war, the near-death experience... We've been really busy. Being presumed dead has some advantages, though. We've done a lot of research and we just need a better lab-

Okay. New plan. Tell Kelsey we'll be in touch, but only Kelsey. Tell everyone else I'm dead - for now. If you keep quiet about Grizzek, you- you can have Feathers.

Do we have a deal?

passages.title: She's in a Happier Place
passages.text:
She's alive?! That's great! I can't wait to catch up and see what she's been working on. I wasn't always a fan of Grizzek's -- he could really grind Saffy's gears! But if they're together again, then it's a packaged deal. Hmmmmm.

<Kelsey looks thoughtful for a moment before a sly grin spreads across her face>

I have an idea or two. You don't worry about a thing, <name>. Enjoy the parrot!

passages.title: He's Dead, Jastor
passages.text:
Hey, uh, so I got a good thing goin' on here, and I really don't want Gallywix to know I'm alive.

I'll make you a deal. You spin some story about how you only found tiny pieces of me spread across Tanaris and that I am totally dead, and... And you can keep the bird.

Deal?

passages.title: He's Dead, Jastor
passages.text:
Nice work convincing Gallywix, <name>. If I didn't know any better I'd have thought Grizzek was actually dead.

He's alive right? Right.

Anyway, here's your bonus pay. Let's just keep this between us, okay?

passages.title: A Queen's Entourage
passages.text:
Princess Talanji was very clear in her orders.

You, <name>, are to join her at de steps of Zanchul. She wishes to have you at her side while she undergoes de rite of queens and kings. I hope you can comprehend what an honor that is.

De queen-to-be will explain what it is you are to do.

Now go, and Pa'ku's winds make you swift.

passages.title: A Queen's Entourage
passages.text:
There you are. I am glad you could make it, <name>.

I am eager to show you how my people celebrate such an occasion.

passages.title: The Rite of Kings and Queens
passages.text:
Now that you are here, we can begin this sacred rite.

Take your place beside Talanji, <name>. She has chosen you for an important task. I will explain while we make our way to Zanchul.

passages.title: The Rite of Kings and Queens
passages.text: Your have more than earned such an honor, <name>.

passages.title: The Rite of Kings and Queens
passages.text: Such an occasion warrants a great deal of ceremony, <name>. Do not worry- there is plenty for you to do while Talanji prepares for what is to come.

passages.title: The New Zanchuli Council
passages.text:
These are sobering developments <name>.

I wish to speak to my priests about what has transpired. I would like you to continue into de depths of Zanchul and up de steps into de Council Chambers. There you will find de new council I have assembled.

Greet them, and make note of my choices. I hope you will find them adequate.

passages.title: The New Zanchuli Council
passages.text: What do you think of my choices, <name>?

passages.title: The New Zanchuli Council
passages.text: I arm myself with de knowledge and wisdom of others in ways my father did not. I hope it is enough.

passages.title: The Instigator Among Us
passages.text:
This situation can be swiftly dealt with if we take out de one that incited this violence.

I heard reports of an enforcer rousing de vagrants and drudges against de shopkeepers and guards in de Zocalo.

One of my own would not do this without cause. See if you can determine de reason for this sudden change.

I am told her name is Malzon. I hope for her sake that she surrenders.

passages.title: The Instigator Among Us
passages.text: If I understand de situation correctly, her concerns did not arise by chance. Be wary, <name>.

passages.title: The Council Has Spoken
passages.text:
Now that you see who I have chosen for my council, it is time to receive their blessing.

It is a symbolic demonstration of support, but I believe there is power in words as well as deeds. When they declare themselves to me, de eyes of de loa are also upon them.

I hope they like what they see, <name>. I know I do.

passages.title: The Council Has Spoken
passages.text:
I will not dwell now on de White Widow's words, but I am not dismissing her criticisms out of hand. I only wish she had chosen to speak to me instead of attacking from de shadows.

We could have worked together to solve de many problems of de Zandalari.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa
passages.text:
My council has given their blessing and we have dealt with an enemy. All that remains is to face de judgment of my loa.

I do not know what this part will be like. My father never spoke of it, at least not to me.

Walk with me. I will explain what is expected of you through this final trial.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa
passages.text: I trust you will restain yourself where you can, <name>. It is important that I overcome these trials on my own.

passages.title: Queen of the Zandalari
passages.text:
De loa have seen fit to grant me de crown. My council accepts me. My priests have given their blessing. My people have expressed their displeasure, but I am determined to right those wrongs.

It is time to accept de responsibility of leadership. I will address them and speak on our future. I would be honored if you would take a place at my side while I do so.

passages.title: Queen of the Zandalari
passages.text: I am resolved to bring our people together, <name>.

passages.title: A Royal Occasion
passages.text:
You wish to hear how the Zandalari joined the Horde? My people have had a... difficult history with the Zandalari.

However, I believe we dealt with the Zandalari of the past. The now Queen Talanji is much different from her father.

I'm rambling, my apologies. Our tale begins after the Alliance sacked the city of Zuldazar and killed King Rastakhan.

The Horde had been invited by the then Princess Talanji to witness her coronation in Zuldazar...

passages.title: A Royal Occasion
passages.text: There you are. De ceremonies are about to begin. De princess has requested your attendance at de steps of Zanchul.

passages.title: Vengeful Venture
passages.text:
<You pick up the note and deduce that the Venture Co. are the killers of Dataguru Gryzix. You search his corpse, and find that his decoder and the Ub3r-Spanner schematic have been stolen.

You need to retrieve his decoder and the schematic and bring them back to Shuga Blastcaps to have any hope of crafting the Ub3r-Spanner.

That mech you have following you should prove itself useful.>

passages.title: Vengeful Venture
passages.text: What's up, <name>? Did Gryzix handle that schematic for you?

passages.title: Vengeful Venture
passages.text:
He's dead? Poor sap, he was a damn fine engineer.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Something Valuable, Perhaps?
passages.text:
<The tablet is too worn to be read. While some of the characters are legible, reading the tablet will be impossible without assistance.

You can discern only a single word: Aegrim.>

passages.title: Something Valuable, Perhaps?
passages.text: You know I love a good artifact!

passages.title: Ancient Armor, Ancient Mystery
passages.text:
By my beard! Do you know what this is?! It's an ancient tablet that describes how to forge the Bulwark of the Mountain King!

The last one to wear that armor was Aegrim Bronzebeard, my ancestor and thane of the Bronzebeard clan.

Talk to Advisor Belgrum. He'll know more about Aegrim's past, and might be able to shine some light on the legends of his armor.

passages.title: Ancient Armor, Ancient Mystery
passages.text: You were wise to come to me. I think I can help!

passages.title: Watch Yer Back
passages.text:
Aegrim, you say? Bulwark of the Mountain King? Well, if we are going to start anywhere, it has to be Aegrim's study. The entrance lies below us in the depths of Old Ironforge.

The only trouble is the troggs in our way. How about you take the lead?

passages.title: Watch Yer Back
passages.text: The guards will tend to sealing the tunnels. We have important work to do.

passages.title: Keep Yer Feet On The Ground
passages.text:
<name>! The Explorers League is setting up a new exhibit in the Hall of Explorer.

A team of dwarves went in search of new artifacts to display in it.

They headed off to Gol'Bolar Quarry in Dun Morogh, but haven't returned. Would you mind checking in on them?

passages.title: Keep Yer Feet On The Ground
passages.text: <The team seems to have been guarding this dwarven tablet.>

passages.title: Aegrim's Study
passages.text:
This leads to Aegrim's study. I still have some scrolls to sort, so I will leave you to search the study at your leisure.

I'm sure Brann would be most interested in any of your findings.

passages.title: Aegrim's Study
passages.text: <The armor stand is empty.>

passages.title: Interest Yah In A Pint?
passages.text:
The armor may be shattered, but there's still hope. With the fragments you found, we might be able to forge it anew.

This is far outside my area of expertise, but there may be someone who can help. We should speak with Grumnus Steelshaper. He retired to Thelsamar in Loch Modan.

Go on ahead, I'll meet you there.

passages.title: Interest Yah In A Pint?
passages.text: Brann filled me in on what happened. This tablet will certainly help guide us.

passages.title: Shards of the Past
passages.text: <The armor that once was here has mysteriously shattered. Pieces of the ancient armor are scattered around the room.>

passages.title: Shards of the Past
passages.text: What do ye have here?

passages.title: Shards of the Past
passages.text: The armor is shattered? Hmmm...

passages.title: Earthen Blessing
passages.text:
Ignis will help with smelting the metal, but the heat from the forge will cook you in yer boots!

Our ancestors, the dwarves who forged Aegrim's armor, could sustain their stoneform for far longer than we can today. That's how they could forge the bulwark in the first place.

Luckily, my friend Bouldercrag can help us with that. He'll need some materials for the ritual.

passages.title: Earthen Blessing
passages.text: Do you have it?

passages.title: Earthen Blessing
passages.text: This will suffice.

passages.title: Recruiting the Furnace Master
passages.text:
Grumnus says we're going to need some help smelting this metal. I just happen to know someone who's perfect for the job.

We're heading to Ulduar!

Years ago, we fought against a construct named Ignis the Furnace Master. I've heard tell that the titan keepers brought him back, and Ulduar's furnace is alive once more.

passages.title: Recruiting the Furnace Master
passages.text: It's been a long time since I've been in Ulduar.

passages.title: Recruiting the Furnace Master
passages.text: With Ignis's help, we're one step closer to reforging this armor!

passages.title: Forging the Armor
passages.text:
It's time to begin. Bouldercrag, Ignis, and I are here to assist you.

You'll be the first dwarf to forge the Bulwark of the Mountain King in generations. This ol' blacksmith is honored to be able to witness this.

Are ye ready?

passages.title: Forging the Armor
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Forging the Armor
passages.text: I never thought I'd see the day.

passages.title: On Whispered Winds
passages.text:
<name>,

I have need of you.

Maiev and Shandris are en route to Stormwind to petition King Wrynn for aid in retaking Darkshore.

You have proven a loyal ally to my people in times past. I ask that you join their audience with the king and lend your voice to our cause.

I suspect we shall meet again soon.

-Tyrande

passages.title: On Whispered Winds
passages.text: I suspected Tyrande might reach out to you once she heard of our intentions.

passages.title: Tooling Around Vol'dun
passages.text:
Okay, <name>. We got almost everything we need. Almost.

You see, I lost my toolbox. I must have dropped it while running from the sethrak a couple days ago. Can ya fetch it for me? I'm not a very good engineer without my tools!

And take a mech with ya. I've spied some mysterious dwarven and troll figures lurking around... better not be the Venture Co. One whiff of the schematic being here and we got trouble.

You'll need the mind enhancer for it to follow you. Just put it on and you'll be good to go!

passages.title: Tooling Around Vol'dun
passages.text: <Gryzix appears to be dead.>

passages.title: Tooling Around Vol'dun
passages.text: <You place the toolbox on the ground, next to his corpse.>

passages.title: Waning Hope
passages.text:
The kaldorei have been steadfast members of the Alliance since the end of the Third War. We have fought on distant shores and even on different worlds without protest.

It is curious that in our moment of need, their resources are stretched too thin to lend so much as a single blade.

Wrynn has already denied Tyrande aid. Witness it for yourself.

passages.title: Waning Hope
passages.text: This will not stand.

passages.title: Waning Hope
passages.text: Nothing a human king says will deter Tyrande now, but he still has the chance to act.

passages.title: Our War Continues
passages.text:
The work to stop the Alliance is far from over, <name>. But thanks to you, we have the methods necessary to break them.

The Abyssal Scepter has been delivered to King Rastakhan, earning us more of his favor.

There is a matter of greater importance that I would speak to you about... but not here.

Meet me aboard the Banshee's Wail within Zuldazar.

passages.title: Our War Continues
passages.text: Derek Proudmoore's corpse will serve us well. In the meantime, we have more work to do.

passages.title: Our War Continues
passages.text:
The work to stop the Alliance is far from over, <name>. 

King Rastakhan now possesses the Abyssal Scepter that you recovered from the Kul Tirans. He has placed it... in his treasury. 

The Dark Lady wishes to speak with you regarding the corpse you found at the bottom of the ocean. Derek Proudmoore.

passages.title: Our War Continues
passages.text:
Our plans are in motion to bring down the Alliance and their allies.

We have much to do.

passages.title: Azerite Denied
passages.text:
The Kul Tirans and Alliance are amassing a vast amount of their Azerite and Azerite weapons within Tiragarde Sound.

They have a new supply of the resource, thanks to the Kul Tirans' conquest over Lady Ashvane and her company.

We must strike at their supplies of Azerite and destroy these weapons, or else we will be behind in this war.

You and Zelling will travel to Tiragarde Sound and meet with Rexxar. Lead the assault on their Azerite supply.

And do not return until you are victorious.

passages.title: Azerite Denied
passages.text:
<Rexxar nods.>

You're here. Our strongest warriors are eager to attack the estate.

Let's not keep them waiting.

passages.title: The Setting Sun
passages.text:
Remember the Sunwell.

We ride into battle with those words for a reason. We lost so much that day...

I lost so much that day.

Shine the lantern on the southern side of the island, where the Dead Scar meets the sea. There you will see how the fall of the Sunwell began. And with it, the last act of the High Elves.

passages.title: The Setting Sun
passages.text: Is it done, champion?

passages.title: The Setting Sun
passages.text: One final task remains.

passages.title: The Fury of the Horde
passages.text:
The Norwington Estate has a large cache of Azerite, along with the Alliance's latest Azerite weapons.

We need to steal these weapons and all of their Azerite. Every weapon stolen is a Horde life saved.

When you are ready to strike, let me know. I shall signal our warriors to begin the assault.

The Alliance and Kul Tirans will see the true might of the Horde!

passages.title: The Fury of the Horde
passages.text: The Alliance will see our might.

passages.title: The Fury of the Horde
passages.text: Our forces have the Kul Tirans pushed back. The hunt begins!

passages.title: Step Into Her Shoes
passages.text:
Another one of those rifts. Normally I'd repair it, but given the circumstances I wish to see where it leads.

It isn't often I commune with versions of myself from other threads of time. But one particular self has been a dear friend for some time.

I feel myself growing weaker. If she perishes...

We don't have much time. We need to enter this rift now.

passages.title: Step Into Her Shoes
passages.text: We must hurry--I fear the worst, otherwise.

passages.title: Step Into Her Shoes
passages.text: What...what's happening?!

passages.title: If The Shoe Fits...
passages.text:
That thing is killing her...it's killing *me*!

We need to stop it!

Please, I need your help to save my self!

passages.title: If The Shoe Fits...
passages.text: Please, we need your help!

passages.title: If The Shoe Fits...
passages.text: This can't be...why is this happening?!

passages.title: Saving Nine
passages.text:
I saw her in there, destroying another part of my timeline.

With every thread she severs, I lose myself more and more...

Perhaps I will perish, but I won't let her ruin the fabric of time.

I need you to join me one last time. 

I can only end this with your support.

passages.title: Saving Nine
passages.text: We can't fail. Not with what's at stake.

passages.title: Saving Nine
passages.text: This is the end, tailor. I will suffer this no longer.

passages.title: Killing Time
passages.text:
Now, <name>, stand with me.

I am weak. So many threads have been severed.

I'll use what power I have left to mend the rift.

Please...make sure the fabric of time is safe from her.

passages.title: Killing Time
passages.text: Please...I need your help!

passages.title: Killing Time
passages.text: So it's done, then. The final thread is severed.

passages.title: Guests at Grommash Hold
passages.text:
adventurer, I've received word that a vulpera caravan has arrived at Grommash Hold. They wish to address the Horde and have requested your presence.

I'm afraid it is not the best time for guests, so please see them as soon as you are able.

passages.title: Guests at Grommash Hold
passages.text:
I'm glad you've come, <name>. 

You should be the first to hear what we have to say.

passages.title: Cleaning Out the Estate
passages.text:
We must keep moving forward. Our goal is to weaken the Alliance, destroy their weapons, and steal their Azerite.

The three of us will carve a path of destruction through our enemies. Let us go!

passages.title: Cleaning Out the Estate
passages.text: Do not give in to the Alliance!

passages.title: Cleaning Out the Estate
passages.text: The Alliance and Kul Tirans are no match for our forces!

passages.title: Cut from the Same Cloth
passages.text:
My Infinite self was right. I can no longer mend time.

Too many of my threads have been purged. I can feel no others.

I'm alone now. And my thread is gone. But not you.

Take this recipe. You've proven yourself a talented tailor in your own time, and a savior in so many more.

The fabric of time needs your hands to mend it. I trust you with that responsibility.

Talk to me when you're ready. I'll take you back to when this all began.

passages.title: Writing on the Wall
passages.text:
Long has the southern wall separated Quel'Thalas from the once great kingdom of Lordaeron. We did not believe that anyone could breach it. That overconfidence was our undoing. 

When the Scourge arrived, the gate was not conquered by force. It was willingly opened by a traitor.

Though caught unaware, every Farstrider, soldier, and magister in the area rushed to the defense of our homeland. Very few of them returned home. The gates now stand as a memorial in their name.

passages.title: Writing on the Wall
passages.text: Take the time you need.

passages.title: Writing on the Wall
passages.text: And now to walk their path.

passages.title: Isolated Victory
passages.text: Alliance forces are pushing deeper into Vol'dun. We can not allow this aggression to go unchecked!

passages.title: Isolated Victory
passages.text: The vulpera appreciate the Horde's protection here. I didn't realize the Alliance could be so... relentless.

passages.title: Isolated Victory
passages.text:
On behalf of all the denizens of Vol'dun, thank you for your help in pushing back the Alliance invaders.

The people here have suffered enough threats without the Alliance adding to the list.

We will not forget the Horde's sacrifice here, nor yours.

passages.title: War Marches On
passages.text:
I hope the Horde will think twice about attacking Kul Tiras in the future, but given the actions of its leadership, it is a faint hope at best. Still, what matters most is my people are safe now.

The fleet and marines should be here soon to help the Outriggers clear out what remains of the Horde forces. Please return to High Commander Wyrmbane and let him know I will join everyone as soon as I am able.

Thank you for your swift actions today, <name>.

passages.title: War Marches On
passages.text: A successful operation, indeed. I'm glad we have Lady Jaina back among the members of the Alliance. We've done our best together but the added power of the Kul Tiran fleet, and their new Lord Admiral, may be just what we need to push this campaign forward.

passages.title: To Anglepoint
passages.text:
An attack on Anglepoint Wharf can only mean one thing: the Horde seeks to destroy the seagate there. 

This is my home. These are my people. I cannot turn my attention to our operations in Zandalar until we've routed the Horde.

The military will take a little time to mobilize, but in the meantime you and I can face these monsters. If we can't stop them, we can slow them down.

War has come to my shores once more. I will not stand aside.

passages.title: To Anglepoint
passages.text: The Horde has overrun the area. We cannot let this continue.

passages.title: To Anglepoint
passages.text: As I suspected, they're trying to establish a foothold and take out the seawall.

passages.title: A Declaration of Intent
passages.text:
Our caravan is ready to explore the world beyond the sands, but Nisha's blade can't be our only defense against the dangers we know await us. 

This is why we've come. 

To declare our intent to join the Horde.

passages.title: A Declaration of Intent
passages.text:
I am disappointed with his answer, but not surprised. 

Our strength is often overlooked.

passages.title: New Allies, New Problems
passages.text:
Baine certainly has his hands full. Taking on new allies means taking on new problems. 

Let us find out what troubles those within the Horde and see what we can do to help. 

Perhaps when Baine isn't so overwhelmed, he'll be able see our true value.

passages.title: New Allies, New Problems
passages.text: Let us find out what troubles those within the Horde and see what we can do to help.

passages.title: New Allies, New Problems
passages.text: Good work, <name>. Sometimes others just want to be heard.

passages.title: No Problem Too Small
passages.text:
These problems might seem small, but they will eat away at the Horde over time if they remain unaddressed. 

We must offer our help. 

The vulpera are skilled at solving problems, no matter their size.

I will investigate the outpost. Nisha and Meerah will see to the others.

Meet me in the Twilight Highlands when you're ready.

passages.title: No Problem Too Small
passages.text: Abandoned, just like Commander Dresh said.

passages.title: Where Are the Workers?
passages.text:
Look at this axe, adventurer. There's still sweat on the hilt. The workers were here not too long ago. 

Let's see if Sasha can track their scent.

passages.title: Where Are the Workers?
passages.text: This must be the place.

passages.title: Where Are the Workers?
passages.text: The peons are revolting? I'm surprised it took this long...

passages.title: A Little Goodwill
passages.text:
It sounds like the peons are feeling undervalued. They do important work for the Horde, but their diligence is often overlooked. A little goodwill would go a long way. 

Let's plan a feast in their honor. We'll need quite a bit of meat to sate their enormous appetites, luckily, I have a totem that can help with that. 

You acquire the ingredients, and I will make a meal guaranteed to boost morale.

passages.title: A Little Goodwill
passages.text: Did you bring the meat?

passages.title: A Little Goodwill
passages.text: We'll be eating well tonight, <name>.

passages.title: Worthwhile Repairs
passages.text:
The peons are right. These tools are inexcusable. 

How can they be expected to complete a job without the proper tools for their trade?

I can make the needed repairs, but I'll need some ore first.

passages.title: Worthwhile Repairs
passages.text: Have you found any ore?

passages.title: Worthwhile Repairs
passages.text: I can work with this.

passages.title: Peon Promotions!
passages.text:
I agree with the plight of the peons. They should be rewarded for the work they do.

It's unlikely that the Horde will agree to increase their wages, but there's no reason they can't be given a promotion. 

Any title other than peon would help build some confidence.

passages.title: Peon Promotions!
passages.text: Have the peons been promoted yet?

passages.title: Peon Promotions!
passages.text: I am sure your praise means a lot to the peons.

passages.title: Stand Fast
passages.text:
The Horde will pay for what it has done, but first I have to attend to the people here. 

<name>, I need to hold a portal open so the injured can evacuate to Boralus.

Keep the Horde's forces off me while the wounded get to safety. We can deal with them once the civilians are safe.

passages.title: Stand Fast
passages.text: That's the last of the wounded.

passages.title: Stand Fast
passages.text: If the attackers didn't know we were here before, they know now.

passages.title: A Party in Your Honor
passages.text:
I think I have everything needed to make tonight a success. 

We just need to make sure the peons show up.

Tell their leader that the Horde is throwing a party in their honor. 

I'm sure they won't decline a night of free food and drink.

passages.title: A Party in Your Honor
passages.text: It's a success, wouldn't you say?

passages.title: Strength and Honor
passages.text:
Those peons certainly look happy, don't they? I have no doubt they'll return to work in the morning. 

However, if their leader goes unchallenged, there will always be risk of revolt. 

You need to face him to battle. 

Show him the true strength of the Horde, but also the honor that comes with showing mercy.

passages.title: Strength and Honor
passages.text: Why don't you go show Foreman Magrok the true strength of your Horde?

passages.title: Strength and Honor
passages.text: As the peons would say: job's done.

passages.title: On the Outskirts
passages.text:
If things are settled for the Commander, you should check in on Nisha. 

I'm sure she could use your help.

passages.title: On the Outskirts
passages.text:
Sonji was right to be worried. 

The naga are planning an attack, but I've got a plan to stop them in their tracks.

We need to work fast, though.

passages.title: We'll Use Their Weapons
passages.text:
We're going to need special weapons to take down Tidecaller Nezara. Good thing it looks like the naga have plenty. 

We'll use their weapons against them. You and I know a thing or two about that. 

Grab an assortment. We'll need more than one.

passages.title: We'll Use Their Weapons
passages.text: You got those weapons?

passages.title: We'll Use Their Weapons
passages.text: Plenty to choose from. Perfect.

passages.title: Explosions Always Work
passages.text:
The area surrounding Tidecaller Nezara is heavily guarded, so I'll need you to create a distraction. 

Take these explosives. Plant them on the naga's harpoon launchers. Once they've been detonated, the blast should be more than enough to send the guards running!

passages.title: Explosions Always Work
passages.text: A fiery distraction is just what we need!

passages.title: Explosions Always Work
passages.text: You sure do excel at blowing things up!

passages.title: Taking Out the Tidecaller
passages.text:
Nezara's shield might be down, but that doesn't mean she's defenseless. 

There's a brute by her side that may cause trouble. I'll take a stab at him so you can take down the Tidecaller.

passages.title: Taking Out the Tidecaller
passages.text: You do good work, <name>. Always a pleasure.

passages.title: Meet with Meerah
passages.text:
It appears we're making good progress.

Would you meet up with Meerah?

I want to be sure she's found her way to the vintner in Suramar.

passages.title: Meet with Meerah
passages.text: Vintner Iltheux has some serious staffing issues.

passages.title: The Vintner's Assistants
passages.text:
Vintner Iltheux oversees all arcwine production for the Horde. 

He's used to making wine himself, but the Horde sent in help to speed up the process. 

It's had the opposite effect. 

We need to get to the bottom of this. 

How about you tour the vineyards and see how things are running? I have a few more questions for the vintner.

passages.title: The Vintner's Assistants
passages.text: Have you had a chance to see how things are running?

passages.title: The Vintner's Assistants
passages.text: It sounds to me like we've found our problem.

passages.title: Playing to Their Strengths
passages.text:
Iltheux isn't properly utilizing the help he's been given.

Let's fix that.

Assign new roles to the workers, ones more suited to their strengths.

If you need suggestions, I'm happy to help.

passages.title: Playing to Their Strengths
passages.text: Vintner Iltheux seems pleased. You've really got a knack for this, <name>!

passages.title: Fermented for the Horde
passages.text:
Vintner Iltheux's recipe doesn't need much improvement. 

Some unique ingredients and slight modifications to the winemaking process is all that's needed. 

I'm thinking adding fermented firebloom should do the trick. Then, filter it though a special cloth made from silkwing fibers. 

There are plenty of silkwings roaming the vineyard, and I have no doubt that Boss Mida can acquire the flowers, for a price.

passages.title: Fermented for the Horde
passages.text: Together, we will make a wine worthy of the Horde.

passages.title: Fermented for the Horde
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>. This will do just the trick.

passages.title: Sip and Savor
passages.text:
I think we're making wine, adventurer!

Let's see if the vintner approves of our vintage. 

Take a sample to Iltheux and see what he thinks.

passages.title: Sip and Savor
passages.text: I hope he likes the wine.

passages.title: Sip and Savor
passages.text: I think our work here is done!

passages.title: Awaiting Our Arrival
passages.text:
Let's head back to Orgrimmar.

I'm sure Kiro's expecting us. 

We really shouldn't make him wait.

passages.title: Awaiting Our Arrival
passages.text:
<name>, I have done the vulpera a disservice. 

I am afraid my oversight may have cost the Horde a notable ally.

passages.title: Besieged Allies
passages.text:
Seawalls can be rebuilt, but lives are lost for good. We need to secure the rest of the people here first.

The Outriggers have been known as some of the fiercest hunters in these waters. Find their leader, Rosaline Madison, and enlist her aid in liberating Anglepoint. Together, clear the north shore of the Horde, save anyone in danger, and rally the dock workers.

You handle the north shore, <name>. I will handle the south. We'll meet in the middle and crush the Horde between us.

passages.title: Besieged Allies
passages.text: You and the Lord Admiral are a sight for sore eyes, <name>.

passages.title: Repel the Horde!
passages.text:
The Horde has overrun Anglepoint, killing my people and destroying their livelihoods. Its raiders have come to Kul Tiras with killing on their minds. I cannot allow that to happen.

Slay any Horde Axe Throwers or Berserkers you see on the north shore. I will do the same on the south. Together we will stop this invasion.

passages.title: Repel the Horde!
passages.text:
I can see the Horde's ranks have thinned quite a bit.

I'm sure the Lord Admiral will be pleased. I know I am. Not bad, mainlander.

passages.title: The Hunt Never Ends
passages.text:
We have our victory, but we must move quickly to take the remaining Azerite from the estate.

Our forces should already be moving the Azerite from the manor into our gyrocopter support.

Let us move and ensure we get every ounce of Azerite away from the Alliance.

passages.title: The Hunt Never Ends
passages.text: We have our Azerite, but something doesn't feel right. The cannoneers should have been here by now.

passages.title: With Honor
passages.text:
The Alliance and Kul Tiran forces are in disarray. I can hear the Azerite tank powering up.

Lieutenant Cole intends to fight us... now that his forces are destroyed.

Let me know when you are ready to fight. The three of us shall destroy this tank while our warriors watch on!

passages.title: With Honor
passages.text: Are you ready?

passages.title: With Honor
passages.text: It is over. Cole, at least, died with some honor.

passages.title: Murder at the Brawl'gar Arena
passages.text:
The Brawl'gar quartermaster lies dead in front of you. He was murdered in broad daylight!

He must have been assassinated while someone was fighting in the arena. Maybe even during one of your fights.

Perhaps there are some clues nearby as to who might have killed him.

passages.title: Murder at the Brawl'gar Arena
passages.text:
So, you took it upon yourself to investigate the murder? Interesting...

<Commander Ravenhide jots something down, looks up at you, and then finishes writing his notes.>

passages.title: Put Up Your Dukes
passages.text:
You know what?

<The commander puts his notebook away.>

I COULD use a good <class> on my investigations team. We've had some personnel issues lately and, frankly, I can use all the help I can get.

But first: why don't you go hop into the arena for a few fights so I can get a good look at your skills?

passages.title: Put Up Your Dukes
passages.text:
While you were fighting, I took the liberty of looking into your background a bit, <name>. Quite impressive, I must say.

I apologize for my earlier suspicions. Welcome to the team.

passages.title: Outrigger Outfitters
passages.text:
My people met the Horde head on when they arrived, but we've been scattered over the wharf. The Horde has been relentless. We haven't been able to form a solid resistance force using just our fists as weapons.

But now the Lord Admiral is here with the champion of the Alliance. That's just the spark we need to rise up and kick these sorry mongrels out of our lands. If you can get my men some weapons, they'll join the fight!

Find those weapons and meet me back here. I'm working on a plan.

passages.title: Outrigger Outfitters
passages.text: For Kul Tiras! For the Lord Admiral!

passages.title: Outrigger Outfitters
passages.text: Now that my people are able to fight back, I have a plan to help stop more of these savages from fouling up my nice wharf.

passages.title: Undercover Agent: Sharisanda
passages.text:
Pit Boss Buxdoggle is one of our primary suspects in this case. Buxdoggle is an infamously aggressive speculator, and has a list of debts a mile long.

He may be in need of money, which is consistent with the evidence you found earlier.

Sharisanda has taken point on the case. I'd like you to assist her. I think you'll work well together.

passages.title: Undercover Agent: Sharisanda
passages.text:
<name>? Sharisanda. Pleased to make your acquaintance.

Buxdoggle is over dere, with de ridiculous hat on him.

No, no... don't just stare right at him! We're undercover, bonehead.

passages.title: Shots Fired
passages.text:
Horde invaders keep sailing in through the seagate, but we have a nasty surprise for them!

The Outriggers are good at fighting monsters of any sort, the Horde included. We'll keep them off you while you take out their boats.

Send 'em to the bottom of the harbor!

For Kul Tiras! For the Lord Admiral!

passages.title: Shots Fired
passages.text: That will hold the Horde for now.

passages.title: Shots Fired
passages.text: We've stopped the tide of Horde. Now we can address the goblin sappers.

passages.title: A Favor for Your Ol' Pal Buxdoggle
passages.text:
Hey, listen, I was thinkin' about somethin'...

You know how you won all that money from me? Well, funny story, that may have been slightly more money than I actually have, and now some very powerful people want to break my elbows and my knees.

I can't pay 'em! I'm broke! Heh heh!

All I need to get out of this hole is for you to lose your next fight. Flop like a fish. Please.

passages.title: A Favor for Your Ol' Pal Buxdoggle
passages.text: Please, ya gotta help me! They said they're gonna break my money bone! I don't even know where that is!

passages.title: A Favor for Your Ol' Pal Buxdoggle
passages.text: Thanks, <name>. You're a real pal.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Pit Boss Buxdoggle
passages.text:
I heard everything. That goblin sure does talk loudly about his crimes and debts, doesn't he?

It sounds like we have enough to bring him in for questioning. I've put together a packet of evidence for Commander Ravenhide to review.

Good job out dere.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Pit Boss Buxdoggle
passages.text: Find anything on Buxdoggle?

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Pit Boss Buxdoggle
passages.text:
<Commander Ravenhide looks over the evidence.>

This is more than enough to get a warrant. Excellent work, <name>. But your job's not over yet.

passages.title: Undercover Agent: Stone Guard Mollivox
passages.text:
I believe you've met one of my other agents: Stone Guard Mollivox. She's investigating our second suspect: Shadowmaster Skrizzik.

You'll find Mollivox near the arena's entrance.

passages.title: Undercover Agent: Stone Guard Mollivox
passages.text:
<name>? Mollivox. Nice to meet you. Again.

Skrizzik's over there. You go take point, I'll hang back and jump in if things get ugly.

passages.title: Cause for Concern
passages.text:
Shadowmaster Skrizzik's behavior was unusual.

His repeated mutterings about "shadow magic" and "void apocalypses" and "ancient creatures hungering for the souls of the living" certainly warrant further investigation.

You should report back to Stone Guard Mollivox.

passages.title: Cause for Concern
passages.text:
<Mollivox listens to your report.>

Hmm. Yes. I think I know what's going on. It looks like we're going to have to solve this problem with science.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Shadowmaster Skrizzik
passages.text:
Sounds like we've found our perp, <name>. This guy's sketchy, desperate, and his shadow magic is consistent with that shadowy scroll you found earlier.

Bring this packet to Arlu, and we can bring him in. Good work out there!

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Shadowmaster Skrizzik
passages.text: Any news on Skrizzik?

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Shadowmaster Skrizzik
passages.text:
<The commander looks over the notes.>

Wow. It's worse than I thought. We'd better bring him in soon, because this guy's a nut job.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Libbiara Blightrunner
passages.text:
Nugg got what Nugg need. Give stupid blood elf one drink and she start getting all self-incriminatey.

You bring packet to Commander. Nugg gonna buy some expensive snacks.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Libbiara Blightrunner
passages.text:
Hmm... I wouldn't be surprised if she killed the quartermaster just for her own entertainment.

For now, we can bring her in on counterfeiting charges, and get more details in court. Good work.

passages.title: The Brawl'gar Trial
passages.text:
I've issued three warrants. Nugg, Mollivox, and Sharisanda are apprehending the suspects as we speak.

It's time to go to court.

You may be called on to testify. Just answer as honestly as you can, and let the wheels of justice do the rest.

passages.title: The Brawl'gar Trial
passages.text:
I really think things were going well there... up to the point where it didn't.

Luckily for us, we've got a new lead. Listen up, <name> - your job isn't done yet.

passages.title: A Clue from Area 52
passages.text:
We've received a letter from Area 52, the goblin outpost in Netherstorm. The author claims to know details about what they call "the situation in Brawl'gar".

They don't say more than that.

I'm tied to my paperwork here. Go check out this lead and see if anything turns up.

passages.title: A Clue from Area 52
passages.text: These mysterious impostors may have gotten the better of me, and they may have gotten away with murder, but little do they know... I hold the trump card!

passages.title: Solving the Mystery
passages.text:
<Bazzelflange produces a challenge card from her pocket.>

I grabbed this challenge card from my attackers while we were fighting each other! I'm sure that you can use it to challenge my attacker to some sort of ultimate showdown!

passages.title: Solving the Mystery
passages.text:
I was there, <name>. I saw your fight.

We've had our suspicions about this "Watcher" character since the incident in Quel'Danas. It seems the rumors are true. They are watching us.

I'll relay the information to the correct authorities. Meanwhile, Boss Bazzelflange and I have arranged for a suitable reward for you. I hope you find it to your liking.

passages.title: Stopping the Sappers
passages.text:
The ice should keep the Horde out while we handle the sapper teams gathered on the beach.

I'm going to keep those Horde galleons busy. I need you to handle whoever is in charge and bring all the Azerite bombs you find back to me.

Then we'll handle disposing of their weapons.

passages.title: Stopping the Sappers
passages.text: Were you able to recover the bombs?

passages.title: Stopping the Sappers
passages.text:
The seagates have protected the heart of Tiragarde Sound for generations. Today is not the day Anglepoint falls.

As for those Azerite bombs... I have an idea.

passages.title: The Ub3r-Spanner
passages.text:
It's a shame that Gryzix had to die. Those Venture Co. make all of us enterprising types look bad!

At least we can still decode the Ub3r-Spanner schematic. Here, hand me that schematic and his decoder and I'll get this whipped up in just a second.

passages.title: The Ub3r-Spanner
passages.text: Here you go, <name>. Go forth and unleash your creations!

passages.title: A Friend in Needle
passages.text:
You can see me?

Oh, thank goodness! I thought I was lost in the folds of time...again!

But for one to see through the folds of time's fabric... you must be a very talented tailor, indeed.

Would you bring me some cloth, then, tailor? I believe I'll be able to place just when I am with your help and right myself.

passages.title: A Friend in Needle
passages.text: When in Azeroth am I...?

passages.title: A Friend in Needle
passages.text: You're back! That was fast--or, was it?

passages.title: Breaching Boralus
passages.text:
Finally! There's no place on Kul Tiras with a stronger Alliance presence. We must be bold and unrelenting if we're going to drive them out here.

Lok-tar ogar!

passages.title: Breaching Boralus
passages.text: What are you doing here? The Horde needs you in Tiragarde Sound!

passages.title: Breaching Boralus
passages.text:
I heard you made quite an impression on Boralus, <name>... Particularly its front gate! Ha!

For the Horde!

passages.title: A Stitch in Time
passages.text:
Hm...I don't know that I've ever been to this time, before.

I suppose I should explain myself. My name is Delormi, and I'm the last remaining member of the Synchronous Tailors.

We make sure the fabric of time stays, well, mended. But I've found a number of new tears cropping up.

In fact, I believe that's why I've arrived here in this time. Perhaps you could assist me in tracking them down and repairing them?

passages.title: A Stitch in Time
passages.text: Something strange is happening. These tears have become too frequent as of late.

passages.title: A Stitch in Time
passages.text: And that takes care of those, although...Something's still wrong...

passages.title: A Mech for a Goblin
passages.text:
Gallywix has a plan to deal with the Alliance and has requested your help. It involves the Azerite you reclaimed.

Speak with him down at Bilgewater Bonanza, and do whatever you can to help him... when it comes to the interest of the Horde.

Oh, and make sure Gallywix stays alive. The Alliance already tried to kill him.

passages.title: A Mech for a Goblin
passages.text: You're here! Good, 'cause we got ourselves problems.

passages.title: The Right Mech for the Job
passages.text:
Okay, <name>, we're good to go. The G.M.O.D has plenty of Azerite to cause some trouble!

We gotta head to my, er, OUR base in Drustvar. Mekkatorque, that freakin' king of the gnomes, is attacking our Azerite supply!

After we take care of the base, we're gonna take care of him! You get what I'm sayin'?

passages.title: The Right Mech for the Job
passages.text: You and Gallywix saved us! Never thought I'd say something nice about that chin waggler.

passages.title: In the Dunes
passages.text:
This schematic you found is encrypted. My tools are no good on it, not without risking the integrity of the data.

However, I do know a guy who can definitely crack this cookie: Mr. Dataguru Gryzix.

If I remember correctly, he's been vacationing on a beach in Vol'dun since the war broke out. Something about not getting the recognition he deserves. 

Anyways, I am sure you can convince him to help you.

passages.title: In the Dunes
passages.text: Ugh, what do you want?

passages.title: Vengeful Venture
passages.text:
<You pick up the note and deduce that the Venture Co. are the killers of Dataguru Gryzix. You search his corpse, and find that his decoder and the Ub3r-Spanner schematic have been stolen.

You need to retrieve his decoder and the schematic and bring them back to Layla Evenkeel to have any hope of crafting the Ub3r-Spanner.

That mech you have following you should prove itself useful.>

passages.title: Vengeful Venture
passages.text: What's up, <name>? Did Gryzix handle that schematic for you?

passages.title: Vengeful Venture
passages.text:
He's dead? Poor sap, he was a damn fine engineer.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Ub3r-Spanner
passages.text:
It's a shame that Gryzix had to die. Those Venture Co. make all of us enterprising types look bad!

At least we can still decode the Ub3r-Spanner schematic. Here, hand me that recipe and his decoder and I'll get this whipped up in just a second.

passages.title: The Ub3r-Spanner
passages.text: Here you go, <name>. Go forth and unleash your creations!

passages.title: Simply Dying of Boredom
passages.text:
Up until now, I've been dying of boredom up here. I think maybe we need some new blood here in the arena. Boss Bazzelflange can be so stingy with her invitations, can't she?

I've had one of my servants write up a few slightly-counterfeit invitations to hand out. Maybe you could help me get them distributed? There's always plenty of tough-looking characters hanging out in front of the auction house near Grommash Hold...

passages.title: Simply Dying of Boredom
passages.text:
You placed the sign? Good. Now we just wait for the newbies to show up.

I like you, <name>. You're like me: willing to commit a crime or two in the name of self-entertainment.

passages.title: Brawl'gar Awaits!
passages.text:
Tired of standing around in the boring old Valley of Strength? Come on over to the Brawl'gar Arena, and fight for the amusement of others!

You might win, or you might get killed, but either way, you're going to have a great time.

Grab an invitation and bring it to Skuglor, near the front door. Brawl'gar awaits!

passages.title: Brawl'gar Awaits!
passages.text:
<Skuglor inspects the invitation intently.>

Hmph. Looks good enough to me. Come on in.

passages.title: Warfront: The Battle for Darkshore
passages.text:
Darkshore belongs to the Horde! We must hold that ground to maintain our dominance over Kalimdor.

Prepare yourselves. Battle awaits!

passages.title: Warfront: The Battle for Darkshore
passages.text: We must do what we can to claim Darkshore for the Horde.

passages.title: Warfront: The Battle for Darkshore
passages.text: Well fought, <name>, though I'm sure it won't be long before the Alliance try to reclaim Darkshore. When they do, we will be ready to fight!

passages.title: Darkshore Recruits
passages.text:
We've got a few recruits that can help us take back Darkshore!

But first, we need our Ancient of War to be back up to good health. To help him, contribute resources to him and he'll perk right up!

Once the Ancient of War is restored, talk to Jarod Shadowsong and recruit a troop. I'm sure they could learn a lot from fighting alongside you.

passages.title: Darkshore Recruits
passages.text: Did you get those recruits?

passages.title: Darkshore Recruits
passages.text: Isn't it nice to have people follow you around sometimes?

passages.title: Armor for Armies
passages.text:
We need to make sure our soldiers have the best equipment possible in the battle against the Horde. 

Once the Hunter's Hall is constructed, speak with Cordressa Briarbow about how to improve the weapons and armor of our troops.

passages.title: Armor for Armies
passages.text: I regret many things that took us to this moment, but we will do what needs to be done.

passages.title: Armor for Armies
passages.text: How are our armaments looking?

passages.title: The Altar of Elders
passages.text:
Now that contributions are in full swing, the Altar of Elders has been rebuilt.

Go, speak with Moon Priestess Lasara to see what the Altar has to offer.

passages.title: The Altar of Elders
passages.text: Have you visited the Altar of Elders yet?

passages.title: The Altar of Elders
passages.text: With that kind of power at our call, we may just stand a chance.

passages.title: Glaiveworks For Me
passages.text:
We've all been on edge since Teldrassil, but Erion took it hard. He jumped at the chance to help out.

Why don't you talk to him and see what he's got going at the Glaiveworks?

passages.title: Glaiveworks For Me
passages.text: How may I help?

passages.title: Glaiveworks For Me
passages.text: Those glaives will make quick work of those Azerite-mech monstrosities.

passages.title: Cut from the Same Cloth
passages.text:
My Infinite self was right--I can no longer mend time.

Too many of my threads have been purged. I can feel no others.

I'm alone now. And my thread is gone. But not you.

Take this recipe. You've proven yourself a talented tailor in your own time, and a savior in so many more.

The fabric of time needs your hands to mend it. I trust you with that responsibility.

Talk to me when you're ready. I'll take you back to when this all began.

passages.title: Ride Out to Meet Them
passages.text:
We must defend our warriors from the Alliance army while we recover this Azerite.

Take the Azerite weapons you stole and load them onto one of these gyrocopters.

Misha and I will ride out and fight the reinforcements from the ground, while you provide air support.

We need to hold them off until our warriors can retreat with the Azerite.

passages.title: Ride Out to Meet Them
passages.text: You fought well! The day is won, and the Alliance has been weakened.

passages.title: Druids of Gloomtide
passages.text:
The latent power at Gloomtide Strand presents us with an opportunity to harness great power. One of our allies, Edgard, has great knowledge into what this might mean for our efforts.

Seek him out and discover the power of nature.

passages.title: Druids of Gloomtide
passages.text: Discover anything?

passages.title: Druids of Gloomtide
passages.text: The enemy stands little chance with this kind of power on our side.

passages.title: Flying at Night
passages.text:
Now that we control Ashwood Depot, it will be much more convenient to travel about the battlefield.

I've drafted plans for a flight network. It's a rather brilliant plan, if I do say so myself. You don't seem busy. Take my notes and deliver them to our commander at once.

Speak to Fidelio and he will provide you with a hippogryph.

passages.title: Flying at Night
passages.text: Excellent work. Though we did not need Mordent's hyperbolic account of his own role in opening the skies for us.

passages.title: Iron in Hand
passages.text:
This won't work at all! We need to gather iron if we want to make any kind of headway against the Horde.

Go down to the ruins at Lornesta and grab that iron. We need it!

passages.title: Iron in Hand
passages.text: We need to collect that iron!

passages.title: Iron in Hand
passages.text: Now we're in business!

passages.title: The War Chest
passages.text:
Welcome to the warfront, <name>! We finally get to see some action. 

Any resources we've collected will go to the War Chest. Once enough has been gathered there, you can grab it!

Why don't you pay it a visit and see what you get?

passages.title: The War Chest
passages.text: Got any of those resources from the War Chest?

passages.title: The War Chest
passages.text: Now we're in business!

passages.title: Gunpowder Plots
passages.text:
Since the Lord Admiral iced all of their zeppelins, the Horde are rowing in through the seagate.

The nice, narrow seagate entrance that makes for a great choke point.

I'll have my people haul over a cannon and some ammunition. If you collect some gunpowder, we'll set up behind the gate where they won't expect the attack.

We'll blast the Horde to the bottom of the harbor!

passages.title: Gunpowder Plots
passages.text: Did you find enough gunpowder?

passages.title: Gunpowder Plots
passages.text: Excellent! We're all set up here to take out the Horde's boats.

passages.title: The Day is Won
passages.text:
The majority of our warriors survived and we have the Alliance's Azerite and weapons.

Be proud of yourself, <name>. You fought with honor today.

Go and inform Nathanos of our victory here. The Azerite should reach them shortly.

passages.title: The Day is Won
passages.text:
I've heard of your victory. Well done. The Alliance will be reeling from this defeat.

The Azerite is being prepared as we speak for our next attack. The Dark Lady trusts you will be willing to aid, when the time comes.

passages.title: The Calm Before
passages.text:
A word, <name>.

There was a raid on the Norwington Estate, where we were testing some new designs of Azerite systems. Lady Jaina asked SI:7 to look into the matter. I have the report here.

I know the Proudmoore family wants a moment together before they're pulled apart again, but the war is still ongoing.

You have been a friend to her family. Take the report to Jaina. I believe they went to pay respects at the family memorial.

passages.title: The Calm Before
passages.text: The Horde cannot be allowed to think it can come to our lands without resistence.

passages.title: The Calm Before
passages.text: Another attack! The Horde is growing bold. I cannot let this stand.

passages.title: Shores of Fate
passages.text:
So be it. You are more trustworthy an ally than any army Wrynn would have sent.

We will reclaim Darkshore together, but first we must find Tyrande. Without her at the front, our forces will crumble against the Horde.

She left for the Zoram Strand with a small force not long ago. If we move now, we may be able to find her before the Horde does.

passages.title: Shores of Fate
passages.text: It seems our wayward priestess has been busy.

passages.title: Hope
passages.text:
No... it is not possible. She would not have died like this!

Search for signs of her departure along the strand. Personal effects. Weapons. Anything!

Tyrande is still out there, <name>. We must not lose hope.

passages.title: Hope
passages.text: Anything?

passages.title: Hope
passages.text: These would not have been set aside so carefully had she been slain. She is alive!

passages.title: In Darkest Night
passages.text:
<name>, I will not mince words. Tyrande foolishly risks her life with the ritual she intends to perform. If she falls, our entire war effort will fall with her.

We must set off for Darkshore and come to her aid. Only then can we march forward and reclaim our homeland.

We have lost Teldrassil. Fool or not, our people cannot afford to lose Tyrande as well.

passages.title: In Darkest Night
passages.text: Our vengeance has just begun.

passages.title: Warfront: The Battle for Darkshore
passages.text:
We will not tolerate further Horde aggression in our territories.

The night elves will not stand alone this day. Darkshore will be theirs once more.

For the Alliance!

passages.title: Warfront: The Battle for Darkshore
passages.text: Darkshore will be ours.

passages.title: Warfront: The Battle for Darkshore
passages.text:
The day is ours thanks to you, but this war is far from over.

For the Alliance!

passages.title: A Voice on the Wind
passages.text:
<A distant, mysterious voice fills your mind.>

My enchantments are not lost...

Find me...

Drustvar...

Fallhaven...

passages.title: A Voice on the Wind
passages.text:
Be at ease, friend. I don't want to hurt you. Instead, I have a proposition for you.

You see, I was a druid once and the only thing I loved more than tending to the forests and creatures within them was enchanting. 

Then I was murdered and cursed to wander this peninsula, unable to cross river nor mountain so long as my body still exists. 

If you destroy my old body and help me make a new one, I will teach you how I made the rod you disenchanted.

passages.title: The Tauren Tanner
passages.text:
Hey, rich mon.

One of ya Tauren stopped by and asked who was de best leatherworker I knew who doesn't mind gettin' their hands dirty.

I give 'im ya name, and he asked for an introduction. Said dat he would be in de Bazaar, by de docks.

He did not say what he needed ma best student for, but de way he was actin' makes me think it is somedin' big.

Head on down to de docks and find dis Tauren. Show 'im what I taught ya.

And focus! Needn't be havin' ya make me look bad!

passages.title: The Tauren Tanner
passages.text:
Earth Mother be praised!

We have much to discuss.

passages.title: Pick Up Sticks
passages.text:
In order for my enchantment to work, we'll need wood from these forests.

When I was alive, I would wander these woods and tend to the trees. While those trees are long gone, perhaps their grandseeds have heard their stories and would be willing to help me.

But don't cut down any of the trees! Please! There are loggers that cut and hew without care for the wilds. Take their hard work so that they will think twice before felling another tree.

Bring me as much wood as you can muster.

passages.title: Pick Up Sticks
passages.text: I miss the voices of the old forest.

passages.title: Pick Up Sticks
passages.text: Excellent! The wood appears devoid of pests and rot. Not too long or short. They look thick enough to bend, but only under stress. This will work perfectly!

passages.title: The Sixth Sense
passages.text:
For my plan to work, we need to break the spell on my body that is anchoring my spirit to this place.

However, my mortal remains are buried deep within this forest. There are wards within it that are designed to trap spirits who are still attached to the material world. Once my remains are cleansed, I will be able to move freely through the woods.

Until then, I'll need you to disenchant the wards we come across.

Speak to me when you are ready, and I will lead you to my grave.

passages.title: The Sixth Sense
passages.text:
Good work!

<Sef looks introspective for a moment.>

I just realized I never told you my plan.

passages.title: Exhumed
passages.text:
As I've said, I'm unable to interact with the material world.

I am able to dominate a creature to control its body, but I find it deplorable. In essence, it is enslaving the poor creature.

What I want is a body of my own. If you build and animate a golem, it would be devoid of intelligence. A shell. One that I could inhabit without issue.

Doing so will require that my soul is not anchored to anything else in this world, so I need you to remove the spell binding my spirit to my physical remains.

passages.title: Exhumed
passages.text: Seeing my old self brings back memories.

passages.title: Exhumed
passages.text:
I feel... different.

It's like I'm in the middle of an enormous pitch black room. Not literally, but there is a sensation that there is something lurking just outside of my sight that is... unsettling.

At least I don't have to worry about the spirit traps any longer, which is nice.

Regardless, with the spell tying me to my remains broken, there is nothing more for us here. Let us continue our journey south.

passages.title: The Threads That Bind
passages.text:
Our destination is near Gol Koval, but there is something else you could pick up along the way.

I don't want to ask because I hate them, but you cannot dispute the resilience of that horrible webbing that they manage to get everywhere.

<Sef grimaces at the thought.>

There are spiders to the southeast. As a guardian of nature, I don't want to say kill them, but if you could... 'obtain' some fresh silk from their bodies, we could use it to bind the limbs of the golem together.

passages.title: The Threads That Bind
passages.text: Did you get the silk?

passages.title: The Threads That Bind
passages.text:
<She shivers in disgust.>

Blech! The thought of that being part of my body makes me regret asking.

As a druid, I was told that there is beauty in all of nature, but I still see none in those spindly legged monstrosities.

Let's keep going. I don't like being near them.

passages.title: The Beat Goes On
passages.text:
We have most of the materials we need, but we require one final item. A heart.

Don't worry. I don't mean one of flesh, but of stone; to bind the materials of the body into a single form.

Find a smooth stone, and enchant it to hold a life force. It will require some reagents, but I would expect a powerful enchanter such as yourself to have some on hand or know where to find them.

Once that's done, it will need to be powered. The souls animating the elementals and undead here should do the trick.

passages.title: The Beat Goes On
passages.text:
That was the last item we needed.

Now we just need to go to my sanctum so we can assemble it undisturbed.

passages.title: We're Going In
passages.text:
This used to be a Drust shrine. There is a series of sigils that, once invoked, will allow us to teleport to my old sanctum.

<Sef looks around somewhat confused and clears her throat.>

It has been centuries since I've been here, I'm having a bit of trouble remembering the order in which the sigils need to be activated to open the portal.

I hope you're feeling adventurous. Oh, and be cautious. I enchanted the runes to keep would be intruders out by force.

passages.title: We're Going In
passages.text: Home sweet home!

passages.title: Putting It All Together
passages.text:
Hmm... Everything seems untouched.

We can begin construction of my new body over here. Afterwards, I'll teach you how to make my enchanting rod.

<Sef smiles at you, beaming with joy.>

passages.title: Putting It All Together
passages.text: This has been a long time coming.

passages.title: Putting It All Together
passages.text:
<Sef looks at you, distressed and heartbroken.>

I'm... We could try again, but... I think this is a sign... You seem more than capable of defending those who need it. Maybe it's time for me to move on. 

<Sef's frown turns into a half smile.>

I'm eternally grateful for what you did. I may not have a body, but because of you, I don't need one anymore.

Before I go, let me show you how I made my enchanting rod.

passages.title: Test Case #1; Mech vs. Mekkatorque
passages.text:
Alright, we got PLENTY of Azerite in this baby to blow up Mekkatorque and his airship.

That radioactive freak is gonna pay for sendin' his toys to attack one of MY, er, OUR bases!

Hop in, <name>. We got a gnome to blow up.

passages.title: Test Case #1; Mech vs. Mekkatorque
passages.text: This ain't over until the fat goblin sings, and buddy, I ain't singing!

passages.title: What the Drust Knew
passages.text:
Ahoy, <name>!

If you have a moment, I could use your assistance. I've recently received a large shipment of Drust relics that I've been processing.

Most of them have been nothing out of the ordinary, but there is this one that is special. Just holding it makes my hair stand on end. 

With you being my best pupil, I was thinking that it would be fun if we disenchanted it together, to see how it was made.

What do you say?

passages.title: What the Drust Knew
passages.text:
I'm sorry, <name>, I didn't think that enchantment would be so complex. I thought I could maintain the incantation.

I guess that's it. With the relic destroyed the technique behind its construction is lost.

A shame, really. It's not often that I'm left dumbfounded by another enchanter.

passages.title: A New Hope
passages.text:
Darkshore belongs to our people once more, in no small part due to your efforts. And, while I disagree with her methods, we would not have succeeded without Tyrande as well.

Differences aside, she is our leader--and an incarnation of the Night Warrior herself.

She is about to begin. You may stand here beside me.

passages.title: A New Hope
passages.text: Dori'thur laid this egg when Elune's shadow fell over us. If you are willing, I would entrust her offspring to your care as a token of my gratitude.

passages.title: Insurance Policy
passages.text:
Mekkatorque called us idiots, can you believe that? Well, if I'm an idiot, then why did I buy an insurance policy on my mech, huh?

I bet that radioactive dimwit doesn't have an insurance policy on HIS mech!

We're gonna be outta here in no time. I just gotta give a quick call for roadside assistance to come out and fix this thing up.

I need you to go hit the button for roadside assistance on my mech.

Just, uh, don't hit the wrong one.

passages.title: Insurance Policy
passages.text: You gonna call these guys up or what?

passages.title: Insurance Policy
passages.text:
Maybe I shoulda bought an insurance policy for my insurance policy. 

Wait, what am I talkin' about? YOU'RE the insurance policy for the insurance policy!

passages.title: Insurance Renewal
passages.text:
You know, all I wanna do is blow up Mekkatorque and whatever airship he's ridin' in. Of course it ain't gonna be easy!

I need you to go rescue my roadside assistance so they can fix this mech! They're probably in the Alliance camp near here.

Meanwhile, I'm gonna cook us up a plan. We're gonna give Mekkatorque a real nice surprise!

And by real nice surprise, I mean we're gonna blow him up. Oh, and also his airship.

passages.title: Insurance Renewal
passages.text:
These guys work fast, look at this thing, it's almost brand new!

Almost.

passages.title: Killing on the Side
passages.text:
Those annoying Alliance nearby are definitely takin' orders from Mekkatorque.

That means they gotta die! And any of their Kul Tiran friends, too. They gotta know the Horde is number one.

And that you don't kidnap someone's roadside assistance!

passages.title: Killing on the Side
passages.text:
Good work mopping up those guys, that'll show 'em to mess with the Horde! 

What? They weren't messin' with us? Of course they were, they kidnapped my insurance policy!

passages.title: Fortunate Souls
passages.text:
adventurer, I am glad to see that you survived the wreck. Many were not as fortunate...

I am capable of stalling the enemy here for now, but this position is not defensible long term.

We need to find somewhere safe for our forces.

Once we have taken measure of the wounded we will push on. In the meantime, find as many survivors as you can.

Nazjatar will claim no more Horde lives today!

passages.title: Fortunate Souls
passages.text: Save as many as you can. We are sorely outnumbered here.

passages.title: Fortunate Souls
passages.text: So few.... It will have to suffice. Without you, we would be even fewer.

passages.title: In Deep
passages.text:
I can keep this barrier up here for a time after our departure, but we cannot remain here.

These soldiers will not be safe for long.

We must go deeper into this place to seek a more defensible position.

passages.title: In Deep
passages.text: Careful! Don't draw attention.

passages.title: Descent
passages.text:
What has transpired! That is to say, what has transpired?! Yes, that is the appropriate response, is it not?

I find our circumstances enthralling! Yet, tragic.

I prattle on... Yes, Lor'themar asked me to send you to him at once. He is in need of your expertise, adventurer.

I'll lower you down the falls safely. Good luck!

passages.title: Descent
passages.text: We have already suffered great losses, <name>. Let us work together to prevent even more.

passages.title: The First Arcanist
passages.text:
Our situation is dire, adventurer.

The Horde fleet was decimated by the attack on Dazar'alor. This naga trap has claimed much of what we had left.

Survivors report seeing the naga taking captives. Thalyssra has gone on ahead to see what she can do to help them. 

I will finish up here while you aid the First Arcanist's efforts. My rangers will provide what little aid they can.

passages.title: The First Arcanist
passages.text: Ah, <name>. I am glad you survived the attack.

passages.title: Mekkatorque's Battle Plans
passages.text:
<You find part of plans that indicate where Mekkatorque will be in Tiragarde Sound, along with his airship.

If you could find the other half of these plans, you would be able to launch an ambush against the gnomish king.>

passages.title: Mekkatorque's Battle Plans
passages.text: What're you lookin' into?

passages.title: Mekkatorque's Battle Plans
passages.text:
What do ya got there?

... WHAT?! This is perfect!

passages.title: Job's Done
passages.text:
I'll stick around here a bit longer to ensure the peons get back to work. 

You should return to Orgrimmar and let Commander Dresh know that he does not need to fret about the outpost any longer.

passages.title: Job's Done
passages.text:
The peons have returned? That is good news, indeed.

Let us hope this doesn't happen again, for their sake.

passages.title: Threat Contained
passages.text:
That should keep those naga down!

You can have the honor of telling Bladeguard Sonji that the threat to Zuldazar's coast has been contained.

passages.title: Threat Contained
passages.text: The naga threat has been contained? I'll trust your word on this, <name>.

passages.title: Mech versus Airship
passages.text:
We're all set to go, thanks to them battle plans ya found. Looks like Mekko ain't gonna be at his airship right now.

Here's the plan. We're gonna go seriously mess up his ship, then Mekko is gonna swing by to try to save his friends.

But instead, he's gonna find you and me standin' on the deck of his burnin' ship, waitin' to take him out!

Get in to the mech, <name>, we're blowin' up an airship and a gnome!

passages.title: Mech versus Airship
passages.text: What a ride, huh?

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Krag'wa
passages.text:
Hello again, small one.

I see Talanji has chosen a worthy witness. I must test Talanji's willingness to sacrifice for her people. I will weigh her commitment to defending the weak. Many great rulers have failed this challenge and still gone on to make powerful monarchs.

But the most beloved, those that find themselves surrounded by loyal followers, always understand the value of devotion to their people.

You will help me with this trial. Speak to me when you are ready to begin.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Krag'wa
passages.text: It is my hope that Talanji will honor your faith in her this day.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Krag'wa
passages.text: I would allow no harm to come to you, <name>. Fortunately for you, an intervention was not needed.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Pa'ku
passages.text:
Two more loa have declared their intent to test Talanji. The next is Pa'ku. She awaits you both at the top of these steps.

I need not warn you about her tempestuous nature, nor her love for watching others fall from great heights.

Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Pa'ku
passages.text: I am not yet satisfied, <name>.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Pa'ku
passages.text:
<Pa'ku wipes a tear from her eye using her wing-claw.>

That was a beautiful demonstration of commitment. Your hair looks lovely.

<Pa'ku cackles.>

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Gonk
passages.text:
The Lord of the Pack has requested to be the next to speak to Talanji. He is just up the steps on the next terrace.

I do not think he will require quite as much of you as I did, but I believe his words will be relevant to your purposes here.

<Krag'wa winks one massive eye.>

Do not think we are not aware of your intentions, <name>.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Gonk
passages.text: Hello again, <name>.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Gonk
passages.text:
<The raptor god eyes you speculatively.>

You will serve to remind Talanji of her priorities, if she is to answer the question I have posed to her.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Bwonsamdi
passages.text:
<Pa'ku's levity subsides.>

Ordinarily the final trial would be given by Rezan. But the loa of kings is no more.

It seems ol' Rastakhan picked a new favorite to take his place.

<Pa'ku sneers.>

Enjoy that. Bwonsamdi waits for you in the temple.

passages.title: Gaze of the Loa: Bwonsamdi
passages.text:
<Talanji nods to you.>

Thank you for standing beside me through all of this. Some choices were easier than others, but I am confident in all of them.

passages.title: A Particular Process
passages.text:
As you might have noticed, Vintner Iltheux is very particular about his wine making process, but his ancient recipe was crafted with only the Nightborne in mind. 

We need something different to please the diverse palates of the Horde!

Talk to Nomi and see what he has in mind to spice things up.

passages.title: A Particular Process
passages.text: Good to see you again, <name>. I've already made improvements to the vintner's recipe.

passages.title: No Survivors
passages.text:
Do you see the encampment on the beach below?

The Horde followed Tyrande here.

No doubt some of them have remained here in the shadows in case she returned.

Kill them.

passages.title: No Survivors
