The leaders of the Alliance have agreed to fund an elite gnomish aerial task force.

And you have been chosen to lead the test team for the Gnomish Elite Aerial Rangers. I have assembled some of the finest tinkers and soldiers from Gnomeregan, who are now under your command.

The three of them are already here in New Tinkertown. Introduce yourself and assemble them.

passages.title: Gnomeregan's Finest
passages.text: Speak up, soldier!

passages.title: Gnomeregan's Finest
passages.text: Time to give you all your briefing.

passages.title: Shadowed Halls and Dusty Cogs
passages.text:
An elite aerial unit wouldn't be complete without the newest innovations in flying machine technology.

There's just one small problem.

The innovative new engine we built was left behind when we evacuated Gnomeregan. We need that prototype if we want these bombers to safely get off the ground!

passages.title: Shadowed Halls and Dusty Cogs
passages.text: Did you find the engine?

passages.title: Shadowed Halls and Dusty Cogs
passages.text: Excellent! I've sent Tinkerbow and Autoblast ahead to prepare for the engine for installation.

passages.title: The Gnome Behind the Trogg
passages.text:
If I just attach the core of this to the input module here... Amplify the matched frequency here...

<Tinkerbow mumbles a few more things while she attaches the communication device to the console.>

Flip the switch, Commander! Just make sure it's the right one. The left one is the self-destruct switch. Or was that reversed...

passages.title: The Gnome Behind the Trogg
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The Gnome Behind the Trogg
passages.text: Give me just a second to trace the origin of the signal...

passages.title: A Tundra Conundrum
passages.text:
While you were in Gnomeregan, we received a distress signal from Fizzcrank Airstrip in Borean Tundra. This seems like the perfect opportunity to show off what G.E.A.R. can do!

I've sent the rest of your squad ahead. Meet them out there.

passages.title: A Tundra Conundrum
passages.text: Oh, Commander! We arrived shortly before you. The airmen here just finished explaining the situation.

passages.title: Now With More Mechanical Fowl
passages.text:
The gnomes here report that troggs came down from the north and started attacking everygnome and everything.

So now it's our job to fix this situation! And luckily, I have the perfect plan for it. We need to calibrate the bomber's gun, and doing so on the ground is much less risky than up in the air.

Give it a go, Commander!

passages.title: Smarter Than Your Average Trogg
passages.text:
<Cog Captain Winklespring's voice springs to life over your personal communication system.>

One of the recon pilots did a scouting run over the station. She reported that there seems to be a trogg on the top level that is larger and smarter than the others. He's somehow managed to get one of the Defendo-Tanks for the station working in his favor.

Take him out!

passages.title: Smarter Than Your Average Trogg
passages.text: Have you found out anything?

passages.title: Smarter Than Your Average Trogg
passages.text: The big trogg was holding this? I think I have an idea...

passages.title: Paragon of the Tortollan Seekers
passages.text: Your allies among the Tortollan Seekers have requested your presence. They wish to reward you for your continued efforts on their behalf.

passages.title: Paragon of the Tortollan Seekers
passages.text:
Greetings, Archmage.

For some time now you have been a paragon in your efforts for the Seekers. Our gratitude goes beyond anything mere words can define.

Take these trophies as a token of our gratitude. The more you aid us, the more we can provide you.

passages.title: Paragon of the Champions of Azeroth
passages.text: A grateful Magni Bronzebeard has requested your presence. He wishes to reward you for your exceptional aid.

passages.title: Paragon of the Champions of Azeroth
passages.text:
Greetings, Archdruid.

For some time now you have been a paragon in your efforts to aid Azeroth. My gratitude goes beyond anything mere words can define.

Take these trophies as a token of my gratitude. The more you aid Azeroth, the more I can provide you.

passages.title: Executing Exorcisms
passages.text:
Even in death, the Alliance foolishly clings to Horde territory.

Drive their vengeful ghosts from the ruins of Stromgarde before their foulness spreads.

passages.title: Sins of the Syndicate
passages.text:
As if the League of Arathor was not trouble enough, Syndicate agents still slither down from the Alterac mountains to drive off honest Horde laborers.

Punish them.

passages.title: Paragon of the 7th Legion
passages.text: Commanders of the 7th Legion forces have requested your presence. They wish to reward you for your exceptional efforts.

passages.title: Paragon of the 7th Legion
passages.text:
Huntmaster, thanks to your efforts against the Horde, our forces have been able to secure additional resources from the battlefield.

The more you continue to dominate the battlefield the more resources our forces can spare.

passages.title: Death to The Defilers
passages.text:
Even with the destruction of Undercity, the Defilers continue to combat our hold on the Arathi Highlands.

The farmland at Go'Shek will belong to the Alliance once more. Go, and defeat the Forsaken.

passages.title: Executing Exorcisms
passages.text:
Even in death, the Horde foolishly clings to Alliance territory.

Drive their vengeful ghosts from the ruins of Ar'gorok before their foulness spreads.

passages.title: Sins of the Syndicate
passages.text:
As if the Defilers were not trouble enough, Syndicate agents still slither down from the Alterac mountains to drive off honest Alliance farmers.

Punish them.

passages.title: Paragon of the Order of Embers
Paragon of the Storm's Wake
passages.text: The grateful Storm's Wake forces have requested your presence. They wish to reward you for your continued efforts on their behalf.

passages.title: Paragon of the Storm's Wake
passages.text:
Greetings, Huntmaster.

For some time now you have been a paragon in your efforts to aid us. Our gratitude goes beyond anything mere words can define.

Take these trophies as a token of our gratitude. The more you aid us, the more we can provide you.

passages.title: Paragon of the Proudmoore Admiralty
passages.text: The grateful leaders of the Proudmoore Admiralty have requested your presence. They wish to reward you for your continued aid to their house.

passages.title: Paragon of the Proudmoore Admiralty
passages.text:
Greetings, Highlord.

For some time now you have been a paragon in your efforts for Boralus and the Proudmoore Admiralty. Our gratitude goes beyond anything mere words can define.

Take these trophies as a token of our gratitude. The more you aid us, the more we can provide you.

passages.title: Paragon of Talanji's Expedition
passages.text: Your allies among Talanji's Expedition have requested your presence. They wish to reward you for your continued efforts on their behalf.

passages.title: Paragon of Talanji's Expedition
passages.text:
Hello, Archdruid.

For some time now you've been a paragon in your efforts for de Expedition. Our gratitude goes beyond what mere words of thanks can offer.

Take dese trophies as a token of our appreciation. De more you aid us, de more we can provide you.

passages.title: Paragon of the Voldunai
passages.text: Your allies among the Voldunai have requested your presence. They wish to reward you for your continued efforts on their behalf.

passages.title: Paragon of the Voldunai
passages.text:
Greetings, Archdruid.

For some time now you have been a paragon in your efforts to support the Voldunai. Our gratitude goes beyond anything mere words can define.

Take these trophies as a token of our gratitude. The more you aid us, the more we can provide you.

passages.title: Paragon of the Zandalari Empire
passages.text: The grateful leaders of the Zandalari Empire have requested your presence. They wish to reward you for your exceptional aid.

passages.title: Paragon of the Zandalari Empire
passages.text:
Greetings, Farseer.

For some time now you have been a paragon in your efforts to aid de Zandalari Empire. Our gratitude goes beyond what mere words of thanks can offer.

Take dese trophies as a token of our appreciation. De more you aid us, de more we can provide you.

passages.title: Mekkatorque's Battle Plans
passages.text:
So we almost got everythin' we need, except for where that airship went!

My insurance pals found out where they're hidin' that primo-info. 

Go and get me Mekkatorque's battle plans, then we can begin the REALLY fun part!

passages.title: Mekkatorque's Battle Plans
passages.text: You get me that thing yet?

passages.title: Mekkatorque's Battle Plans
passages.text: This is perfect! Let's blow us up that annoying mook.

passages.title: A Signal in Storm Peaks
passages.text:
It looks like the signal is being transmitted from Storm Peaks. 

Time to put these flying machines to work! I'll keep tracking the signal en route in order to get a cleaner read.

passages.title: A Signal in Storm Peaks
passages.text: Need something, Commander?

passages.title: A Signal in Storm Peaks
passages.text: I've set up a cloaking device that will cover our current location. We should be safe for now.

passages.title: Gnomercy!
passages.text:
We need to give Tinkerbow some cover while she figures out our new trajectory.

<The Cog Captain hands you a miniature spider tank.>

It may not look like much, but this is a fully functional spider tank. You'll just need to de-shrinkify it. Use it to distract the troggs down below by thinning their numbers.

passages.title: Gnomercy!
passages.text: Give those troggs something to worry about, Captain!

passages.title: Gnomercy!
passages.text: Glad you found your way here safely, Commander!

passages.title: For Gnomeregan!
passages.text:
It's time to bring down Sparkspanner, Commander.

Just give me the word, and I'll turn this machine straight towards the Halls of Stone!

passages.title: For Gnomeregan!
passages.text: Sparkspanner needs to be defeated, for the sake of all Gnomanity.

passages.title: For Gnomeregan!
passages.text: Is everyone alright? Our tinker can set up a Medic Bot if necessary.

passages.title: The War Chest
passages.text:
Welcome to the warfront, <name>. I am glad we have you fighting on our side.

First things first: We need to collect resources in order to strengthen our hold on Bashal'Aran and bolster our troops.

Any resources that we collect will go to the War Chest. Open the chest and see what you can use.

passages.title: The War Chest
passages.text: Have you collected those resources from the War Chest?

passages.title: The War Chest
passages.text: Good. Now we can get down to business.

passages.title: An Explosive Situation
passages.text:
We have some iron available, but we could always use more.

Get down to the mine at the Ruins of Lornesta. Seize it from any enemies, and get those goblins to do their job.

Giving them something suitably destructive should do the trick.

passages.title: An Explosive Situation
passages.text: We need more iron if we want to win this battle!

passages.title: An Explosive Situation
passages.text: I can hear the explosive productivity. Well done.

passages.title: Darkshore Recruits
passages.text:
We will not win unless we have the power of numbers on our side.

First, we need the Barracks restored so Signe can do her work. Signe is one of the Dark Lady's val'kyr, and she can raise forces for us.

Once the Barracks is built, talk to Signe and recruit a troop. I'm sure they could learn a lot from fighting alongside you.

passages.title: Darkshore Recruits
passages.text: Have you recruited those troops?

passages.title: Darkshore Recruits
passages.text: Some of these recruits are a little... fresher than others.

passages.title: Arms and Armor
passages.text:
Keever knows troops need weapons. And armor. Armor and weapons. 

Keever wants Archibald to make armor and weapons for troops. You listen to Keever and talk to Archibald.

passages.title: Arms and Armor
passages.text: We are a long way from the Undercity, yet here is where I belong.

passages.title: Arms and Armor
passages.text: Keever would like fancy new armor and weapons.

passages.title: The Altar of Storms
passages.text:
The Altar of Storms has been rebuilt. It is a unique kind of altar. The goblin kind.

Keever is pleased. Keever wishes to wield that kind of power.

Go, listen to Keever, talk to little goblin Mizzyk and find what the Altar can do.

passages.title: The Altar of Storms
passages.text: Keever wonders if you have seen the Altar of Storms yet.

passages.title: The Altar of Storms
passages.text:
Keever knows that with this great power, you will do responsible things.

Keever knows.

passages.title: An Alchemist for Everything
passages.text:
When we first conquered Darkshore, we set up an Alchemy Lab on the shore at Gloomtide Strand to tap into this area's latent power.

Unfortunately, things did not go so well and the Alliance have overrun the lab.

Would you see them off, and then speak with Professor Blightwell to see what he can do for you?

passages.title: An Alchemist for Everything
passages.text: Did you find anything at Gloomtide Strand?

passages.title: An Alchemist for Everything
passages.text: We Apothecaries know what we're doing, believe me. Between us we've written loads of treatises on the theory of what can be accomplished with just a few pounds of flesh.

passages.title: Throwing Blight
passages.text:
We need more firepower, and the goblins are oh so obliging, aren't they. Zarvik in particular has honed his craft ever since our conquest of Darkshore.

Why don't you talk to him and see what he's got going at the Workshop?

passages.title: Throwing Blight
passages.text: You got anything you need built?

passages.title: Throwing Blight
passages.text: Those Blight Throwers are sure to take down those Ancients in no time.

passages.title: Echolocation
passages.text:
Glad you're here! These bats have got to get up and start giving us some more air support.

I've got a draft of a flight plan here in Darkshore. It's helped by the fact that our bats can see in the dark, when most of us can't.

Talk to Avery and she'll make sure you get safely back to Bashal'Aran.

passages.title: Echolocation
passages.text: Well done. These bats will help us win the battle of the skies.

passages.title: The Missing Blade
passages.text:
<The echo of the blade Xal'atath lingers before you. Though the consciousness that resided within the dagger is gone, the place it once occupied still resonates with power.

You sense the weapon now speaks another voice. Another purpose....

You feel compelled to warn the king that the blade may now reside in the hands of the enemy.>

passages.title: The Missing Blade
passages.text:
<You tell Anduin about Xal'atath and N'Zoth. His expression darkens.>

This is grim news, champion.

The Alliance stands on the threshold of victory. If the Banshee Queen has learned of a new weapon, she will use it to keep the war going indefinitely.

passages.title: The Black Blade
passages.text:
<The blade that was known as Xal'atath rests on the ground before you. Though the consciousness that resided within the dagger is gone, it still resonates with power.

Almost as if the weapon speaks with another voice. Another purpose....

You feel a compulsion to bring this artifact to the warchief.>

passages.title: The Black Blade
passages.text:
<As you present the dagger to Sylvanas, a faint smile curls her lips. For the briefest moment, it seems her eyes darken. A trick of the light, no doubt.>

Once again, you have proven yourself a worthy champion, <name>. This blade is the compass that will guide us to victory.

passages.title: Express Delivery
passages.text:
The Horde appears to have misplaced some of its Azerite. It would be rude of us not to return it, don't you think?

The most efficient way is for me to teleport it back.

I've enchanted the harpoons in that launcher over there. Fire them onto the Horde ships in the bay. I can use them as beacons to return the Azerite to the Horde... and send its ships on their way.

passages.title: Express Delivery
passages.text: Well done, <name>.

passages.title: Express Delivery
passages.text:
It appears as if the fleet won't be needed for much more than hauling wreckage out of the bay.

Thank you for helping me to save my people before more could be killed by the Horde. Our foes are growing bolder. Clearly, we need to strike back. Kul Tiras will fight beside the Alliance when we do.

passages.title: Made in Kul Tiras
passages.text:
Are you curious about how the Kul Tirans joined the Alliance? 

It was assumed that Kul Tiras would rejoin the Alliance after everything that was done to stabilize their nation.

Lady Jaina Proudmoore wanted to cement the allegiance by building King Anduin a ship worthy of the Kul Tiran navy.

She wished for help in finding the best shipwright in Kul Tiras, Dorian Atwater. It wouldn't be easy, as Dorian was retired.

It all began with a trip to see Cyrus in Boralus Harbor...

passages.title: Made in Kul Tiras
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Made in Kul Tiras
passages.text: I may be able to help you find this shipwright, <name>.

passages.title: Home, Home On the Range
passages.text:
<Cyrus peruses a map.>

Hmm... Along the road to Fort Daelin... to the north... somewhere in the Deadwash.

<He points to a section of road on the map.>

I've marked a spot on your map that seems likely. I think that will get you close enough. 

I'll report back to the Lord Admiral with what we've learned. Good luck, and I hope our shipwright is willing.

passages.title: Home, Home On the Range
passages.text: Now what's this?

passages.title: Home, Home On the Range
passages.text: <Dorian takes her time to read over the letter. Her brows steadily rise.>

passages.title: I'm Too Old for This Ship
passages.text:
If I understood this correctly, the Lord Admiral of the Kul Tiran navy wants me to come out of retirement specifically to build a ship for the king of Stormwind.

Can't say I've had THAT request before.

<Dorian leans back in her chair for a moment and rubs at her eyes.>

I'm getting too old for this nonsense.

<Dorian heaves a long sigh.>

Go on out back and saddle Hurricane for me while I pack my things. We will meet you at Port Fogtide.

We're going to need a slip.

passages.title: I'm Too Old for This Ship
passages.text: I don't go anywhere without my horse, <name>.

passages.title: I'm Too Old for This Ship
passages.text: Well. This complicates things a touch.

passages.title: Covering Our Masts
passages.text:
When I was younger, I hid my ships out of vanity.

I often went through a number of designs before I was satisfied. I didn't want anyone to see that. It might ruin the mystique, I reasoned.

Now... I think it best to hide this ship from the likes of those tentacle-faced creeps. I don't think they intend to let us build unchallenged.

Go into the port and place my wards around the main slip. 

You'll see what they do.

passages.title: Covering Our Masts
passages.text: Did you place the wards?

passages.title: Covering Our Masts
passages.text: That should give us some cover. Hopefully they stay away long enough to finish construction.

passages.title: The Deep Ones
passages.text:
I've spent my whole life on and around the sea. 

Until very recently I feel like I've always had one foot in the water. I knew there were... things... best left untouched.

Now they're here. In Stormsong Valley. Occupying the slip I need to build your ship.

Do I really need to tell you what to do about it?

passages.title: The Deep Ones
passages.text: I never thought I would see such things in the flesh. Have you dealt with them?

passages.title: The Deep Ones
passages.text: All this gives me the shivers, <name>.

passages.title: Frame Work
passages.text:
Now that I have a slip to work in, I'm going to need lumber.

Lots of lumber.

The only lumber mill that could handle this kind of volume at such short notice would be the Algerson Lumber Yard outside of Boralus.

I know this because I've made this exact request of them before.

I will meet you there. Algerson might need a little persuasion.

passages.title: Frame Work
passages.text: I overestimated Algerson's usefulness here, but don't worry. I have a plan.

passages.title: Team Carry
passages.text:
Algerson is about as useful as a legless horse. We're going to do this ourselves.

The mill is overrun with bizarre creatures. I'll handle those. You and these hearty volunteers will need to be the muscle of this operation.

Don't look at me like that, <class>. It's just a little lifting.

Once we have enough lumber, Sal will meet us for a pick up. Just stay close to me and focus on not dropping my wood, yes?

passages.title: Team Carry
passages.text: Why are you all sweaty?

passages.title: This Lumber is Haunted
passages.text:
I don't much believe in ghosts, or hauntings for that matter.

That said, there is something wrong with this lumber. I can feel it in my bones. They're achier than normal.

I only know of one group that would know what to do. They're reclusive, but we share a love of nature.

Seek out Thornspeaker Birchgrove in Drustvar. I trust no one else with this.

passages.title: This Lumber is Haunted
passages.text: There's a deep rend in the balance, and it is centered on you. Curious.

passages.title: This Lumber is Haunted
passages.text:
Ah, I see... this is the source of that wrongness I felt.

This is troubling indeed, <name>.

passages.title: The Bleak Hills
passages.text:
While you are visiting Drustvar, I need you to run another errand for me.

The Wright family owned a mine up near Corlain. Years past, they supplied all the metal ore I used to build my ships.

I can't imagine they're faring too well, based on what we've seen here.

Find Chelsea Wright, the foreman's daughter, and see what they need to get another ore shipment together.

Just tell her Dorian sent you.

passages.title: The Bleak Hills
passages.text: Boy, am I glad to see you. I thought that beast was going to eat me alive!

passages.title: Gorak Tul's Influence
passages.text:
Long have the Thornspeakers struggled against such magics. It is a conflict as old as the Drust themselves.

Gorak Tul's influence, however, has vastly shifted the balance toward that of decay and death. It corrupts what would be an ordinary curse.

I believe Ulfar can correct this.

Go into Gol Koval. Slay our enemies, destroy their cairns, and collect their magics into this vessel.

With it, Ulfar may be able to find a way to cleanse your materials.

passages.title: Gorak Tul's Influence
passages.text: Be careful, <name>. Drust magic is older than most things that are, and older than some that were.

passages.title: Gorak Tul's Influence
passages.text: The concentration chills me to my bones, but it will be needed. We must hurry before the corruption can touch you.

passages.title: Balance in All Things
passages.text:
The confluence of energies around that vessel is truly disturbing. My skin crawls with the wrongness of it.

We have reached the limit of my ability to help you, <name>.

Go to Ulfar, the High Thornspeaker. Arthur will carry you, if you wish it.

Only he knows enough about these ancient magics to undo the corruption that taints your materials.

Go quickly. You do not want to hold that vessel longer than you must.

passages.title: Balance in All Things
passages.text: I sense a terrible power emanating from that vessel, <name>.

passages.title: Balance in All Things
passages.text:
We will take what we have learned here and see what can be done about the rest of Drustvar.

For now, the Drust Vessel will be of use to you and Dorian.

Give her my regards. She is an ally to the Thornspeakers, always.

passages.title: Drop It!
passages.text:
You must be the person Dorian sent to collect the ore.

I got a message a short while ago requesting a rather large shipment, which in itself is a feat given the state of this place. I was on my way to our storehouse when that... beast!... cornered me.

It took my keys. I can't get you that shipment without them. Find out where that mongrel took them and bring them back.

Let it be known I wouldn't do this for anyone else.

passages.title: Drop It!
passages.text: <The Wicker Beast stares blankly at you.>

passages.title: Drop It!
passages.text: <The Wicker Beast sniffs the key.>

passages.title: Make it Wright
passages.text:
<Chelsea stares in horror at the Wicker Beast.>

I don't know how this happened, or why... but I know this beast. 

<Chelsea hastily wipes away a tear.>

I've unlocked our storage chest. Thank you. Thank you so much.

Tell Dorian she can call upon us at any time.

passages.title: Make it Wright
passages.text:
A note is affixed to the chest.

It reads:

"Dorian-

The mine has been in a bad way of late, but you will be glad to know that our standards remain as high as ever. 

Give Sal our best,

Chelsea W.
Wright & Co."

passages.title: Summons from Dorian
passages.text:
<The elemental has a piece of parchment whipping around madly inside its tornado.>

HHsssssss.

<The elemental ejects the page into your face.>

HHHHSSSSSSsssshh.

passages.title: Summons from Dorian
passages.text: I see my little helper found you just fine.

passages.title: Summons from Dorian
passages.text: I'm not fond of nobles sticking their nose in my work before it's finished. Deal with this.

passages.title: A Worthy Crew
passages.text:
If Dorian really can build this ship before the day is out, we need to find a crew for the new vessel.

This crew should represent the best of Kul Tiran society, the highest naval prowess, and the faith of our people as we present this gift to Anduin.

I have a captain in mind, but you'll want to speak to him yourself. I will let him decide who else he wants aboard.

Seek out my brother, Tandred Proudmoore, in Boralus. He will help you fill out the ranks from there.

passages.title: A Worthy Crew
passages.text: Have you found a suitable crew?

passages.title: A Worthy Crew
passages.text: This is a fine group you've assembled. Very well done.

passages.title: Garbage for the Garbage God
passages.text: Richmon, you found a thing I been looking for for a long time. Bring it to me in the Port of Zandalar, and I will grant you my favor.

passages.title: Garbage for the Garbage God
passages.text:
I remember da orphan who first carved dis offering. I remember da tears and desperation and da hope for somethin' to save dem. I remember tastin' da power in dat hope.

And I remember da look of fear on da cruel richmon who made da child cry. "Never again" not just be hollow words with Jani.

passages.title: The Loa of Scavengers
passages.text:
Richmon, you bring me many shiny things. You helped some of those that no one else would. And ya dumb enough to keep comin' back to me trash piles.

I like ya style.

Now for da big one. Go to the steps of Dazar'alor, and find the Chronicler Ash'tari. Her chisel makes da shrines there. Tell her to build me a shrine and I will grant you my boon.

Unlike the flappy Pa'ku or running Gonk, I just gonna let ya scrap your trash in my pile and I'll give ya stuff back. Anywhere my trash piles be.

passages.title: The Loa of Scavengers
passages.text:
Well, I don't have any extra statues to Jani lying around. It is not as if that... thing... has ever asked for one before. How about I just clear a spot to throw trash down on our sacred shrines?

Are you sure this is not a prank? 

Fine! But just know that if you want to put a proper loa's statue back up, speak to me.

passages.title: When Spirits Whisper
passages.text:
Ah, <name>! I have a message for you.

Baine Bloodhoof asks that you join him in Thunder Bluff at once.

I suggest you hurry.

passages.title: When Spirits Whisper
passages.text: Greetings, <name>. I am pleased you have answered my call.

passages.title: The Spiritwalkers
passages.text:
As you know, the spiritwalkers commune with our ancestors and maintain balance within the spirit realm. It is a sacred duty that links our present to our past.

But lately the spiritwalkers have been troubled by visions of chaos and turmoil. Of a rising darkness.

They tell me that the spirits have whispered your name. We are unsure why, but Spiritwalker Ussoh means to find out.

Seek Ussoh on Fargaze Mesa to the south. Good luck, <name>. I believe you may need it.

passages.title: The Spiritwalkers
passages.text:
Hmph. I expected you sooner. 

No matter. Have a seat.

passages.title: Spirit Guide
passages.text:
The ancestors have whispered your name, <name>. Now it is time for you to reach out to them.

Here in this sacred place, we spiritwalkers commune with those who came before us. Sit within the circle and light the incense.

If you open your heart, a spirit guide will present itself to you. Let us hope it will lead you to the answers we seek.

passages.title: Spirit Guide
passages.text: Have you found your guide?

passages.title: Spirit Guide
passages.text: What did you see?

passages.title: A Small Retreat
passages.text:
I believe your guide was delivering a warning. The unrest within the spirit realm may be even more dire than first feared.

We must cross over at once, from a place with a strong bond to the spirit realm.

In ages past, tauren made pilgrimages to Sun Rock Retreat to engage in such a ritual. It is said that long ago, An'she himself kissed the mountain where the retreat now stands.

Meet me there and we will begin the crossing.

passages.title: A Small Retreat
passages.text: Shall we begin?

passages.title: Crossing Over
passages.text:
We are ready to begin. 

You will be crossing into the spirit realm. Take caution, for it can be a place of both tranquility and danger.

Make contact with your spirit guide. There must be a reason it was in pain when it revealed itself to you.

When you are ready, raise this vessel to enter the spirit realm.

passages.title: Crossing Over
passages.text: Are you ready to enter the spirit realm?

passages.title: Crossing Over
passages.text:
Your guide is a chieftain ancestor? That is a great honor.

But if your guide was under attack, then I fear balance has been lost.

passages.title: Storm in Bloodhoof
passages.text:
This is worse than I feared.

The people of Bloodhoof Village are in grave danger. Even the brave young tauren who train there are woefully unprepared for the danger that is coming.

Do what you can to stop this threat. I will go to Thunder Bluff to warn the High Chieftain.

passages.title: Storm in Bloodhoof
passages.text: You heard the horn, <name>! We are in dire need of your help.

passages.title: Answer the Call
passages.text:
It is fortunate that Spiritwalker Ussoh passed along your spirit guide's warning. We were able to evacuate most of the citizens.

This cursed spirit is full of malevolence and hatred. It must be destroyed, <name>!

We attack on your command.

passages.title: Answer the Call
passages.text:
You have saved Thunder Bluff, <class>. However, The spirit realm is growing more restless and balance is tipping. We have restored it for now. But how long until the scales are moved again and what is causing it?

I do not have those answers, but I do have another favor to ask.

passages.title: Masking For a Friend
passages.text:
The Outriggers have fought some pretty tough monsters and Horde savages aren't so much different. The Blight Specialists they brought weren't especially tough, but they were the most dangerous.

Kill a few of them and bring back their face masks. Okri can work his mechanical wizardry and build us better masks of our own in case any Horde scum dare show their blight-spreading faces around here again.

passages.title: Masking For a Friend
passages.text: Did you get rid of those blighted wretches?

passages.title: Masking For a Friend
passages.text: Thank you, mainlander. I'm sure Okri can make us some top-notch gear with these.

passages.title: Remaining Threats
passages.text:
Though our forces maintain a steady hold on Darkshore, this land still festers with enemies at every turn.

Do what you can to keep them at bay, and you will be well rewarded.

passages.title: Remaining Threats
passages.text: Is the deed done?

passages.title: Remaining Threats
passages.text:
Excellent. 

None will stand in our way!

passages.title: Tapping the Breach
passages.text:
Darkshore is home to several elemental breaches which hold massive amounts of power. 

The remnants of the Twilight's Hammer know this. While we were preoccupied with the Kaldorei, their elementalists have moved to exploit these locations of power, calling forth massive elementals to do their bidding.

Their actions must not go unchecked.

passages.title: Tapping the Breach
passages.text: What of the cultist threat?

passages.title: Tapping the Breach
passages.text:
These cultists simply don't know when to give up, do they? I hope this is the last we see of them.

Well done, <class>.

passages.title: Buzzkill
passages.text:
Some gnome's been goin about planting these strange machines in the woods here. I don't know what they do, but I'll be dead before I let gnomish machines sully goblin territory!

Find these "buzzboxes" and reduce them to scrap. I'll make sure you're compensated for your troubles.

passages.title: Buzzkill
passages.text: Did you take care of our gnomish problem?

passages.title: Buzzkill
passages.text:
Thanks for the assist there, pal.

If you ask me, the only place gnomish technology belongs is the scrap heap!

passages.title: Operation: Troggageddon
passages.text:
Tinkerbow has finished installing the guns on our flying machines, so it's time to give them a trial by fire. We've got confirmation that our target is in fact within the Halls of Stone.

Let's start clearing out the forces out in front. We'll take the earliest opportunity to bring the fight to Sparkspanner!

passages.title: Blessing of the Tides
passages.text:
Dorian certainly lives up to her reputation, <name>.

This magnificent vessel is complete and now it has a crew. Two pieces remain.

First, we must give the ship a name.

Then it falls to Brother Pike to bless this vessel. As is tradition, a tidesage's blessing fortifies the ship against storms and encourages fair weather and smooth seas. It is as much ceremonial as it is practical.

Once that is done, we will set sail for Stormwind.

passages.title: Blessing of the Tides
passages.text: I chose you for this honor to thank you for all you have done for my people, and all that you have done for me.

passages.title: Blessing of the Tides
passages.text:
It has been so long since I have seen such a rite performed. I was only a child.

It means a great deal to me to have had your help in this. Thank you.

passages.title: We Are Coming
passages.text:
We must press our advantage before the Horde can further its hold on Darkshore.

The kaldorei stand ready to fight for our home, and the Gilneans stand alongside us.

We will show our enemies our fury. They will learn to fear us.

Rally any you can. We march at once.

passages.title: We Are Coming
passages.text: I will call anyone with the will to fight as soon as our supplies are in order!

passages.title: Remaining Threats
passages.text:
We have managed to route the Horde presence in Darkshore, but several threats remain throughout the countryside.

If we wish to hold this land, they must be eliminated.

passages.title: Remaining Threats
passages.text: How's your progress?

passages.title: Remaining Threats
passages.text:
You have strengthened our position and brought some measure of safety to the people of Darkshore

You have my thanks.

passages.title: Tapping the Breach
passages.text:
We had thought the Twilight's Hammer's presence in Darkshore was snuffed out with the defeat of Deathwing. Apparently, we were mistaken.

Remnants of their cult have used the conflict in Darkshore as an opportunity to re-establish their presence here. Darkshore is home to several breaches of elemental power, and it looks like they aim to use these to unleash powerful elementals to devastate the land.

This must not stand.

passages.title: Tapping the Breach
passages.text:
You have saved countless lives today. For this I am greatful.

Still, I'm afraid this won't be the last we will see of the Twilight's Hammer. We must be ever vigilant.

passages.title: Buzzkill
passages.text:
Some nefarious no-goodnik is tampering with my Buzzboxes!

I've been trying to get the Buzzbox network back online since we were able to drive the Horde out of Darkshore, but I'm getting no reading from boxes 456, 627, 111, and 854! I'd be willing to bet that some stragglers from the Bilgewater Cartel are to blame!

See if you can get those Buzzboxes back online, will you? We'll need their readings if we ever want to permanently fix the corruption problem here.

passages.title: Buzzkill
passages.text:
You did it! The Buzzbox network is back online!

Now, if I can only remember the passcode to this thing we'll be in business!

passages.title: Spark of Genius
passages.text:
<name>, I have wondrous news!

A recent energy signature tripped several detection relays I installed after that unfortunate incident with Sargeras.

I require further data to know for certain, but initial diagnostics suggest that these energies are coming from Hati! We might still be able to save him!

Hati's spirit is still bound to your own, so I'll need your help. Meet me at my library in the Storm Peaks right away!

passages.title: Spark of Genius
passages.text:
Our scientific team simply would not be complete without Bronzebeard here.

Let's begin!

passages.title: Telemetry Online
passages.text:
When Titanstrike's power was expended in Silithus, Hati's essence managed to sever itself from the Thunderspark just in time to avoid destruction.

The only problem is that his essence was then scattered across Azeroth, and we don't know where.

Now that we've locked onto his energy signature, we should be able to triangulate Hati's position!

passages.title: Telemetry Online
passages.text: Everything is possible with science!

passages.title: Telemetry Online
passages.text: Now that we've located Hati's essence, we can move to phase two of my glorious plan!

passages.title: The Huntsman's Creed
passages.text:
Through the glorious wonder of science, I have managed to keep the Thunderspark powered precisely for this purpose.

All you need to do is get to the Temple of Storms and absorb Hati's essence into it. Just... kind of point it in his general direction.

Oh, and do keep in mind that this is only one part of Hati. You may run into a few... technical difficulties before he's subdued enough for the absorption protocol.

passages.title: The Huntsman's Creed
passages.text: One down, one tae go!

passages.title: Paid in Blood
passages.text:
If Mimiron's fancy gadgets be right, then the other half o' Hati is near the wound in Silithus.

We'll have tae move quickly. Even with part o' his essence contained, I can feel him fadin' away fast!

'Tis a long trip, <lad/lass>. Let's get movin'!

passages.title: Paid in Blood
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Paid in Blood
passages.text: No time to chat. I need you at my lab in Ulduar at once!

passages.title: Spark of Imagination
passages.text:
I've diverted all non-essential power to prepare for Hati's reformation, so I cannot teleport you to Ulduar from here.

Be extremely careful with the Thunderspark on your way. It is charged with highly volatile energy. One wrong bump could lead to serious complications!

passages.title: Spark of Imagination
passages.text: Quickly, now! We may not have much time!

passages.title: Bonds of Thunder
passages.text:
While you infused Hati's essence into the Thunderspark, I have concocted a flawless plan the likes of which the scientific world has never seen!

I'll spare you the technical details. Just follow my instructions and Hati will be back in one piece in no time at all!

...Or we will all explode. But risks must be taken in the pursuit of knowledge and the well-being of our furry companions, wouldn't you agree?

passages.title: Bonds of Thunder
passages.text: I know how long you have been waiting for this day, <name>.

passages.title: Bonds of Thunder
passages.text: I have never seen a creature so excited!

passages.title: Homeward Bound
passages.text:
The reformation procedure went positively flawlessly! Most excellent results indeed--and plenty of data to analyze!

I'm not sure what it is Thorim has to show you, but I suggest you get to the Temple of Storms right away. He gets a bit destructive when he's kept waiting.

Take my teleporter pad directly out of Ulduar. I'm afraid the normal route to the entrance is... inoperable at the moment.

passages.title: Homeward Bound
passages.text: You brought the Thunderspark with you, I trust. We shall need it!

passages.title: The Nuts and Bolts of It
passages.text:
I started working on the leg gearing. Most the gearing around here is built from spare parts we find in the scrap heaps. 

We're going to need a lot of spare parts to fix this thing. See what you can find.

passages.title: The Nuts and Bolts of It
passages.text: Bring me those spare parts!

passages.title: The Nuts and Bolts of It
passages.text: Nice work, this will help a lot.

passages.title: Heresy!
passages.text:
My own prelates are among them that revolted against Talanji. This is an unspeakable heresy.

 I will not tolerate it! 

<She gestures to the prelate before her with her spear.>

This one has wisely told me who is to blame. My second, Kaj'ra.

I would have heard her, had she used any other means to make her concerns known. Now she must be disposed of.

You will find her in de Terrace of de Chosen.

passages.title: Heresy!
passages.text: Death is too good for that heretic.

passages.title: Heresy!
passages.text:
<High Prelate Rata spits on the ground.>

Bwonsamdi keep her.

passages.title: Ready to Rumble
passages.text:
We're going to need a new Sixteen-Servo-Actuator if we're going to fix the controls on this thing.

Bondo's gang at the yard probably has one, but they usually aren't too helpful.

Talk to Bondo, see if you can get us one.

passages.title: Ready to Rumble
passages.text: Did you head over to the yard yet?

passages.title: Ready to Rumble
passages.text: I really didn't think Bondo would give us one of these!

passages.title: Mechanical Liberation
passages.text:
Since you successfully interrupted my nap, my defenses are obviously lacking to say the least. 

That's because the sethrak, in addition to stealing my gadgets and gizmos, stole my mechs! Those morons don't even have the keys!

<Gryzix laughs>

Here, take my keys and get my mechs back.

passages.title: Mechanical Liberation
passages.text:
Ah, yes. My mechs!

A little muscle goes a long way it seems...

passages.title: A Brother's Help
passages.text:
We're gonna need all the help we can get te save the planet.

I've got an idea.

Meet me in Nazmir, outside the Heart of Darkness. Together, we'll seek guidance from someone who may be able to help.

passages.title: A Brother's Help
passages.text: Can ye please talk some sense into Brann fer me?

passages.title: Necessity is the MOTHER
passages.text:
I may be Azeroth's speaker, but Brann's the expert on titan archaeology. If he says that MOTHER can help us save Azeroth, then I'm more than willing tae place my faith in her.

Come, champion. Let's hear what guidance she has tae offer.

passages.title: Necessity is the MOTHER
passages.text: I'll never understand exactly how all these machines work. That's what Brann does!

passages.title: Necessity is the MOTHER
passages.text: It's just as I feared. We don't have much time, champion. This may be our only hope.

passages.title: Scouting The Strand
passages.text:
It has been a long time since we have heard from our scouts at the outpost.

They may have been cut off from us due to the naga attack. I need to check in with them and get an update on the movements of the naga forces.

You should come with me, this will be a good opportunity for you to meet more of the clan and get a closer look at our operation.

passages.title: Let's Get It Started
passages.text:
I theorize this to be a communication relay. It is non-operational, but gnomish ingenuity and your strong back shall soon solve that problem!

I need you to help get this device functional.

passages.title: Let's Get It Started
passages.text: We need this device repaired.

passages.title: Let's Get It Started
passages.text: This is a monumental success. The device appears to be fully operational!

passages.title: Report to Gila
passages.text:
I was quite fortunate that King Mechagon found me worthy! 

I will send my assistant Gila Crosswires ahead to Boralus to gather a new team. Meet up with her and help out as you can.

I will join both of you shortly.

passages.title: Report to Gila
passages.text: The Tinkmaster has entrusted me with this task, so let's not mess it up!

passages.title: A Small Team
passages.text:
I've determined the single attribute that is most important for a team member to survive an expedition to Mechagon. 

That attribute is...being a gnome!

Gather these gnomes and meet Tinkmaster Overspark and myself at the departure point.

passages.title: A Small Team
passages.text: Everyone and everything is packed up and ready to go.

passages.title: Ships in the Night
passages.text:
Sylvanas has gone too far this time. We may be at war with the Alliance, but there are certain lines we cannot cross.

I must right this situation, but I need your assistance. Derek Proudmoore is being held on the Swift Vengeance, which is moored in the harbor here for supplies. 

We must take him and bring him back to his family. Are you with me?

passages.title: Ships in the Night
passages.text: There's no time to waste.

passages.title: Ships in the Night
passages.text:
Proudmoore is here, but this cage may prove problematic.

I don't think we're going to be able to brute force this lock.

passages.title: A Bitter Reunion
passages.text:
We've done it! Zelling will guide the ship to Theramore, and we can put an end to this foul business once and for all.

Speak to Zelling when you are ready to leave, and we will set sail.

passages.title: A Bitter Reunion
passages.text: We sail at your command, <class>.

passages.title: A Bitter Reunion
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, <class>. 

I must return home, but Zelling has a plan to hide our actions from Sylvanas' eyes.

The Banshee Queen must not learn of what transpired here, for it would put far more lives at risk than our own.

passages.title: Righting Wrongs
passages.text:
Champion! I come with an urgent request from Baine Bloodhoof. He asks that you meet him at Plunder Harbor to help him with a... sensitive situation.

You must tell no one of this request, <class>. 

Ancestors watch over you.

passages.title: Righting Wrongs
passages.text: I see you've received my message.

passages.title: Righting Wrongs
passages.text:
You're here.

Good, now we can proceed.

passages.title: A One-Way Ticket to the Heart
passages.text:
These titan facilities never cease tae amaze me. I can only imagine how many of their secrets Brann has yet tae uncover.

I just hope that one o' them holds the answer tae saving Azeroth.

It's time tae bring MOTHER tae the Chamber of Heart. Be prepared for anythin', champion. Ye can never be quite sure what will happen when ye activate a titan machine.

passages.title: A One-Way Ticket to the Heart
passages.text:
That was close! But we made it back tae the Chamber of Heart. Now tae see if MOTHER can find a way to heal Azeroth.

Thank ye, <name>.

passages.title: Chopped Bots
passages.text:
Chopping up bots is my business. Any bots you bring to my scrapper will be broken up into useful parts. It's a win for both of us!

Use the Bot-Energizer to bring me dead bots, and we'll break them into spare parts.

passages.title: Chopped Bots
passages.text: Re-animate dead bots and bring them to me!

passages.title: Chopped Bots
passages.text: I love those spare parts! You're can grind up bots here anytime you want!

passages.title: Descent
passages.text:
We've lost the bulk of our forces already; any more and we won't have enough to make a stand.

This wreckage won't keep the naga at bay, so we must find safety elsewhere.

You will have to trust me here, adventurer. Leap off the falls and you will descend safely.

passages.title: Descent
passages.text: Never give up.

passages.title: Descent
passages.text: Thank you for giving me your trust.

passages.title: A Brief Respite
passages.text:
We have much to do, <name>. However, we are all weary and require rest. Decisions made while fatigued are almost always the wrong ones to make.

The Ankoan have offered their home to us, yet they are barely holding on themselves. We should do what we can to support them while we think about our next move.

See what you can do to aid their hunting parties, it may be the only way we survive in this place.

passages.title: A Brief Respite
passages.text:
Good work. Your efforts have helped us establish some trust with our new allies and gained some much-needed combat experience in this strange place.

They have entrusted us with this item, I sense incredibly power within. It is clearly attuned to the Heart of Azeroth, you should take it. Hopefully it is of use to us.

passages.title: The Shadow of Gilneas
passages.text:
Champion of Gilneas!

I have a letter for you from Princess Tess Greymane. She requests your presence in Stormwind Keep.

passages.title: The Shadow of Gilneas
passages.text: You have arrived just in time, <name>.

passages.title: Into Duskwood
passages.text:
There is a night elf I met in Teldrassil, Vassandra Stormclaw, who may be able to teach Tess without resorting to such an extreme measure. She is the one who originally helped our people with their affliction.

Vassandra is currently in Duskwood, assisting the residents of Raven Hill with their attempts to cure the feral worgen in the area. If anyone knows about the curse, it is her.

As a more personal request, do not let my daughter do anything too rash. She takes after her father in that way.

passages.title: Into Duskwood
passages.text: Is there something you need, <class>?

passages.title: Bane of the Nightbane
passages.text:
Princess Greymane has informed me of the situation and I do have an idea of how to help.

But first, a favor for a favor. The residents of Duskwood have been plagued recently by a particularly ferocious member of the Nightbane pack that they call 'Bloodeyes'. Take Master Harris's sedative and bring the worgen back to me alive. She will be a perfect subject to test cures on.

passages.title: Bane of the Nightbane
passages.text: If we can cure even the most feral of <race>, then the curse will mean nothing to us.

passages.title: Bane of the Nightbane
passages.text: I thank you for your help. Tess has yet to return from her task.

passages.title: Cry to the Moon
passages.text:
Duskwood has a direct connection to the Emerald Dream. Through this connection, I may be able to call forth the Ancient Goldrinn. He will be able to give the princess a taste of the curse she so dangerously chases.

A rare bloom grows on the east side of the woods, gather its bloom and meet me in Twilight Grove. It will help me with this ritual.

passages.title: Cry to the Moon
passages.text: Such flowers have been known to attract wolves, but I doubt you will have a problem with that.

passages.title: Cry to the Moon
passages.text: Perfect. This should help lure the great wolf out of hiding.

passages.title: The Spirit of the Hunter
passages.text:
The other thing I may need for this ritual are the fangs of a wolf.

There is a pack that has newly settled in around Manor Mistmantle. Bring me their fangs. I will await your return at Twilight Grove.

passages.title: The Spirit of the Hunter
passages.text: Did you claim your trophy?

passages.title: The Spirit of the Hunter
passages.text: The Scythe of Elune was formed using the fang of Goldrinn. This ritual attempts to echo just a small bit of that power.

passages.title: Waking a Dreamer
passages.text:
This should be all I need to call upon the Ancient.

Some unwanted visitors may answer the call first. Protect me as I perform the ritual!

passages.title: Waking a Dreamer
passages.text: The Dream can be a perilous place. Do you wish to join her?

passages.title: Let Sleeping Wolves Lie
passages.text:
Tess's essence now wanders a section of the Emerald Dream I have twisted into her thoughts. And I have given her my gift, but she could still use a guide.

Enter the Dream through the portal behind me. It will place you near where she sleeps. See if you can help show her how rage may blind a mortal.

passages.title: Let Sleeping Wolves Lie
passages.text: I... I need to talk with my father.

passages.title: The New Guard
passages.text:
I need to speak with my parents again. I think my father and I have a bit to discuss.

Meet me back at Stormwind Keep. I would like to thank you in a more formal manner.

passages.title: The New Guard
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The New Guard
passages.text: Consider it more of an honorary title. I hope I never see the day where I am forced to rely on it.

passages.title: The Start of Something Bigger
passages.text:
We have coordinates locked into the gyrocopters. You and Captain Winklespring will fly the lead. If we run into any trouble, Tinkmaster Overspark wants the most experienced pilots out front.

Board whenever you are ready to go.

passages.title: The Start of Something Bigger
passages.text: It appears King Mechagon mistook us for enemies.

passages.title: A Savage Path Through Time
passages.text: The brutal star shines upon the land, threatening to trample underfoot all who stand in its path. This star is many things: primal, fierce, and noble. While its influence holds, new paths may open up to distant places and even distant times. No sage truly understands the nature of this sign, but fortune favors the daring.

passages.title: A Savage Path Through Time
passages.text: Ah, <name>, you have returned. An otherworldly air hangs heavy about you.

passages.title: Remembrance
passages.text:
You may remember the day Thunder Bluff was attacked. It was your efforts and your guide who saved us.

Now we take time to honor our ancestors and give thanks for the path they have set for us.

Bring this offering to the cliffs overlooking Thunder Bluff and give thanks to your guide and all our ancestors.

A simple gesture to commemorate our past. This is our way.

passages.title: Remembrance
passages.text: On this day we remember and give thanks to the ones who have come before us. May the Earth Mother guide you.

passages.title: Dead in the Water
passages.text:
Once Proudmoore is freed, we will need to commandeer this ship to transport him to Theramore, where his sister awaits us. 

Zelling's magic can guide the ship there, but first we'll need to take care of the crew.

passages.title: Dead in the Water
passages.text:
The ship is clear. 

I will signal Zelling to join us.

passages.title: Murder at the Brawlpub
passages.text:
The Brawlpub quartermaster lies dead in front of you. He was murdered in broad daylight!

He must have been assassinated while someone was fighting in the arena. Maybe even during one of your fights.

Perhaps there are some clues nearby as to who might have killed him.

passages.title: Murder at the Brawlpub
passages.text:
So, you took it upon yourself to investigate the murder? Interesting...

<Commander Daalo jots something down, looks up at you, and then finishes writing his notes.>

passages.title: Put Up Your Dukes
passages.text:
You know what?

<The commander puts his notebook away.>

I COULD use a good <class> on my investigations team. We've had some personnel issues lately and, frankly, I can use all the help I can get.

But first: why don't you go hop into the arena for a few fights so I can get a good look at your skills?

passages.title: Put Up Your Dukes
passages.text:
While you were fighting, I took the liberty of looking into your background a bit, <name>. Quite impressive, I must say.

I apologize for my earlier suspicions. Welcome to the team.

passages.title: Undercover Agent: Ann Dennyson
passages.text:
Lord Winifred Browne is one of our primary suspects in this case. Browne is an infamously aggressive speculator, and has a list of debts a mile long.

He may be in need of money, which is consistent with the evidence you found earlier.

My associate Ann has taken point on the case. I'd like you to assist her. I think you'll work well together.

passages.title: Undercover Agent: Ann Dennyson
passages.text:
<name>? Ann. Pleased to make your acquaintance.

Lord Browne is over there, with the ridiculous hat on him.

No, no... don't just stare right at him! We're undercover, bonehead.

passages.title: A Favor for Your Old Chum Winifred
passages.text:
A moment of your time, <good sir/madam>.

It's about all that money you won from me. Interestingly enough, that may have been slightly more money than I actually have, and now it would appear that some very powerful people want to break my elbows and my knees.

I cannot pay them! I am quite broke! Ha ha!

All I need to get back above water is for you to lose your next fight. Flop like a fish, as they say. Please.

passages.title: A Favor for Your Old Chum Winifred
passages.text: You must help me! Their threats were quite descriptive, and slightly scatological!

passages.title: A Favor for Your Old Chum Winifred
passages.text: Many thanks, <name>.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Lord Winifred Browne
passages.text:
I heard everything. That guy sure does talk loudly about his crimes and debts, doesn't he?

It sounds like we have enough to bring him in for questioning. I've put together a packet of evidence for Commander Daalo to review.

Good job out there.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Lord Winifred Browne
passages.text: Find anything on Browne?

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Lord Winifred Browne
passages.text:
<Commander Daalo looks over the evidence.>

This is more than enough to get a warrant. Excellent work, <name>. But your job's not over yet.

passages.title: Undercover Agent: Saralara Fizzlesprang
passages.text:
I believe you've met one of my other agents: Saralara Fizzlesprang. She's investigating our second suspect: Shadowmaster O'Flannerty.

You'll find Saralara near the scene of the crime.

passages.title: Undercover Agent: Saralara Fizzlesprang
passages.text:
<name>? Saralara Fizzlesprang. Nice to meet you. Again.

O'Flannerty's back over there, to my left. You go take point, I'll hang back and jump in if things get ugly.

passages.title: Cause for Concern
passages.text:
Shadowmaster O'Flannerty's behavior was unusual.

His repeated mutterings about "shadow magic" and "void apocalypses" and "ancient creatures hungering for the souls of the living" certainly warrant further investigation.

You should report back to Saralara Fizzlesprang.

passages.title: Cause for Concern
passages.text:
<She listens to your report.>

Hmm. Yes. I think I know what's going on. It looks like we're going to have to solve this problem with science.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Shadowmaster O'Flannerty
passages.text:
Sounds like we've found our perp, <name>. This guy's sketchy, desperate, and his shadow magic is consistent with that shadowy scroll you found earlier.

Bring this packet to Daalo, and we can bring him in. Good work out there!

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Shadowmaster O'Flannerty
passages.text: Any news on O'Flannerty?

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Shadowmaster O'Flannerty
passages.text:
<The commander looks over the notes.>

Wow. It's worse than I thought. We'd better bring him in soon, because this guy's a nut job.

passages.title: Simply Dying of Boredom
passages.text:
Up until now, I've been dying of boredom up here. I think maybe we need some new blood here in the arena. Bizmo can be so stingy with his invitations, can't he?

I've had one of my servants write up a few slightly-counterfeit invitations to hand out. Maybe you could help me get them distributed? There's always plenty of tough-looking characters hanging out in front of the auction house in the Trade District...

passages.title: Simply Dying of Boredom
passages.text:
You placed the sign? Good. Now we just wait for the newbies to show up.

I like you, <name>. You're like me: willing to commit a crime or two in the name of self-entertainment.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Grant Lazarby
passages.text:
Good work. I never expected Lazarby to be so... self-incriminating.

You may bring the packet to Commander. I'm going to go buy some expensive snacks at the VIP bar.

passages.title: Evidence Packet: Grant Lazarby
passages.text:
Hmm... I wouldn't be surprised if he killed the quartermaster just for his own entertainment.

For now, we can bring him in on counterfeiting charges, and get more details in court. Good work.

passages.title: The Brawlpub Trial
passages.text:
I've issued three warrants. Jussho, Saralara, and Anne are apprehending the suspects as we speak.

It's time to go to court.

You may be called on to testify. Just answer as honestly as you can, and let the wheels of justice do the rest.

passages.title: The Brawlpub Trial
passages.text:
I really think things were going well there... up to the point where it didn't.

Luckily for us, we've got a new lead. Listen up, <name> - your job isn't done yet.

passages.title: A Clue from Area 52
passages.text:
We've received a letter from Area 52, the goblin outpost in Netherstorm. The author claims to know details about what they call "the situation in the Brawlpub".

They don't say more than that.

I'm tied to my paperwork here. Go check out this lead and see if anything turns up.

passages.title: A Clue from Area 52
passages.text: These mysterious impostors may have gotten the better of me, and they may have gotten away with murder, but little do they know... I hold the trump card!

passages.title: Solving the Mystery
passages.text:
<Bizmo produces a challenge card from his pocket.>

I grabbed this challenge card from my attackers while we were fighting each other! I'm sure that you can use it to challenge my attacker to some sort of ultimate showdown!

passages.title: Solving the Mystery
passages.text:
I was there, <name>. I saw your fight.

We've had our suspicions about this "Watcher" character since the incident in Quel'Danas. It seems the rumors are true. They are watching us.

I'll relay the information to the correct authorities. Meanwhile, Bizmo and I have arranged for a suitable reward for you. I hope you find it to your liking.

passages.title: Bizmo's Brawlpub Awaits!
passages.text:
Tired of standing around in the boring old Trade District? Come on over to Bizmo's Brawlpub, and fight for the amusement of others!

You might win, or you might get killed, but either way, you're going to have a great time.

Grab an invitation and bring it to Han Heavypaw, near the front door. The Brawlpub awaits!

passages.title: Bizmo's Brawlpub Awaits!
passages.text:
<Han inspects the invitation intently.>

Hmph. Looks good enough to me. Come on in.

passages.title: Blueprint: Scrap Trap
passages.text:
<This blueprint details how to build what appears to be some sort of land mine using little more than scrap metal.

You should be able to upload the blueprint to Pascal-K1N6's database in Rustbolt.>

passages.title: Blueprint: Scrap Trap
passages.text:
Have you recovered a new blueprint, my fleshy friend?

I will add it to my database posthaste.

passages.title: Ashes to Ashvane
passages.text:
This place is just crawling with Ashvane loyalists, <name>.

How about we do the Kul Tirans a favor and get rid of some of them.

<Kelsey grins.>

I got a head start on the way here, but there's plenty to go around!

passages.title: Ashes to Ashvane
passages.text: Nice work. They'll have a harder time recruiting now.

passages.title: A Terrible Place
The Master Shipwright
passages.text:
Now I am starting to remember...

Dorian Atwater was a very secretive builder. Their slips were famously warded against prying eyes until the vessel was complete. It made something of a stir any time one of their works was revealed.

Last I heard, they retired in Stormsong Valley. I am not certain how reliable that information is.

Hm. We should head to Brennadam. It is a crossroads of sorts. If anyone knows where to find our shipwright, they will be there.

passages.title: The Master Shipwright
passages.text: You've got that letter? I have a feeling we'll be needing it before long.

passages.title: The Master Shipwright
passages.text: Right. Let's get started.

passages.title: Looking Inside
passages.text:
This vault screams of ancient gnomish tech! I believe this could be the key that leads us to King Mechagon!

I can't risk putting myself in danger though, so you will lead the way into the vault. 

Well, what are we waiting for? Let's see what's inside!

passages.title: Looking Inside
passages.text: This is such a great moment in gnomish history. Your help here will be noted in the historical journals.

passages.title: Fish Tales and Distant Sails
passages.text:
I have an idea where to start, but it couldn't hurt to ask the locals. 

I hope it goes without saying that you shouldn't believe everything you hear, <name>. My people are very fond of embellishing the truth.

I will meet you in The Golden Flagon when you've had a chance to ask around.

passages.title: Fish Tales and Distant Sails
passages.text: Did you learn anything useful?

passages.title: Fish Tales and Distant Sails
passages.text:
<He studies a map of Stormsong Valley.>

What's the word, <name>?

passages.title: Don't Shoot the Messenger
passages.text:
While he was the gladiator known as Lo'Gosh, King Varian fought beside Valeera Sanguinar. He trusted her and that allowed SI:7 to have a... cordial relationship with her. Valeera's loyalty has carried on to King Anduin.

During the fight with the Legion, I came to know her as a capable if... independent operative. She can go where even some of my agents cannot.

We should listen to whatever message she brings. I imagine the source will be interesting.

passages.title: Don't Shoot the Messenger
passages.text: This is... surprising news.

passages.title: Don't Shoot the Messenger
passages.text: Anduin is very trusting. Varian was much less so and chose his friends and allies carefully. But Master Shaw has a finely tuned sense of paranoia, shall we say. If he believes Valeera speaks the truth about Baine, then I am inclined to follow his lead.

passages.title: Securing Warfang Hold
passages.text:
The Dark Lady has important work for you, <name>.

Preparations are beginning for a meeting of the Horde's leadership at Warfang Hold. I trust I don't need to emphasize that security is of the highest import for this gathering.

The goblin, Gallywix, has sent his underlings to make sure the area is swept of any... unwanted guests. I need you to make sure they succeed in their task.

passages.title: Securing Warfang Hold
passages.text:
So Nathanos thinks we don't have the situation under control? Well, he's right. 

Just don't tell him that. Smug jerk would never let me hear the end of it.

passages.title: Spy Games
passages.text:
The Alliance must've got wind of this meeting and they've sent SI:7 spies to try to listen in.

The problem is, they're using some kind of gnomish tech to sneak past our detectors. One of our techs was able to put together something that should be able to neutralize whatever they're using, but the range is short. 

I'll need you to take it out into the field and look for evidence of SI:7 activity. Just mash the button on that thing when you think they're close, and it should zap 'em back into view.

passages.title: Spy Games
passages.text:
Looks like goblin tech wins again!

Seriously though, thanks for saving my hide.

passages.title: Communication Breakdown
passages.text:
It looks like the stealth generators aren't the only tech that SI:7 is bringing into the field. Our scouts have reported what look like listening devices set up at key points around Warfang. 

Obviously, these things have to go, but the goons haven't been able to get close to them on account of the hidden spies. 

While you're out there, make sure to trash 'em.

passages.title: Communication Breakdown
passages.text:
Looks like I owe you another one, pal.

I'll have Kazit add it to the books.

passages.title: Tickets, Please?
passages.text:
There's another problem we could use your help with, <class>. 

Gallywix knew this meeting was going to be a big deal, so naturally he decided to sell tickets. The thing is, I've done a headcount here, and we've got a lot more people here than tickets sold, so some of these spectators are trying to pull a fast one.

Most of our muscle is out in the Clearcut getting killed by spies, so we could use the help. Care to make an honest wage?

passages.title: Tickets, Please?
passages.text: The nerve of these people!

passages.title: Tickets, Please?
passages.text:
<Kazit makes some tallies in his notebook.>

Yeah, that's lookin' about right. Here's your pay.

Hey, don't give me that look. I said an honest wage, not a good one!

passages.title: A Display of Power
passages.text:
It looks like all the big players are here. This thing's gonna be starting any moment now.

You'll probably want to get a good seat.

passages.title: A Display of Power
passages.text:
This is a troublesome turn of events.

I'm afraid the Banshee Queen may have set in motion a ruinous path for the Horde. 

Keep your eyes and ears open, <name>. The day is not yet done.

passages.title: Securing Warfang Hold
passages.text:
<name>, the Dark Lady has need of your services once more.

The traitor, Baine, is being brought before the leaders of the Horde at Warfang Hold. Preparations are underway as we speak to secure the area.

The efforts are headed up by Gallywix's minions, who I wouldn't trust to secure a kennel. You will need to go to Warfang Hold and make sure the area is locked down.

We are counting on you, <name>.

passages.title: Securing Warfang Hold
passages.text:
So Nathanos thinks we don't have the situation under control? Well, he's right. 

Just don't tell him that. Smug jerk would never let me hear the end of it.

passages.title: Upheaval
passages.text:
We're surrounded by the dead, dying, and other detritus.

Feels like war, does it not?

Oculeth and others have gone ahead to see to the soldiers.

Perhaps you ought to see to them as well?

passages.title: Upheaval
passages.text: Not to worry, <name>. It's not as if I'd magic you into the middle of the ocean without notice! Well, I suppose that is where we are, is it not?

passages.title: Build A Bigger Fish Trap
passages.text:
With those minnows and some spare parts, you should be able to build a Hundred-Fathom Lure.

Visit Pascal-K1N6 in Rustbolt and build one.

Then come back here, and we'll catch a huge fish!

passages.title: Build A Bigger Fish Trap
passages.text: Get to it, we have a fish to catch!

passages.title: Build A Bigger Fish Trap
passages.text: Now, let's catch us a fish!
